other synonyms: Singapore Diabetic Nephropathy|Singapore Study of Diabetic Nephropathy
definition: A cohort of outpatients with type 2 diabetes of Chinese, Malay and Asian Indian ancestry recruited from the diabetes centre of a regional hospital in Singapore between 2004 and 2015 to study the development and progression of diabetic nephropathy and of major cardiovascular disease.
diseases: patients with: diabetic kidney disease (MONDO:0005016)|patients with: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: Singapore Study of Macro-Angiopathy and Micro-Vascular Reactivity in Type 2 Diabetes
other synonyms: Singapore Study of Macro-angiopathy and Micro-vascular Reactivity in Type 2 Diabetes
definition: A prospective cohort of adults with type 2 diabetes of Chinese, Malay, Indian and other ancestry recruited in 2011–2014 from a public hospital and primary care polyclinics in northern Singapore and followed in three-yearly waves to study risk factors for vascular function and diabetes-related complications such as kidney disease, retinopathy and cognitive dysfunction.

label: Women's Health Initiative
other synonyms: Womens Health Initiative
definition: A cohort of postmenopausal women aged 50–79 enrolled from 1993 at 40 clinical centres across the United States into a clinical trial of dietary modification, hormone therapy and calcium and vitamin D supplementation or into a parallel observational study, followed to study the prevention of cancer, cardiovascular disease and osteoporotic fractures.

label: Study of Health in Pomerania-TREND
other synonyms: Study of Health in Pomerania Trend
definition: A population-based cohort of adults aged 20–79 sampled from Western Pomerania, a rural region of north-eastern Germany, and recruited in 2008–2012 as the second, independent cohort of the Study of Health in Pomerania, examined at baseline and followed up to study health, disease and their risk factors.

label: Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study
other synonyms: KoGES Consortium|Korea Biobank Array|Korean Biobank Array|Korean Genome Epidemiology Study|National Institute of Health launched the Korea Biobank Array project
definition: A consortium of six Korean cohorts, population-based and gene–environment model studies initiated from 2001 with about 245,000 participants, investigating the genetic and environmental determinants of health, disease and ageing in the Korean population.

label: Netherlands Epidemiology of Obesity Study
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of 6,673 men and women aged 45–65 from the greater area of Leiden, the Netherlands, oversampling people with overweight or obesity, recruited in 2008–2012 for extensive phenotyping to investigate the pathways that lead to obesity-related diseases.

label: Wisconsin Registry for Alzheimer's Prevention
definition: A longitudinal observational cohort of middle-aged adults enriched for persons with a parental history of probable Alzheimer disease dementia, enrolled since 2001 at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, United States, and followed with serial cognitive assessments, medical and lifestyle histories, laboratory tests, genetics and linked imaging and cerebrospinal fluid studies to study the early course of Alzheimer disease.

label: Wisconsin Alzheimer's Disease Research Center
other synonyms: Wisconsin ADRC Clinical Core
definition: A longitudinal cohort, the Clinical Core study of the Wisconsin Alzheimer's Disease Research Center, a National Institute on Aging-funded centre established in 2009 at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, United States, in which adults aged 45 and over, recruited into subgroups with mild late-onset Alzheimer disease, mild cognitive impairment, healthy older controls, and middle-aged adults with a positive, negative or indeterminate parental history of Alzheimer disease, attend annual or every-other-year visits with a study partner for memory and thinking evaluations, blood draws and biomarker visits with MRI, lumbar puncture and PET, to study memory, ageing and Alzheimer disease.
diseases: patients with: Alzheimer disease (MONDO:0004975)|patients with: cognitive disorder (MONDO:0002039)

label: Food Chain Plus
other synonyms: Food Chain Plus Cohort
definition: A cohort of 1,795 adults aged 18–83 from the Kiel region of northern Germany, enrolled in 2011–2014 at random via residents' registration offices and via the Obesity Outpatient Centre of the University Medical Center Schleswig-Holstein, for population-based research on metabolic inflammation with multi-omics, nutrition and follow-up every five years.
diseases: population study of: obesity disorder (MONDO:0011122)|population study of: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: Amish Complex Disease Research Program
other synonyms: Amish Research Program|Amish Study|Genetics of Cardiometabolic Health in the Amish Study|Old Order Amish|The older order AMISH population studies
definition: A research programme of the University of Maryland studying adults of the Old Order Amish founder population of Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, of whom over 7,000 have taken part in one or more of its studies of the genetics of complex diseases.

label: BioVU
other synonyms: Nashville Biosciences|Vanderbilt Biobank|Vanderbilt DNA Databank
definition: A biobank of Vanderbilt University Medical Center in Nashville, Tennessee, United States, which since February 2007 has banked DNA extracted from blood left over from routine clinical testing of its patients, originally under an opt-out model and now from patients who sign the BioVU consent form, with more than 300,000 samples by January 2023, each linked to a de-identified copy of the patient's electronic health record (the Synthetic Derivative), as a resource for genotype–phenotype studies and personalised medicine.

label: Southall and Brent Revisited
other synonyms: Southall And Brent REvisited|Southall and Brent Revisited Study
definition: A tri-ethnic longitudinal cohort of people of European, South Asian and African Caribbean ethnicity living in West and North London, United Kingdom, set up in 1988 to examine ethnic differences in chronic disease.
diseases: population study of: cardiovascular disorder (MONDO:0004995)|population study of: diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005015)

label: Gut-and-Liver Axis in Alcoholic Liver Fibrosis
other synonyms: GALAXY cohort
definition: A cohort of the EU Horizon 2020 GALAXY (Gut-and-liver axis in alcoholic liver fibrosis) consortium, recruited between 2013 and 2018 by Odense University Hospital in the Region of Southern Denmark, of about 460 consecutively recruited patients with a history of harmful drinking (more than 36 g of alcohol a day for men and 24 g for women for at least a year) and early, asymptomatic alcohol-related liver disease (GALA-ALD), most with a liver biopsy, and some 140 to 150 healthy participants matched to them by age and sex (GALA-HP), to study the gut–liver axis and non-invasive markers of alcohol-related liver fibrosis.
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to alcohol abuse (ECTO:6000009)

label: Cardiovascular Risk in Young Finns Study
other synonyms: Young Finns Study
definition: A population-based cohort of 3,596 randomly selected Finnish children and adolescents aged 3–18 years at baseline in 1980, followed into adulthood for over three decades to study how cardiovascular risk factors in childhood relate to preclinical markers of cardiovascular disease in adulthood.

label: Study of Colorectal Cancer in Scotland
other synonyms: Scottish Colorectal Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case–control study of colorectal cancer in Scotland, recruiting colorectal cancer cases and population controls since 1999, whose genotyped cases are followed for survival, used to study genetic susceptibility to colorectal cancer and its outcomes.

label: China Kadoorie Biobank
other synonyms: Kadoorie Study of Chronic Disease in China
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of more than 512,000 adults recruited in 2004–2008 from 10 geographically diverse regions of China, with baseline questionnaires and physical measurements, periodic resurveys, genome-wide genotyping of over 100,000 participants and electronic linkage to death, disease and health-insurance records, supporting studies of disease risk factors, genetics and drug targets.

label: All of Us Research Program
other synonyms: All of Us|NIH All of Us Research Program|Precision Medicine Initiative Cohort Program
definition: A national research cohort led by the National Institutes of Health that aims to enrol at least one million diverse adults in the United States, most from groups historically under-represented in biomedical research, through more than 340 recruitment sites, collecting health questionnaires, electronic health records, physical measurements, digital health data and biospecimens to advance precision medicine.

label: BioMe Biobank
other synonyms: BioMe BioBank Program|Charles R Bronfman Institute for Personalized Medicine - IPM / BioBank Genome Wide Association Study of Cardiovascular, Renal and Metabolic Phenotypes|IPM Biobank|Institute for Personalized Medicine (IPM) BioMe Biobank Project|MT. SINAI BioMe Biobank Platform|Mount Sinai BioMe BioBank|Mount Sinai BioMe Biobank|Mount Sinai School of Medicine BioBank
definition: An electronic health record-linked biobank founded in 2007 at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai that enrols participants non-selectively from the Mount Sinai Health System in New York City, comprising about 60,000 ancestrally diverse participants with genotype and sequence data for genetic and clinical research.

label: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults Study
other synonyms: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults
definition: A prospective cohort of young adults aged 18–30 years, balanced by sex and by Black and White race, recruited in 1985–1986 at four field centres in Birmingham, Alabama, Chicago, Illinois, Minneapolis, Minnesota and Oakland, California, and followed with repeated examinations into midlife to study the development of cardiovascular risk factors and disease.

label: Health for Life in Singapore
other synonyms: HELIOS Study|Health for Life in Singapore Study
definition: A prospective population-based cohort of 10,004 men and women of Chinese, Indian or Malay background aged 30–84, recruited from the Singapore general population in 2018–2022 by Nanyang Technological University, with behavioural, phenotypic and multi-omic measurements and health-record linkage for precision-medicine research in Asian populations.

label: Cleveland Family Study
definition: A family-based longitudinal cohort of index probands with laboratory-confirmed obstructive sleep apnoea, their relatives, and neighbourhood control families recruited from the Cleveland metropolitan area, Ohio, with four examinations between 1990 and 2006, designed to study the familial and genetic basis of sleep-disordered breathing.
diseases: at risk of: Sleep-related breathing disorders (HP:5200283)|at risk of: obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (MONDO:0007147)

label: deCODE genetics Icelandic cohort
other synonyms: deCODE Genetics
definition: A population sample of Icelanders recruited through the disease-specific and general-population research projects of deCODE genetics in Reykjavik, Iceland, including the deCODE Health Study, whose chip genotypes and whole-genome sequences, combined with the nationwide Icelandic genealogy, are used for genome-wide association studies of diseases and other traits.

label: PainOMICS Retrospective Study
other synonyms: A Retrospective Study to Identify New "Omics" Biomarkers of Chronic/Persistent Low Back Pain|PainOmicc Retrospective Study|PainOmics retrospective study|PainOmics study
definition: A retrospective, multicentre case–control study of adults of Caucasian ancestry with chronic low back pain and controls without chronic pain, run within the European Union FP7-funded PainOMICS project (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02037789), which enrolled 3,400 participants between September 2014 and February 2016 at clinical centres in Italy, Belgium, the United Kingdom and Croatia (the registered protocol also listed sites in the United States and Australia), collecting clinical data and blood samples for genome-wide association, glycomics and activomics analyses of chronic low back pain.

label: The Pomak cohort
other synonyms: Pomak
definition: A population-based cohort of adults from the Pomak villages of the regional unit of Xanthi, a set of religiously isolated mountainous villages of the Muslim Pomak minority in northern Greece, 1,702 of whom were recruited as volunteers through the local health centre in Echinos between July 2010 and March 2013 within the Hellenic Isolated Cohorts (HELIC) study, with interview-based questionnaires, anthropometric, haematological and biochemical measurements and blood samples for DNA that were genotyped and whole-genome sequenced, to study the genetics of cardiometabolic and other medically relevant complex traits in an isolated population.

label: Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging
other synonyms: GERA cohort|Genetic Epidemiology Research in Adult Health and Aging|Genetic Epidemiology Research on Aging|Kaiser Permanente Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging cohort
definition: A multi-ethnic cohort of over 100,000 adult members of the Kaiser Permanente Northern California health plan who consented to the Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health (RPGEH), linking survey data, saliva-derived DNA with genome-wide genotypes and telomere length, and electronic health records for research on the genetic and environmental determinants of common age-related diseases.

label: Correlated Expression and Disease Association Research
other synonyms: CEDAR cohort|Correlated Expression & Disease Association Research
definition: A cohort of about 320 healthy adult Europeans visiting the Academic Hospital of the University of Liège, Belgium, as part of a national colon-cancer screening campaign, from whom peripheral blood and intestinal biopsies were collected to generate transcriptomes of circulating immune cell types and gut tissues for expression quantitative trait locus analysis of inflammatory bowel disease risk loci.

label: Generation Scotland: Scottish Family Health Study
other synonyms: Generation Scotland|Generation Scotland Scottish Family Health Study
definition: A family-based population cohort of 24,084 adults, including 5,501 families, recruited in Scotland between 2006 and 2011 by Generation Scotland, a collaboration of the Universities of Aberdeen, Dundee, Edinburgh and Glasgow and NHS Scotland. It comprises 6,665 probands aged 35–65, selected from lists of collaborating general practices in the Glasgow and Tayside areas (extended to Ayrshire, Arran and Grampian in 2010), and 17,419 of their adult relatives. Participants completed questionnaires, attended a clinic visit or took part by post, gave DNA for genome-wide genotyping and consented to record linkage and recontact, for the study of the genetic, lifestyle and environmental determinants of common diseases such as heart disease, stroke and depression.

label: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy
other synonyms: GENOA Study|Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA) study
definition: A community-based family study of hypertensive sibships, recruited from 1996 among non-Hispanic Black adults in Jackson, Mississippi, non-Hispanic white adults in Rochester, Minnesota and (initially) Hispanic adults in Starr County, Texas, to identify genes influencing blood pressure and hypertensive target-organ damage.

label: Northern Finland Birth Cohorts
other synonyms: Northern Finland Birth Cohorts - Research program for health and well-being|Northern Finnish Birth Cohort Study
definition: A longitudinal research programme of the University of Oulu comprising two general-population birth cohorts from the two northernmost provinces of Finland, Oulu and Lapland, the Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966 (NFBC1966) and 1986 (NFBC1986), whose members have been followed since the fetal period to study health and well-being.

label: Taiwan Biobank
definition: An ongoing prospective population biobank of more than 150,000 predominantly Han Chinese volunteers aged 20-70 recruited across Taiwan, with questionnaire, physical-measurement, biomarker and genome-wide genetic data and linkage to national health insurance records, built as a resource for biomedical and public health research in East Asia.

label: GeneRISK study
other synonyms: GeneRISK cohort
definition: A prospective cohort of about 7,300 adults aged 45-66 recruited in southern Finland in 2015-2017 (from the Kymenlaakso population register, occupational health care customers in Helsinki and Turku, and blood donors) to assess the impact of communicating genetic risk information for cardiovascular disease to participants.

label: Healthy Aging in Neighborhoods of Diversity across the Life Span
other synonyms: HANDLS Study|Healthy Aging in Neighborhoods of Diversity across the Life Span Study
definition: A community-based prospective longitudinal cohort of 3,722 socioeconomically diverse African American and white adults aged 30-64, recruited between 2004 and 2009 by household screening from an area probability sample of 13 neighbourhoods of Baltimore, Maryland, in a factorial design by age, sex, race and poverty status, to examine how race and socioeconomic status influence the development of age-related health disparities.

label: Mount Sinai Crohn's and Colitis Registry
definition: A prospective cross-sectional cohort of about 1,500 adults with Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis and non-IBD controls (people undergoing colon cancer screening), recruited between December 2013 and September 2016 during their endoscopy visits to the outpatient and endoscopy units of the Mount Sinai Hospital, with paired intestinal biopsies and blood samples, RNA sequencing, genotype data and clinical, endoscopic and histological assessments for molecular studies of inflammatory bowel disease.
diseases: patients with: Crohn disease (MONDO:0005011)|patients with: ulcerative colitis (MONDO:0005101)

label: Netherlands Study of Depression and Anxiety
definition: A multi-site naturalistic longitudinal case-control cohort in the Netherlands of 2,981 adults aged 18-65, 2,329 with a current or remitted depressive and/or anxiety disorder and 652 healthy controls, recruited from 2004 in the general population, primary care and specialised mental health care in the regions of Amsterdam, Leiden and Groningen, extended from 2014 with 367 of their siblings to 3,348 participants and reassessed repeatedly over more than nine years, to study the aetiology, long-term course and consequences of depressive and anxiety disorders by integrating psychological, social, biological and genetic factors.
diseases: patients with: anxiety disorder (MONDO:0005618)|patients with: depressive disorder (MONDO:0002050)

label: Health, Aging and Body Composition Study
other synonyms: Health Aging and Body Composition|Health, Aging, and Body Composition Study|Health, Aging, and Body Composition study|Health, aging and body composition study
definition: A prospective cohort of 3,075 community-dwelling Black and white adults aged 70-79, recruited from 1997 from white Medicare beneficiaries and all eligible Black residents in and around Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania and Memphis, Tennessee, and followed for about 17 years to study body composition, functional decline and disease in older age.

label: Michigan Genomics Initiative
other synonyms: Michigan cohort
definition: A single-health-system biobank of more than 91,000 adult patients recruited mainly during surgical encounters at Michigan Medicine, the University of Michigan health system, linking genotypes to electronic health records for disease genetics research.

label: Immune and Metabolic Markers during Pregnancy and Child Development Study
other synonyms: IMPaCT Study|IMPaCT cohort
definition: A case-control study of mothers and children born at Kaiser Permanente Northern California from January 2011 to January 2016, oversampling children later diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder or other developmental delay alongside general-population controls, with maternal first- and second-trimester blood samples from the RPGEH pregnancy cohort, to study maternal immune and metabolic markers and child neurodevelopment.
diseases: patients with: autism spectrum disorder (MONDO:0005258)|patients with: neurodevelopmental disorder (MONDO:0700092)

label: Cohorts for Heart and Aging Research in Genomic Epidemiology Consortium
other synonyms: CHARGE Consortium|Cohorts for Heart and Aging Research in Genomic Epidemiology
definition: A consortium of large prospective population-based cohort studies from the United States and Europe, founded with the Age, Gene/Environment Susceptibility-Reykjavik Study, the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study, the Cardiovascular Health Study, the Framingham Heart Study and the Rotterdam Study, formed to facilitate genome-wide association meta-analyses and replication across cohorts with similarly measured phenotypes.

label: Helsinki Birth Cohort Study
definition: A birth cohort of the 13,345 singletons born in one of the two maternity hospitals in Helsinki, Finland, between 1934 and 1944, followed up in later life to study how early life shapes adult health.

label: Generation R Study
other synonyms: Generation R|Generation R Study Group|The Generation R Study
definition: A population-based prospective cohort from fetal life onwards of 9,778 mothers with delivery dates from April 2002 to January 2006 in Rotterdam, the Netherlands, and their children, designed to identify early environmental and genetic causes of normal and abnormal growth, development and health.
exposures: designed to study: exposure event (ExO:0000002)|designed to study: exposure to lifestyle (ECTO:6000015)|designed to study: exposure to nutrient (ECTO:9001695)

label: 500 Functional Genomics
other synonyms: 500 Functional Genomics cohort|500FG cohort
definition: A cohort of about 500 healthy adult volunteers of Western European ancestry recruited at Radboud University Medical Center in Nijmegen, the Netherlands, in 2013–2014 within the Human Functional Genomics Project, to study how genetic, environmental, host and microbiome factors shape individual cytokine and immune responses.

label: MyCode Community Health Initiative
acronyms: GHS|GMC|GeHS|Geisinger Cohort - MyCode Community Health Initiative|MyCode
other synonyms: Geisinger Medical Center|Geisinger MyCode|Geisinger MyCode Community Health Initiative|MyCode Health Initiative|MyCode biobank
definition: A biobank cohort of patients of Geisinger Health System, an integrated health system in central and eastern Pennsylvania, United States, who since 2007 have given opt-in consent to link their samples to electronic health record data for broad research use, with genotype and exome sequence data generated in collaboration with the Regeneron Genetics Center.

label: 23andMe research cohort
other synonyms: 23andMe cohort|23andMe research participants
definition: A cohort of customers of 23andMe, Inc., a direct-to-consumer genetics company, who have been genotyped and have consented to take part in online research, answering web-based questionnaires under an IRB-approved protocol, whose genotype and self-reported data are used for genome-wide association studies.

label: LIFE-Adult-Study
other synonyms: LIFE Adult Study
definition: A population-based cohort of 10,000 randomly selected adults, mainly aged 40–79, from the city of Leipzig in eastern Germany, examined in 2011–2014 by the Leipzig Research Centre for Civilization Diseases (LIFE) with deep phenotyping to study the prevalence, early markers, genetic predispositions and lifestyle factors of major civilization diseases.

label: Red Blood Cell-Omics Study
other synonyms: REDS RBC Omics|REDS RBC Omics Index cohort|REDS-III RBC-Omics|REDS-III RBC-Omics study|Red Blood Cell Omics Study
definition: A cohort of 13,403 racially and ethnically diverse volunteer blood donors aged 18 or older, enrolled from December 2013 to October 2015 at four large blood centres across the United States (in Connecticut, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin and California) by the NHLBI Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study-III (REDS-III), who completed a questionnaire and gave blood for blood counts, ferritin and DNA and a sample of their red cells for haemolysis testing at the end of storage, with donors of extreme haemolysis recalled for a second donation, to study the genetic and biological determinants of donor iron metabolism, pica, restless legs syndrome and red cell storage haemolysis, and to link donors to the outcomes of the patients transfused with their red cells.

label: Corogene Study
other synonyms: Corogene|Genetic Predisposition of Coronary Heart Disease in Patients Verified with Coronary Angiogram
definition: A prospective cohort of consecutive Finnish patients referred for coronary angiography at Helsinki University Central Hospital in 2006–2008, assembled to study the genetic predisposition to coronary heart disease; its acute coronary syndrome cases, with controls sampled from FINRISK, form a genotyped case-control sample.
diseases: patients with: acute coronary syndrome (MONDO:0005542)|patients with: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)

label: Health 2000 GenMets Study
other synonyms: GenMets sub cohort for the Health 2000 Study|Genetics of METabolic Syndrome|Health2000 GenMets Study
definition: A case-control sub-cohort of the Finnish Health 2000 survey, collected in 2000–2001, comprising participants with metabolic syndrome and matched controls, genotyped to study the genetics of metabolic syndrome and related traits.

label: Qatar Metabolomics Study on Diabetes
definition: A cross-sectional case–control study of 374 people with and without type 2 diabetes, of Arab and Asian descent, enrolled in February–June 2012 at the Dermatology Department of Hamad Medical Corporation in Doha, Qatar, with metabolomic profiling of saliva, blood plasma and urine to study metabolic dysregulation in diabetes.

label: Genetic Study of Atherosclerosis Risk
other synonyms: GeneSTAR family-based study|Genetic STudy of Aspirin Responsiveness|Genetic Studies of Atherosclerosis Risk|Genetic Study of Aspirin Responsiveness|Johns Hopkins - Genetic STudy of Atherosclerosis Risk|Johns Hopkins GeneSTAR Research Program|Johns Hopkins Genetic Study of Atherosclerosis Risk|Johns Hopkins Sibling and Family Heart Study
definition: A prospective family-based cohort, begun in 1983 at Johns Hopkins, of European American and African American families of probands with premature coronary disease identified in Baltimore-area hospitals, studied to determine the environmental, phenotypic and genetic causes of premature cardiovascular disease, including platelet response to a two-week aspirin trial.
diseases: at risk of: Premature coronary artery atherosclerosis (HP:0005181)

label: Nurses' Health Study
other synonyms: Nurses Health Study|Nurses' Health Study I
definition: A prospective cohort of 121,700 female registered nurses in the United States aged 30–55 when enrolled through a baseline questionnaire in 1976, followed by repeated questionnaires and biospecimen collection to study lifestyle and other risk factors for major chronic diseases in women.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to lifestyle (ECTO:6000015)

label: Penn Medicine BioBank
other synonyms: Penn Medicine Biobank
definition: An electronic health record-linked biobank cohort of more than 170,000 patients of the University of Pennsylvania Health System (Penn Medicine), about 30% of non-European ancestry, who consented to link their health records to genomic and biomarker data and to recontact, for genomic discovery and precision medicine research.

label: Epidemiological Investigation of Rheumatoid Arthritis
other synonyms: Epidemiological Investigation of RA
definition: A population-based case-control study established in Sweden in 1996, enrolling incident rheumatoid arthritis cases (now more than 5000) from the middle and southern regions of Sweden together with population controls, used to study genetic risk factors for rheumatoid arthritis and its ACPA-defined subsets and environmental factors such as cigarette smoking.
exposures: designed to study: exposure event (ExO:0000002)|designed to study: exposure to Cigarette Smoking (ECTO:6000038)

label: Ludwigshafen Risk and Cardiovascular Health Study
other synonyms: LURIC Health Study|LURIC study|LURIC/AtheroRemo|LURIC/AtheroRemo 1|LURIC/AtheroRemo 2|Ludwigshafen Risk and Cardiovascular Health
definition: A prospective cohort of 3,808 patients from the Ludwigshafen, Mannheim and Heidelberg area of south-west Germany, enrolled between July 1997 and March 2002 when they underwent coronary angiography at the municipal hospital of Ludwigshafen, with and without coronary artery disease, examined at baseline (medical history, physical examination, glucose tolerance test and blood sampling) and followed up from 2004, to investigate genetic and environmental risk factors for cardiovascular diseases. Most analyses use its 3,316 participants of German ancestry recruited between July 1997 and January 2000.
diseases: patients with: cardiovascular disorder (MONDO:0004995)|patients with: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)

label: Diabetes Heart Study
other synonyms: The Diabetes Heart Study
definition: A community-based, family-based study of European American and African American siblings concordant for type 2 diabetes and their unaffected relatives (1,443 participants from 564 families), recruited from internal medicine and endocrinology clinics in western North Carolina, United States, and examined at Wake Forest Baptist Medical Center to study genetic and epidemiological contributions to diabetic heart disease and subclinical cardiovascular disease; a parallel African American-Diabetes Heart Study (AA-DHS) later enrolled unrelated African Americans with type 2 diabetes to study ethnic differences in calcified atherosclerotic plaque.
diseases: patients with: cardiovascular disorder (MONDO:0004995)|patients with: heart disorder (MONDO:0005267)|patients with: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: Genetics of Personality Consortium
definition: A consortium of about 30 cohorts with genome-wide genotype and personality data, which harmonized personality measures across inventories in more than 63,000 participants for genome-wide association meta-analyses of personality traits such as neuroticism and their relation to major depressive disorder.

label: Genetic Risk Assessment for Chinese Eaglet-T1D
definition: A case–control collection of children with type 1 diabetes and controls from multiple paediatric centres in China, used to validate polygenic risk scores for type 1 diabetes in an East Asian population.

label: Academic Medical Center Amsterdam Premature Atherosclerosis Study
other synonyms: Premature Atherosclerosis Study
definition: A prospective cohort of patients of the Academic Medical Center, Amsterdam, with symptomatic coronary artery disease (myocardial infarction, coronary revascularization or at least 70% stenosis of a major epicardial artery) before the age of 51, used in genetic studies of premature atherosclerosis and coronary artery disease.
diseases: patients with: Precocious atherosclerosis (HP:0004416)|patients with: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)

label: Bogalusa Heart Study
definition: A long-term community-based cohort of Black and white children and adolescents in the rural biracial community of Bogalusa, Louisiana, United States, begun in 1972 by an NHLBI-funded research centre to study cardiovascular risk factors from early life and followed into adulthood.

label: Cleveland Family Speech and Reading Study
definition: A family-based longitudinal cohort of children with speech sound disorder of unknown cause and their siblings, ascertained through probands referred by speech-language pathologists in the Cleveland area of Ohio, United States, and followed for about 25 years to study long-term speech, language and literacy outcomes and their genetic basis.
diseases: patients with: childhood apraxia of speech (MONDO:0011184)|patients with: speech-sound disorder (MONDO:0012038)

label: Genetics of Opioid Addiction Consortium
definition: A consortium of investigators who attend the National Institute on Drug Abuse Genetics and Epigenetics Cross-cutting Research Team meetings and have genome-wide association data on opioid addiction, pooling previously unpublished genome-wide association studies of opioid addiction from twelve cohort samples, ten with European-ancestry and seven with African-ancestry participants, among them Yale-Penn, the Collaborative Study on the Genetics of Alcoholism and the Urban Health Study in the United States, the Vancouver Injection Drug Users Study in Canada, deCODE in Iceland, the Genetic Epidemiology of Opioid Dependence in Bulgaria study, the Comorbidity and Trauma Study in Australia and the AIDS Linked to the IntraVenous Experience cohort, to study the genetics of opioid addiction.

label: Genetics of Opioid Addiction Study
other synonyms: GENetics of Opioid Addiction|Genetics of Opioid Addiction research collaborative|Genetics of Opioid Addiction research program
definition: A prospective cohort of adults with opioid use disorder receiving treatment, mainly methadone maintenance treatment, at Canadian Addiction Treatment Centre (formerly Ontario Addiction Treatment Centres) clinics in Ontario, Canada, recruited by McMaster University with the clinics in a pilot at four clinics in 2011–2012 and a main phase in 2013–2016 (about 1,500 participants, interviewed at entry, giving blood for DNA and followed through the urine drug screens in their medical records), to identify factors, including genetic risk factors, associated with opioid use and treatment outcomes.

label: deCODE Health Study
other synonyms: deCODE health study
definition: A general-population sample of Icelanders, enriched for carriers of rare and potentially high-impact mutations, comprehensively phenotyped by deCODE genetics in Iceland (e.g. audiometry, speech recordings, DXA body composition, plasma proteomics) and combined with the Icelandic genotype and sequence data for genetic association studies.

label: Qatar Biobank
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of adult Qatari nationals and long-term residents (living in Qatar for at least 15 years), recruited by the Qatar Biobank from December 2012 with extensive lifestyle, clinical, imaging and biological-sample data and long-term follow-up, to study the causes, progression and burden of disease in the Qatari population.

label: Reykjavik Study
other synonyms: Reykjavík Study
definition: A population-based cohort of men born 1907–1934 and women born 1908–1935, randomly selected from residents of the Reykjavik area, examined at the Heart Preventive Clinic in Reykjavik from 1967 and followed since in Iceland by the Icelandic Heart Association, to study cardiovascular disease and its risk factors.

label: Human Functional Genomics Project
definition: A research programme based at Radboud University Medical Center in Nijmegen, the Netherlands, that collects distinct cohorts of healthy volunteers and patients (among them 500FG, 200FG, 300BCG, 300OB, 300DM and 2000HIV) profiled with genetic, immunological and other omics data, to identify the genetic and non-genetic determinants of human immune and cytokine responses.

label: Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study-III
other synonyms: NHLBI Recipient Epidemiology Donor Evaluation Study|National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study|Recipient Epidemiology Donor Evaluation Study III
definition: A seven-year multicentre transfusion-medicine research programme launched in 2011 by the US National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, with a domestic component of four blood centres and 12 hospitals and international programmes in Brazil, China and South Africa, which built linked donor, donation and transfusion-recipient databases and ran more than 25 focused studies of blood donors and recipients, such as RBC-Omics and the Brazil sickle cell disease cohort.

label: Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health
other synonyms: Kaiser Permanente Northern California Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health|Kaiser Permanente Research Program on Genes, Environment, and Health|Research Program on Genes, Environment, and Health
definition: A research resource developed by the Kaiser Permanente Northern California Division of Research from consenting members of the KPNC health plan, linking surveys, biospecimens and electronic health records and including the Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging cohort and a pregnancy cohort, for research on the genetic and environmental determinants of common, age-related complex health conditions.

label: Africa America Diabetes Mellitus Study
other synonyms: AADM study|Africa America Diabetes Mellitus
definition: A genetic epidemiology study of type 2 diabetes begun in 1997 as a collaboration of West African and US investigators, enrolling affected sib-pairs with type 2 diabetes and unaffected controls in Ghana and Nigeria and later participants in Eldoret, Kenya, to map type 2 diabetes susceptibility genes in the West African ancestral populations of African Americans.

label: Danish Blood Donor Study
other synonyms: DBDS Genomic Cohort
definition: An ongoing nationwide prospective cohort of blood donors aged 18-70 at inclusion, recruited at Danish blood donation facilities since 2010 (all facilities in Denmark by 2015), with questionnaires, plasma samples, genotyping and linkage to national health registries for research on donor health and general public health.

label: Howard University Family Study
definition: A population-based family study of African Americans from the Washington, DC metropolitan area, enrolling randomly ascertained families and unrelated individuals through Howard University without selection on any phenotype, to study the genetic and environmental basis of common complex diseases including hypertension, obesity and type 2 diabetes.

label: Stabilization of Atherosclerotic Plaque by Initiation of Darapladib Therapy Trial
other synonyms: STABILITY trial|STabilization of Atherosclerotic plaque By Initiation of darapLadIb TherapY
definition: An international randomized, placebo-controlled trial of darapladib, a lipoprotein-associated phospholipase A2 inhibitor, in 15,828 patients with chronic coronary heart disease recruited at 663 centers in 39 countries from December 2008 to April 2010 and sponsored by GlaxoSmithKline, whose baseline plasma biobank has been used for biomarker, proteomic and genetic studies of cardiovascular outcomes.

label: Swedish BioFINDER Study
other synonyms: BioFINDER One|Biomarkers For Identifying Neurodegenerative Disorders Early and Reliably
definition: A prospective, longitudinal cohort, the first Swedish BioFINDER study (BioFINDER-1, NCT01208675), of cognitively unimpaired older adults and patients with mild cognitive impairment, dementias and parkinsonian disorders, recruited from 2009 to 2014 at three neurology and memory clinics in southern Sweden and followed for up to 10 years with cerebrospinal fluid, plasma, MRI, amyloid PET and genetic data to develop early and accurate diagnosis of Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease and related disorders. It is distinct from the later, independent BioFINDER-2 study (NCT03174938), launched in 2017.
diseases: patients with: Alzheimer disease (MONDO:0004975)|patients with: Parkinson disease (MONDO:0005180)|patients with: dementia (MONDO:0001627)|patients with: parkinsonian disorder (MONDO:0021095)

label: CROATIA-Vis Study
other synonyms: Vis Island Study (Croatia)|Vis Study
definition: A population-based cohort of 1,008 adult Croatians aged 18-93 from the isolated villages of Vis and Komiza on the Dalmatian island of Vis, Croatia, recruited in 2003 and 2004, genotyped and richly phenotyped for genetic studies of complex traits in an isolated population.

label: National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center
definition: A US data resource, founded in 1999 and funded by the National Institute on Aging, that combines the standardized longitudinal clinical (Uniform Data Set), neuropathology, imaging, biomarker and genetic data of participants of the NIA-funded Alzheimer's Disease Research Centers, more than 56,000 people from over 42 centers, for research on Alzheimer disease and related dementias.
diseases: patients with: Alzheimer disease (MONDO:0004975)|patients with: dementia (MONDO:0001627)

label: Singapore Prospective Study Program
other synonyms: Singapore Cardiovascular Cohort Study 2|Singapore Prospective Study Programme
definition: A population-based study of diabetes and cardiovascular disease in Singapore that re-visited, between 2003 and 2007, Chinese, Malay and Asian-Indian adults randomly sampled for four earlier cross-sectional studies (the Thyroid and Heart Study, the 1992 and 1998 National Health Surveys and the National University of Singapore Heart Study), with questionnaires and clinical examinations.
diseases: population study of: cardiovascular disorder (MONDO:0004995)|population study of: diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005015)

label: Colorado Center for Personalized Medicine Biobank
other synonyms: Colorado Center for Personalized Medicine
definition: An electronic health record-linked biobank jointly developed by the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus and UCHealth, enrolling adult UCHealth patients since September 2015 (more than 200,000 participants by 2022, mostly from the Rocky Mountain region), as a dual-purpose resource for genomic research and for returning clinical genetic results to participants.

label: Adult Changes in Thought Study
other synonyms: Adult Changes in Thought
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of dementia-free adults aged 65 and older enrolled since 1994 from the membership of Kaiser Permanente Washington (formerly Group Health Cooperative) in the Seattle area, United States, and followed longitudinally to identify risk and preventive factors for dementia, with brain autopsy, genetic and abstracted medical-record data.

label: Hypertension Genetic Epidemiology Network
other synonyms: HyperGEN Study
definition: A family study of the NHLBI Family Blood Pressure Program that from 1995 to 2000 recruited African American and white sibships with two or more members with hypertension diagnosed before age 60, with their untreated adult offspring and random population samples, at centres in Birmingham (Alabama), Forsyth County (North Carolina), Framingham (Massachusetts), Minneapolis (Minnesota) and Salt Lake City (Utah), to identify genes promoting hypertension.

label: Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial
other synonyms: PLCO Cancer Screening Trial|Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial
definition: A multicentre randomized cancer screening trial of about 155,000 men and women aged 55–74, enrolled from 1993 to 2001 at ten screening centres across the United States under the National Cancer Institute, testing whether screening reduces mortality from prostate, lung, colorectal and ovarian cancer, with participants followed for cancer incidence and death.
diseases: population study of: colorectal cancer (MONDO:0005575)|population study of: lung cancer (MONDO:0008903)|population study of: ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170)|population study of: prostate cancer (MONDO:0008315)

label: Korean Cancer Prevention Study-II Biobank
acronyms: KCPS|KCPS-II|KCPS-II Biobank|KCPS2|KMSRI|Korean Cancer Prevention Study (KCPS-II Biobank)
other synonyms: Korean Cancer Prevention Study-II|Korean Cancer Prevention Study-II (KCPS-II) Biobank|Korean Metabolic Syndrome Research Initiative
definition: A prospective population-based biobank cohort of 156,701 Korean adults aged 20–85 recruited in 2004–2013 at 18 health promotion centres across Korea during routine health examinations, genotyped and followed through national mortality, cancer registry and health insurance records, to study cancer, cardiovascular and other chronic diseases and their metabolic risk factors.

label: Leipzig Research Center for Civilization Diseases-Heart Study
other synonyms: Leipzig (LIFE) Heart Study|Leipzig Research Center for Civilization Diseases - Heart Study
definition: A hospital-based cohort of patients with suspected stable coronary artery disease, acute myocardial infarction or known left main coronary artery disease undergoing coronary angiography at the Heart Center Leipzig, Germany, recruited from December 2006 by Leipzig University and its Leipzig Research Center for Civilization Diseases (LIFE) as a biobank and database for studying clinical, metabolic, cellular and genetic factors of atherosclerosis and coronary artery disease.
diseases: patients with: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)|patients with: myocardial infarction (MONDO:0005068)

label: Bandim Health Project
definition: A health and demographic surveillance and research platform in Guinea-Bissau, run by the Bandim Health Project with Statens Serum Institut, that has followed women and children in an urban surveillance system in the capital, Bissau, since 1978 and in a nationally representative rural surveillance system of 182 clusters since 1989-1990, to study health interventions, child mortality and the non-specific effects of vaccines. Randomised trials are run within it, such as the 2008-2013 trial of early BCG vaccination in low-birth-weight newborns in Bissau.

label: Center for Applied Genomics Biobank
acronyms: CAG|CHOP|Center for Applied Genomics, Children's Hospital of Philadelphia
other synonyms: CAG biobank|CHOP biobank|Children's Hospital of Philadelphia|Childrens Hospital of Philadelphia
definition: A paediatric biobank of the Center for Applied Genomics at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, recruiting children at the hospital since 2006 with broad consent for research use of their samples and electronic health records (about 85,000 juvenile subjects of diverse ancestries by 2025), used for genome-wide and phenome-wide studies of childhood disease.

label: Danish Twin Registry
definition: A nationwide population-based register of more than 175,000 Danish twins from birth cohorts 1870 to 2009, established in the 1950s, that combines repeated surveys, in-person assessments, a biobank and linkage to Danish national registers, for studies of genetic and environmental influences on health, disease and ageing.

label: Electronic Medical Records and Genomics Network
other synonyms: Electronic Medical Records and Genomics|Medical Records and Genomics study|eMERGE Network
definition: A National Human Genome Research Institute-funded consortium, established in 2007, of US academic and integrated health systems, each with its own biorepository linking DNA samples to electronic medical records, which pooled its sites' data into a network-wide genome-wide dataset of about 105,000 participants for genomic discovery and later sequenced about 25,000 participants to study the return of genomic results.

label: Sorbs Study
other synonyms: Sorbs cohort|Sorbs population
definition: A volunteer-based cohort of about 1,000 adults from the self-contained population of Sorbs in eastern Germany, recruited and extensively metabolically phenotyped by the University of Leipzig in 2005–2007 for genome-wide studies of metabolic, anthropometric and other quantitative traits.

label: Dose-Responses to Exercise Training
other synonyms: DR's EXTRA study|Dose-Responses to Exercise Training study
definition: A four-year randomised controlled trial of resistance and aerobic exercise and dietary interventions in a population-based random sample of men and women aged 55-74 years living in Kuopio, Finland, drawn from the national population registry, of whom 1,479 attended baseline examinations in 2005-2006, to study the health effects of regular physical exercise and a healthy diet in middle-aged and older people.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to eating behavior (ECTO:6000021)|designed to study: exposure to exercise (ECTO:6000002)

label: Genetics of Lipid-Lowering Drugs and Diet Network
other synonyms: GOLDN study|Genetics of Lipid Lowering Drugs and Diet Network study|Genetics of Lipid-Lowering Drugs and Diet Network study
definition: A family intervention study of the NHLBI Programs in Gene by Environment Interaction, of 1,048 white participants in 184 three-generation pedigrees previously screened at the Minnesota and Utah centres of the NHLBI Family Heart Study, who took a standardised high-fat meal challenge and three weeks of fenofibrate treatment, to study genetic determinants of the lipid response to diet and lipid-lowering drugs.

label: Study of Women's Health Across the Nation
definition: A multi-site, multiethnic, community-based longitudinal cohort of 3,302 women aged 42–52 enrolled in 1996–1997 at seven US sites (Boston, Chicago, Detroit, Los Angeles, Pittsburgh, Oakland and Newark) and followed about yearly to study how women's physical, biological, psychological and social health in midlife affects health during ageing.

label: Finnish Diabetic Nephropathy Study
other synonyms: FinnDiane Study|Finnish Diabetic Nephropathy
definition: An ongoing nationwide multicentre observational study in Finland, established in 1997 and run from the Folkhälsan Research Center and the University of Helsinki, of nearly 9,000 adults with type 1 diabetes recruited and clinically characterised at study centres across the country and followed through re-examinations, national registries and medical records, to identify factors leading to diabetic kidney disease and other diabetic complications.
diseases: patients with: diabetic kidney disease (MONDO:0005016)|patients with: type 1 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005147)

label: IMAGEN study
other synonyms: IMAGEN cohort
definition: A longitudinal multicentre genetic-neuroimaging cohort of about 2,000 healthy 14-year-old adolescents recruited from high schools at eight European sites in England, Ireland, France and Germany, followed up at ages 16, 19 and 22 with behavioural, neuropsychological, MRI and genome-wide data, to study the genetic and neurobiological basis of impulsivity, reinforcer sensitivity and emotional reactivity and their value in predicting psychiatric disorders.

label: Munich Antidepressant Response Signature
other synonyms: Munich Antidepressant Response Signature project|Munich Antidepressant Response Signature study
definition: A naturalistic, open-label longitudinal treatment study of inpatients admitted with a moderate to severe unipolar or bipolar depressive episode to the hospital of the Max Planck Institute of Psychiatry in Munich and collaborating hospitals in Southern Bavaria and Switzerland, characterised clinically, neuroendocrinologically (dex/CRH test) and genetically and followed weekly during treatment, to identify predictors of antidepressant treatment response.
diseases: patients with: bipolar disorder (MONDO:0004985)|patients with: depressive disorder (MONDO:0002050)

label: Minority Aging Research Study
definition: A longitudinal epidemiologic cohort of older African Americans without known dementia, recruited from 2004 from churches, senior buildings and community organisations in the Chicago metropolitan area and followed at Rush University Medical Center, with optional brain donation, to study decline in cognitive function and risk of Alzheimer disease.

label: Older Australian Twins Study
other synonyms: Older Australian Twin Study
definition: A longitudinal study of Australian twins aged 65 years and over, with some of their equivalently aged siblings, recruited through the Australian Twin Registry and a recruitment drive and assessed every two years with psychiatric, neuropsychological, cardiovascular, metabolic, neuroimaging and genetic measures, to study genetic and environmental influences on healthy brain ageing and ageing-related neurocognitive disorders.

label: LymeProspect
other synonyms: LymeProspect cohort|LymeProspect study
definition: A prospective observational cohort of adults with proven or probable Lyme borreliosis in the Netherlands, included at the start of antibiotic treatment from 2015 and followed for one year with questionnaires and repeated blood sampling, run by RIVM with the Lyme borreliosis expert centres of Amsterdam UMC and Radboudumc to study the prevalence and determinants of persistent symptoms after treatment.

label: 300-Tanzania-FG
other synonyms: 300 Tanzania functional genomics (FG) study
definition: A cross-sectional cohort of 323 healthy adults aged 18-65 living in the Kilimanjaro region of northern Tanzania, enrolled within the Human Functional Genomics Project by Radboudumc and Tanzanian partners, with ex vivo cytokine stimulations at the Kilimanjaro Clinical Research Institute in Moshi, to study genetic and environmental determinants of immune responses in an African population.

label: UCLA ATLAS Community Health Initiative
other synonyms: ATLAS Community Health Initiative
definition: An ancestrally diverse biobank embedded in the UCLA Health medical system in Los Angeles County, run by the UCLA Institute for Precision Health, that links genomic data from blood samples of consenting UCLA Health patients (36,736 genotyped in 2022) to their de-identified electronic health records, for genetic and precision-health research.

label: Insulin Resistance Atherosclerosis Family Study
other synonyms: IRAS Family Study
definition: A family study of Hispanic (Mexican American) families recruited at clinical centres in San Antonio, Texas and the San Luis Valley, Colorado and African American families recruited in Los Angeles, California, selected on family size rather than health status and examined with CT scans of visceral fat and frequently sampled glucose tolerance tests, to identify the genetic and environmental determinants of insulin resistance and visceral adiposity.

label: WHI Genomics and Randomized Trials Network
other synonyms: Genome-wide Association Research Network into Effects of Treatment|Genomics and Randomized Trials Network|Womens Health Initiative Genome-wide Association Research Network into Effects of Treatment
definition: A nested case-control genome-wide association sub-study of the Women's Health Initiative hormone therapy trials, comprising the coronary heart disease, stroke, venous thromboembolism and selected diabetes cases that arose during the active intervention phase and age-matched controls, genotyped under the NHGRI Genomics and Randomized Trials Network (GARNET).
diseases: patients with: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)|patients with: diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005015)|patients with: stroke disorder (MONDO:0005098)|patients with: venous thromboembolism (MONDO:0005399)

label: ALS Utrecht
definition: A case-control sample of 158 people of European ancestry, patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and healthy controls, from University Medical Center Utrecht, the Netherlands, with longitudinal 3.0 T brain MRI and whole-genome sequencing, contributed to the ENIGMA Plasticity Working Group genome-wide meta-analysis of brain structure change.

label: Brain Imaging Genetics study
other synonyms: Brain Imaging Genetics
definition: A pool of self-reported healthy volunteers, many of them university students, who took part in diverse imaging studies at the Donders Centre for Cognitive Neuroimaging in Nijmegen, the Netherlands, and consented to pooling of their anatomical MRI scans with DNA for imaging genetics; established in 2007 and now part of the Cognomics initiative.

label: BrainSCALE study
other synonyms: Brain SCALE|Brainscale Study
definition: A longitudinal study of Dutch twin families recruited from the Netherlands Twin Register, starting with 112 families of 9-year-old twins and an older sibling who were assessed at three-year intervals with IQ and neuropsychological tests, behavioural ratings, pubertal hormones, brain MRI and DNA collection, to study genetic and environmental influences on brain structure and cognition from childhood into adolescence.

label: Norwegian Cognitive NeuroGenetics sample
other synonyms: Norwegian Cognitive NeuroGenetics Study
definition: A genetically homogeneous sample of healthy Norwegian adults spanning the adult life span, collected from 2003 to study cognitive ageing and genetic risk factors and genome-wide genotyped in 2009, with MRI and experimental cognitive data on attention and working memory, for studies of the genetics of cognitive and brain function.

label: NeuroIMAGE study
definition: A multi-site prospective cohort following up the Dutch families of the International Multicenter ADHD Genetics project together with newly recruited families, comprising 1,069 children from ADHD and control families and 848 parents assessed with diagnostic interviews, questionnaires, cognitive tests, structural and functional MRI and genome-wide genotyping, to study the course of ADHD into adolescence and adulthood and its genetic, environmental and neural underpinnings.

label: Inter99 Study
other synonyms: Inter99 cohort
definition: A population-based randomised non-pharmacological lifestyle intervention trial for the prevention of ischaemic heart disease, run in 1999–2006 at the Research Centre for Prevention and Health in Glostrup, Copenhagen, Denmark, on random samples of adults aged 30–60 drawn from a population of 61,301 and followed through questionnaires and central registers.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to lifestyle (ECTO:6000015)|designed to study: exposure to smoking cessation (ECTO:6000014)

label: iPSYCH case-cohort study
other synonyms: Lundbeck Foundation Initiative for Integrative Psychiatric Research|iPSYCH Danish case-cohort study|iPSYCH2012 case-cohort sample|iPSYCH2015 case-cohort sample
definition: A Danish population-based case-cohort sample established by the Lundbeck Foundation Initiative for Integrative Psychiatric Research (iPSYCH) to study the genetic and environmental architecture of severe mental disorders, combining persons diagnosed with schizophrenia, autism, ADHD or affective disorder with a random sample of the population, genotyped from neonatal dried blood spots in the Danish Neonatal Screening Biobank and linked to national registers. Its first wave (iPSYCH2012, 86,189 individuals born 1981-2005) was expanded as iPSYCH2015 to 141,265 samples, including 50,615 population controls, nested within the Danish population born 1981-2008 and adding schizophrenia spectrum and post-partum disorder cases.
diseases: patients with: attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (MONDO:0007743)|patients with: autism (MONDO:0005260)|patients with: mood disorder (MONDO:0005371)|patients with: schizophrenia (MONDO:0005090)

label: Long Life Family Study
other synonyms: Long-Life Family Study|NIA Long Life Family Study
definition: A longitudinal, multicentre, multinational family study of 4,953 members of 539 two-generation families selected for exceptional familial longevity, recruited in 2006-2009 through field centres in Boston, New York and Pittsburgh in the United States and in Denmark and re-examined in 2014-2017, to study the genetic and non-genetic determinants of exceptional longevity and healthy ageing.

label: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD
other synonyms: COPDGene study|Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Gene Study|Genetic Epidemiology of COPD study
definition: A multicentre observational cohort of about 10,000 non-Hispanic white and African American current and former smokers with and without COPD, aged 45-80, enrolled at 21 clinical centres across the United States and followed longitudinally with chest CT imaging and genome-wide genotyping to identify genetic factors and CT-defined subtypes of COPD.
diseases: patients with: chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (MONDO:0005002)
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to Cigarette Smoking (ECTO:6000038)

label: Genetic and phenotypic determinants of blood pressure and other cardiovascular risk factors
other synonyms: GAPP study|The genetic and phenotypic determinants of blood pressure and other cardiovascular risk factors (Liechtenstein)
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of a representative sample of healthy adults aged 25-41 in the Principality of Liechtenstein, enrolled from June 2010 without cardiovascular disease, diabetes or severe obesity, with ambulatory blood pressure, Holter ECG, spirometry, sleep oximetry and blood, urine and genetic sampling, and followed up every 3-5 years to study genetic and phenotypic predictors of cardiovascular risk factors in young adults.
diseases: population study of: cardiovascular disorder (MONDO:0004995)|population study of: hypertensive disorder (MONDO:0005044)

label: Women's Genome Health Study
other synonyms: Womens Genome Health Study
definition: A prospective genome-wide association cohort of more than 25,000 initially healthy American female health professionals aged 45 or older from the Women's Health Study who gave a baseline blood sample, followed since 1992 for incident cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes and other outcomes.

label: Cameron County Hispanic Cohort
definition: A community-based cohort of Mexican Americans in Brownsville, Cameron County, Texas, on the United States-Mexico border, established in 2004 by the University of Texas School of Public Health Brownsville campus from households in randomly selected census tract blocks, to study the prevalence and determinants of obesity, diabetes and related chronic disease in this population.
diseases: population study of: diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005015)|population study of: obesity disorder (MONDO:0011122)

label: Alzheimer's Disease Genetics Consortium
other synonyms: Alzheimer Disease Genetic Consortium|Alzheimer's Disease Genetic Consortium
definition: A US consortium that assembles genome-wide genotype data and harmonized phenotypes from many case-control, family-based, population-based and longitudinal Alzheimer disease cohorts, in more than 30 GWAS datasets of several ancestries, for genetic studies of late-onset Alzheimer disease.

label: Consortium for the Analysis of the Diversity and Evolution of Latin America
other synonyms: CANDELA cohort
definition: A sample of about 7,300 adult volunteers of mixed African, European and Native American ancestry, mostly university students and staff (and, in Chile, mainly soldiers), recruited by a consortium of Latin American and UK groups in México City, Medellín, Lima, Arica and Porto Alegre and characterised for physical appearance, facial photographs, self-perceived ancestry and genetic ancestry, with genome-wide genotyping of about 6,000 of them, to study admixture and the genetics of physical traits in Latin America.

label: Mexico City Prospective Study
other synonyms: Mexico City Prospective Cohort
definition: A prospective cohort of more than 150,000 adults aged 35 and over, recruited in 1998-2004 from the contiguous urban districts of Coyoacán and Iztapalapa in Mexico City with the University of Oxford, and followed to investigate known and new risk factors for mortality in people of Mexican descent; its participants have exome and genome-wide genetic data.

label: Airwave Health Monitoring Study
definition: An occupational cohort of police officers and staff of police forces across Great Britain, enrolled from 2004 (42,112 participants by the end of 2012, most of whom attended a health screening with questionnaires, food diaries, physical and cognitive measurements and stored blood and urine), set up to evaluate possible health risks of the TETRA digital radio system and broadened to study the health of the police workforce.
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to occupation (ECTO:0001591)|participants with exposure: exposure to radiowave radiation (ECTO:8000054)

label: Cohorte Lausannoise
other synonyms: CoLaus Study|Cohort Lausanne
definition: A population-based cohort of a random sample of 6,188 Caucasian adults aged 35 to 75 living in Lausanne, Switzerland, extensively phenotyped and genotyped genome-wide at baseline to study the prevalence and genetic determinants of cardiovascular risk factors and the metabolic syndrome, and followed up prospectively (with its psychiatric arm PsyCoLaus) from 2003 for cardiovascular events and mortality.
diseases: population study of: cardiovascular disorder (MONDO:0004995)|population study of: metabolic syndrome X (MONDO:0011565)

label: Melbourne Collaborative Cohort Study
other synonyms: Health 2020
definition: A prospective cohort of 41,513 middle-aged and older adults of white European origin, almost all aged 40–69, recruited in Melbourne, Australia, in 1990–1994 by Cancer Council Victoria and followed up face to face in 2003–2007 and by record linkage to cancer and death registries, collecting socio-demographic, lifestyle and health data to study risk factors for cancer and other chronic diseases.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to lifestyle (ECTO:6000015)

label: TRacking Adolescents' Individual Lives Survey
other synonyms: Tracking Adolescents Individual Lives Survey
definition: A Dutch prospective cohort study, run in the North of the Netherlands, consisting of a population cohort of 2,230 children born between October 1989 and September 1991 and a clinical cohort of 543 children referred to child psychiatric outpatient care before age 11, followed from about age 11 into young adulthood with repeated assessments of mental health, social development and physical health.

label: ADDITION-PRO Study
other synonyms: ADDITION-PRO cohort
definition: A population-based longitudinal cohort of 2,082 Danish adults at different levels of diabetes risk, sampled from the 16,136 high-risk individuals identified by the 2001–2006 stepwise diabetes screening programme in Danish general practice of the Danish arm of ADDITION-Europe, examined in 2009–2011 with detailed cardiometabolic phenotyping and followed for cardiovascular disease and death.
diseases: at risk of: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: Finnish Cardiovascular Study
definition: A clinical cohort of about 4,500 patients scheduled for an exercise stress test at Tampere University Hospital, Finland, recruited between October 2001 and December 2007 with continuous high-resolution ECG, haemodynamic measurements, genotyping and follow-up of clinical events and deaths, to construct risk profiles for cardiovascular disease, events and death.

label: Health Professionals Follow-up Study
other synonyms: Health Professional Follow-up Study
definition: A prospective cohort of 51,529 US male health professionals aged 40 to 75 enrolled in 1986, whose demographics, health, diet and lifestyle are updated by questionnaire every two years (diet every four), with follow-up exceeding 90% of eligible person-time.

label: ARGO study
other synonyms: Arthroplasty and the Genetics of Osteoarthritis
definition: A Greek collection of more than 1,500 well-phenotyped patients with severe hip or knee osteoarthritis undergoing total joint replacement, recruited in hospitals of Athens (2015-2017) and Larissa together with healthy controls, set up to study the genetic architecture of osteoarthritis.

label: Ansan and Ansung Study
other synonyms: Ansan Study|Ansan-Ansung cohort|Ansan/Ansung study|Ansung Study|KARE cohort|KoGES_Ansan and Ansung study|Korea Association Resource|Korean Association Resource|Korean Association Resource Project
definition: A community-based prospective cohort of 10,030 men and women aged 40–69 from the urban city of Ansan and the rural town of Ansung (Anseong) in Gyeonggi Province, South Korea, recruited in 2001–2002 as the first cohort of the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study and re-surveyed every two years, to study common chronic diseases and their genetic and environmental risk factors.

label: Nagahama Prospective Cohort for Comprehensive Human Bioscience
other synonyms: Nagahama Prospective Genome Cohort for the Comprehensive Human Bioscience|Nagahama cohort
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of about 9,800 residents aged 30–74 years of Nagahama City, a largely rural city in Shiga Prefecture, central Japan, recruited in 2008–2010 and run from Kyoto University Graduate School of Medicine, with blood samples, questionnaires, health examinations, genotyping and follow-up examinations (the first in 2013–2016) for genomic and clinical research.

label: Chronic Kidney Disease Genetics Consortium
other synonyms: CKD Genetics Consortium|CKDGen Consortium|Chronic Kidney Disease Genetics (CKDGen) Consortium
definition: An international collaborative consortium, co-directed by Anna Köttgen and Cristian Pattaro with its data hosted at the University of Freiburg, that meta-analyses genome-wide association results from many, mostly population-based, studies to investigate the genetic basis of kidney function and disease, releasing summary statistics for markers such as estimated glomerular filtration rate and blood urea nitrogen.
diseases: population study of: chronic kidney disease (MONDO:0005300)

label: Tohoku Medical Megabank Project
acronyms: IMM|TMM|ToMMo|Tohoku Medical Megabank|Tohoku University, Tohoku Medical Megabank Organization|Tonhoku
other synonyms: Iwate Tohoku Medical Megabank|The Tonhoku Medical Megabank Organisations|Tohoku Medical Megabank Organization|Tohoku University Tohoku Medical Megabank Organization
definition: A Japanese genome cohort project launched after the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and run by the Tohoku Medical Megabank Organization of Tohoku University and the Iwate Tohoku Medical Megabank Organization of Iwate Medical University, comprising two prospective cohorts in Miyagi and Iwate Prefectures, the TMM Community-Based Cohort Study of adults and the TMM Birth and Three-Generation Cohort Study, with an integrated biobank of health information, biospecimens and genome and omics data.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to earthquake (ECTO:8000011)

label: Fred Hutchinson Prostate Cancer Study
other synonyms: Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center Prostate Cancer Study|Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center, Seattle US|King County (Washington) Prostate Cancer Studies|King County Prostate Cancer Studies
definition: A prostate cancer study run at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center that comprises two population-based case-control studies in King County, Washington, whose cases, identified through the Seattle-Puget Sound SEER cancer registry, were men aged 40–64 diagnosed in 1993–1996 and men aged 35–74 diagnosed in 2002–2005, and whose controls without prostate cancer were found by random-digit dialling and frequency-matched to cases by age; its genotyped samples contribute to the PRACTICAL consortium.

label: Whole Genome Association Analysis of Hematopoietic Cell Transplant (HCT) Outcomes
other synonyms: FHCRC study cohort|Fred Hutch cohort|STAMPEED: Whole Genome Association Analysis of Hematopoietic Cell Transplant (HCT) Outcomes
definition: A retrospective cohort of patients with a haematological malignancy or myelodysplastic syndrome who had a first allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplant at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center and Seattle Cancer Care Alliance from 1990 to 2011, together with their donors, genotyped to find variants associated with graft-versus-host disease, recurrent malignancy and other complications after transplantation.
diseases: patients with: hematopoietic and lymphoid cell neoplasm (MONDO:0044881)|patients with: myelodysplastic syndrome (MONDO:0018881)

label: Meta-Analyses of Glucose and Insulin-related traits Consortium
other synonyms: Meta-Analyses of Glucose and Insulin-related Traits Consortium|Meta-Analysis of Glucose and Insulin-related traits Consortium
definition: A collaborative consortium that combines genome-wide association and exome-array data from many cohorts of individuals without diabetes in meta-analyses of glycaemic traits (fasting glucose, fasting insulin, 2-hour glucose and HbA1c) and measures of insulin secretion and sensitivity, to find loci influencing glycaemic and metabolic traits, and releases its summary results.

label: Molecular Genetics of Adverse Drug Reactions in Childhood Study
other synonyms: Molecular Genetics of Adverse Drug Reactions in Children Study|United Kingdom MAGIC|United Kingdom Molecular Genetics of Adverse Drug Reactions in Children Study
definition: A UK study of the molecular genetics of adverse drug reactions in children, recruiting carefully phenotyped retrospective cohorts of treated children at UK hospitals; its cisplatin cohort comprises platinum-treated paediatric cancer patients recruited between 2012 and 2018 at eight UK sites for genetic studies of ototoxicity.
diseases: patients with: childhood malignant neoplasm (MONDO:0006517)|patients with: platinum-induced ototoxicity (MONDO:0800178)

label: Raine Study
other synonyms: The Raine Study|Western Australian Pregnancy Cohort (Raine) Study|Western Australian Pregnancy Cohort Study
definition: A pregnancy cohort in Western Australia for which 2,900 pregnant women were recruited between 1989 and 1991 at King Edward Memorial Hospital, Perth, and nearby private clinics, with the mothers (Generation 1) and their 2,868 offspring (Generation 2) followed from 18 weeks' gestation through childhood and adolescence into adulthood, to study how early life shapes later health and behaviour.

label: Prospective Study of Pravastatin in the Elderly at Risk
definition: A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial population of 5,804 men and women aged 70 to 82 with pre-existing vascular disease or risk factors for it, screened in Scotland, Ireland and the Netherlands and randomised to pravastatin 40 mg/day or placebo for about 3.2 years to test whether statin treatment reduces coronary and cerebrovascular events in the elderly.
diseases: at risk of: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)|at risk of: stroke disorder (MONDO:0005098)|at risk of: vascular disorder (MONDO:0005385)

label: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Salt Sensitivity
other synonyms: GenSalt Study|Genetic Epidemiology Network of Salt-Sensitivity|Genetic Epidemiology Network of Salt-Sensitivity Study
definition: A family feeding study in rural northern China that recruited 3,153 Han Chinese participants from 658 families, each ascertained through a proband with untreated prehypertension or stage-1 hypertension, of whom 1,906 eligible probands and their siblings, spouses and offspring underwent seven-day low-sodium, high-sodium and high-sodium with potassium supplementation dietary interventions, to localise and identify genes influencing blood pressure responses to dietary sodium and potassium.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to potassium via ingestion (ECTO:0900037)|designed to study: exposure to sodium chloride food material via ingestion (ECTO:0070218)

label: Kaiser Permanente Research Bank
other synonyms: KP Research Bank|Kaiser Permanente
definition: A research resource of Kaiser Permanente, launched in May 2016 and built on the Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health, that collects biospecimens and surveys linked to electronic health records from consenting adult members across Kaiser Permanente's eight US regions (about 396,000 consented by July 2021), with general, pregnancy and cancer cohorts.

label: Minnesota Center for Twin and Family Research
definition: A collection of longitudinal, community-representative twin and adoptive family studies in Minnesota, including the Minnesota Twin Registry, the Minnesota Twin Family Study, the Enrichment Study, the Adolescent Brain study and the Sibling Interaction and Behavior Study, focusing on psychological adjustment, personality, cognitive ability and brain function with an emphasis on substance use and related psychopathology.
diseases: population study of: psychiatric disorder (MONDO:0002025)|population study of: substance-related disorder (MONDO:0002494)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to substance abuse (ECTO:6000007)

label: Relationship between Insulin Sensitivity and Cardiovascular disease
other synonyms: EGIR-RISC Study|Relationship between Insulin Sensitivity and Cardiovascular disease Study
definition: A prospective cohort of about 1,500 healthy men and women of European ancestry aged 30 to 60, recruited without diabetes, hypertension or dyslipidaemia at centres in 13-14 European countries by the European Group for the Study of Insulin Resistance, with baseline oral glucose tolerance tests and euglycaemic insulin clamps and follow-up after 3 and 10 years to study how insulin resistance relates to atherosclerosis, cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes.
diseases: population study of: cardiovascular disorder (MONDO:0004995)|population study of: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: Rotterdam Study I
other synonyms: Rotterdam Study, first cohort|first cohort of the Rotterdam Study
definition: The first cohort of the Rotterdam Study, a prospective population-based cohort of 7,983 inhabitants aged 55 and over of Ommoord, a suburb of Rotterdam in the Netherlands, started in 1990 and re-examined about every 4 years with home interviews and clinical assessments to study determinants of chronic diseases in older adults.

label: Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study
other synonyms: ABCD Study|Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development
definition: A longitudinal cohort of about 11,500 children aged 9-10, including about 1,720 twins, recruited largely through schools at 21 data acquisition sites across the United States to reflect the nation's diversity, and followed for ten years with annual assessments and biennial MRI to study adolescent brain and cognitive development.

label: Study to Understand the Genetics of the Acute Response to Metformin and Glipizide in Humans
other synonyms: The Study to Understand the Genetics of the Acute Response to Metformin and Glipizide in Humans
definition: A pharmacogenetic study established in 2007 at Massachusetts General Hospital, which from 2008 enrolled about 1,000 adults of diverse ancestry enriched for risk of type 2 diabetes and challenged them with glipizide and metformin at clinical research centres in Boston, Massachusetts, to identify genetic variants influencing the acute response to glucose-lowering drugs.
diseases: at risk of: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: Colon Cancer Family Registry
other synonyms: Colon Cancer Family Registry Cohort|Colorectal Cancer Family Registry|Cooperative Familial Registry for Colorectal Studies
definition: An international registry and cohort, funded by the US National Cancer Institute and begun in 1997, of colorectal cancer cases, their unaffected relatives and population-based controls recruited through six centres in Australasia and North America (the Australasian, Mayo Clinic, Ontario, Seattle, University of Hawaii and USC Consortium registries), as a resource for research on familial and sporadic colorectal cancer.

label: DIAbetes COhoRtE
other synonyms: DIAbetes COhoRtE study
