definition: A prospective cohort of adults at high risk of cardiovascular disease, enrolled from November 2013 at Severance Hospital in Seoul, South Korea, to develop preventive strategies for high-risk patients. Participants qualify through high-risk hypertension, diabetes with albuminuria, end-stage renal disease on dialysis, asymptomatic atherosclerotic disease, rheumatoid arthritis treated with methotrexate and steroids, atrial fibrillation, a kidney transplant, or being a relative of a patient with early acute myocardial infarction.

label: French CF Modifier Gene Study
other synonyms: French CF Gene Modifier Consortium|French CF Gene Modifier Study|French Cystic fibrosis Gene Modifier study|French Gene Modifier Study
definition: A cohort of patients with cystic fibrosis enrolled from January 2004 at participating CF centres across France to study modifier genes of the disease, with longitudinal clinical data abstracted from medical records retrospectively before 2004 and collected prospectively since.

label: German Dupuytren Study
other synonyms: German Dupuytren study
definition: A case collection of people with Dupuytren's disease from Germany and Switzerland who had undergone surgical treatment for it, whose blood samples were collected by the German Dupuytren Study Group for genetic studies of the disease, with population controls taken from the PopGen and KORA studies.

label: German Study on the Genetics of Addiction
other synonyms: German Study of the Genetics of Addiction|German Study of the Genetics of Addictions|German Study of the Genetics of Alcoholism
definition: A case–control sample of men of German ancestry with severe alcohol dependence requiring hospitalisation, recruited from consecutive admissions to psychiatry and addiction medicine departments of psychiatric hospitals in the German addiction research network, together with population-based controls, assembled for genetic studies of alcohol dependence.
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to alcohol abuse (ECTO:6000009)

label: Korean Psychiatric GWAS Project
other synonyms: Korean Psychiatric Genome-Wide Association Study Project|Korean psychiatric GWAS project
definition: A multicentre case–control sample recruited through seven academic institutions and their affiliated hospitals in South Korea for genome-wide association studies of psychiatric disorders, with patients with DSM-IV schizophrenia or bipolar I or II disorder and a shared group of healthy controls.

label: Quebec Founder Population cohort
other synonyms: Quebec founder population|Québec Founder Population
definition: A case–control sample for Alzheimer's disease from the Quebec founder population, assembled by Genizon BioSciences, of people aged 65 or older with probable (DSM-IV) or autopsy-confirmed Alzheimer's disease and sex-matched cognitively normal controls aged 75 or older, whose blood DNA is used in genetic studies of the disease.

label: German Sepsis Competence Network
other synonyms: Critical Care Trials Group of the German Sepsis Competence Network
definition: A German sepsis research network whose genetic studies draw on the randomised controlled trials VISEP (recruitment 2003–2005) and MAXSEP (recruitment 2007–2010), combining patients with all-cause sepsis from German hospitals who gave separate consent for genetic analyses.
diseases: patients with: infectious disease with sepsis (MONDO:1040015)

label: Study of ALS Reversals 2: Genetic Analyses
other synonyms: Study of ALS Reversals 2
definition: A cohort of patients who met diagnostic criteria for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) or had progressive muscular atrophy but then improved substantially and lastingly (the ALS Reversal phenotype), invited from the investigators' database of such patients compiled from published case reports and medical records. Participants, enrolled from June 2018 under a protocol approved by Duke University Health System, gave saliva for whole-genome sequencing to identify genetic correlates of the phenotype.

label: Steno 2007
definition: A sub-cohort of the Danish Childhood Diabetes Register (DanDiabKids) made up of individuals newly diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, whose serum was sampled within three months of clinical onset and who had been genotyped on the ImmunoChip array.

label: Studies of a Targeted Risk Reduction Intervention through Defined Exercise
other synonyms: Studies of a targeted risk reduction intervention through defined exercise
definition: A group of three randomised trials of supervised exercise training, STRRIDE I (1999–2003), STRRIDE AT/RT (2004–2008) and STRRIDE-PD (2009–2012), that enrolled previously sedentary adults with overweight or obesity and mild-to-moderate dyslipidaemia or prediabetes at Duke University Medical Center and East Carolina University, to study the effects of exercise amount, mode and intensity, and of weight loss by caloric restriction, on cardiometabolic health.
diseases: patients with: Abnormal circulating lipid concentration (HP:0003119)|patients with: Overweight (HP:0025502)|patients with: obesity disorder (MONDO:0011122)|patients with: prediabetes syndrome (MONDO:0006920)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to calorie restrictive diet intake (ECTO:2000065)|designed to study: exposure to exercise (ECTO:6000002)

label: Rare Variants for Hypertension in Taiwan Chinese
other synonyms: Taiwan Study of Hypertension using Rare Variants
definition: A study of rare variants for hypertension in Taiwan Chinese that combines three cohorts based in Taiwan: families from the SAPPHIRe study, launched in 1995, with at least two hypertensive siblings, and unrelated participants from Tri-Service General Hospital and Taichung Veterans General Hospital matched to SAPPHIRe participants for age, sex and BMI category. All its participants were selected for whole-genome sequencing in the NHLBI TOPMed programme.

label: Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine Program
other synonyms: NHLBI Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine|Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine|Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine program
definition: A programme of the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) that adds whole-genome sequencing and other omics data to existing, deeply phenotyped studies of ethnically and ancestrally diverse participants, to elucidate the genetic architecture and biology of heart, lung, blood and sleep disorders and improve their diagnosis, treatment and prevention.

label: Umeå Fracture and Osteoporosis Study
other synonyms: Umeå Fracture and Osteoporosis (UFO) study|Umeå Fracture and Osteoporosis study
definition: A population-based study sampled from the Northern Sweden Health and Disease Study cohort in the county of Västerbotten, Sweden, whose hip and forearm fracture cases, identified by linking the cohort with medical records and radiographic reports, are compared with controls from the same cohort to identify the genetic and environmental determinants of osteoporotic fractures.

label: Multicenter Study of Hydroxyurea in Sickle Cell Anemia
other synonyms: Multicenter Study of Hydroxyurea|Multicenter Study of Hydroxyurea in Patients With Sickle Cell Anemia
definition: A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, conducted in 1992–1995 at 21 sickle cell referral centres in the United States and Canada, of whether hydroxyurea reduces vaso-occlusive events in adults with sickle cell anaemia and frequent painful episodes, whose participants were then followed observationally in 1996–2001.

label: PanCareLIFE Work Package 4b
definition: A subgroup of the PanCareLIFE ototoxicity genetics study made up of patients diagnosed with cancer before age 18 who were treated with upfront cisplatin and had no radiotherapy to the brain or inner ear, recruited in 2015–2017 through data providers in Switzerland, Italy, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Germany, Austria and the Netherlands for a genome-wide association study of cisplatin-induced hearing loss.

label: African American Breast Cancer Consortium
other synonyms: African American Breast Cancer Cohort|African American Breast Cancer GWAS|African American Breast Cancer consortium
definition: A consortium of nine epidemiological studies of breast cancer in the United States, mostly population-based case-control studies, whose African American cases and controls were genotyped together for a genome-wide association study of breast cancer in women of African ancestry.

label: African American-Diabetes Heart Study
other synonyms: African American DHS|African American-DHS|African American-diabetes heart study
definition: A study at Wake Forest School of Medicine that, after the family-based Diabetes Heart Study and in parallel with it, enrolled unrelated African Americans with type 2 diabetes under the same inclusion criteria and analyses them together with that study's African American participants, to investigate ethnic differences in and inherited contributions to calcified atherosclerotic plaque and related traits such as bone density, vitamin D and, in its MIND extension, brain structure and cognition.

label: Anti-Aging Study Cohort
other synonyms: Anti-aging study cohort|anti-aging study cohort
definition: A cohort of middle-aged and older residents of Ehime Prefecture, Japan, who since 2006 have attended the health check-up programme of the Anti-aging Center at Ehime University Hospital, designed to evaluate ageing-related disorders such as atherosclerosis, cardiovascular disease, physical function and mild cognitive impairment, and who are followed in the Japan Shimanami Health Promoting Program (J-SHIPP), a longitudinal study of factors related to cardiovascular disease, dementia and death.

label: Department of Defense Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative
other synonyms: ADNI Department of Defense studies
definition: A multi-site extension of the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, funded by the US Department of Defense, that enrolled Vietnam War veterans with a history of traumatic brain injury and/or ongoing post-traumatic stress disorder, with or without mild cognitive impairment, and veteran controls without either, identified mainly through Veterans Affairs records, and studies them with ADNI's clinical, cognitive, imaging and fluid biomarker methods to find whether these conditions contribute to the development of Alzheimer's disease.
diseases: patients with: Alzheimer disease (MONDO:0004975)|patients with: post-traumatic stress disorder (MONDO:0005146)|patients with: traumatic brain injury (MONDO:0858950)
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to occupation (ECTO:0001591)

label: Anorexia Nervosa Genetics Initiative
definition: An international collaboration, sponsored by the Klarman Family Foundation and the US National Institute of Mental Health, that recruited individuals with a lifetime history of anorexia nervosa and controls in the United States, Australia, New Zealand, Sweden and Denmark, through treatment centres, national registers and traditional and social media, with blood samples and an online eating-disorder questionnaire, to rapidly expand the samples available for genome-wide association studies of anorexia nervosa.

label: Ashford study
other synonyms: Ashford cohort|Asthma in Ashford|Asthma in Ashford study
definition: An unselected birth cohort of children born in 1992–1993 in Ashford, Kent, England, whose mothers were recruited in pregnancy from 1991 as the UK cohort of the Asthma Multicentre Infant Cohort Study, with house-dust allergen measured in infancy and follow-up by questionnaire, lung function and skin prick tests to age 14 years and a questionnaire at about age 20, to study how early-life allergen exposure and other factors relate to the development of atopy, wheeze and asthma.
diseases: population study of: asthma (MONDO:0004979)|population study of: atopic IgE-mediated allergic disorder (MONDO:0005202)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to allergen via inhalation (ECTO:0900047)

label: Serial Biomarker Measurements and New Echocardiographic Techniques in Chronic Heart Failure Patients Result in Tailored Prediction of Prognosis
other synonyms: Serial Biomarker Measurements and New Echocardiographic Techniques in chronic Heart Failure Patients Result in Tailored Prediction of Prognosis
definition: A prospective multicentre cohort of clinically stable adult outpatients with chronic heart failure, enrolled from 2011 at Erasmus MC, Rotterdam, and Northwest Clinics, Alkmaar, the Netherlands, and seen every three months for blood sampling and clinical assessment, with echocardiography in a subset, to assess whether serial measurements of biomarkers can track disease progression and predict prognosis in individual patients.

label: Bonn Study of COVID Genetics
other synonyms: Bonn Study of COVID19 genetics|Bonn study of COVID genetics
definition: A study run by the Institute of Human Genetics, University of Bonn, Germany, that continuously recruits adults with SARS-CoV-2 infection confirmed by PCR or antibody testing from the general population through public announcements, collecting questionnaires on demographics, pre-existing conditions and the course of infection (and, from September 2021, on long COVID) and DNA for genotyping, to study host genetic factors in COVID-19.

label: Biobanque québécoise de la COVID-19
other synonyms: Banque Québécoise de la COVID-19|Banque québécoise de la COVID-19|Biobanque Quebec COVID19|Biobanque Québécoise de la COVID-19|Biobanque Québécoise de la Covid-19|COVID-19 Québec Biobank|Quebec COVID-19 Biobank|biobanque québécoise de la COVID-19
definition: A province-wide biobank and prospective cohort in Québec, Canada, launched in March 2020 by the Fonds de recherche du Québec–Santé and Génome Québec, which recruits through a network of Québec hospitals adults and children with PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, both hospitalised and non-hospitalised, and PCR-negative controls, with longitudinal biosamples and clinical data, to study the clinical and biological determinants of COVID-19 clinical trajectories.

label: Childhood Asthma Management Program
definition: A multicentre, randomized, double-masked clinical trial of long-term inhaled treatment for mild to moderate asthma (budesonide, nedocromil or placebo, each with albuterol as needed) in children aged 5–12 years, who were enrolled in 1993–1995 at eight clinical centres in the United States and Canada and followed after the trial into adulthood, with a genetic ancillary study of the children and their parents.

label: Continental Origins and Genetic Epidemiology Network
definition: A network of cohorts of African ancestry and of other populations under-represented in genome-wide association studies, whose consortia meta-analyse the cohorts' genome-wide data to find genetic variants for complex traits, such as white blood cell count, blood pressure and hypertension in African-ancestry cohorts (COGENT-BP) and kidney traits across diverse ancestries (COGENT-Kidney, established in 2014).

label: Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia
definition: The cohort studies of the Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia, established in 2000 by the University of Pittsburgh in partnership with West Virginia University to find the factors behind poor oral health in northern Appalachia. They are a family-based etiology study (COHRA1), which recruited households in West Virginia and western Pennsylvania, and a longitudinal cohort (COHRA2), which since 2011 has recruited pregnant women in Pennsylvania and West Virginia and followed them and their children.

label: Diabetes Genetics Initiative
other synonyms: Diabetes Genetics Initiative of Broad Institute of Harvard and MIT, Lund University, and Novartis Institutes of BioMedical Research
definition: A genome-wide association study of type 2 diabetes and related quantitative traits by the Broad Institute of Harvard and MIT, Lund University and the Novartis Institutes for BioMedical Research. Its participants were patients with type 2 diabetes and matched non-diabetic controls from Finland and Sweden, genotyped and characterised for glucose metabolism, lipids, obesity and blood pressure.

label: DIAbetes Meta-ANalysis of Trans-Ethnic association studies
other synonyms: DIAMANTE Consortium|DIAbetes Meta-ANalysis Trans-Ethnic association studies|Diabetes Meta-Analysis of Trans-Ethnic association studies
definition: A consortium established to assemble genome-wide association studies of type 2 diabetes across diverse ancestry groups. It meta-analyses them within its European and East Asian ancestry components and, together with African, Hispanic and South Asian ancestry studies, in a multi-ancestry meta-regression, to discover and fine-map type 2 diabetes loci.

label: Discovery, Biology, and Risk of Inherited Variants in Breast Cancer
other synonyms: Discovery, Biology and Risk of Inherited Variants in Breast Cancer Consortium
definition: A breast cancer genetics consortium, one of the five projects funded in 2010 under the NCI's Genetic Associations and Mechanisms in Oncology (GAME-ON) post-GWAS initiative. It meta-analysed genome-wide summary data shared by existing breast cancer GWAS and genotyped breast cancer cases and controls on the OncoArray, to replicate known and find new breast cancer susceptibility loci.

label: European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition–Cardiovascular Disease Study
other synonyms: EPIC-CVD case-cohort study|European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition – Cardiovascular Disease
definition: A case-cohort study nested within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition, designed to investigate the determinants of cardiovascular disease. EPIC participants with incident coronary heart disease or stroke, identified from 1991 to 2010, are compared with a centre-stratified random subcohort of EPIC participants with stored blood samples, in which molecular factors, including genotypes, are measured.
diseases: patients with: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)|patients with: stroke disorder (MONDO:0005098)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to alcohol consumption (ECTO:0001082)|designed to study: exposure to fatty acid (ECTO:9000308)|designed to study: exposure to tobacco smoking (ECTO:6000029)

label: Fangshan Family-based Ischemic Stroke Study in China
other synonyms: Fangshan Family-Based Ischemic Stroke Study|Fangshan Family-Based Ischemic Stroke Study in China|Fangshan/Family-based Ischemic Stroke Study In China|Fangshan/Family-based Ischemic Stroke Study in China
definition: A family-based study of the genetic and environmental causes of ischaemic stroke, begun in June 2005 in the Fangshan District, a rural area southwest of Beijing, China. It recruited people with ischaemic stroke as probands, with their parents and siblings, through hospital and community stroke registries, and in a second phase in 2011–2012 enrolled participants aged 40 or over through posters and community health centre records. The families enrolled between 2005 and 2012 are followed up every two years.

label: International FTLD-TDP Whole-Genome Sequencing Consortium
other synonyms: FTLD-TDP WGS International consortium|FTLD-TDP WGS consortium|International FTLD-TDP WGS consortium|Whole genome sequencing consortium on Frontotemporal dementia with underlying TDP-43 pathology|international FTLD-TDP whole-genome sequencing consortium
definition: An international consortium, established to characterise the known genetic causes of frontotemporal lobar degeneration with TDP-43 inclusions (FTLD-TDP) and to find new genetic risk factors for it and its pathological subtypes. It whole-genome sequences people with pathologically confirmed FTLD-TDP (and, from its second phase, clinically diagnosed FTLD subtypes enriched for FTLD-TDP) and neurologically normal controls, compiled from institutions and brain banks in North America, Europe and Australia.

label: Genetic Epidemiology of Lung Cancer Consortium
definition: A family study of lung cancer in the United States in which the recruitment sites of the Genetic Epidemiology of Lung Cancer Consortium enrolled lung cancer patients with a family history of the disease, relatives in families with several affected members, and unaffected controls frequency-matched to the cases on age and sex, collecting pedigrees, smoking histories and biospecimens to identify inherited factors that confer a high risk of lung cancer.

label: Genetics of Hypertension Associated Treatment
other synonyms: Genetics of Hypertension Associated Treatments|Genetics of Hypertension-Associated Treatment
definition: An ancillary pharmacogenetic study of the Antihypertensive and Lipid-Lowering Treatment to Prevent Heart Attack Trial (ALLHAT), a double-blind randomised trial of antihypertensive drugs in people aged 55 or older with hypertension and at least one other cardiovascular risk factor, conducted in 1994–2002 at centres in the United States and Canada. GenHAT genotyped the ALLHAT participants with available DNA to test whether variants in hypertension genes modify the effect of the randomised treatment on coronary heart disease and other cardiovascular outcomes.

label: Genetics of Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease
other synonyms: Bergen, Norway COPD Cohort|Genetics of COPD in Norway Study
definition: A genetic case-control study of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease conducted in Bergen, Norway, in 2003–2005 and sponsored by GlaxoSmithKline, which enrolled current and former smokers aged 40 or older: patients with at least moderate COPD, recruited from a hospital patient registry and from the general population, and smokers with normal lung function as controls.
diseases: patients with: chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (MONDO:0005002)
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to Cigarette Smoking (ECTO:6000038)

label: Genetic Links to Anxiety and Depression Study
other synonyms: Genetic Links to Anxiety and Depression
definition: A recontactable cohort of people aged 16 or over living in the United Kingdom, run by the NIHR Mental Health BioResource at King's College London, which recruits online people with current or past depression or anxiety, and also people with no history of mental disorder, into the NIHR BioResource. Participants complete questionnaires, give saliva samples for genotyping and consent to medical record linkage and recontact, to support research on risk factors for depression and anxiety.
diseases: patients with: anxiety disorder (MONDO:0005618)|patients with: depressive disorder (MONDO:0002050)

label: Genetics of the Scottish Health Research Register
other synonyms: Genetics of SHARE|Genetics of Scottish Health Research Register|Genetics of Share|Genetics of the NHS Scotland Health Research Register
definition: A biobank sub-study of SHARE, the Scottish Health Research Register, in NHS Tayside and NHS Fife, Scotland, which collects, with consent, blood left over from registrants' routine clinical tests at hospital or GP clinics for genotyping linked to their anonymised electronic health records; it began as a Wellcome Trust-funded pilot in NHS Tayside.

label: Genes, Reading and Dyslexia Study
other synonyms: Genes, Reading and Dyslexia|Genes, Reading, and Dyslexia
definition: A multisite case-control study of reading disability (developmental dyslexia) in Hispanic American and African American children aged 8 to 15, led by Yale University at sites in the United States, Puerto Rico and Canada, in which the children were assessed with reading and reading-related measures and gave DNA for genetic studies of reading ability and dyslexia.
diseases: patients with: dyslexia (MONDO:0005489)|patients with: reading disorder (MONDO:0001697)

label: Genetic Resource Investigating Diabetes
other synonyms: Genetics Resource Investigating Diabetes|JDRF/WT British case collection|Juvenile Diabetes Research Foundation International/Wellcome Trust British case collection|Juvenile Diabetes Research Foundation/Wellcome Trust Diabetes and Inflammation Laboratorys British case collection|UK Genetic Resource Investigating Diabetes
definition: A collection of people with type 1 diabetes diagnosed before the age of 17, assembled by the JDRF/Wellcome Trust Diabetes and Inflammation Laboratory from paediatric and adult diabetes clinics at National Health Service hospitals across mainland United Kingdom, whose DNA and plasma samples are used in genetic and other studies of type 1 diabetes.

label: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Registry
other synonyms: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy registry|NHLBI HCM Registry
definition: An international prospective observational registry and natural history study of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, which enrolled patients aged 18 to 65 with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy) at centres in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Italy, Germany and the Netherlands in 2014–2017. Participants underwent clinical evaluation, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and blood sampling for genetic and biomarker analysis, and are followed for cardiovascular events to improve risk prediction.

label: Hypertension-Insulin Resistance Family Study
other synonyms: Hypertension-Insulin Resistance Family study|The Hypertension-Insulin Resistance Family Study
definition: A family study of Mexican Americans in the Los Angeles area, United States, which recruited the family members of probands with documented hypertension and measured insulin sensitivity by euglycaemic clamp, to examine the genetic basis of hypertension and insulin resistance.
diseases: at risk of: Insulin resistance (HP:0000855)|at risk of: hypertensive disorder (MONDO:0005044)

label: International AMD Genomics Consortium
other synonyms: International AMD genomics consortium|International Age-Related Macular Degeneration Genomics Consortium|International Age-related Macular Degeneration Genomics Consortium
definition: An international consortium of 26 studies of age-related macular degeneration, mainly in the United States, Europe, Israel and Australia, which gathered DNA from advanced and intermediate AMD cases, mostly recruited from ophthalmology clinics, and from controls, predominantly of European ancestry. The samples were genotyped centrally at the Center for Inherited Disease Research on a custom-modified HumanCoreExome array to examine common and rare genetic variants in AMD.

label: International Stroke Genetics Consortium intracerebral hemorrhage GWAS
definition: A group of six genome-wide association case-control studies of spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage in people of European ancestry, meta-analysed under the auspices of the International Stroke Genetics Consortium to find susceptibility loci for lobar and nonlobar haemorrhage. It comprises the multicentre Genetics of Cerebral Hemorrhage with Anticoagulation study in the United States, the Genetic and Environmental Risk Factors for Hemorrhagic Stroke studies I and II in Cincinnati, and four European studies in Barcelona, Krakow and Lund.

label: UK lung cancer GWAS from the Institute for Cancer Research
other synonyms: ICR-GWA study|UK-GWA study
definition: A genome-wide association case-control study of lung cancer in the United Kingdom, run at the Institute of Cancer Research, which genotyped lung cancer patients recruited in 1999–2004 through UK oncology centres for the Genetic Lung Cancer Predisposition Study (GELCAPS) and compared them with genotyped controls from the 1958 British Birth Cohort.

label: Indian Migration Study
definition: A cross-sectional sib-pair study at four factories in Lucknow, Nagpur, Hyderabad and Bangalore in north, central and south India, which in 2005–2007 examined factory workers and their spouses who had migrated from rural areas together with a rural-dwelling sibling of each, and a random sample of urban non-migrant workers and spouses together with an urban-dwelling sibling, to study the effect of rural-to-urban migration on obesity, diabetes and other cardiovascular risk factors.
diseases: population study of: diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005015)|population study of: obesity disorder (MONDO:0011122)
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to Physical Activity (ECTO:6000039)|participants with exposure: exposure to eating behavior (ECTO:6000021)

label: Institute of Rheumatology, Rheumatoid Arthritis
other synonyms: Institute of Rheumatology Rheumatoid Arthritis
definition: A single-centre prospective observational cohort of Japanese patients with rheumatoid arthritis, established in October 2000 at the Institute of Rheumatology, Tokyo Women's Medical University, Tokyo, which registers consenting patients with rheumatoid arthritis treated at the institute and collects patient questionnaires, physician assessments of disease activity and laboratory data twice a year, in April and October.

label: International Suicide Genetics Consortium
other synonyms: International Suicide Genomics Consortium
definition: An international consortium that meta-analyses genome-wide association data on suicide attempt and suicide death from cohorts worldwide, including cohorts ascertained for psychiatric disorders or substance use, studies of suicide or suicide attempt, and population-based biobanks, to identify genetic risk loci for suicidal behaviour and separate them from those of psychiatric disorders.
diseases: patients with: Suicide behaviors (HP:5200330)|patients with: Suicide behaviors (HP:5200330)

label: Myocardial Applied Genomics Network
other synonyms: Myocardial Applied Genetics Consortium|Myocardial Applied Genetics Network|Myocardial Applied Genomics Network study
definition: A multicentre biorepository for genomic studies of human myocardial disease, led by investigators at the Perelman School of Medicine, University of Pennsylvania, which collects left ventricular tissue from failing hearts at cardiac transplantation and from donor hearts not used for transplantation, at sites including the University of Pennsylvania, the Cleveland Clinic and Stanford, together with genotyped patients with prevalent heart failure referred to a heart failure specialty centre for case-control studies of heart failure.

label: Massachusetts General Hospital Atrial Fibrillation Study
other synonyms: MGH AF Study
definition: A case series of patients with atrial fibrillation enrolled at Massachusetts General Hospital, Boston, United States, since 2001, together with affected and unaffected family members of probands with an extensive family history of atrial fibrillation, each assessed at enrolment by a structured interview on medical history, treatment and family history, an electrocardiogram, echocardiogram results and a blood sample; its early-onset cases (onset before age 66) were whole-genome sequenced in the NHLBI TOPMed programme.

label: NIMH Alzheimer's Disease Genetics Initiative
other synonyms: NIMH AD Genetics Initiative|NIMH Alzheimer's disease Genetics Initiative|National Institute of Mental Health Alzheimer Disease Genetic Initiative|National Institute of Mental Health Genetics Initiative Alzheimer's Disease Study Sample
definition: A family study of Alzheimer's disease in the United States in which three academic medical centres (Massachusetts General Hospital, Johns Hopkins University and the University of Alabama at Birmingham) ascertained families with two or more members affected by Alzheimer's disease (mostly affected sibling pairs), together with unaffected relatives, from 1991 through memory disorder clinics, nursing homes and the community, using uniform procedures. It is the Alzheimer's disease collection of the NIMH Human Genetics Initiative, whose data and DNA are shared through the NIMH repository for genetic linkage and association studies.

label: Genomic Health Initiative
other synonyms: Genomic Health Initiative at NorthShore University HealthSystem|Genomic Health Initiative of Endeavor Health|North Shore University Health systems Genomic Health Initiative
definition: A healthcare-system-based research biobank of NorthShore University HealthSystem (now Endeavor Health) in Illinois, United States, started in 2014, which enrols patients of the health system who consent to give a blood sample for DNA and to linkage of their electronic health records, for translational and discovery research combining genomic and clinical data.

label: MRC National Survey of Health and Development
other synonyms: 1946 National Birth Cohort|National Survey of Health and Development
definition: A birth cohort of people born in one week in March 1946 in England, Scotland and Wales, selected as a social-class-stratified sample of the singleton births to married mothers that week and followed up repeatedly from birth into old age through home visits, questionnaires and clinic assessments. The oldest of the British national birth cohort studies, it is core-funded by the UK Medical Research Council and has been developed since 2008 by the MRC Unit for Lifelong Health and Ageing at UCL into an interdisciplinary study of ageing.

label: Oxford Down Syndrome Cohort Study
other synonyms: Oxford DS Cohort Study
definition: A prospective cohort of newborns with Down syndrome enrolled at birth in 18 hospitals in the United Kingdom from 2006 to 2017, screened for GATA1 mutations and followed with serial clinical and haematological data from birth to 4 years of age, to study transient abnormal myelopoiesis, preleukaemic GATA1 mutations and the risk of myeloid leukaemia in children with Down syndrome.
diseases: patients with: Down syndrome (MONDO:0008608)|patients with: myeloid leukemia associated with down syndrome (MONDO:0850271)|patients with: transient myeloproliferative syndrome (MONDO:0008040)

label: Pharmacogenetics of Opioid Substitution Treatment Response
definition: A prospective cohort of patients aged 16 or older receiving methadone or buprenorphine–naloxone treatment for opioid use disorder at outpatient clinics of the Canadian Addiction Treatment Centres across Ontario, Canada, recruited by McMaster University researchers from May 2018 to January 2023 as an extension of the Genetics of Opioid Addiction study with a similar protocol. Participants were interviewed at entry, gave a saliva sample for DNA and were followed for up to 12 months through their medical records and urine drug screens, to study biopsychosocial and genetic factors in treatment outcomes.

label: PROCAM-2 Study
definition: An occupational cohort of employees of regional companies and government authorities in and around Münster, Germany, who volunteered and underwent a cardiovascular examination in 2000–2007, forming the second part of the Prospective Cardiovascular Münster (PROCAM) Study of cardiovascular risk factors and disease, initiated and conducted by the Leibniz Institute for Arteriosclerosis Research at the University of Münster. Follow-up lapsed until 2018, when the cohort was revived for genotyping, followed by a postal follow-up questionnaire in 2021.

label: PsyCourse Study
other synonyms: PsyCourse study
definition: A multicentre, naturalistic longitudinal study of adults with schizophrenia-spectrum, bipolar or recurrent depressive disorders and of healthy controls, recruited at clinical centres in Germany and Austria from 2011 to 2019 and assessed four times at six-month intervals over 18 months with deep phenotyping, dimensional ratings of psychopathology, cognitive tests and blood sampling, to identify clinical, neurobiological and genetic signatures of the course of major psychiatric disorders across the affective-to-psychotic continuum.
diseases: patients with: Transient psychotic episodes (HP:0006932)|patients with: bipolar I disorder (MONDO:0001866)|patients with: bipolar II disorder (MONDO:0000693)|patients with: major depressive disorder (MONDO:0002009)|patients with: schizoaffective disorder (MONDO:0005487)|patients with: schizophrenia (MONDO:0005090)|patients with: schizophreniform disorder (MONDO:0001265)

label: Queensland Study of Melanoma: Environmental and Genetic Associations
other synonyms: Queensland Study of Melanoma: environmental and genetic associations|Queensland study of Melanoma: Environment and Genetic Associations|Queensland study of Melanoma: Environmental and Genetic Associations|Queensland study of Melanoma: Environmental and Genetics Associations
definition: A population-based study of cutaneous melanoma in Queensland, Australia, that brings together four earlier population-based studies of melanoma patients conducted in 1987–1995: the Queensland Familial Melanoma Project of adult cases and their families, including twins, and studies of melanoma in children, in adolescents and in men over 50. Their participants and some relatives were re-contacted in 2002–2005 for telephone interviews on sun exposure and phenotype and for blood samples, to investigate genetic and environmental factors, and their interaction, in the aetiology of melanoma.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to Solar radiation (ECTO:8000061)

label: Royal Brompton & Harefield Cardiovascular Research Centre Biobank
other synonyms: Cardiovascular Research Centre Biobank, Royal Brompton & Harefield NHS Foundation Trust|Royal Brompton & Harefield Hospital Cardiovascular Research Centre Biobank|Royal Brompton & Harefield Hospitals NHS Trust Cardiovascular Research Biobank|Royal Brompton Hospital Cardiovascular Research Centre Biobank|Royal Brompton and Harefield Hospital Cardiovascular Research Centre Biobank
definition: A research biobank of the Royal Brompton and Harefield hospitals in London, United Kingdom, which since 2009 has collected blood and other samples, including cardiac tissue, with clinical, imaging and follow-up data from adult and paediatric patients attending the hospitals for the investigation or treatment of cardiovascular conditions, and from their relatives, to find genes and biomarkers for the diagnosis and prognosis of cardiovascular disease.
diseases: patients with: cardiovascular disorder (MONDO:0004995)|patients with: dilated cardiomyopathy (MONDO:0005021)|patients with: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (MONDO:0005045)

label: Genome-Wide Association Study of Breast Cancer in the African Diaspora
other synonyms: GWAS in Breast Cancer in the African Diaspora|GWAS of Breast Cancer in the African Diaspora|ROOT consortium|The GWAS of Breast Cancer in the African Diaspora consortium|The Root consortium
definition: A consortium for a genome-wide association study of breast cancer in women of African ancestry in Nigeria, Barbados and the United States, pooling the cases and controls of six epidemiological studies (the Nigerian Breast Cancer Study, the Barbados National Cancer Study, the Racial Variability in Genotypic Determinants of Breast Cancer Risk Study, the Chicago Cancer Prone Study, the Baltimore Breast Cancer Study and the Southern Community Cohort Study), genotyped together on the Illumina HumanOmni2.5 array.

label: Study of Eczema and Asthma To Observe the influence of Nutrition
other synonyms: Aberdeen Study of Eczema and Asthma To Observe the Effects of Nutrition|Aberdeen Study of Eczema and Asthma to Observe the Effects of Nutrition|Study of Eczema and Asthma To Observe the Effects of Nutrition|Study of Eczema and Asthma to Observe the Influence of Nutrition|Study of Eczema and Asthma to Observe the influence of Nutrition
definition: An unselected birth cohort established in 1997 in Aberdeen, United Kingdom, recruiting pregnant women through an antenatal clinic and following their children prospectively from birth, to investigate how antenatal dietary exposures relate to asthma, wheeze and eczema in childhood.
diseases: population study of: asthma (MONDO:0004979)|population study of: atopic eczema (MONDO:0004980)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to antioxidant via ingestion (ECTO:0900200)|designed to study: exposure to pregnancy diet intake (ECTO:2000076)

label: Treatment of Emphysema with a Gamma-Selective Retinoid Agonist
other synonyms: Treatment Of Emphysema With A Selective Retinoid Agonist|Treatment of Emphysema With a Gamma-Selective Retinoid Agonist|Treatment of Emphysema with a Selective Retinoid Agonist|Treatment of Emphysema with a gamma-Selective Retinoid Agonist
definition: A multicentre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled phase II trial sponsored by Hoffmann-La Roche and run from 2007 to 2010 at sites in Europe, Israel, South Africa and the United States, in which ex-smokers over 44 years old with smoking-related moderate to severe COPD with emphysema, on optimised COPD therapy, were assigned to the gamma-selective retinoid agonist palovarotene or placebo.
diseases: patients with: chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (MONDO:0005002)|patients with: pulmonary emphysema (MONDO:0004849)
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to Cigarette Smoking (ECTO:6000038)

label: TRoglitazone In the Prevention Of Diabetes
other synonyms: Troglitazone In the Prevention Of Diabetes|Troglitazone in Prevention of Diabetes|Troglitazone in the Prevention of Diabetes
definition: A single-centre, randomised, double-masked, placebo-controlled trial in which nondiabetic Hispanic women with prior gestational diabetes mellitus, recruited in the Los Angeles area, United States, were assigned to troglitazone or placebo to test whether treating insulin resistance improves insulin sensitivity, preserves pancreatic beta-cell function and prevents type 2 diabetes.
diseases: at risk of: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: UK Digital Heart Project
other synonyms: Digital Heart Project
definition: A cohort of healthy adult volunteers without known cardiovascular disease, recruited prospectively by advertisement from 2011 at the MRC Clinical Sciences Centre, Imperial College London, United Kingdom, who underwent standard and high-resolution three-dimensional cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and genotyping, to study the genetic determinants of cardiac structure and function.

label: Vitamin Intervention for Stroke Prevention
definition: A double-blind, randomised, multicentre trial run from 1996 to 2003 at 56 hospitals and neurology practices in the United States, Canada and Scotland, in which adults aged 35 or older with a recent nondisabling ischaemic stroke and a screening plasma homocysteine above the 25th percentile received high-dose or low-dose folic acid, vitamin B6 and vitamin B12, to test whether lowering homocysteine prevents recurrent stroke.

label: Women of African Ancestry Breast Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of breast cancer in women of African ancestry, established in Nigeria in 1998 and expanded to Uganda and Cameroon in 2011 using the same questionnaires and protocol.

label: Wake Forest School of Medicine Study
other synonyms: Wake Forest University School of Medicine Study
definition: A case-control study of African Americans in North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Tennessee and Virginia, United States, recruited by Wake Forest School of Medicine for genetic studies of type 2 diabetes and nephropathy. Cases with type 2 diabetes and end-stage kidney disease were recruited from dialysis facilities and controls without diabetes or kidney disease from the community and internal medicine clinics, later joined by people with type 2 diabetes but no nephropathy and people with non-diabetic end-stage kidney disease.
diseases: patients with: end stage renal failure (MONDO:0004375)|patients with: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: University of Miami/Texas Alzheimer's Research Care Consortium Wave 2/Case Western Reserve University
other synonyms: UM/CWRU/TARCC wave 2
definition: A case-control dataset of the Alzheimer's Disease Genetics Consortium made up of people with late-onset Alzheimer's disease and cognitively normal controls from the University of Miami, Case Western Reserve University and the second wave of the Texas Alzheimer's Research and Care Consortium in the United States.

label: MexGen-COVID Initiative
definition: A host genetics study of COVID-19 in Mexico, run under the ethics approval of the Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Médicas y Nutrición Salvador Zubirán (INCMNSZ) in Mexico City, of genotyped COVID-19 cases and controls of admixed American ancestry who were also asked about long COVID symptoms by telephone questionnaire.
diseases: patients with: COVID-19 (MONDO:0100096)|patients with: long COVID-19 (MONDO:0100233)

label: Genetics of Long COVID
other synonyms: Genetics Of Long Covid|Genetics of Long COVID study|Sano GOLD|Sano Genetics GOLD study
definition: A study run by Sano Genetics in the United Kingdom in which participants recruited between 2020 and 2022 gave saliva samples for an at-home DNA test and completed a questionnaire on the Sano Genetics platform about their acute COVID-19 and long COVID symptoms, demographics and other chronic conditions, to study genetic factors influencing long COVID risk and severity.
diseases: patients with: COVID-19 (MONDO:0100096)|patients with: long COVID-19 (MONDO:0100233)

label: Japan COVID-19 Task Force
other synonyms: Japan COVID-19 task force|Japan Coronavirus Taskforce
definition: A nationwide multicentre consortium of hospitals across Japan led by core academic institutes, established in early 2020, that collects DNA, RNA and plasma with detailed clinical information from patients hospitalised with COVID-19 to study the host genetics of the disease.

label: NIDDM-Atherosclerosis Study
other synonyms: NIDDM-Atherosclerosis
definition: A family study in the Los Angeles area, United States, in which Hispanic family members of probands with type 2 diabetes were recruited to examine the genetic basis of subclinical atherosclerosis and diabetes, with insulin sensitivity measured by euglycaemic clamp.
diseases: at risk of: atherosclerosis (MONDO:0005311)|at risk of: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: Dementia Genetics Spanish Consortium
other synonyms: Dementia Genetic Spanish Consortium|The Dementia Genetic Spanish Consortium
definition: A Spanish national consortium of research centres and hospitals, created in 2013 under the institutional coverage of the Network Center for Biomedical Research in Neurodegenerative Diseases (CIBERNED), that brings together dementia cohorts to study the genetic architecture of neurodegenerative dementias in the Spanish population.
diseases: patients with: Alzheimer disease (MONDO:0004975)|patients with: dementia (MONDO:0001627)

label: COVID-19 Ioannina Biobank
other synonyms: Covid-19 Ioannina Biobank|Covid19 Ioannina Biobank
definition: A biobank of patients hospitalised with COVID-19 at the University Hospital of Ioannina, Greece, genotyped for host genetic studies of COVID-19 and long COVID, with population controls drawn from the Epirus Health Study cohort.
diseases: patients with: COVID-19 (MONDO:0100096)|patients with: long COVID-19 (MONDO:0100233)

label: Australian Breast Cancer Family Study
other synonyms: Australian Breast Cancer Family Registry
definition: A population-based case-control-family study of breast cancer with an emphasis on early-onset disease, carried out in Melbourne and Sydney, Australia, which enrolled women with a first primary breast cancer identified through cancer registries in 1992-1999, with controls selected from the electoral roll; it is the Australian site of the Breast Cancer Family Registry.

label: Asia Colorectal Cancer Consortium
definition: A consortium, initiated in 2010, that pools genome-wide genotype data on colorectal cancer cases and cancer-free controls of East Asian ancestry from studies in China, Japan and South Korea, among them the Shanghai Women's and Men's Health Studies and colorectal cancer studies from Shanghai, Guangzhou, Aichi, BioBank Japan and several Korean centres, to identify genetic risk factors for colorectal cancer.

label: AIDS Clinical Trials Group
definition: A clinical trials network founded in 1987 as a cooperative group of the US National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, the largest and longest-running network of trials in HIV and other infectious diseases, now with sites on four continents. Participants of its trials may give DNA to its DNA bank (protocol A5128) for genetic studies, and treatment-naive participants with advanced HIV disease from its antiviral treatment trials were the progressors of the International HIV Controllers Study genome-wide association study.
diseases: patients with: AIDS (MONDO:0012268)|patients with: HIV infectious disease (MONDO:0005109)

label: genetic Association study in individuals from Diverse Ancestral backgrounds with Multiple Sclerosis
other synonyms: A Genetic Association study in Diverse Ancestries of Multiple Sclerosis|ADAMS project
definition: A UK genetic cohort study, run by the Preventive Neurology Unit of Queen Mary University of London and recruiting since November 2021, of adults with multiple sclerosis from diverse, mostly non-European, ancestral backgrounds, enrolled online, at clinical sites and through the UK MS Register, who give saliva DNA for genotyping, questionnaire data and consent to health-record linkage, to study the genetics of multiple sclerosis susceptibility and severity; it has no controls of its own.

label: ADVANCE trial
other synonyms: ADVANCE Study of DTG + TAF + FTC vs DTG + TDF + FTC and EFV + TDF+FTC in First-line Antiretroviral Therapy|WRHI 060
definition: A randomised, open-label, investigator-led phase 3 non-inferiority trial of first-line antiretroviral therapy, run by the University of the Witwatersrand (study WRHI 060) at sites in Johannesburg, South Africa, which from February 2017 randomised people aged 12 years or older with HIV-1 who had not received antiretroviral therapy in the previous 6 months to dolutegravir and emtricitabine with either tenofovir alafenamide or tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, or to efavirenz, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate and emtricitabine, and followed them for 96 weeks, later extended to 192 weeks.

label: Atherosclerotic Disease, Vascular Function, and Genetic Epidemiology Study
other synonyms: Atherosclerotic Disease VAscular functioN and genetiC Epidemiology study|Atherosclerotic Disease, VAscular FunctioN, and GenetiC Epidemiology|Atherosclerotic Disease, VAscular functioN, and genetiC Epidemiology|Atherosclerotic Disease, Vascular function, and Genetic Epidemiology
definition: A multi-ethnic case-control genetic association study of coronary artery disease by Stanford University and Kaiser Permanente Northern California, which from October 2001 to December 2003 enrolled Kaiser Permanente members in the San Francisco Bay area into three case groups (early-onset coronary artery disease, and incident stable exertional angina or myocardial infarction at an older age) and two control groups free of clinical cardiovascular disease (younger adults, including some CARDIA participants, and adults aged 60 to 69), with questionnaires, stored blood samples, cardiac computed tomography in older controls and later follow-up through health plan records.

label: Antioxydants, Lipides Essentiels, Nutrition et maladies OculaiRes
other synonyms: Antioxydants Lipides Essentiels Nutrition et Maladies Oculaires|Antioxydants, LIpides Essentiels, Nutrition et maladies OculaiRes
definition: A population-based cohort of elderly residents of Bordeaux, France, recruited from 2006 as an ophthalmological follow-up nested within the Three-City Study, assessing associations between eye diseases such as age-related macular degeneration and nutritional factors through plasma measurements, dietary-intake estimation and repeated eye examinations.
diseases: population study of: age-related macular degeneration (MONDO:0005150)|population study of: cataract (MONDO:0005129)|population study of: eye disorder (MONDO:0005328)|population study of: glaucoma (MONDO:0005041)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to antioxidant (ECTO:9001647)|designed to study: exposure to nutrient (ECTO:9001695)|designed to study: exposure to omega-3 fatty acid (ECTO:9002766)|designed to study: exposure to terpenoid (ECTO:9002364)

label: Autopsy-Confirmed Parkinson Disease GWAS Consortium
other synonyms: Autopsy-Confirmed PD GWAS Consortium|Autopsy-Confirmed Parkinson Disease Genetics Consortium|Autopsy-confirmed Parkinson Disease GWAS Consortium
definition: A case-control sample assembled by a consortium of twelve US autopsy centres, several of them Morris K. Udall Centers of Excellence in Parkinson's Disease Research, of people clinically diagnosed with Parkinson's disease whose diagnosis was confirmed at autopsy (nigral neuronal loss and Lewy bodies, with little Alzheimer pathology) and of neuropathologically normal controls, often patients' spouses, genotyped genome-wide at the Center for Inherited Disease Research to find genetic risk factors for Parkinson's disease with less diagnostic misclassification.

label: Alcohol-Related Cancers and Genetic susceptibility in Europe
other synonyms: Alcohol Related CAncers and Genetic susceptibility in Europe|Alcohol Related Cancers and Genetic Susceptibility in Europe Study|Alcohol-Related Cancers and Genetic Susceptibility Study in Europe|Alcohol-Related Cancers and Genetic Susceptibility in Europe|Alcohol-related cancers and genetic susceptibility in Europe
definition: A multicentre case-control study of upper aerodigestive tract cancers (oral cavity, pharynx, larynx and oesophagus), initiated by the International Agency for Research on Cancer in 2002, that recruited newly diagnosed cases and hospital controls (population controls in the United Kingdom) at centres in about ten European countries, mostly in 2002-2005, with interviews on smoking, drinking and diet and biological samples, to study genetic susceptibility to these cancers and its interplay with lifestyle factors.
diseases: patients with: esophageal cancer (MONDO:0007576)|patients with: larynx cancer (MONDO:0002352)|patients with: oral cavity cancer (MONDO:0005515)|patients with: pharynx cancer (MONDO:0005517)|patients with: upper aerodigestive tract neoplasm (MONDO:0005398)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to alcohol consumption (ECTO:0001082)|designed to study: exposure to tobacco smoking (ECTO:6000029)|designed to study: exposure to vegetable food product via ingestion (ECTO:0070232)

label: Base de Datos de Ictus del Hospital del Mar
other synonyms: BASICMAR register|BASe de datos de ICtus del hospital del MAR|Base de Datos de Ictus del Hospital del Mar Genetic Study
definition: A prospective hospital-based register of patients admitted with acute stroke to Hospital del Mar, a tertiary public university hospital serving about 330,000 people in three districts of Barcelona, Spain, with records from 2005 onwards, standardised clinical and imaging assessment and outcome follow-up; its patients who gave DNA form the BASICMAR genetic study, a contributing site of the NINDS Stroke Genetics Network.

label: Bavarian Breast Cancer Cases and Controls Study
other synonyms: Bavarian Breast Cancer Cases and Controls
definition: A case-control study of breast cancer based at the University Breast Center for Franconia, Erlangen University Hospital, Bavaria, Germany, which in the 2000s enrolled women aged 18 or older with invasive breast cancer treated there, with tumour tissue for tissue microarrays, and controls recruited in hospital, through a breast cancer screening programme or by newspaper advertisement, to study genetic and non-genetic risk factors and prognostic and predictive factors of breast cancer.

label: Breast Cancer Employment and Environment Study
other synonyms: Breast Cancer Environment and Employment Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of women aged 18-80 recruited in Western Australia between May 2009 and January 2011 to investigate occupational and environmental risk factors for breast cancer.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to ionizing radiation (ECTO:7000047)

label: BiDirect Study
other synonyms: BiDirect study|The BiDirect study
definition: A prospective observational study run by the University of Münster, Germany, of three cohorts of adults aged 35–65 examined in parallel with identical methods: patients treated for an acute depressive episode and patients after an acute myocardial infarction or acute coronary syndrome, recruited through psychiatric and cardiological hospitals and clinics in and around Münster, and reference participants randomly sampled from the city's population register, with a baseline examination in 2010–2013 and repeated follow-ups, to investigate the bidirectional relationship between depression and subclinical arteriosclerosis.
diseases: patients with: acute coronary syndrome (MONDO:0005542)|patients with: arteriosclerosis disorder (MONDO:0002277)|patients with: depressive disorder (MONDO:0002050)

label: Blue Mountains Eye Study
other synonyms: Blue Mountain Eye Study
definition: A population-based cohort study of common eye diseases and other health outcomes among permanent residents aged 49 years or older of two postcode areas in the Blue Mountains, west of Sydney, Australia, identified through a census and examined at baseline in 1992–1994 and then every five years to 2007–2009, with newly eligible residents added in an extension study in 1999–2000.

label: Bonn OMNI cohort
other synonyms: Bonn OMNI
definition: A cohort of Alzheimer's disease cases and controls in Germany, drawn from a larger German GWAS sample recruited through the German Dementia Competence Network, the AgeCoDe study of ageing, cognition and dementia in primary care patients, and the Memory Clinic at the University Hospital of Bonn. Controls were drawn from the population-based Heinz Nixdorf Recall study cohort.

label: Bio-Repository of DNA in Stroke
other synonyms: Bio-Repository of DNA in stroke|Bio-repository of DNA in stroke
definition: An ongoing international hospital-based DNA repository, run from Imperial College London, of adults with ischaemic or haemorrhagic stroke recruited at stroke centres in the United Kingdom (patients of European ancestry and British South Asians), India and Qatar, together with controls, to compare genetic risk factors for stroke between European, South Asian and Middle Eastern populations.

label: Breast Oncology Galicia Network
other synonyms: BREast Oncology GAlicia Network|BREast Oncology GAlician Network|Breast Oncology Galician Network
definition: A population-based case-control study of breast cancer conducted since 1997 in Vigo and Santiago de Compostela, Galicia, Spain, recruiting incident breast cancer cases from Galician hospitals with blood and tumour tissue samples and risk-factor questionnaires, and controls frequency-matched by age, public health registry inclusion and place of residence.

label: Kita-Nagoya Genomic Epidemiology Study
other synonyms: KItaNagoya Genome|Kita-Nagoya Genomic Epidemiology study|Kitanagoya Genome Study
definition: An ongoing community-based prospective observational study of the genetic basis of cardiovascular disease and its risk factors, begun in 2005 by Nagoya University with Aichi Gakuin University, of local residents of Kitanagoya, Aichi Prefecture, Japan, aged 50 or older, enrolled at community-based annual health check-ups.

label: Cleveland Clinic Atrial Fibrillation Study
other synonyms: Cleveland Clinic AF Study|Cleveland Clinic AF study
definition: A collection of clinical and genetic data from patients with atrial fibrillation and controls enrolled at the Cleveland Clinic in its CV/Arrhythmia Biobank, including the Cleveland Clinic Lone Atrial Fibrillation GeneBank of patients with atrial fibrillation without significant structural heart disease, for genetic studies of atrial fibrillation; its early-onset cases were whole-genome sequenced in the NHLBI TOPMed programme.

label: California Childhood Cancer Record Linkage Project
other synonyms: California Cancer Records Linkage Project
definition: A statewide record-linkage case–control study that links California birth records for 1982–2009, maintained by the California Department of Public Health, to diagnoses of cancer before the age of 15 in the California Cancer Registry for 1988–2011, with cancer-free California-born controls matched on date of birth, sex and maternal race or ethnicity through vital statistics records, and uses archived newborn dried blood spots from the California Biobank Program for genetic studies of childhood cancers such as acute lymphoblastic leukaemia and glioma.
diseases: patients with: acute lymphoblastic leukemia (MONDO:0004967)|patients with: childhood malignant neoplasm (MONDO:0006517)|patients with: glioma (MONDO:0021042)

label: CLOZUK study
other synonyms: The CLOZUK cohort
definition: A sample of people in the United Kingdom with treatment-resistant schizophrenia who were prescribed clozapine, whose anonymised blood samples and clinical monitoring data were obtained through the clozapine monitoring services, first in collaboration with Novartis and later through the Zaponex Treatment Access System (second wave 2013–15, third wave 2019–21), for Cardiff University's genetic studies of schizophrenia and clozapine metabolism.

label: Colorado Longitudinal Twin Study
other synonyms: Colorado Longitidinal Twin Study|Colorado Longitudinal Twin Sample
definition: A prospective longitudinal study of same-sex twin pairs born in 1984–1990 and recruited in Colorado, United States, from the Colorado Twin Registry of the Institute for Behavioral Genetics at the University of Colorado, assessed almost yearly from 14 months to age 16 and again in adulthood to investigate genetic and environmental influences on individual differences in psychological development.

label: Combined Small Datasets Collection
definition: A harmonized dataset of the Alzheimer's Disease Genetics Consortium that merges six separately ascertained datasets or dataset waves of Alzheimer's disease cases and cognitively normal elders (BIOCARD, CHAP2, EAS, RMAYO, ROSMAP2 and WASHU2), each too small to be analysed on its own, so that they can be analysed together in common-variant association studies.

label: Columbia University COVID-19 Biobank
other synonyms: Columbia COVID-19 Biobank|Columbia University COVID19 Biobank
definition: A biobank set up at Columbia University Irving Medical Center in New York City, United States, in response to the city's COVID-19 surge in March 2020, which kept residual blood and urine samples left over from clinical testing of consecutive patients with PCR-confirmed COVID-19, of any age, sex or ancestry, treated at the medical center.

label: FIN-D2D 2007
other synonyms: Dehko 2D 2007
definition: A population-based health examination survey of a random sample of people aged 45–74, drawn from the National Population Register and stratified by sex, age group and area, in the hospital districts of Pirkanmaa, South Ostrobothnia and Central Finland, Finland, examined in October–December 2007 at the end of FIN-D2D, the implementation project of Finland's national type 2 diabetes prevention programme, to measure the prevalence of diabetes, cardiovascular disease and their risk factors and to evaluate the programme.
diseases: population study of: obesity disorder (MONDO:0011122)|population study of: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: DietBB sample
other synonyms: The Diet-Body-Brain cohort
definition: A subsample of the German Study on Ageing, Cognition and Dementia in Primary Care Patients (AgeCoDe), a general-practice registry-based longitudinal study of people aged 75 and over recruited in 2002–2003 in six German cities, made up of participants who were free of dementia at baseline and had DNA available and who either developed Alzheimer-type dementia during follow-up or stayed free of dementia, selected for a genome-wide DNA methylation study of dementia and also genotyped genome-wide.
diseases: patients with: Alzheimer disease (MONDO:0004975)|patients with: dementia (MONDO:0001627)

label: Dietary, Lifestyle and Genetic Determinants of Obesity and Metabolic Syndrome study
other synonyms: DIetary, Lifestyle and Genetic determinants of Obesity and Metabolic syndrome study|DIetary, Lifestyle, and Genetic determinants of Obesity and Metabolic syndrome Survey
definition: A population-based cohort of Finnish adults aged 25–74, recruited at baseline in 2007 as a sub-study of the FINRISK2007 survey to investigate the factors leading to obesity and metabolic syndrome, with follow-up in 2014.
diseases: population study of: metabolic syndrome X (MONDO:0011565)|population study of: obesity disorder (MONDO:0011122)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to eating behavior (ECTO:6000021)|designed to study: exposure to lifestyle (ECTO:6000015)

label: Finnish Diabetes Prevention Study
definition: A randomised controlled trial at five centres in Finland (Helsinki, Kuopio, Turku, Tampere and Oulu) that from 1993 to 1998 randomised overweight men and women aged 40–64 with impaired glucose tolerance to intensive individual diet and exercise counselling or to a control group, to test whether lifestyle change prevents type 2 diabetes, and whose participants continued to be followed with yearly visits after the trial.
diseases: at risk of: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: Duke study of Functional Endpoints for Age-related Macular Degeneration
definition: A single-centre, prospective, longitudinal observational natural-history study at the Duke Eye Center in Durham, North Carolina, United States, which from 2013 enrolled people aged 50 or over with early or intermediate (dry) age-related macular degeneration from the centre's patients, together with controls from Duke optometry and comprehensive eye clinics or the patients' family and friends, and assessed them with retinal imaging and with visual function tests repeated about every six months over 24 months, to find functional end points for clinical trials.

label: Epidemiology of Endometrial Cancer Consortium
definition: An NCI-supported consortium, begun in 2006, of case-control and cohort studies in North America, Europe, Asia and Australia that combines data across its member studies, including in a genome-wide association study, to investigate the etiology of endometrial cancer.

label: Epidemiology of Dementia in Singapore
other synonyms: Epidemiology of Dementia In Singapore|Epidemiology of Dementia in Singapore Study|Epidemiology of Dementia in Singapore study
definition: A population-based study of the prevalence and risk factors of cognitive impairment and dementia in Chinese, Malay and Indian adults in Singapore, which drew participants aged 60 and over from the Singapore Epidemiology of Eye Diseases study (the Singapore Chinese Eye Study, 2009–2011, the Singapore Malay Eye Study, 2010–2013, and the Singapore Indian Eye Study, 2013–2015). Participants were screened with the Abbreviated Mental Test and a history of progressive forgetfulness, and those who screened positive were invited for neuropsychological testing and brain MRI.
diseases: population study of: cognitive disorder (MONDO:0002039)|population study of: dementia (MONDO:0001627)

label: Early-Onset Venous Thrombosis
other synonyms: Early Onset Venous Thrombosis
definition: A French case-control study of venous thrombosis whose cases, from medical centres in Grenoble, Marseille, Montpellier and Paris, had a documented idiopathic deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism before the age of 50 without acquired risk factors or major thrombophilia defects, and whose controls were healthy French participants of the SU.VI.MAX study. It was genotyped genome-wide for genetic association studies of venous thrombosis.

label: Family History Risk Study
definition: A study of women aged 20–79 attending the Family History Risk and Prevention Clinic in Manchester, United Kingdom, recruited in 2010–2012, who completed risk-factor questionnaires and consented to DNA testing for SNP analysis and to breast density measurement, set up to validate and improve the breast cancer risk prediction models used in family history clinics.

label: German Aortic Stenosis Cohort
other synonyms: German aortic stenosis cohort
definition: A cohort of patients with aortic valve stenosis, diagnosed by echocardiography or by a history of valve replacement for severe stenosis, recruited from the German Heart Center Munich and the University of Bonn/Marburg, Germany, and genotyped for studies of the genetics of aortic stenosis.

label: Greater Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky Stroke Study
other synonyms: Greater Cincinnati Northern Kentucky Stroke Study
definition: A population-based study of stroke incidence, risk factors, treatment and outcomes in the biracial population of a five-county region of southwestern Ohio and northern Kentucky, United States, around Cincinnati, which ascertains all hospitalized and autopsied strokes and transient ischaemic attacks among residents during one-year study periods held since 1993 (July 1993 to June 1994, 1999, 2005, 2010 and 2015), to measure temporal trends in stroke incidence and outcome.
diseases: patients with: stroke disorder (MONDO:0005098)|patients with: transient ischemic attack (MONDO:0005264)

label: Genotek COVID-19 study
definition: Participants of the COVID-19 genetic studies of the Russian genetic testing company Genotek: its customers who consented to research use of their data and answered online questionnaires about COVID-19, studied for long COVID and, when aged 40 or over with non-severe COVID-19, as controls in a genome-wide association study of severe COVID-19 whose cases were patients hospitalised in Moscow and Ufa.
diseases: patients with: COVID-19 (MONDO:0100096)|patients with: long COVID-19 (MONDO:0100233)

label: Genetics of Kidneys in Diabetes Study
other synonyms: Genetics of Kidneys in Diabetes US Study|Genetics of Kidneys in Diabetes study
definition: A collection of DNA and clinical data for genetic association studies of diabetic nephropathy in type 1 diabetes, assembled with support from the JDRF, NIDDK and CDC by the Joslin Diabetes Center, from patients of its clinic in New England, and by the George Washington University Biostatistics Center, from volunteers across the United States and Canada. Participants aged 18–59 with type 1 diabetes diagnosed before age 31 were enrolled as cases with diabetic nephropathy (persistent proteinuria or end-stage renal disease) or as controls with normoalbuminuria after at least 15 years of diabetes, with both parents enrolled where possible to form family trios.
diseases: patients with: diabetic kidney disease (MONDO:0005016)|patients with: type 1 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005147)

label: Graz Stroke Study
definition: A hospital-based series of patients with ischaemic stroke admitted to the stroke unit of the Department of Neurology of the Medical University of Graz, Austria, investigated with brain imaging and a standardised diagnostic protocol and subtyped by stroke neurologists, whose cases are compared in genetic studies of ischaemic stroke with participants of the Austrian Stroke Prevention Study from the same catchment area as controls.

label: Head and Neck 5000
other synonyms: Head and Neck 5000 study|Head and neck 5000
definition: A prospective clinical cohort of people newly diagnosed with head and neck cancer, recruited before treatment at NHS centres across the United Kingdom and coordinated from Bristol, with health, lifestyle, quality-of-life and sexual-history questionnaires, clinical data, blood, saliva and tumour tissue samples and follow-up, set up to evaluate the centralisation of head and neck cancer care and as a biomedical resource for translational and prognostic research.
diseases: patients with: head and neck cancer (MONDO:0005627)

label: International Agency for Research on Cancer Central Europe Study
other synonyms: Central Europe study|IARC Central Europe study
definition: A multicentre hospital-based case–control study of cancers of the upper aerodigestive tract (oral cavity, pharynx, larynx and oesophagus), coordinated by the International Agency for Research on Cancer in Bucharest (Romania), Lodz (Poland), Moscow (Russia), Banská Bystrica (Slovakia), and Olomouc and Prague (Czech Republic) to investigate genetic susceptibility to these cancers and its interaction with alcohol and tobacco use. It is the upper aerodigestive tract arm of IARC's central European multicentre case–control study of lung, head and neck and kidney cancers, and part of its controls are shared with the lung cancer arm.
diseases: patients with: upper aerodigestive tract neoplasm (MONDO:0005398)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to Tobacco Use (ECTO:6000041)|designed to study: exposure to alcohol consumption (ECTO:0001082)

label: Institute for Behavioral Genetics
definition: A combined sample of two longitudinal family studies of the Institute for Behavioral Genetics at the University of Colorado Boulder, United States: the Colorado Adoption Project, a prospective adoption study of behavioural development begun in 1975, and the Colorado Twin Registry, a population-based registry of twins born since 1968 that has recruited since 1982. Their genotyped participants are analysed together in genome-wide association meta-analyses of childhood and adolescent psychiatric traits.

label: International Collaboration for the Genomics of HIV
other synonyms: International Consortium for the Genomics of HIV
definition: An international collaboration of the HIV host genetics community, established to combine all available genome-wide SNP data sets on people living with HIV-1 worldwide, which pools genotype and clinical data from HIV cohorts and studies in North America, Europe, Australia and Africa, many of them natural-history cohorts, to study host genetic influences on HIV-1 acquisition, viral load and spontaneous control.

label: International Endometriosis Genetics Consortium
definition: An international consortium of research groups studying the genetics of endometriosis, which pools genome-wide association data from studies in Europe, the United States, Australia and Japan, with cases identified by surgical confirmation, medical records or self-report, in meta-analyses of endometriosis risk.

label: INGI-Val Borbera
other synonyms: Italian Network on Genetic Isolates-Val Borbera|Val Borbera|Val Borbera cohort|Val Borbera study
definition: A population-based cohort of adults descended from the inhabitants of the upper Val Borbera, a genetically isolated valley in the Apennine mountains of Piedmont, north-west Italy, recruited on the basis of their ancestry in the valley's villages and nearby areas, with clinical and anthropometric data collected by physicians of San Raffaele Hospital, Milan, to identify genes and variants underlying common disorders and quantitative traits; one of the isolated populations of the Italian Network of Genetic Isolates.

label: Ischemic Stroke Genetics Study
other synonyms: Ischemic Stroke Genetic Study
definition: A prospective multicentre case–control study, funded by the US National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, of adults with a first-ever ischaemic stroke confirmed by CT or MRI and enrolled within 30 days of onset at five academic medical centres in the United States, with centrally adjudicated stroke subtypes, and of stroke-free controls matched by age and sex and recruited mainly among the patients' spouses and unrelated friends, to investigate genetic risk factors for ischaemic stroke and its subtypes.

label: Karolinska Mammography Project for Risk Prediction of Breast Cancer
other synonyms: KARMA study|KARolinska MAmmography Project for Risk Prediction of Breast Cancer|Karolinska Mammography Project for Risk Prediction of Breast Cancer – Cohort Study
definition: A prospective cohort of women recruited in 2011–2013 when attending mammography screening or clinical mammography at four hospitals in Sweden (in Stockholm, Helsingborg, Lund and Landskrona), with questionnaires, mammograms, blood samples and linkage to Swedish health registers, established to determine how mammographic density, genetic factors and lifestyle influence breast cancer risk and to build risk prediction models for individualised prevention and screening.

label: Kathleen Cuningham Foundation Consortium for Research into Familial Breast Cancer
other synonyms: Kathleen Cuningham Consortium for Research into Familial Breast Cancer|Kathleen Cuningham Foundation Consortium for Research into Familial Aspects of Breast Cancer
definition: A research resource of epidemiological, family-history, lifestyle and clinical data and biospecimens collected since 1997 from affected and unaffected members of families with multiple cases of breast and/or ovarian cancer, recruited by research nurses through family cancer clinics in Australia and New Zealand, and made available to researchers anywhere in the world for studies of familial breast cancer.
diseases: at risk of: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|at risk of: ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170)

label: Krakow stroke genetics study
definition: An ongoing, prospective, single-centre, hospital-based study of consecutive consenting patients of European origin with first-ever or recurrent ischaemic stroke admitted since 2002 to the Stroke Unit of the Jagiellonian University in Krakow, Poland, with stroke subtypes assigned by TOAST and CCS criteria, together with unrelated stroke-free controls from the population of southern Poland; one of the genetic research centres of the Stroke Genetics Network.

label: Leuven Stroke Genetics Study
other synonyms: Leuven Stroke genetics study
definition: A prospective hospital-based study of patients of European descent with cerebral ischaemia (a clinical stroke with imaging confirmation, or a transient ischaemic attack with a new ischaemic lesion on diffusion-weighted imaging) admitted to the Stroke Unit of the University Hospitals Leuven, Belgium, from 2005 to 2009, with standardised diagnostic work-up and TOAST subtyping, together with controls recruited from the same population; one of the genetic research centres of the Stroke Genetics Network.
diseases: patients with: ischemic stroke (MONDO:1060198)|patients with: transient ischemic attack (MONDO:0005264)

label: Men of African Descent and Carcinoma of the Prostate
other synonyms: Men of African Descent and Carcinoma of the Prostate Consortium|Men of African Descent and Carcinoma of the Prostate Network
definition: A multicentre, clinic-based case-control study of prostate cancer run since 2016 by the Men of African Descent and Carcinoma of the Prostate (MADCaP) Network at seven accrual centres in Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal and South Africa, with partner institutions in the United States, which under common eligibility criteria, instruments and biosample protocols enrols men over 30 who self-identify as black African: incident, histologically confirmed prostate cancer cases from urology and oncology clinics, and cancer-free controls frequency-matched by age from other clinics in the same catchment areas, to study the genetics and epidemiology of prostate cancer in sub-Saharan Africa.

label: Maywood Cohort
other synonyms: Loyola Maywood Study|Maywood cohort|Maywood cohort study
definition: A cohort of African-American families in Maywood, Illinois, United States, recruited from 1995 by Loyola University Chicago Stritch School of Medicine from a representative random sample of residents aged 18 to 74 for its family studies of blood pressure and the genetics of hypertension in populations of West African origin, in which Maywood was the United States site alongside Nigeria and Jamaica.
