label: Minnesota Breast Cancer Family Study
definition: A historical cohort of multigenerational families in Minnesota, United States, ascertained through a consecutive, family-history-unselected series of breast cancer probands diagnosed from 1944 to 1952 at the University of Minnesota, followed up by telephone interview and mailed questionnaire to measure cancer incidence and risk factors in their relatives (sisters, daughters, granddaughters, nieces and marry-ins).

label: Middlesex County Ischemic Stroke Study
definition: A prospective hospital-based registry of adults with ischaemic stroke, of any ethnic or racial group, admitted through the emergency room to the dedicated stroke unit of the New Jersey Neuroscience Institute at JFK Medical Center in Edison, New Jersey, United States, which enrolled first-ever and recurrent strokes of any severity from 2000 to 2009 with standardised investigations and TOAST subtyping; one of the genetic research centres of the Stroke Genetics Network.

label: HARMONISATION study
other synonyms: Harmonization Study|Harmonization study|Memory Clinic in Singapore|Memory Clinic in Singapore Study|Memory Clinic in Singapore study
definition: A prospective observational cohort of older multi-ethnic Asian patients aged 50 or over with no cognitive impairment, mild cognitive impairment or dementia due to Alzheimer's disease and/or cerebrovascular disease, recruited from 2010 at the memory clinics of the National University Hospital and St Luke's Hospital in Singapore and assessed by the Memory Aging and Cognition Centre, National University of Singapore, with annual clinical and neuropsychological follow-up for up to five years and brain MRI, retinal and blood biomarker data, to study vascular cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease.
diseases: patients with: Alzheimer disease (MONDO:0004975)|patients with: Cognitive impairment (HP:0100543)|patients with: dementia (MONDO:0001627)

label: Genes Affecting Stroke Risk and Outcome Study
other synonyms: Genes Affecting Stroke Risk and Outcomes Study|Genes Affecting Stroke Risks and Outcomes Study|Genes Associated with Stroke Risk and Outcomes Study|MGH Genes Affecting Stroke Risk and Outcome Study|Massachusetts General Hospital – Genes Affecting Stroke Risk and Outcome Study
definition: A hospital-based study at the Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston, United States, that from 2003 enrolled adults with acute ischaemic stroke (consecutive patients admitted to its stroke unit through the emergency department, or seen in its neurology clinics or on other inpatient services), with stroke-free controls from the hospital's outpatient clinics matched on age, sex and ancestry, to study genetic influences on the risk and outcome of ischaemic stroke; one of the genetic research centres of the Stroke Genetics Network.

label: Melanoma Institute Australia cohort
other synonyms: Melanoma Institute Australia
definition: A cohort of patients with histopathologically confirmed cutaneous melanoma managed at Melanoma Institute Australia in Sydney, Australia, identified with written informed consent from the institute's Biospecimen Bank and Research Database, whose germline DNA was genotyped genome-wide in phases from 2014 and who are followed prospectively for outcomes including death from melanoma, ascertained from clinical records and linkage to Australian cancer registries.

label: Montrachet Study
other synonyms: Maculopathy Optic Nerve nuTRition neurovAsCular and HEarT diseases|Montrachet Study Cohort
definition: A population-based study of people aged 75 years or older in Dijon, France, recruited from 2009 to 2013 among participants of the Three-City (3C) Study, who had eye examinations, including photographs and optical coherence tomography of the macula and optic disc, at Dijon University Hospital, designed to find associations between age-related eye diseases and neurologic and heart diseases in the elderly.

label: MUNICH stroke study
other synonyms: MUNICH study|WTCCC2-Munich
definition: A hospital-based collection of consecutive patients of European ancestry with ischaemic stroke, recruited from 2002 to 2009 at the dedicated stroke unit of the Department of Neurology, Klinikum Großhadern, Ludwig-Maximilians-University, Munich, Germany, with stroke subtypes assigned by TOAST criteria; the cases were genotyped genome-wide in the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium 2 ischaemic stroke study and contribute to METASTROKE, the Stroke Genetics Network (SiGN) and MEGASTROKE.

label: Murcia Twin Registry
definition: A population-based register of adult twins and other multiples from the region of Murcia, southeast Spain, created in 2006 through an agreement between the University of Murcia and the Murcia Health Council, which identifies twins in the computerised databases of the regional health system and collects interview, questionnaire and anthropometric data in successive waves, with a biobank, for research on genetic and environmental influences on health and health-related behaviours; it began with female twins born 1940-1966 and later added male and opposite-sex twins.

label: Norwegian, Exeter and King's College Consortium for Genetics of Neuropsychiatric Symptoms in Dementia
definition: A collaboration of the University of Exeter, King's College London, Innlandet Hospital Trust, the University of Oslo and Stavanger University Hospital that undertakes secondary analysis of data on patients with Alzheimer's disease from cohort studies and patient registries, to study the genetics of neuropsychiatric symptoms such as psychosis in dementia. Its sources are the Norwegian registry of persons assessed for cognitive symptoms (NorCog) with the affiliated Progression of Alzheimer's Disease and Resource Use study, the REDIC-NH and Health and Memory Study nursing-home cohorts in Norway, AddNeuroMed, and hospital outpatient clinics in Italy and Greece.

label: NeuroGenetics Research Consortium
definition: A case-control sample of people with Parkinson's disease, diagnosed by modified UK Brain Bank criteria, and neurologically healthy controls (community volunteers and patients' spouses), recruited by the NeuroGenetics Research Consortium at affiliated neurology and movement disorder clinics in Oregon, Washington, Georgia and New York, United States, with uniform, standardised methods for diagnosis, subject selection, data collection and DNA preparation, for genetic and gene-environment studies of Parkinson's disease, and genotyped genome-wide.

label: Genetics of Hypertension in Blacks
definition: A Loyola University Chicago project on the genetics of hypertension in people of West African origin, whose genome-wide association sample consists of unrelated Yoruba-speaking adults with normal or raised blood pressure from Igbo-Ora, a rural town, and Idikan, a low-income neighbourhood of Ibadan, in southwest Nigeria, recruited as part of a long-term study of the environmental and genetic factors underlying hypertension; the Idikan participants were controls of the Africa America Diabetes Mellitus study.

label: Nanjing Medical University Global Screening Array project
acronyms: NJMU GSA|NJMU GSA Project|NJMU GSA project
other synonyms: NJMU Global Screening Array project|Nanjing Medical University Global Screening Array Project
definition: A case-control sample of Chinese patients with histologically confirmed incident non-small cell lung cancer, untreated by chemotherapy or radiotherapy before diagnosis, and cancer-free controls from community screening for non-communicable diseases, frequency-matched on age, sex and region, genotyped on the Illumina Global Screening Array by Nanjing Medical University, China; it combines three regional case-control studies, from Nanjing and Shanghai, from Beijing and Tianjin, and from Guangdong.
diseases: patients with: non-small cell lung carcinoma (MONDO:0005233)

label: Parkinson's Disease Cognitive Genetics Consortium
other synonyms: PD Cognitive Genetics Consortium
definition: A consortium of academic Parkinson's disease research centres in the United States, several of them Morris K. Udall Centers of Excellence for Parkinson's Disease Research, that pools patients with Parkinson's disease enrolled in the centres' studies, each given a detailed neurological evaluation and a shared core battery of cognitive tests, with a coordinating centre at the University of Washington and VA Puget Sound Health Care System in Seattle, to identify genetic risk factors for cognitive impairment in Parkinson's disease.

label: Poland Ovarian Cancer Study
other synonyms: Polish Ovarian Cancer Study
definition: A case-control study of ovarian cancer in Poland, with participants from Szczecin, Poznań, Opole and Rzeszów, that is one of the studies of the Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium.

label: Screening Across the Lifespan Twin survey, Younger cohort
other synonyms: Screening Across the Lifespan Twin study in Younger adults
definition: A study of the younger part of the Screening Across the Lifespan Twin study (SALT) cohort of the Swedish Twin Registry, twins born 1943–1958, who in 2008–2010 were sent an extensive self-report questionnaire, a request for saliva for DNA and an invitation to a web-based investigation, carried out by the registry with researchers in epidemiology, medicine, political science and economics.

label: Severe Asthma Research Program
other synonyms: NHLBI Severe Asthma Research Program|Severe Asthma Network
definition: A research programme of the US National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, established in 2001 (also called the Severe Asthma Network), in which a network of investigators at academic health centres in the United States recruits adults and children with severe and non-severe asthma for detailed phenotypic characterization, in the SARP I and II cohorts (2001–2012) and the longitudinal SARP III cohort (from 2012), to study the mechanisms that distinguish severe from non-severe asthma; the genomes of some of its participants were sequenced in NHLBI's Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine programme.

label: Sickle Cell Clinical Research and Intervention Program
definition: A lifespan cohort study of people with sickle cell disease in the United States, established in 2014 by St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, that prospectively enrols patients at St. Jude (the coordinating site), two other sickle cell centres and St. Jude affiliate sites, collects retrospective and longitudinal clinical, neurocognitive, geospatial, psychosocial and health-outcome data and banks biological samples, to study disease progression from childhood into adulthood and the long-term effects of therapies.

label: Asian Indian Diabetic Heart Study/Sikh Diabetes Study
other synonyms: Asian Indian Diabetes Heart Study/Sikh Diabetes Study|Asian Indian Diabetic Heart Study|Asian Indian diabetic heart study|Khatri Sikh Diabetes Study|Sikh Diabetes Study
definition: A genetic epidemiological study of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease in Punjabi-speaking Sikhs of North Indian origin, begun as a family-based study of Khatri Sikh families with at least two siblings affected by type 2 diabetes and extended as a case-control study, with participants recruited in northern India from 2003, to investigate genetic and environmental risk factors for type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.
diseases: patients with: cardiovascular disorder (MONDO:0004995)|patients with: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: Sickle Cell Genome Project
definition: A cohort of individuals with sickle cell disease recruited from Baylor College of Medicine and from the Sickle Cell Clinical Research and Intervention Program (SCCRIP) cohort at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, whose whole genomes were sequenced to define genotype-phenotype relations in sickle cell disease.

label: St George's stroke cohort
other synonyms: St George's Stroke Study, London, UK
definition: A hospital-based collection of patients with ischaemic stroke, including some with transient ischaemic attack and recent brain infarction, recruited at St George's in London, United Kingdom, from 1995 to 2008, genotyped in the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium 2 ischaemic stroke study and one of the genetic research centres of the NINDS Stroke Genetics Network.

label: Sisters in Breast Screening Study
other synonyms: Sisters in Breast Screening|Sisters in Breast Screening study
definition: A family study in the United Kingdom that from October 2002 recruited women attending the Cambridge and Huntingdon NHS breast screening services who had one or more female blood relatives (sisters, half-sisters, first cousins, aunts or nieces) who had also had screening mammograms, with further families found through newspaper and radio advertisements, to map genes underlying quantitative phenotypes related to breast cancer, in particular mammographic breast density and sex steroid hormone levels.

label: St. Jude Lifetime Cohort Study
other synonyms: St Jude Lifetime Cohort Study|St. Jude Lifetime Cohort|St. Jude Lifetime Cohort study
definition: A retrospective cohort with prospective follow-up, established in 2007 by St. Jude Children's Research Hospital in Memphis, Tennessee, of survivors of paediatric cancer diagnosed and treated there between 1962 and 2012 who have survived at least five years from diagnosis (until 2015, only adults who had survived ten years), with frequency-matched community controls, who are invited back to the hospital at least every five years for protocol-based medical assessments, patient-reported outcomes and biospecimen collection, to study late health outcomes of childhood cancer and its treatment.

label: Swedish Low-risk Colorectal Cancer Study
other synonyms: Colorectal Cancer Low-risk study|Colorectal cancer low-risk study|Swedish Colorectal Cancer Low-risk study|Swedish Low-Risk Colorectal Cancer Study Group
definition: A multicentre study in central Sweden of consecutive patients newly diagnosed with colorectal cancer of any stage, recruited between 2004 and 2009 at 14 hospitals by the Swedish Low-Risk Colorectal Cancer Study Group and interviewed on their family history of cancer, with a lifestyle questionnaire for those recruited in 2004–2006 and cancer-free spouses of participants serving as controls; its cases and controls are used in genetic studies of colorectal cancer risk.

label: Screening Markers for Colorectal Cancer Study
other synonyms: Screening Markers for Colorectal Cancer Study (advanced adenomas)
definition: A two-phase case-control study of colorectal polyps among enrollees of Group Health Cooperative (now Kaiser Permanente Washington), an integrated health-care delivery system in western Washington State, United States, aged 24–79 years who had an index colonoscopy for any indication in 1998–2003 or 2004–2007, comprising patients diagnosed with adenomas or serrated polyps and polyp-free controls who gave buccal-cell or blood samples and completed a structured questionnaire; its advanced-adenoma cases and matched polyp-free controls were genotyped for consortium genome-wide studies of colorectal cancer.
diseases: at risk of: colorectal cancer (MONDO:0005575)|at risk of: polyp of large intestine (MONDO:0021392)

label: Siblings With Ischemic Stroke Study
other synonyms: Sibling with Ischemic Stroke Study|Siblings with Ischemic Stroke Study
definition: A family-based study of ischaemic stroke that from 1999 to 2011 enrolled, at clinical centres in the United States and Canada, adult probands with radiographically confirmed ischaemic stroke who had at least one living full sibling with stroke, together with their stroke-affected siblings, confirmed by central review of medical records, and where possible a stroke-free sibling, confirmed by structured telephone interview, all contacted through the proband, to search the genome for genetic risk factors for ischaemic stroke by linkage and family-based association analysis.

label: Saguenay Youth Study
definition: A two-generation, family-based study in the Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean region of Quebec, Canada, a genetic founder population, of adolescent sibships aged 12–18 of French-Canadian origin recruited through high schools in 2003–2012, half of them exposed prenatally to maternal cigarette smoking and matched with non-exposed adolescents for maternal education and school, and of their parents (partly assessed in 2003–2012 and fully in 2012–2015), with extensive phenotyping including brain and abdominal MRI, cardiometabolic assessments and genome-wide genotyping, to investigate the aetiology, early stages and trans-generational trajectories of common cardiometabolic and brain diseases.
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to cigarette smoking via maternal (ECTO:0300003)

label: ThyroidOmics Consortium
other synonyms: The ThyroidOmics Consortium
definition: An international consortium of large, well-phenotyped cohort studies, mostly population-based, formed to study the determinants and effects of thyroid diseases and thyroid function with genomic, epigenomic, transcriptomic, proteomic and metabolomic data, which meta-analyses genome-wide association data from its member cohorts on thyroid-stimulating hormone, free thyroxine, triiodothyronine, thyroid dysfunction and related traits and makes the summary statistics available.
diseases: population study of: thyroid gland disorder (MONDO:0003240)

label: Treatment Options for Type 2 Diabetes in Adolescents and Youth
other synonyms: Treatment Options for type 2 Diabetes in Adolescents and Youth
definition: A multicentre randomized clinical trial funded by the US National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases that from 2004 to 2009 enrolled children and adolescents aged 10–17 years with type 2 diabetes of less than two years' duration, a body-mass index at or above the 85th percentile and no diabetes autoantibodies at 15 clinical centres in the United States, and compared metformin alone with metformin plus rosiglitazone or plus an intensive lifestyle intervention for durable glycaemic control until 2011; its participants were then followed into adulthood in the observational TODAY2 study (2011–2020).

label: Tracking Parkinson's
other synonyms: Parkinson's repository of biosamples and networked datasets|Tracking Parkinson's Disease
definition: A prospective, multicentre, longitudinal epidemiological and biomarker study of Parkinson's disease in the United Kingdom, funded by Parkinson's UK, that recruited patients aged 18–90 with a clinical diagnosis of Parkinson's disease of recent onset (diagnosed within the preceding 3.5 years) or young onset (diagnosed at or before age 50) at 72 National Health Service secondary-care sites, together with unaffected siblings of patients, and follows them with repeated motor, non-motor and quality-of-life assessments, genotyping and biosamples, to explain variation in the clinical phenotype of Parkinson's disease, including its relation to genetic variation.

label: Universitatsklinikum Saarlandes case-control dataset
other synonyms: UKS cohort|Universitatsklinikum Saarlandes
definition: A case-control cohort from Universitatsklinikum Saarlandes, Germany, consisting of individuals clinically diagnosed with sporadic Alzheimer's disease together with cognitively healthy, age-, gender- and ethnicity-matched population-based controls.

label: Viborg Vascular
other synonyms: VIVA screening trial|Viborg Vascular screening trial
definition: A randomised controlled screening trial of Viborg Hospital in which the men aged 65-74 living in the Central Denmark Region were randomised, from October 2008, either to an invitation to combined screening for abdominal aortic aneurysm, peripheral arterial disease and hypertension, with preventive treatment for those found to have disease, or to no invitation, to assess the effect of screening on all-cause mortality and its cost-effectiveness.
diseases: population study of: abdominal aortic aneurysm (MONDO:0005350)|population study of: hypertensive disorder (MONDO:0005044)|population study of: peripheral arterial disease (MONDO:0005386)

label: West Bank Cancer Registry
definition: The cancer registry of the West Bank, kept by the Palestinian Ministry of Health, which records incident cancer cases among West Bank residents; it continues the West Bank part of the population-based Palestinian Cancer Registry, established in 1996 and working regularly from 1998, which was split into separate West Bank and Gaza registries in 2007.

label: Washington University St. Louis Stroke Study
other synonyms: Washington University St. Louis Study
definition: A hospital-based collection of ischaemic stroke patients admitted from August 2008 to Barnes-Jewish Hospital/Washington University Medical Center in St. Louis, Missouri, identified by screening emergency department and inpatient stroke service admissions regardless of age, race or ethnicity and followed up at 90 days, whose DNA came from an acute tPA pharmacogenomics study, the Recovery Genomics after Ischemic Stroke (ReGenesIS) study and the Cognitive Rehabilitation and Recovery Group (CRRG) stroke registry; one of the genetic research centres of the NINDS Stroke Genetics Network.

label: Sea Islands Genetics Network – Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke
other synonyms: Sea Islands Genetic Network – Reasons for Geographic And Racial Differences in Stroke
definition: The subset of the African American participants of the REGARDS cohort that the Sea Islands Genetics Network (SIGNET) project genotyped on the Affymetrix 6.0 array: all African American REGARDS participants with type 2 diabetes recruited in South Carolina, Georgia, North Carolina and Alabama, an equal number of diabetes-free controls matched by sex and age strata, and all other participants living in the 15-county Low Country region of South Carolina and Georgia.

label: Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium 2 Parkinson's disease study
other synonyms: Genome-wide association scan in Parkinson's disease
definition: The Parkinson's disease genome-wide case-control study of the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium 2 and the UK Parkinson's Disease Consortium: UK patients with idiopathic Parkinson's disease meeting UK Brain Bank criteria, randomly selected from population- and hospital-based clinics through five UK centres and genotyped at the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute, compared with the WTCCC2 controls from the 1958 British Birth Cohort and the UK Blood Services.

label: CALGB 80303
definition: A double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised phase III trial of the Cancer and Leukemia Group B that enrolled patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic cancer at its participating institutions in the United States between June 2004 and April 2006, comparing gemcitabine plus bevacizumab with gemcitabine plus placebo, with overall survival as the primary end point.

label: CALGB 90401
definition: A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III trial designed by the Cancer and Leukemia Group B and endorsed by the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group that enrolled men with chemotherapy-naive progressive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer at participating institutions in the United States between May 2005 and December 2007, comparing docetaxel and prednisone with or without bevacizumab, with overall survival as the primary end point.

label: Colonomics
other synonyms: COLONOMICS
definition: A multi-omics colon cancer study run by the Catalan Institute of Oncology of patients with microsatellite-stable stage II colon adenocarcinoma who had radical surgery without adjuvant therapy at Bellvitge University Hospital (Barcelona, Spain) in 1996-2000 and were selected in 2012; their tumour and paired adjacent normal mucosa, with colon mucosa from healthy donors undergoing colonoscopy as reference, were profiled for gene expression, DNA methylation, SNPs, copy number and miRNAs to find diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers of colorectal cancer.

label: CALGB 40503
definition: A randomised, multicentre trial of the Cancer and Leukemia Group B (now the Alliance for Clinical Trials in Oncology), begun in the United States in 2008, of first-line endocrine therapy alone or with bevacizumab for women with hormone receptor-positive advanced-stage breast cancer who were postmenopausal or receiving ovarian suppression: a phase III comparison with letrozole, run in parallel with a phase II comparison with tamoxifen.

label: 23Mofang cohort
other synonyms: 23Mofang Inc. cohort|23mofang Personal Genome Services
definition: A research cohort of customers of 23Mofang (Chengdu 23Mofang Biotechnology Co., Ltd.), a Chinese direct-to-consumer genetic testing company, who were genotyped through its personal genome service and consented to the research use of their genotypes and of traits they self-reported in the company's web-based surveys.

label: 3D Facial Norms cohort
other synonyms: 3D Facial Norms|3D Facial Norms Database|3D Facial Norms Dataset|3D Facial Norms Project|3D Facial Norms dataset|Pittsburgh 3D Facial Norms|Pittsburgh 3D Facial Norms study|Pittsburgh 3DFN cohort
definition: A normative craniofacial study begun in 2009 as part of the FaceBase Consortium of the US National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research, which recruited healthy people aged 3 to 40 of self-reported European ancestry and without craniofacial conditions at four US sites (Pittsburgh, Seattle, Houston and Iowa City), collecting 3D facial surface images, anthropometric measurements, a demographic questionnaire and saliva DNA for genome-wide genotyping, and shares the data through a web-based repository.

label: 4D-SZ cohort
other synonyms: 4D-SZ study
definition: A multi-omics cohort of adult Chinese volunteers in Shenzhen, China, run by BGI-Shenzhen and recruited largely at annual physical examinations from 2017 (some gave samples from 2015), with sampling repeated over time. It combines whole-genome sequencing, metagenomes of the gut, mouth and other body sites, plasma metabolites, medical tests and questionnaires on diet and lifestyle, to study how host genetics and environment shape the microbiome and health.

label: Age-Related Eye Disease Study
definition: A multicentre prospective study sponsored by the US National Eye Institute that recruited people aged 55 to 80, with or without age-related macular degeneration or lens opacities, at 11 retinal specialty clinics in the United States from 1992 to 1998 and followed them to 2005. It studied the clinical course and risk factors of age-related macular degeneration and cataract, and included randomised, placebo-controlled trials of high-dose antioxidant vitamins and zinc for these conditions.
diseases: patients with: age-related macular degeneration (MONDO:0005150)|patients with: senile cataract (MONDO:0004847)

label: Age-Related Eye Disease Study 2
definition: A multicentre, randomised, double-masked, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial sponsored by the US National Eye Institute and run from 2006 to 2012 at 82 clinical centres in the United States. It enrolled people aged 50 to 85 at risk of progressing to advanced age-related macular degeneration to test whether adding lutein plus zeaxanthin or omega-3 fatty acids to the AREDS supplement formulation, or removing beta carotene or lowering zinc, changes that risk.

label: African Research on Kidney Disease
other synonyms: African Research Kidney Disease study|African Research into Kidney Diseases|African Research on Kidney Disease Study
definition: A study of kidney function in adults with and without chronic kidney disease in sub-Saharan Africa, run by the African Research on Kidney Disease collaboration within existing population cohorts in Malawi (Karonga and Lilongwe), South Africa (the Agincourt health and demographic surveillance site) and Uganda (the General Population Cohort). It measured glomerular filtration rate by iohexol plasma clearance to test equations for estimating it, with serial biobanking, cross-sectionally in Malawi and Uganda and longitudinally in South Africa.
diseases: population study of: chronic kidney disease (MONDO:0005300)

label: Berkeley Aging Cohort Study
other synonyms: Berkeley Aging Cohort|Berkeley Aging Cohort study|Berkeley aging cohort study
definition: A longitudinal study of typical cognitive aging at the University of California, Berkeley, and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. It recruits cognitively normal older adults (and some young adults) living in the community in the San Francisco Bay Area through advertisements and word of mouth, and follows them with repeated neuropsychological testing, MRI, and PET imaging of amyloid and tau, to study brain changes in normal aging and early Alzheimer's disease pathology.

label: Diabetes UK Warren 1 Repository
other synonyms: BDA Warren I|British Diabetes Association|British Diabetes Association Warren 1|British Diabetes Association Warren I|British Diabetic Association Warren Repository|British Diabetic Association–Warren repository|Diabetes UK Warren 1 repository|Diabetes UK Warren I repository
definition: A repository of DNA samples from British families of European ancestry with at least two siblings affected by type 1 diabetes, and their parents, recruited in the United Kingdom between 1989 and 1996 for the British Diabetic Association (now Diabetes UK) and made publicly available for genetic linkage and association studies of type 1 diabetes.

label: Brain Development and Air Pollution Ultrafine Particles in School Children
other synonyms: BREATHE project|BREATHE study|BRain dEvelopment and Air polluTion ultrafine particles in scHool childrEn|Brain dEvelopment and Air polluTion ultrafine particles in scHool childrEn
definition: A prospective cohort of children aged 7–10 years in grades 2 to 4 at 39 primary schools in Barcelona, Spain, selected as pairs with high and low traffic-related air pollution, whose working memory and attention were tested four times, every three months, from January 2012 to March 2013, with brain MRI in a subsample, to study the effects of traffic-related air pollution on cognitive and brain development.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to air pollution (ECTO:8000036)|designed to study: exposure to nitrogen dioxide (ECTO:9000252)|designed to study: exposure to particulate matter (ECTO:7000068)|designed to study: exposure to ultrafine respirable suspended particulate matter (ECTO:7000118)

label: National Cancer Institute Breast and Prostate Cancer Cohort Consortium
other synonyms: Breast and Prostate Cancer Cohort Consortium|NCI Breast and Prostate Cancer Cohort Consortium|The National Cancer Institute Breast and Prostate Cancer Cohort Consortium
definition: A consortium of large prospective cohorts in the United States, Europe and Australia, among them ATBC, CPS-II, EPIC, HPFS, the Multiethnic Cohort, NHS, PHS, PLCO and WHS, which pools nested case–control studies of breast and prostate cancer with DNA and prospectively collected questionnaire data, first to relate variation in genes of the steroid-hormone metabolism and insulin-like growth factor pathways to cancer risk, and later for genome-wide association studies of aggressive prostate cancer and oestrogen receptor-negative breast cancer.
diseases: patients with: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|patients with: prostate cancer (MONDO:0008315)

label: Biomarkers and Stratification To Optimise outcomes in Psoriasis
other synonyms: Biomarkers of Systemic Treatment Outcomes in Psoriasis|Biomarkers of Systemic Treatment Outcomes in Psoriasis study|UK Biomarkers of Systemic Treatment Outcomes in Psoriasis study
definition: An ongoing prospective observational study and biobank of people aged 16 or over with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis starting systemic or biologic therapy, established in 2011 at the St John's Institute of Dermatology, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, and recruiting at more than 80 dermatology centres across the United Kingdom. It pairs DNA from every participant, and further blood and skin samples from some, with clinical data, captured partly through the British Association of Dermatologists Biologics and Immunomodulators Register, to identify biomarkers of response to psoriasis treatments.

label: Black Women's Health Study
other synonyms: Black Womens Health Study
definition: A prospective cohort of Black women in the United States, run by the Slone Epidemiology Center at Boston University, who enrolled in 1995 by returning health questionnaires mailed to subscribers of Essence magazine, members of the Black Nurses' Association, participants in its feasibility studies, and friends and relatives of respondents. The women are followed by repeated mailed questionnaires, with medical record and cancer registry review, to study the causes of illnesses common in Black women, such as breast cancer, hypertension, diabetes, lupus and uterine fibroids.

label: Coronary Artery Calcification in Type 1 Diabetes Study
other synonyms: Coronary Artery Calcification in T1D|Coronary Artery Calcification in Type 1 Diabetes|The Coronary Artery Calcification in Type 1 Diabetes
definition: A prospective cohort of adults aged 19–56 years without known coronary heart disease, with long-standing type 1 diabetes or without diabetes (controls, mostly spouses, friends and neighbours of those with diabetes), examined from March 2000 to April 2002 at the Barbara Davis Center for Childhood Diabetes and the University of Colorado in Denver, United States, and re-examined about six years later. Coronary artery calcification was measured by electron-beam computed tomography, to study the prevalence and progression of subclinical coronary atherosclerosis in type 1 diabetes.
diseases: patients with: atherosclerosis (MONDO:0005311)|patients with: type 1 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005147)

label: Collaborative Association Study of Psoriasis
other synonyms: Collaborative Association Study of psoriasis
definition: A case–control collection of people of white European ancestry, with psoriasis diagnosed by dermatologists and controls without psoriasis, that pooled the long-standing psoriasis genetics collections of three United States groups, at the University of Michigan, the University of Utah and Washington University in St. Louis. It was genotyped genome-wide on the Perlegen platform through the Genetic Association Information Network (GAIN) to identify psoriasis susceptibility loci.

label: California and Uganda Prostate Cancer Study
other synonyms: California Uganda Study
definition: A case–control study of prostate cancer in men of African ancestry, genotyped on the Illumina H3Africa array. It combines African American cases from Los Angeles, California, identified through the SEER cancer registry, and cancer-free controls from the African American Eye Disease Study in Inglewood, California, with incident cases and controls from other clinics at Mulago Hospital in Kampala, Uganda.

label: Cryptosporidiosis and Enteropathogens in Bangladesh Birth Cohort
other synonyms: Cryptosporidiosis Birth Cohort|Cryptosporidiosis and Enteropathogens in Bangladesh
definition: A prospective birth cohort of children enrolled within a week of birth between June 2014 and March 2016 in Mirpur, an urban neighbourhood of Dhaka, and Mirzapur, a rural subdistrict north-west of Dhaka, Bangladesh, whose mothers were identified in the second trimester of pregnancy. The children were followed with twice-weekly home visits for diarrhoea, monthly stool samples and three-monthly growth measurements, to study the incidence of cryptosporidiosis, the immune response to it, host genetic susceptibility and its effect on child growth.

label: Childhood Cancer Survivor Study
definition: A multi-institutional retrospective cohort, with longitudinal follow-up, of five-year survivors of the most common childhood cancers diagnosed before age 21 at participating paediatric centres in the United States and Canada, with a comparison cohort of their siblings. It was funded by the US National Cancer Institute in 1994 for survivors diagnosed in 1970-1986 and later expanded to those diagnosed in 1987-1999, as a resource for research on the long-term effects of childhood cancer and its treatment.

label: Collaborative European NeuroTrauma Effectiveness Research in Traumatic Brain Injury
other synonyms: Collaborative European NeuroTrauma Effectiveness Research|Collaborative European NeuroTrauma Effectiveness Research in TBI|Collaborative European Neurotrauma Effectiveness Research in TBI|Collaborative European Neurotrauma Effectiveness Research in Traumatic Brain Injury
definition: A prospective, multicentre, longitudinal observational cohort of patients with traumatic brain injury who presented to hospital within 24 hours of injury with an indication for CT, recruited between December 2014 and December 2017 at centres in 18 countries across Europe and in Israel. Funded by the European Union's Seventh Framework Programme, it comprises a core study, with neuroimaging, biospecimens and outcome assessment, and a broader registry, and aims to improve the characterisation and classification of TBI and to identify best clinical care through comparative effectiveness research.

label: Cystic Fibrosis-Related Diabetes Study
other synonyms: CF-Related Diabetes Study|CF-related Diabetes Study
definition: A Johns Hopkins University study that enrolled people with cystic fibrosis both with and without cystic fibrosis-related diabetes; its participants are among those whose genomes were sequenced by the Cystic Fibrosis Genome Project.
diseases: patients with: cystic fibrosis (MONDO:0009061)|patients with: cystic fibrosis-related diabetes (MONDO:7770003)

label: US Cystic Fibrosis Twin and Sibling Study
other synonyms: CF Twin and Sibling Study|CF Twin-Sibling Study|Cystic Fibrosis Twin and Sibling Study|Cystic Fibrosis Twin-Sibling Study|U.S. CF Twin and Sibling Study
definition: A family-based cohort of living twins, triplets and siblings who all have cystic fibrosis, and their parents, recruited from 2000 by Johns Hopkins University through CF care centres mostly in the United States and also in Australia, Israel and Scotland, to assess genetic and environmental modifiers of clinical outcomes in CF.

label: Chicago Health and Aging Project
definition: A population-based longitudinal cohort of Black and White adults aged 65 and over living in four adjacent neighbourhoods on the south side of Chicago, Illinois, recruited through a door-to-door census from 1993, with later age groups entered as residents turned 65. Participants were followed until 2012 with in-home interviews every three years and clinical evaluation of stratified random samples, to study common chronic conditions of late life, especially risk factors for Alzheimer's disease.

label: Christchurch Health and Development Study
definition: A population-based longitudinal birth cohort of the children born in the Christchurch urban region of New Zealand during a four-month period from April to August 1977, studied by the University of Otago, Christchurch, at birth, 4 months, 1 year, annually to age 16 and at intervals into adulthood (to age 40), on their health, development, social circumstances and wellbeing across the life course.

label: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke Exploratory Trials in Parkinson's Disease Long-Term Study-1
other synonyms: Long-term Study 1|Long-term Study-1|NET-PD Long term Study-1|NINDS Exploratory Trials in PD Long-Term Study 1|NINDS Exploratory Trials in PD Long-term Study-1|National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke Exploratory Trials in Parkinson Disease Long-Term Study-1|Neuroprotection Exploratory Trials in Parkinson's disease
definition: A randomised, multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III trial population of adults with early, treated Parkinson's disease (within five years of diagnosis and receiving dopaminergic therapy). Participants were enrolled at 45 sites in the United States and Canada from March 2007 to May 2010 by the NINDS Exploratory Trials in Parkinson's Disease (NET-PD) network, to test whether creatine slows long-term clinical decline, and were followed until September 2013. DNA from the participants who consented to banking is held in the Coriell Institute for Medical Research biorepository.

label: Dunedin Multidisciplinary Health and Development Study
other synonyms: Dunedin Longitudinal Study|Dunedin Multidisciplinary Child Development Study|Dunedin Study
definition: A longitudinal study of the health and behaviour of a complete birth cohort: children born at Queen Mary Maternity Hospital, Dunedin, New Zealand, between April 1972 and March 1973 and still living in the greater Dunedin area at age 3. They were assessed in day-long multidisciplinary phases from age 3 through childhood and adolescence into midlife, by the Dunedin Multidisciplinary Health and Development Research Unit of the University of Otago.

label: European Community Respiratory Health Survey
definition: A multicentre, population-based cohort of adults aged 20 to 44 years who were selected at random from population registers in 1990-1994 in centres mainly in Western Europe, and also in Australia, New Zealand, the United States and elsewhere, and surveyed with a standardised protocol (a screening questionnaire, then a clinical examination of a random subsample and of those reporting asthma symptoms) to compare the prevalence of asthma and allergic disease, their risk factors and their treatment across countries. Those examined were followed up in ECRHS II (1998-2002), ECRHS III (2008-2014) and ECRHS IV (from 2021) to study the incidence and prognosis of asthma and allergy, lung function decline and COPD.
diseases: population study of: allergic disease (MONDO:0005271)|population study of: asthma (MONDO:0004979)|population study of: chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (MONDO:0005002)

label: EDRN Colorectal and Pancreatic Neoplasm Virtual Biorepository
other synonyms: Colorectal and Pancreatic Neoplasm Virtual Biorepository|Early Detection Research Network Colorectal and Pancreatic Neoplasm Virtual Biorepository
definition: A University of Pittsburgh biorepository, funded by the National Cancer Institute in 2001 as an Early Detection Research Network resource, of clinically annotated biospecimens and data from adults with, or suspected of having, digestive diseases who were managed in University of Pittsburgh Medical Center hospitals for colorectal cancer screening or for gastrointestinal malignancies, premalignant conditions, inflammatory bowel disease, pancreatic diseases or pancreatic and colorectal cancers. Patients followed from 1990 to 2000 were gathered retrospectively and new patients have been enrolled prospectively since 2001 and followed continuously, to support translational research.
diseases: patients with: colorectal cancer (MONDO:0005575)|patients with: digestive system cancer (MONDO:0002516)|patients with: inflammatory bowel disease (MONDO:0005265)|patients with: malignant pancreatic neoplasm (MONDO:0009831)|patients with: pancreas disorder (MONDO:0002356)|patients with: precancerous condition (MONDO:0021074)

label: Echinococcus Multilocularis and Internal Diseases in Leutkirch
other synonyms: EMIL study|EMIL-Cohort|EMIL-Study|Echinococcus multilocularis in Leutkirch study|Ulm-EMIL
definition: A population-based study of the residents of the town of Leutkirch in Baden-Württemberg, south-western Germany, designed by the State Health Department of Baden-Württemberg and the University of Ulm, for which inhabitants aged 10 to 65 years were selected at random from the municipal population register and examined in November and December 2002 (EMIL-I) with a questionnaire, anthropometry, abdominal ultrasound and blood sampling. Its original aim, the prevalence of infection with the fox tapeworm Echinococcus multilocularis, was extended to internal diseases and public health, and a subsample was re-examined in 2013 (EMIL-II).

label: Early Pseudomonas Infection Control Observational Study
other synonyms: EPIC Observational Study|EPIC observational cohort|Early Pseudomonas Infection Control Observational study
definition: A prospective, multicentre observational cohort of children with cystic fibrosis aged 12 years or younger who were free of Pseudomonas aeruginosa at enrolment (no earlier positive respiratory culture, or at least two years of negative cultures) or were taking part in the companion Early Pseudomonas Infection Control clinical trial, enrolled in 2004-2006 at 59 cystic fibrosis care centres in the United States and led from the University of Washington and Seattle Children's Hospital. Participants were followed through encounter-based data collection built on the Cystic Fibrosis Foundation Patient Registry, annual family surveys, respiratory cultures and banked serum, bacterial isolates and DNA, to identify risk factors for early acquisition of P. aeruginosa and to describe its clinical consequences.
diseases: patients with: Pseudomonas aeruginosa infectious disease (MONDO:0040732)|patients with: cystic fibrosis (MONDO:0009061)

label: Environmental Risk Longitudinal Twin Study
other synonyms: E-Risk Study|Environmental Risk (E-Risk) Longitudinal Twin Study
definition: A nationally representative birth cohort of same-sex twins born in England and Wales in 1994-1995, drawn from a birth register of twins and recruited to represent UK families with newborns in the 1990s (ensuring enough children in disadvantaged homes and avoiding an excess of twins born to well-educated women after assisted reproduction). Proposed in 1997, funded by the Medical Research Council from 1998 and based at King's College London, it assessed the families at home when the twins were 5 (1999-2000), 7, 10, 12 and 18 years old, surveyed them online in their mid-twenties and planned a further assessment at age 30 for 2024-2025, to study how environmental and genetic factors contribute to behaviour, health and mental health problems from childhood into adulthood.

label: Gabapentin for chronic pelvic pain in women
other synonyms: GaPP2 trial
definition: The participants of a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial at 39 UK hospital centres, funded by the Medical Research Council and National Institute for Health Research Efficacy and Mechanism Evaluation programme, in which women aged 18-50 years with chronic pelvic pain of at least three months and no obvious pelvic pathology at laparoscopy, screened between November 2015 and March 2019, were randomly assigned to gabapentin or matching placebo for 16 weeks to measure the efficacy and safety of gabapentin. Participants could give a saliva sample for genetic study at trial entry.

label: Interdisciplinary Group for Advanced Research on BirtH outcomes - DBT India Initiative
other synonyms: GARBH-Ini cohort|GARBH-Ini pregnancy cohort|Interdisciplinary Group for Advanced Research on Birth Outcomes - DBT India Initiative|interdisciplinary Group for Advanced Research on BirtH outcomes - DBT India Initiative
definition: A single-centre prospective pregnancy cohort at Gurugram Civil Hospital, a secondary-care hospital in Gurugram district, Haryana, north India, that from May 2015 enrolled pregnant women before 20 weeks' gestation (dated by ultrasound) and followed them through pregnancy to delivery and once within six months after delivery, building repositories of clinical data, biospecimens and ultrasound images. Coordinated by the Translational Health Science and Technology Institute and funded by India's Department of Biotechnology, it aims to identify clinical, epidemiological, genomic, epigenomic, proteomic and microbial correlates of preterm birth and to develop risk-prediction tools for it.

label: Global Biobank Meta-analysis Initiative
definition: A collaborative network of biobanks and genomics initiatives, formed in 2019 by 23 biobanks from four continents (North America, Europe, East and West Asia, and Australia) and since joined by others, whose participants have genotypes linked to electronic health records or other health data. Member biobanks run genome-wide association studies with harmonised phenotype definitions and methods, stratified by ancestry and sex, and GBMI meta-analyses the summary statistics across biobanks and ancestries, beginning with 14 diseases and endpoints, and releases them publicly, to increase the power and ancestral diversity of genetic studies of human disease.

label: Treatment program of DLBCL patients from the Groupe d'Etude des Lymphomes de l'Adulte
other synonyms: Treatment program of DLBCL patients from the Groupe dEtude des Lymphomes de lAdulte
definition: Patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) enrolled in the LNH03 (LNH 2003) programme of treatment trials of the Groupe d'Etude des Lymphomes de l'Adulte (GELA, later the Lymphoma Study Association, LYSA), who consented to DNA analysis. The programme's trials, opened from December 2003 at centres mainly in France and Belgium for patients of different ages and prognostic risk, were the randomised trials LNH03-1B, LNH03-2B and LNH03-6B, the phase 2 trial LNH03-3B, LNH03-39B and a phase 2 trial of R-miniCHOP in patients over 80. The patients' germline DNA was genotyped as the case series of GELA's genome-wide association study of DLBCL, with controls drawn from the French component of EPIC.
diseases: patients with: diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (MONDO:0018905)

label: Genetic and Environmental Risk Factors for Alzheimer's Disease Among African Americans Study
other synonyms: GenerAAtions Study|Genetic and Environmental Risk Factors for Alzheimer Disease Among African Americans Study|Genetic and Environmental Risk Factors for Alzheimer's Disease Among African Americans
definition: A case-control study of Alzheimer's disease in community-dwelling African Americans aged 65 or older, led from Johns Hopkins University, whose participants were identified through the electronic claims database of the Henry Ford Health System in Detroit, Michigan, and had a proxy informant; cases met NINCDS-ADRDA criteria for possible or probable Alzheimer's disease at a consensus conference, and controls were cognitively normal.

label: Gene Environment Interaction and Breast Cancer in Germany
other synonyms: Gene Environment Interactions and Breast Cancer study|Gene-ENvironment Interaction and breast CAncer|gene environment interaction and breast cancer
definition: A population-based case-control study of breast cancer in women of the Greater Bonn region, Germany, run by the GENICA network of German research institutions, in which incident cases, enrolled from all hospitals of the region in 2000–2004 within six months of diagnosis, and controls drawn from the population registries of 31 communities of the region and matched in five-year age classes were interviewed and gave blood, to study how genes and environmental exposures interact in breast cancer.
exposures: designed to study: exposure event (ExO:0000002)|designed to study: exposure to occupation (ECTO:0001591)

label: Genizon GWAS
other synonyms: Genizon BioSciences
definition: A case-control sample of people with psoriasis, ascertained through dermatologists or other secondary-care specialists, and controls, all drawn from the Québec founder population (people whose four grandparents had French-Canadian family names and were born in Québec or neighbouring areas), assembled by Genizon BioSciences of Saint-Laurent, Québec, and genotyped genome-wide on the Illumina Human 1M BeadChip; it is one of the European-ancestry GWAS datasets of the international psoriasis genetics meta-analyses.

label: GEnetic analysis of NUclear Families with Atopic Dermatitis
other synonyms: GENUFAD study|GEnetic studies in NUclear Families with Atopic Dermatitis|Genetic Analysis of Nuclear Families with Atopic Dermatitis|Genetic Studies in Nuclear Families with Atopic Dermatitis
definition: A family-based genetic study of atopic dermatitis run from Charité Universitätsmedizin Berlin, which recruited complete nuclear families, mostly German and a few Swedish, through at least two children with physician-diagnosed, moderate to severe atopic dermatitis that began before the age of two, and in its extended phase also unrelated children with such early-onset disease, recording asthma and hay fever at recruitment, for genetic studies of atopic dermatitis and allergic disease.

label: German Myocardial Infarction Family Study
other synonyms: German MI Family Studies|German MI Family Study|German Myocardial Infarction Family Studies
definition: A series of German case collections for genetic studies of myocardial infarction and coronary artery disease, numbered GerMIFS I to VII, that began as a family study recruiting, from all parts of Germany, people with myocardial infarction before the age of 60 and relatives with premature coronary artery disease. Later collections added patients with early-onset myocardial infarction, non-fatal myocardial infarction cases from the KORA registry of the Augsburg region, and patients with coronary artery disease or myocardial infarction referred for coronary angiography, mostly compared with population controls from other German studies.
diseases: patients with: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)|patients with: myocardial infarction (MONDO:0005068)

label: Gene-Lifestyle Interactions and Complex Traits Involved in Elevated Disease Risk Study
other synonyms: GLACIER Study|Gene x Lifestyle interactions And Complex traits Involved in Elevated disease Risk Study|Gene-Lifestyle interactions And Complex traits Involved in Elevated disease Risk Study
definition: A prospective population-based cohort of adults from the county of Västerbotten in northern Sweden, nested within the Northern Sweden Health and Disease Study, whose members had baseline health and lifestyle examinations in the Västerbotten Intervention Programme between 1985 and 2004, in the years of their 40th, 50th or 60th birthdays, with a repeat examination about ten years later. It was established in 2008 to study the genetics of cardiometabolic traits and interactions between genes and lifestyle.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to lifestyle (ECTO:6000015)

label: German Multicenter Allergy Study
other synonyms: German Multicentre Allergy Study|German multicentre atopy study|Multicenter Allergy Study|Multicentre Allergy Study
definition: A birth cohort of children born in 1990 and recruited in the maternity wards of university hospitals in five German cities (Berlin, Düsseldorf, Freiburg, Mainz and Munich), enriched for newborns at high risk of allergy, with two allergic immediate family members or raised cord-blood IgE, alongside a random sample of low-risk newborns, and followed with repeated examinations and questionnaires from infancy into adulthood to study the course of asthma, allergic rhinitis, eczema and allergic sensitisation.
diseases: population study of: allergic disease (MONDO:0005271)|population study of: allergic rhinitis (MONDO:0011786)|population study of: asthma (MONDO:0004979)|population study of: atopic eczema (MONDO:0004980)

label: Genetic Modifier Study
other synonyms: GMS Lung Study|Gene Modifier Study|US extremes of phenotype study|University of North Carolina/Case Western Reserve University Case-Control Study
definition: A case-control study of genetic modifiers of cystic fibrosis lung disease, led by the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and Case Western Reserve University, that enrolled unrelated patients homozygous for F508del whose lung function for age was at either extreme (severe or mild disease) from cystic fibrosis centres across the United States, together with a smaller population-based sample from children's hospitals in Denver, Wisconsin and Boston.

label: Genetic Modifier Study of Severe CF Liver Disease
other synonyms: GMS of Severe CF Liver Disease|Genetic Modifier Study of Severe Cystic Fibrosis Liver Disease|Genetic Modifier Study of Severe Liver Disease in Cystic Fibrosis
definition: A two-stage case-control study of genetic modifiers of severe liver disease in cystic fibrosis, coordinated by the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, which from January 1999 enrolled people with cystic fibrosis and cirrhosis with portal hypertension from cystic fibrosis centres in the United States, Canada and other countries of Europe, Australia, South America and the Middle East, and compared them with people with cystic fibrosis aged 15 or over without liver disease, many of them from the Genetic Modifier Study of lung disease.
diseases: patients with: cystic fibrosis (MONDO:0009061)|patients with: cystic fibrosis-related liver disease (MONDO:7770005)

label: GSK
other synonyms: Glaxo Smith Kline|Glaxo-Smith Kline
definition: A pharmacogenetic sample of adult outpatients of white European ancestry with moderate to severe major depressive disorder who completed escitalopram treatment in two identically designed randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled GlaxoSmithKline trials run in the United States in 2003–2004 to compare bupropion XL with escitalopram for antidepressant efficacy and effects on sexual functioning; GlaxoSmithKline contributed their DNA to the NEWMEDS consortium for genetic studies of antidepressant response.

label: GSK Munich recurrent major depression case-control study
other synonyms: GlaxoSmithKline|Southern German Recurrent Depression
definition: A case-control sample for recurrent major depressive disorder, collected with GlaxoSmithKline, of German patients with recurrent moderate or severe major depression recruited at the Max Planck Institute of Psychiatry in Munich and two satellite hospitals in the Munich area (BKH Augsburg and Klinikum Ingolstadt), and age- and sex-matched controls from a Munich community sample screened free of lifetime mood and anxiety disorders, genotyped genome-wide for studies of the genetics of depression.

label: Great Smoky Mountains Study
other synonyms: Great Smoky Mountains Study of Youth
definition: A longitudinal, population-based study of children from 11 predominantly rural counties of western North Carolina, United States, recruited in 1993 as three cohorts aged 9, 11 and 13 through a two-phase design that screened a random sample of children for behavioural problems and oversampled those with high scores, together with all age-eligible American Indian children of the area. The participants were interviewed annually to age 16 and then repeatedly into adulthood, to study the development of psychiatric and substance use disorders and the need for and use of mental health services.

label: Hasselt Appendicitis Immunology and Environmental Study
other synonyms: HAPPIEST cohort|Hasselt APPendicitis Immunologic and Environmental STudy|Hasselt APPendicitis Immunology and Environmental Cohort STudy
definition: A prospective cohort of patients aged 5 to 85 who presented with acute appendicitis at the emergency department of Jessa Hospital in Hasselt, Belgium, and had an appendectomy, recruited from June 2012 to October 2016 in a study led by Hasselt University with Jessa Hospital and Radboud University Medical Center. Questionnaires on diet, lifestyle and environment were collected together with blood, appendix tissue and stool samples, to study how environmental factors, the innate immune system and its genetic make-up, and the gut microbiota influence the development and severity of acute appendicitis.
exposures: designed to study: exposure event (ExO:0000002)|designed to study: exposure to eating behavior (ECTO:6000021)|designed to study: exposure to lifestyle (ECTO:6000015)

label: Hwasun Cancer Epidemiology Study-Breast
definition: The breast cancer arm of the Hwasun Cancer Epidemiology Study, a hospital-based case-control study at Chonnam National University Hwasun Hospital, a cancer hospital in Jeollanam-do province, South Korea, that aims to identify factors in cancer development and clinical progression in a Korean population. Its cases are women newly diagnosed with breast cancer at the hospital from April 2004 to February 2013, excluding secondary or recurrent tumours, and its controls are women with no previous cancer drawn at random from the Namwon Study and the Dong-gu Study, community-based cohorts in South Korea.

label: Health2008 Study
other synonyms: Health 2008 study|Health2008 cohort
definition: A cross-sectional population-based study of the Research Centre for Prevention and Health in Glostrup, Denmark, conducted in 2008–2009 on a random sample of men and women aged 30–60, drawn from the Danish Central Personal Register, living in the western part of the Copenhagen area; pregnant women and people with known diabetes, cardiovascular disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, hypertension or a history of blood clots, or unable to do physical activities such as climbing stairs, were excluded. The examination included questionnaires, clinical and biochemical measurements, an oral glucose tolerance test and two tests estimating maximal oxygen uptake.

label: Health2010 Study
other synonyms: Health2010 cohort
definition: A population-based study of the Research Centre for Prevention and Health in Glostrup, Denmark, begun in 2010, which examined a random sample of adults aged 18–69, drawn from the Danish Central Personal Register, living in the western part of the Capital Region of Denmark, with questionnaires, a clinical examination and blood samples, focusing on cardiovascular disease, diabetes, asthma and allergy.

label: Hong Kong Diabetes Register
other synonyms: Hong Kong Diabetes Registry|Prince of Wales Hospital Diabetes Registry
definition: A prospective register of patients with diabetes, with a biobank, established in 1995 by the Chinese University of Hong Kong at its teaching hospital, the Prince of Wales Hospital, as a research-driven quality-improvement programme. Patients referred by hospital specialty clinics, community clinics and general practitioners to the hospital's Diabetes Mellitus and Endocrine Centre were enrolled consecutively for a structured assessment of complications and metabolic control and then followed until death, to study the risk factors, complications and outcomes of diabetes.
diseases: patients with: diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005015)|patients with: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: HostSeq initiative
other synonyms: CGEn HostSeq Initiative|HostSeq Databank|HostSeq project
definition: A pan-Canadian databank set up in 2020 by CGEn, Canada's national platform for genome sequencing and analysis, within Genome Canada's Canadian COVID-19 Genomics Network, that brings together independent clinical and epidemiological studies enrolling people of any age infected with SARS-CoV-2 across Canada. Each partner study contributes blood (rarely saliva) samples for whole-genome sequencing at the CGEn centres and clinical information on a standard case report form, creating a resource for research on host genetic factors in SARS-CoV-2 infection and COVID-19 outcomes.

label: Hvidoere Remission Phase Study
other synonyms: HSG remission phase cohort|Hvidoere Study Group on Childhood Diabetes|Hvidoere Study Group on Childhood Diabetes remission phase cohort
definition: A multinational longitudinal cohort of children and adolescents under 16 with newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes, recruited from August 1999 to December 2000 at 18 paediatric departments in 15 countries of Europe and Japan by the Hvidoere Study Group on Childhood Diabetes, an international group of paediatric diabetes centres, and followed through the first 12 months after diagnosis with meal-stimulated C-peptide tests, HbA1c, insulin doses, islet autoantibodies and HLA typing, to study residual beta-cell function and the partial remission period.

label: Nord-Trøndelag Health Study 1995–97
other synonyms: HUNT2 survey
definition: The second survey of the HUNT Study, conducted in 1995–97, to which all residents of Nord-Trøndelag, Norway, aged 20 or over were invited for questionnaires, interviews, a clinical examination and biological sampling. Its participants have consented to linkage with Norwegian health and administrative registries, and many of them have been genotyped.

label: HypnoLaus Sleep Cohort Study
other synonyms: HypnoLaus Study|HypnoLaus cohort
definition: A population-based sleep cohort nested in the CoLaus/PsyCoLaus study of Lausanne, Switzerland: consecutive participants of CoLaus/PsyCoLaus's first follow-up (2009–12), who also answered sleep questionnaires and had clinical and biological phenotyping, were invited from September 2009 to June 2013 to a full polysomnography at home, organised from the sleep centre of Lausanne University Hospital, to study the prevalence and determinants of sleep disorders such as sleep-disordered breathing and their links with cardiometabolic and mental health. Participants were re-examined at the cohort's second follow-up in 2014–17.
diseases: population study of: Sleep-related breathing disorders (HP:5200283)|population study of: sleep-wake disorder (MONDO:0003406)

label: Interaction of Gene and Environment of Depression during PostPartum
other synonyms: Interaction Between Genetic Factors and Maternal Stressors During Pregnancy in the Risk of Postpartum Depression|Interaction of Gene and Environment of Depression in PostPartum|interaction of gene and environment of depression during postpartum
definition: A French prospective multicentre cohort, sponsored by Assistance Publique – Hôpitaux de Paris, of women of European ancestry aged over 18 who gave birth in eight maternity departments of the Paris metropolitan area and were included two to five days after delivery between November 2011 and June 2016. The women gave a blood sample for DNA and were assessed for depression by trained clinicians with DSM-5 criteria at inclusion, at 8 weeks and at 1 year postpartum, to study how genetic factors and maternal stressors interact in the risk of postpartum depression.

label: Impact of Neurodevelopmental disorders and School performance: genes and environment
other synonyms: INSchool cohort
definition: A school-based cohort of children and adolescents aged 5–17 from primary and secondary general-education schools across Catalonia, Spain, set up to study neurodevelopmental disorders, school performance and their genetic and environmental factors. Since the 2011–2012 school year, parents and teachers complete screening questionnaires for mental health problems and learning difficulties, children who screen positive are assessed by psychiatrists and neuropsychologists for DSM diagnoses, academic marks are taken from school records, and DNA is collected from saliva or buccal swabs.

label: Japanese Consortium for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis research
other synonyms: Japanese Consortium for ALS research|Japanese Consortium for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis|Japanese Consortium for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Research|Japanese consortium for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis research
definition: A multicentre patient registry established in Japan in 2006 to register and follow up patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis across many participating institutions, collecting DNA samples and clinical data with periodic telephone follow-up to study the natural history, genetic background and prognosis of ALS.

label: JAPC GWAS
definition: A nested case-control genome-wide association study of prostate cancer in Japanese American men of the Multiethnic Cohort Study in Hawaii and California. Incident cases found by linkage to the SEER cancer registries, and controls matched on ethnicity, area of residence and age, were genotyped on the Illumina Human660W array at the Broad Institute as the Japanese component of the Multiethnic Genome-wide Scan of Prostate Cancer (GENEVA), to search for prostate cancer risk variants in Japanese men.

label: Japan Prospective Studies Collaboration for Aging and Dementia
definition: A multisite, population-based prospective cohort study of dementia, coordinated from Kyushu University. Community-dwelling residents aged 65 years or older at eight research sites across Japan (Hirosaki, Yahaba, Nakajima, Arakawa, Ama, Nakayama, Hisayama and Arao) were examined in 2016–2018 under a common standardized protocol, including questionnaires, cognitive assessment, blood tests, brain MRI and DNA samples, and are followed up for incident dementia, to study environmental and genetic risk factors for dementia and their interaction.

label: Korean Research Project on the Integrated Exposure Assessment of Hazardous Substances for Food Safety
other synonyms: Korean research project on the integrated exposure assessment of hazardous substances for food safety
definition: A nationwide Korean survey population of all ages, set up in 2010 by the National Institute of Food and Drug Safety Evaluation as the first integrated assessment of dietary exposure to hazardous substances from food, herbal medicine and functional food. Adults were drawn by region-, sex- and age-stratified probability sampling from 102 town and township clusters in 15 metropolitan areas and provinces, and children, adolescents and mothers were recruited through schools, kindergartens, health centres and hospitals. All were surveyed in 2010–2011 with food frequency and 24-hour recall questionnaires, blood and urine biomonitoring, and health examinations.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to cadmium (ECTO:0001566)|designed to study: exposure to environmental food contaminant (ECTO:9002126)|designed to study: exposure to lead (ECTO:9000945)|designed to study: exposure to mercury (ECTO:0001571)

label: LAPC GWAS
definition: A nested case-control genome-wide association study of prostate cancer in Latino men of the Multiethnic Cohort Study in Hawaii and California. Incident cases found by linkage to the SEER cancer registries, and controls matched on ethnicity, area of residence and age, were genotyped on the Illumina Human660W array at the Broad Institute as the Latino component of the Multiethnic Genome-wide Scan of Prostate Cancer (GENEVA), to search for prostate cancer risk variants in Latinos.

label: Levodopa in Early Parkinson's Disease
other synonyms: Levodopa in EArly Parkinson's Disease|Levodopa in EArly Parkinson's disease|Levodopa in Early Parkinson's disease
definition: A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled delayed-start trial of patients aged 30 or over whose Parkinson's disease had been diagnosed within the previous two years and did not yet need medication. They were recruited between August 2011 and May 2016 through academic and community hospitals across the Netherlands, with the Academic Medical Center in Amsterdam as the coordinating centre. Patients received levodopa/carbidopa for 80 weeks, or placebo for 40 weeks followed by levodopa/carbidopa for 40 weeks, with follow-up visits at 3 and 5 years, to test whether starting levodopa early modifies the course of the disease.

label: Luxembourg Parkinson's Study
other synonyms: Luxembourg Parkinson Study|Luxembourg Parkinson's study
definition: A nation-wide, monocentric, observational, longitudinal-prospective cohort of people with Parkinson's disease or atypical parkinsonism at any disease stage, and of control subjects without a neurodegenerative disorder, recruited since 2015 in Luxembourg and the surrounding Greater Region of Germany, France and Belgium within the National Centre of Excellence in Research on Parkinson's Disease (NCER-PD). Patients are followed up annually with deep clinical phenotyping and biosampling, to find markers for early diagnosis and progression.
diseases: patients with: Parkinson disease (MONDO:0005180)|patients with: parkinsonian disorder (MONDO:0021095)

label: Lung Tissue Research Consortium
definition: A biobank cohort set up by the US National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) in 2004 that, from 2005 to 2019, enrolled adults undergoing clinically indicated thoracic surgery (resection of lung nodules or masses, diagnostic biopsy for interstitial lung disease, lung volume reduction surgery or lung transplantation) at Mayo Clinic, Temple University and the Universities of Colorado, Michigan and Pittsburgh, and banked their excess lung tissue and blood together with questionnaire, lung function and chest CT data. Participants with and without lung disease were included, to support research on the pathobiology of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, interstitial lung diseases such as idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, and related lung diseases.
diseases: patients with: chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (MONDO:0005002)|patients with: idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (MONDO:0800504)|patients with: interstitial lung disease (MONDO:0015925)

label: Mammary Carcinoma Risk Factor Investigation
other synonyms: Mammary carcinoma Risk factor Investigation
definition: A population-based case-control study of postmenopausal breast cancer in two regions of Germany, Hamburg and Rhine-Neckar-Karlsruhe, which from 2002 to 2005 enrolled women aged 50–74 with incident invasive or in situ breast cancer and population controls frequency-matched to them, interviewed face to face to investigate risk factors, notably menopausal hormone therapy. Its cases were re-interviewed in 2009 and followed for survival and recurrence until 2015 as the MARIE patient cohort.

label: Mayo Clinic Study of Aging
definition: A prospective population-based cohort of residents of Olmsted County, Minnesota, United States, randomly sampled with age and sex stratification from the population enumerated by the Rochester Epidemiology Project medical records-linkage system: people aged 70–89 from 2004, extended in 2012 to ages 50–69 and later to younger adults. Participants have in-person clinical, neurological and neuropsychological evaluations with a consensus diagnosis of normal cognition, mild cognitive impairment or dementia, repeated about every 15 months together with neuroimaging and biomarkers, to study the prevalence, incidence, risk factors and biomarkers of mild cognitive impairment and dementia.
diseases: population study of: cognitive disorder (MONDO:0002039)|population study of: dementia (MONDO:0001627)

label: MedStar
other synonyms: MedSTAR cardiac catheterization study|Medstar
definition: A hospital-based case-control study designed for biomarker and genetic studies of coronary artery disease, which from August 2004 to March 2007 recruited patients with and without angiographic coronary artery disease undergoing cardiac catheterisation at the Washington Hospital Center, Washington, DC, United States, with support from the MedStar Research Institute.

label: Melanoma in Southern Sweden
other synonyms: Melanoma In Southern Sweden|Melanoma Inquiry in Southern Sweden|Melanoma Inquiry of Southern Sweden
definition: A prospective population-based cohort of Swedish-born women aged 25–64 without a history of cancer, randomly selected from the population registry of the southern Swedish healthcare region and recruited in 1990–1992, who answered a baseline questionnaire on sun exposure habits, constitutional characteristics and other risk factors for melanoma and follow-up questionnaires every ten years, with cancer incidence and mortality followed through Swedish national registers. It was set up to study risk factors for melanoma and is also used to study the health effects of sun exposure.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to Solar radiation (ECTO:8000061)|designed to study: exposure to ultraviolet radiation (ECTO:0000006)

label: Michigan State University Twin Registry
other synonyms: Michigan State University Twin Register
definition: A twin registry at Michigan State University, begun as a university-based registry of undergraduate twins and since 2004 recruiting twins identified from birth records by the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services. Its population-based mail-in registry enrols child and adolescent twins aged 3–17 with their families and adult twins aged 18–55 living in lower Michigan, United States, and in-depth in-person twin family studies are drawn from it, to examine developmental differences in genetic, environmental, neural and neurobiological influences on psychopathology and resilience, particularly in childhood and adolescence.

label: Mater-University of Queensland Study of Pregnancy
other synonyms: Mater University of Queensland Study of Pregnancy|Mater-University of Queensland Study of Pregnancy and its outcomes
definition: A birth cohort of women recruited at their first antenatal clinic visit at the Mater Hospital in Brisbane, Australia, in 1981–1983, and of their live singleton children, followed up after the birth, at 6 months and at 5, 14 and 21 years, and in adulthood (mothers at 27 years, children at 30 years) with later record linkage. Begun as a study of pregnancy and its outcomes, it has become a longitudinal study of growth, development and ageing that emphasises the transmission across generations of factors affecting adult health.

label: Myositis Genetics Consortium
other synonyms: International Myositis Genetics Consortium
definition: An international consortium of myositis research centres through which DNA samples with clinical and autoantibody data from patients of European ancestry with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (adult and juvenile polymyositis and dermatomyositis, and inclusion body myositis) were collected at participating centres in Europe, the United States and Australia, including national collections such as the UK Adult Onset Myositis Immunogenetic Collaboration, for genome-wide and Immunochip association studies of myositis and its clinical and serological subgroups, analysed against controls supplied by other disease consortia.
diseases: patients with: acquired idiopathic inflammatory myopathy (MONDO:0020122)

label: Carolina Breast Cancer Study
other synonyms: North Carolina Breast Cancer Study
definition: A population-based study of breast cancer among women aged 20–74 in central and eastern North Carolina, United States, run from the University of North Carolina, which identifies newly diagnosed cases through rapid case ascertainment with the North Carolina Central Cancer Registry and oversamples Black and younger women. Phases I (1993–1996) and II (1996–2001) in 24 counties were a case-control study with controls drawn from Department of Motor Vehicles and Medicare enrolment records; phase III (2008–2013) enrolled invasive cases in 44 counties and followed them for recurrence, to study the biology, risk factors and outcomes of breast cancer and their differences by race and age.

label: North Carolina Bladder Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of bladder cancer in North Carolina, United States, which enrolled patients with transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder and control patients without cancer (mainly presenting with benign prostatic hypertrophy or impotence), frequency-matched on race, sex and age, at the urology clinics of Duke University Medical Center and the University of North Carolina Hospitals, to study inherited variation in carcinogen-metabolism and DNA-repair genes, smoking and bladder cancer risk.

label: NCI-Maryland Prostate Cancer Case-Control Study
other synonyms: Maryland Prostate Cancer Case-Control Study|NCI-Maryland prostate Cancer Case-Control Study
