definition: A case-control study of prostate cancer of the US National Cancer Institute in the Baltimore area of Maryland, which from 2005 to 2015 enrolled African American and European American men diagnosed with prostate cancer at the Baltimore Veterans Affairs Medical Center and the University of Maryland Medical Center, and population controls identified through the Maryland motor vehicle administration and frequency-matched to cases on age and race. Participants were interviewed about their demographics, lifestyle and medical and family history and gave blood or mouthwash samples, to study environmental and genetic factors in prostate cancer among African American men.

label: Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966
other synonyms: Northern Finland Premature Birth Study|Northern Finland birth cohort 1966
definition: A prospective birth cohort of the University of Oulu comprising the children of all mothers in the two northernmost provinces of Finland, Oulu and Lapland, whose expected date of delivery fell in 1966, recruited during pregnancy at the region's antenatal clinics from 1965. Set up to study the risk factors for and consequences of preterm birth and intrauterine growth retardation, it has followed its members with questionnaires at 1, 14, 31 and 46 years of age, clinical examinations in adulthood and linked national registers to study the life-course origins of health and disease.

label: Linxian General Population Nutrition Intervention Trial
other synonyms: Linxian Nutrition Intervention Trial
definition: A randomized, double-blind primary prevention trial of the Cancer Institute of the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and the US National Cancer Institute in Linxian, Henan province, China, a rural county with some of the world's highest rates of oesophageal and gastric cardia cancer, which in 1985 enrolled healthy adults aged 40–69 from four communes in northern Linxian and gave them daily combinations of vitamins and minerals or placebo in a fractional factorial design from March 1986 to May 1991. Its participants have since been followed as a prospective cohort for cancer incidence and cause-specific mortality.
diseases: population study of: esophageal cancer (MONDO:0007576)|population study of: gastric cardia carcinoma (MONDO:0003834)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to multivitamin supplementation (ECTO:2000123)

label: Neuro-Ophthalmology Research at Fundació ACE
other synonyms: Neuro-Ophthalmology Research at Fundació ACE Cohort
definition: A cohort of individuals evaluated for cognitive decline at Ace Alzheimer Center Barcelona (Fundació ACE), Spain, recruited from its Memory Clinic, Open House Initiative, the FACEHBI study and the BIOFACE project. Founded in 2014, it studies retinal biomarkers via optical coherence tomography and their relationship to neurodegenerative disorders.
diseases: patients with: Alzheimer disease (MONDO:0004975)|patients with: cognitive disorder (MONDO:0002039)|patients with: dementia (MONDO:0001627)

label: New York Cancer Project
other synonyms: New York Control Population
definition: A prospective cohort and biorepository of racially and ethnically diverse adults aged 30 or older living in the New York tri-state area, enrolled from January 2000 to December 2002 by the Academic Medical Development Company (AMDeC) Foundation, a consortium of New York institutions, at medical centres, community hospitals and community health centres in all five boroughs of New York City and at New York Blood Center donor drives. Participants completed a baseline questionnaire and gave blood for DNA and plasma, to be followed by questionnaires and registry linkage for studies of cancer aetiology and of racial and ethnic disparities in cancer risk, prevention and outcomes.

label: Okinawa Bioinformation Bank
other synonyms: Okinawa Bioinformation Bank Project
definition: A population-based biobank study established in 2016 in Okinawa Prefecture, Japan, through the Okinawa Bioinformation Bank Project promoted by the University of the Ryukyus and Okinawa Prefecture, whose participants, recruited on Okinawa's islands including the Miyako Islands, give blood or saliva for DNA and genome-wide genotyping together with health check-up results, lifestyle questionnaires and, for some, the birthplaces of their four grandparents. It aims to clarify the population history of the Ryukyu islanders and to find genetic factors in common and rare diseases.

label: Pancreatic Cancer Cohort Consortium
definition: A consortium formed in 2006 within the US National Cancer Institute's Cohort Consortium by investigators of 12 prospective cohort studies to run PanScan, a multi-stage genome-wide association study of pancreatic cancer funded by the NCI. PanScan I genotyped cases and controls from the cohorts and one case-control study, PanScan II (from 2007) those of eight case-control studies, and PanScan III new incident cases from 14 cohorts and from case series and case-control studies, mostly people of European ancestry from the United States and Europe.

label: Prostate Cancer Genome-wide Association Study of Uncommon Susceptibility Loci
other synonyms: NCI Prostate Cancer Genome-Wide Association Study of Uncommon Susceptibility Loci Study|ProstatE cancer Genetic Association Study of Uncommon Susceptibility loci|Prostate cancer Genome-wide Association Study to Uncover Susceptibility loci
definition: A genome-wide association study of prostate cancer run by the Division of Cancer Epidemiology and Genetics of the US National Cancer Institute as a nested case-control study within the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening Trial, in which men of European ancestry with pathologically confirmed prostate cancer detected during screening or reported during the trial, and men of the trial without prostate cancer matched to them on age and year of randomization, were genotyped genome-wide to find prostate cancer susceptibility loci, including loci for aggressive disease.

label: University of Pennsylvania Catheterization Study
definition: A hospital-based study of genes and biomarkers for coronary artery disease at the University of Pennsylvania Medical Center, United States, which from July 1998 to March 2003 recruited consecutive patients undergoing cardiac catheterisation and coronary angiography. A nested case-control genome-wide association study of angiographic coronary artery disease in its white patients is one of the core studies of the CARDIoGRAM consortium.

label: Pediatric Imaging, Neurocognition, and Genetics
other synonyms: PING study|Pediatric Imaging, Neurocognition and Genetics study|Pediatric Imaging, Neurocognition, and Genetics study
definition: A multi-site cross-sectional study of typically developing children, adolescents and young adults aged 3 to 20 years, recruited through local postings and outreach in eight metropolitan areas of the United States and assessed at ten US sites, with its coordinating centre at the University of California, San Diego, that collected developmental histories, cognitive assessments, multimodal brain imaging and genome-wide genotypes to create a shared repository for studying brain and cognitive development.

label: Karolinska Mammography Project for Risk Prediction of Breast Cancer - Case-Control Study
other synonyms: prevalent KARMA
definition: A Swedish breast cancer case-control study, known as prevalent KARMA, that combines women diagnosed with primary breast cancer in Stockholm between 2001 and 2008, identified through the regional cancer register for the LIBRO-1 study, with breast-cancer-free women from the Karolinska Mammography Project for Risk Prediction of Breast Cancer (KARMA) cohort as controls, all of whom gave blood samples, and whose genotypes contribute to the Breast Cancer Association Consortium's studies of breast cancer risk.

label: Parkinson Research Examination of CEP-1347 Trial
other synonyms: Parkinson Research Examination of CEP-1347 Trial/A Longitudinal Follow-up of the PRECEPT Study Cohort
definition: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial run by the Parkinson Study Group, which enrolled people with early Parkinson's disease not yet requiring dopaminergic therapy at 65 sites in the United States and Canada between April 2002 and April 2004 to test whether the mixed lineage kinase inhibitor CEP-1347 could slow disease progression; the trial was stopped early for futility in 2005, and its participants were then followed in the observational PostCEPT study.

label: Predictors For ECT
other synonyms: PREFECT study|Predictors for ECT
definition: A Swedish study that between 2013 and 2017 recruited adults who had received electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) recorded in the Swedish National Quality Register for ECT, inviting registered patients by letter to a telephone interview and blood sampling and recruiting others at Swedish psychiatric hospitals before an ECT series, and that links their DNA, stored at the Karolinska Institutet Biobank, to the register's data on each treatment series, to study predictors of ECT outcome, including genetic ones, and the genetics of severe depressive episodes.
diseases: patients with: Depression (HP:0000716)|patients with: major depressive disorder (MONDO:0002009)

label: Performance of Rotavirus and Oral Polio Vaccines in Developing Countries
other synonyms: PROVIDE Study|PROVIDE study
definition: A birth cohort of children enrolled with their mothers within seven days of birth in low-income wards of Mirpur, Dhaka, Bangladesh, from May 2011, into a randomized controlled trial with a two-by-two factorial design, conducted by the International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research, Bangladesh (icddr,b) with the University of Vermont and the University of Virginia, that tested a delayed-dose oral rotavirus vaccine and the replacement of one oral polio vaccine dose by an injectable polio vaccine, and followed the children through their first two years of life to study why oral vaccines underperform in children living with poverty, poor sanitation and overcrowding.

label: Queensland Twin Registry
other synonyms: Queensland Twin Register|Queensland Twin Registry Study|Queensland Twin and Family Registry
definition: A population-based registry of identical and non-identical twins and triplets of all ages living in Australia, established in 2006 at the QIMR Berghofer Medical Research Institute in Brisbane, whose members are invited into twin research projects on health and disease; genetic studies drawing on QIMR Berghofer's genotyped twin and family samples report them under the registry's name.

label: Research in African American Alzheimer Disease Initiative
other synonyms: Research in African American Alzheimer's Disease Initiative|The Research in African American Alzheimer Disease Initiative
definition: A multi-site US study of African Americans, a sub-study of the Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project run by investigators at North Carolina Agricultural and Technical State University, Wake Forest School of Medicine, the University of Miami, Columbia University and Case Western Reserve University, that ascertains African American families affected by Alzheimer's disease through community outreach and collects blood or saliva samples, medical and family histories and cognitive assessments, to identify rare variants, genes and pathways associated with Alzheimer's disease in African Americans.

label: The Roskilde cohort of pregnant women
other synonyms: Roskilde Cohort
definition: A prospective cohort of unselected pregnant women enrolled from 2009 at the nuchal translucency scan in the obstetrics and gynaecology department of Roskilde Hospital, Region Zealand, Denmark, with ultrasound, uterine artery Doppler and blood samples at about 12, 20, 25 and 32 weeks of gestation and outcomes taken from medical records, set up to study whether serum YKL-40 predicts preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction, and later used in genetic studies of gestational diabetes and glucose levels in pregnancy.
diseases: population study of: fetal growth restriction (MONDO:0005030)|population study of: preeclampsia (MONDO:0005081)

label: Shanghai Breast Cancer Genetics Study
other synonyms: Shanghai Breast Cancer Genetic Study
definition: A breast cancer case-control genetics study, led from Vanderbilt University, that genotyped Chinese women with breast cancer and controls drawn from four population-based studies in urban Shanghai, China: the Shanghai Breast Cancer Study, the Shanghai Breast Cancer Survival Study, the Shanghai Women's Health Study and, for controls only, the Shanghai Endometrial Cancer Study.

label: Scandinavian Lymphoma Etiology study
other synonyms: Scandinavian Lymphoma Etiology|Scandinavian Lymphoma Etiology Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of the causes of malignant lymphomas (non-Hodgkin lymphoma, including chronic lymphocytic leukaemia, and Hodgkin lymphoma) among residents of Denmark and Sweden aged 18–74, recruited in 1999–2002, with incident cases identified shortly after diagnosis through a rapid case-ascertainment network and controls sampled from the national population registers, and with a telephone interview and blood sampling.
diseases: patients with: B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia (MONDO:0004948)|patients with: Hodgkins lymphoma (MONDO:0004952)|patients with: lymphoma (MONDO:0005062)|patients with: non-Hodgkin lymphoma (MONDO:0018908)

label: Spanish Coalition to Unlock Research on Host Genetics on COVID-19
other synonyms: Spanish Coalition to Unlock Research of Host Genetics on COVID-19
definition: A cohort of COVID-19 patients with detailed clinical information, recruited from hospitals across Spain from March to December 2020 and in Latin America from March 2020 to July 2021 by a Spanish research consortium launched in May 2020 to study host genetic factors in COVID-19 and find biomarkers of its course and prognosis.

label: Steno Diabetes Center T2D Cases
definition: A sample of patients with clinical-onset type 2 diabetes and of non-diabetic control individuals (screened by oral glucose tolerance test) ascertained at the outpatient clinic of Steno Diabetes Center in Copenhagen, Denmark, used in genetic association studies of type 2 diabetes and metabolic traits.

label: Scottish Diabetes Research Network Type 1 Bioresource
other synonyms: Scottish Diabetes Research Network Type 1 Bioresource Study|Scottish Type 1 Bioresource
definition: A cohort of adults aged 16 or older with a clinical diagnosis of type 1 diabetes, latent autoimmune diabetes of adulthood or monogenic diabetes, recruited mainly at diabetes outpatient clinics across Scotland between December 2010 and November 2013, whose biosamples were banked and genotyped and who are followed through linkage to national electronic health records, set up to study the genetic determinants, biomarkers and complications of type 1 diabetes.

label: Shanxi Upper Gastrointestinal Cancer Genetics Project
other synonyms: Shanxi UGI Cancer Genetics Project
definition: A case-control study of upper gastrointestinal cancers conducted from 1997 to 2007 by the Shanxi Cancer Hospital and Institute under contract with the US National Cancer Institute in Shanxi Province, China, in the high-risk western Taihang Mountain area, which enrolled adults newly diagnosed with oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma or gastric adenocarcinoma and treated surgically at the Shanxi Cancer Hospital, with neighbourhood controls matched on age and sex, plus a case-only component, and collected questionnaire data and blood to study genetic and environmental risk factors for these cancers.
diseases: patients with: esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (MONDO:0005580)|patients with: gastric adenocarcinoma (MONDO:0005036)|patients with: gastric cardia adenocarcinoma (MONDO:0003835)

label: Swiss HIV Cohort Study
definition: A nationwide prospective longitudinal cohort of people with HIV aged 16 or older in Switzerland, established in 1988 as a collaboration of the Swiss university hospitals, large cantonal hospitals, affiliated smaller hospitals and private physicians, who recruit and follow the participants, to improve the health of people with HIV through clinical, translational and basic research.

label: Study of Osteoporotic Fractures
definition: A prospective multicentre cohort of community-dwelling women aged 65 or older in the United States, whose original, white members were recruited from population-based listings in four areas (Baltimore, Maryland; Minneapolis, Minnesota; Portland, Oregon; and the Monongahela Valley, Pennsylvania) between September 1986 and October 1988 and were joined by African American women enrolled at the Year 10 examination in 1997–1998, followed by regular contacts and repeat examinations to study risk factors for osteoporotic fractures.

label: Study of Twin Adults: Genes and Environment
other synonyms: Screening Twin Adults: Genes and Environment|Swedish Twin Study of Adults: Genes and Environment
definition: A cohort of the Swedish Twin Registry made up of twins born in Sweden between 1959 and 1985, who were invited to a web-based health screening survey in 2005–2006 and have since been followed through linkage to national health registers and further web surveys.

label: Sequenced Treatment Alternatives to Relieve Depression
definition: A multisite, prospective, randomised, multistep clinical trial, funded by the US National Institute of Mental Health through the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center at Dallas, that from 2001 enrolled adult outpatients aged 18 to 75 with nonpsychotic major depressive disorder from primary and specialty (psychiatric) care practices across the United States, to determine which treatments work best for those who do not respond adequately to initial treatment with citalopram.

label: Tyypin 1 Diabeteksen Genetiikka
definition: A Finnish collection of people with type 1 diabetes, made up of cases only (without family members or controls), that has contributed independent cases to international ImmunoChip genetic studies of type 1 diabetes.

label: Swedish Twin study of CHild and Adolescent Development
other synonyms: Swedisch Twin study of CHild and Adolescent Development|Swedish Twin study of Child and Adolescent Development|Twin Study of Child and Adolescent Development|Twin study of CHild and Adolescent Development
definition: A population-based longitudinal study, run from Karolinska Institutet, of all twins born in Sweden between May 1985 and December 1986, identified through the Swedish Twin Registry, in which the twins and their parents completed questionnaires in four waves from 1994 to 2005, when the twins were aged 8–9, 13–14, 16–17 and 19–20, with a further follow-up at age 26, to study how genes and environments contribute to the development of health and behavioural problems from childhood to adulthood.

label: Transforming Research and Clinical Knowledge in Traumatic Brain Injury
other synonyms: Transforming Research and Clinical Knowledge in TBI
definition: A prospective, multicentre, longitudinal observational cohort study, led from the University of California, San Francisco, with funding from the US National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, that from February 2014 to July 2018 enrolled patients presenting within 24 hours of a traumatic brain injury who received a clinically indicated head CT scan, together with orthopaedic trauma controls, at 18 level I trauma centres in the United States, and collected clinical, neuroimaging, blood biomarker, genetic and outcome data to improve the characterisation, diagnosis and prognosis of traumatic brain injury.

label: Type 1 Diabetes TrialNet
other synonyms: Type 1 Diabetes TrialNet Research Group|Type 1 Diabetes TrialNet Study Group|Type 1 Diabetes TrialNet study
definition: A cohort of people with or at risk of type 1 diabetes recruited since 2001 by Type 1 Diabetes TrialNet, an international network of clinical research centres established by the US National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases: chiefly relatives of people with type 1 diabetes who are screened for islet autoantibodies and followed for progression in its Pathway to Prevention natural-history study, and people at risk of or newly diagnosed with type 1 diabetes enrolled in its trials aimed at delaying or preventing the disease.
diseases: at risk of: type 1 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005147)

label: UCI Breast Cancer Study
definition: A population-based breast cancer case-control study run from the University of California, Irvine, whose cases were breast cancer patients diagnosed in Orange County, California, in the year from March 1994, ascertained through the population-based Cancer Surveillance Program of Orange County and enrolled as probands in the UCI population-based breast and ovarian cancer family registry, and whose controls were Orange County residents recruited in 1998–2003 by random digit dialling and frequency-matched to cases by age and race/ethnicity.

label: U.S. Radiologic Technologists Study
other synonyms: Rad Tech Study|U.S. Radiologic Technologists Cohort|US Radiologic Technologist Study|US Radiologic Technologists Cohort|US Radiologic Technologists Study
definition: A cohort of current and former radiologic technologists in the United States, women and men certified by the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists for at least two years between 1926 and 1982, assembled in 1982 by the US National Cancer Institute with the University of Minnesota and the Registry and followed through four mailed questionnaires (1983–1989, 1994–1998, 2003–2005 and 2012–2014), to assess risks of cancer and other diseases from protracted low-dose occupational and personal medical ionising radiation and other exposures.
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to ionizing radiation (ECTO:7000047)|participants with exposure: exposure to ultraviolet radiation (ECTO:0000006)

label: Vanderbilt Atrial Fibrillation Ablation Registry
other synonyms: Vanderbilt AF Ablation Registry
definition: A prospective clinical and genetic biorepository at Vanderbilt University Medical Center in Nashville, Tennessee, founded in 2011, that enrols adults scheduled for catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation, recording their medical history, pre-ablation imaging and procedure details, collecting blood for DNA at the time of ablation and following them for arrhythmia recurrence at 3, 6 and 12 months, to identify predictors of response to ablation and to support research on the mechanisms of atrial fibrillation.

label: Vietnam Era Twin Study of Aging
other synonyms: The Vietnam Era Twin Study of Aging
definition: A longitudinal behavioural genetic study of cognitive and brain aging in men, and later of early risk of mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease, whose participants are twins randomly selected from the Vietnam Era Twin Registry of male twin pairs who both served in the US military between 1965 and 1975, recruited in their 50s and assessed at two sites, San Diego and Boston, from 2003, with follow-up waves every 5 to 6 years.
diseases: population study of: Alzheimer disease (MONDO:0004975)|population study of: cognitive disorder (MONDO:0002039)
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to occupation (ECTO:0001591)

label: VHIR-FMT-Barcelona
other synonyms: Barcelona GWAs Study
definition: A case-control collection from Barcelona, Spain, of European-ancestry patients with non-lacunar ischaemic stroke confirmed by neuroimaging within 7 days, a subset of those enrolled in the Genetic contribution to functional Outcome and Disability after Stroke (GODS) project, and of controls over 40 years old without ischaemic stroke, collected in Barcelona primary care centres and Spanish network hospitals for the ISSYS and GRECOS studies, genotyped together and used as a case-control set in ischaemic stroke genome-wide association studies.

label: Virginia Twin Study of Adolescent Behavioral Development
other synonyms: GEDI Virginia Twin Study on Adolescent Behavioral Development|Virginia Twin Study on Adolescent Behavioral Development
definition: A population-based, cohort-sequential longitudinal study of European-ancestry twin pairs born in 1974-1983, ascertained at ages 8 to 16 through the state and participating private schools of Virginia, United States, who with their parents were assessed by psychiatric interviews and questionnaires in four waves about 18 months apart and again in their mid-20s, to study genetic and environmental influences on the development of child and adolescent psychopathology and substance use.

label: Vanderbilt Atrial Fibrillation Registry
other synonyms: Vanderbilt AF Registry|Vanderbilt Genetic Basis of Atrial Fibrillation
definition: A clinical and genetic registry at Vanderbilt University Medical Center in Nashville, Tennessee, United States, founded in 2001, that prospectively enrols patients with atrial fibrillation together with affected and unaffected family members, recording a detailed medical and drug history, an atrial fibrillation symptom severity assessment and a blood sample for DNA, and follows them with serial symptom assessments; its early-onset cases were whole-genome sequenced by the NHLBI TOPMed programme.

label: WeGene cohort
other synonyms: WeGene Biobank|WeGene Personal Genome Services
definition: A research cohort of customers of WeGene, a direct-to-consumer genetic testing company based in Shenzhen, China, who were genotyped from saliva on microarrays through the WeGene Personal Genome Services and consented to take part in research online, answering surveys posted on WeGene's online platform, website and WeChat channels.

label: Wisconsin Sleep Cohort Study
other synonyms: University of Wisconsin Sleep Cohort Study|Wisconsin Sleep Cohort
definition: A population-based longitudinal cohort study of the University of Wisconsin-Madison in which Wisconsin state employees aged 30 to 60, sampled from state payroll files, answered a mailed sleep and health survey in 1988, after which all respondents at high risk of sleep-disordered breathing by self-reported snoring, with an age- and sex-matched random sample of the others, were invited to overnight in-laboratory polysomnography repeated at about 4-year intervals, to study the natural history and health consequences of sleep-disordered breathing and other sleep disorders.
diseases: population study of: Sleep-related breathing disorders (HP:5200283)|population study of: sleep apnea syndrome (MONDO:0005296)

label: ZOE 2.0
other synonyms: ZOE 2.0 cohort
definition: A community-based, multi-ethnic, cross-sectional genetic epidemiologic study of early childhood oral health, run by the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, that enrolled children aged 3 to 5 attending public preschools (Head Start programmes) across North Carolina, United States, from August 2016 to February 2019, examining their teeth in the preschools and collecting guardian questionnaires, saliva for genotyping and dental plaque, to study the genomics of early childhood caries.

label: Protection Against Allergy: Study in Rural Environments
other synonyms: Protection Against Allergy Study in Rural Environments|Protection against Allergy STUdy in Rural Environments|Protection against Allergy-Study in Rural Environments
definition: A prospective birth cohort, begun in 2002 within an EU-funded project, of children from rural areas of Austria, Finland, France, Germany and Switzerland whose mothers were invited during the third trimester of pregnancy in 2002-2005, children of mothers living on family-run livestock farms forming the farm group and children of mothers from the same rural areas not living on a farm the reference group, followed from birth into school age with questionnaires, biological samples and clinical measurements to evaluate risk and protective factors, particularly farm exposures, for asthma and allergic diseases.
diseases: population study of: asthma (MONDO:0004979)|population study of: atopic IgE-mediated allergic disorder (MONDO:0005202)
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to cow milk (liquid) via ingestion (ECTO:0070204)|participants with exposure: exposure to farm (ECTO:1000034)

label: Project Viva
definition: A prospective pre-birth cohort, run from Harvard Medical School and the Harvard Pilgrim Health Care Institute, of women recruited in early pregnancy at eight obstetric offices of Atrius Harvard Vanguard Medical Associates, a multi-specialty group practice in eastern Massachusetts, United States, from April 1999 to November 2002, and their children, followed with in-person visits during pregnancy, at delivery, in infancy, early and mid-childhood and early adolescence and with annual mailed questionnaires, to examine prenatal diet and other early-life factors in relation to maternal and child health.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to pregnancy diet intake (ECTO:2000076)

label: GERO cohort
other synonyms: GERO cohort study|Gero cohort
definition: A population-based cohort of community-dwelling adults aged 70 or over without dementia but with a subjective cognitive complaint. They were recruited door to door from 2017 in three districts of Santiago, Chile (Macul, Peñalolén and La Reina), by the Geroscience Center for Brain Health and Metabolism (GERO), and are followed at 18 and 36 months with clinical, neuropsychological, neuroimaging, blood and stool assessments to study the rate of functional decline and progression to dementia and their risk factors.

label: Alzheimer's Genetics in Argentina–Alzheimer Argentina consortium
other synonyms: AGA-ALZAR study
definition: A multisite case-control study of sporadic Alzheimer's disease in Argentina, recruiting since 2013. Older people with Alzheimer's disease and cognitively unimpaired controls are enrolled at outpatient neurology departments of hospitals in the city and province of Buenos Aires and at centres in Jujuy, Córdoba and Mendoza provinces, to identify genes for susceptibility to sporadic Alzheimer's disease and genes that modify its phenotypes.

label: STORK study
other synonyms: Project STORK|STORK Rikshospitalet|STORK Rikshospitalet study|Stork Rikshospitalet
definition: A prospective cohort of healthy pregnant women of Scandinavian heritage with singleton pregnancies who registered for obstetric care and gave birth at Oslo University Hospital, Rikshospitalet, Norway, in 2001–2008. The women had four antenatal visits (weeks 14–16, 22–24, 30–32 and 36–38) with fasting blood samples and ultrasound, and oral glucose tolerance tests at weeks 14–16 and 30–32, to study the determinants of fetal growth and birthweight in healthy pregnancies.

label: San Antonio Longitudinal Study of Aging
other synonyms: The San Antonio Longitudinal Study of Aging
definition: A community-based longitudinal study of the disablement process in older Mexican Americans and European Americans in San Antonio, Texas. Its participants, the oldest members (aged 65 and over) of the San Antonio Heart Study cohort, had been randomly sampled from low-, middle- and high-income (barrio, transitional and suburban) neighbourhoods. They had a baseline examination in 1992–1996, combining a home-based assessment with a performance-based assessment at a clinical research center, and three follow-up examinations 18 months apart in 2000–2005.

label: Northern Ireland GRID Collection
other synonyms: Northern Irish GRID
definition: A collection of people with type 1 diabetes from Northern Ireland, most of them diagnosed in childhood. It is analysed separately from the Genetic Resource Investigating Diabetes (GRID) cases of Great Britain, and its DNA was genotyped on the ImmunoChip at the University of Virginia under the Type 1 Diabetes Genetics Consortium grant for genetic studies of type 1 diabetes.

label: Genome-wide assessment of the gene variants associated with severe COVID-19 phenotype in Iran
definition: A case-control genetic association study of COVID-19 severity in Iran, based at Shariati Hospital, Tehran University of Medical Sciences. It genotyped people of Middle Eastern ancestry hospitalised with COVID-19, and controls, on the Illumina Global Screening Array, and contributed them to the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative's meta-analyses of COVID-19 severity and of long COVID.

label: Northern Ireland Young Hearts Project
other synonyms: Northern Ireland Young Hearts Study|Young Hearts Project|Young Hearts Study|yh3, yh2000
definition: A longitudinal study of cardiovascular disease risk factors in young people in Northern Ireland, which screened a random sample of 12- and 15-year-olds from post-primary schools in 1989–1990, re-examined the younger group at age 15 in 1992–1993, and invited the whole sample back for examination as young adults in 1997–1999. A second school sample of 12- and 15-year-olds was surveyed in 1999–2001 as Young Hearts 2000.

label: Active Life Expectancy, Ageing, and Disability Related to Obesity Study
other synonyms: ALEXANDROS study|Active Life Expectancy, Aging and Disability Related to Obesity Study|Active Life Expectancy, Aging and Disorders Related to Obesity Study|Alexandros longitudinal study
definition: A longitudinal study of community-dwelling people aged 60 years and older in Santiago, Chile, designed to study disability and dementia associated with obesity. It follows three cohorts: Santiago participants of the SABE survey, born before 1940 and first recruited in 1999–2000; people born in 1940–1948, recruited from public primary health care centre registries in 2005–2008; and people of high socioeconomic status selected from private health insurance registries.
diseases: population study of: dementia (MONDO:0001627)|population study of: obesity disorder (MONDO:0011122)

label: Genetics of Glaucoma in People of African Descent Consortium
other synonyms: GGLAD consortium|Genetics of Glaucoma in People of African Descent
definition: A multicentre research consortium formed to carry out genome-wide association studies of primary open-angle glaucoma in people of African ancestry, which brought together case-control collections recruited in 2003–2018 through clinics and population-based studies in Ghana, Nigeria, South Africa, the United States, Tanzania, Britain, Cameroon, Saudi Arabia, Brazil, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Morocco, Peru and Mali. Besides its own site collections, it included participants of African ancestry from existing studies such as the Women's Health Initiative, the Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging cohort and the African Descent and Glaucoma Evaluation Study.
data collection locations: Brazil|Cameroon|Democratic Republic of the Congo|Ghana|Nigeria|Peru|Saudi Arabia|South Africa|Tanzania|United Kingdom|United States

label: International Collaboration on Ovarian Neoplasms 7 trial
other synonyms: Gynecologic Cancer Intergroup International Collaboration on Ovarian Neoplasms 7|ICON7 trial|International Collaboration on Ovarian Neoplasms 7
definition: An international, open-label, randomised phase 3 trial of the Gynecologic Cancer InterGroup, led by the UK Medical Research Council, in which women with newly diagnosed high-risk early-stage or advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer were recruited in 2006–2009 at centres in Europe, Canada, Australia and New Zealand and randomised to carboplatin and paclitaxel chemotherapy with or without concurrent and maintenance bevacizumab.

label: Genetics of Parkinson's in India – Young Onset Parkinson's Disease
other synonyms: Genetics Of Parkinson's in India - Young Onset Parkinson's Disease|Genetics of PAN-India Young Onset Parkinson Disease|PRAI cohort|Parkinson's Research Alliance of India cohort
definition: A prospective, pan-India, multicentre study of people with juvenile-, young- and early-onset Parkinson's disease (onset by about 50 years of age), started by the Parkinson Research Alliance of India, which over two years recruited patients under the care of movement disorder specialists at ten specialty movement disorder centres and neurology clinics across India, to study the clinical and genetic patterns of early-onset Parkinson's disease in India.

label: SweCovid study
other synonyms: Follow-UP study of patients with critical COVID-19|PronMed-Cohort|Pronmed cohort|SweCOVID study|The genetic predisposition to severe COVID-19
definition: A study of patients with critical COVID-19 admitted from March 2020 to the intensive care unit of Uppsala University Hospital, Sweden, who were enrolled in the prospective observational PronMed cohort and invited to follow-up three to six months after discharge, in which researchers at Uppsala University and Karolinska Institutet investigate the mechanisms of acute and long-term organ dysfunction in critical COVID-19, including its host genetics.

label: COVID-19 Kohortenstudie am Klinikum München Rechts der Isar
other synonyms: COMRI cohort|COVID-19 Cohort Study of the University Hospital of the Technical University Munich
definition: A prospective cohort study and registry of patients who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 at the Klinikum rechts der Isar, the university hospital of the Technical University of Munich, Germany, from 2020, in which hospitalised patients' clinical and laboratory data were collected prospectively for research on COVID-19.

label: Placental Abruption Genetic Epidemiology study
other synonyms: Placental Abruption Genetic Epidemiology
definition: A population-based case-control study of women admitted for obstetric care at seven hospitals in Lima, Peru, between March 2013 and December 2015, with cases of placental abruption and of preterm birth and controls selected at random from women delivering at the same hospitals, designed to investigate the genetic and environmental determinants of placental abruption and other adverse pregnancy outcomes.
diseases: patients with: Premature birth (HP:0001622)|patients with: placental abruption (MONDO:0004846)

label: STORK Groruddalen
other synonyms: STORK Groruddalen research programme|STORK Groruddalen study
definition: A population-based cohort of pregnant women of diverse ethnic origin attending three public Child Health Clinics for antenatal care in Groruddalen, a multi-ethnic area of Oslo, Norway, recruited in 2008–2010 and followed with their offspring through pregnancy and after birth, to study gestational diabetes, physical activity and obesity in pregnancy and to identify predictors of gestational diabetes and fetal growth.
diseases: population study of: gestational diabetes (MONDO:0005406)|population study of: obesity disorder (MONDO:0011122)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to Physical Activity (ECTO:6000039)

label: Mount Sinai COVID-19 Biobank
other synonyms: Mount Sinai COVID Biobank|Mount Sinai COVID-19 Biobank Study
definition: A research biobank of patients hospitalised with COVID-19 in the Mount Sinai Health System in New York City, enrolled from April to June 2020 through daily review of new admissions together with a smaller group of healthy and hospitalised controls, whose blood was sampled repeatedly alongside routine clinical draws during their hospital stay for multi-omic study of the host response to SARS-CoV-2, and whose survivors were later surveyed for post-acute sequelae of COVID-19.

label: Die Deutsche Diabetes Dialyse Studie
other synonyms: 4D Study|German Diabetes and Dialysis Study
definition: A multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, begun in 1998 at dialysis centres throughout Germany, of adults aged 18–80 with type 2 diabetes who had been on maintenance haemodialysis for less than two years, which tested whether atorvastatin lowers the risk of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction and stroke, and followed its participants for a median of four years.
diseases: patients with: end stage renal failure (MONDO:0004375)|patients with: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: African Descent and Glaucoma Evaluation Study
definition: A multicentre prospective observational cohort study, which from 2003 enrolled people of African descent and of European descent without glaucoma, with suspected glaucoma or with glaucoma at the University of California San Diego, the New York Eye and Ear Infirmary and the University of Alabama at Birmingham, United States, and followed them with repeated visual function testing and optic nerve imaging to identify why glaucoma onset and progression differ between people of African and European descent. Its third phase (ADAGES III) recruited, in 2014–2016 at five US centres, patients with primary open-angle glaucoma and controls of African or European descent, with DNA, to study the genetics of the disease in people of African descent.
diseases: patients with: glaucoma (MONDO:0005041)|patients with: open-angle glaucoma (MONDO:0005338)

label: ADMIxture and Risk of Acute Leukemia Study
other synonyms: ADMIRAL Study|Admixture and Risk of Acute Leukemia
definition: A case-control study of B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia in Black or African American children and young adults diagnosed at ages 0–25 in the United States, run from the University of Minnesota, which gathered germline DNA of cases from Children's Oncology Group frontline trials, from newborn dried blood spots held by the Michigan BioTrust for Health and linked to the state cancer registry, and from hospital leukaemia biobanks, with controls matched on sex and ancestry from Michigan newborn blood spots and paediatric well-child visits. It investigates African ancestry-specific genetic susceptibility to B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia and its relation to disease subtype and survival.
diseases: patients with: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (MONDO:0004947)

label: Amish Family Osteoporosis Study
definition: A family study of the Old Order Amish of Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, United States, begun by the University of Maryland in 1997, which identified Amish adults with osteoporosis by bone mineral density screening and recruited their first-degree relatives aged 20 and over and their spouses, measuring bone density by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, to find genetic and clinical determinants of osteoporosis and bone health in large multigenerational families.

label: Asian Genetic Epidemiology Network
other synonyms: Asian Genetic Epidemiology Network Consortium|Asian Genetic Epidemiology Network Type 2 Diabetes Consortium
definition: A consortium of genetic epidemiology studies of type 2 diabetes and related traits in people of East Asian ancestry, mostly population-, hospital- or family-based cohorts in East and South-East Asia, which meta-analyses its member studies' genome-wide association results in trait-specific groups (such as AGEN-T2D and AGEN-BP) for type 2 diabetes, glycaemic traits, adiposity, adiponectin, blood pressure and kidney function.
diseases: population study of: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: AIDS Linked to the IntraVenous Experience
other synonyms: AIDS Linked to the Intravenous Experience|AIDS linked to the IntraVenous experience
definition: An ongoing community-based cohort of current and former people who inject drugs in and around Baltimore, Maryland, United States, established in 1988 as a natural history study of the incidence and progression of HIV infection.
diseases: at risk of: HIV infectious disease (MONDO:0005109)
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to drug abuse (ECTO:6000008)

label: Australian Melanoma Family Study
definition: A multicentre, population-based case-control-family study in Australia, recruiting people with early-onset first-primary cutaneous melanoma, population-based and spouse or friend controls, and their relatives, between 2001 and 2005, to investigate genetic and environmental influences on melanoma risk.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to Solar radiation (ECTO:8000061)|designed to study: exposure to ultraviolet radiation (ECTO:0000006)

label: Anxiety NeuroGenetics STudy
other synonyms: Anxiety NeuroGenetics STudy (ANGST) Consortium|Anxiety NeuroGenetics STudy Consortium
definition: A consortium of seven independent studies of people of European ancestry in the United States, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Germany and Australia (the Molecular Genetics of Schizophrenia control sample, PsyCoLaus, the Rotterdam Study, the Study of Health in Pomerania, the QIMR twin sample, TRAILS and NESDA/NTR), with interview-based DSM diagnoses of anxiety disorders, formed to meta-analyse genome-wide association studies of generalized anxiety disorder, panic disorder, social phobia, agoraphobia and specific phobia.

label: Anglo-Australasian Osteoporosis Genetics Consortium
definition: A sample of postmenopausal women aged 55–85 of white European ancestry with extreme high or extreme low hip bone mineral density, recruited from population-based and clinical sources at centres in Australia, New Zealand and the United Kingdom by the Anglo-Australasian Osteoporosis Genetics Consortium and genotyped together for a genome-wide association study of bone mineral density and fracture that used extreme truncate selection.

label: Anakinra for Pustular Psoriasis: Response in a Controlled Trial
other synonyms: Anakinra for Pustular psoriasis: Response in a Controlled Trial|Anakinra for pustular psoriasis trial
definition: A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-stage adaptive trial, funded by the NIHR Efficacy and Mechanism Evaluation programme, that enrolled adults with palmoplantar pustulosis severe enough to need systemic therapy at 16 sites in England, Scotland and Wales between October 2016 and January 2020, to test whether 8 weeks of the interleukin-1 receptor antagonist anakinra reduces disease severity.

label: Assessment of Renal and Cervical Artery DysplasIA
other synonyms: Assessment of Renal and Cervical Artery Dysplasia
definition: A prospective national registry, sponsored by Assistance Publique–Hôpitaux de Paris and coordinated at the Hôpital Européen Georges Pompidou in Paris, of adults with renal, cervical or intracranial artery fibromuscular dysplasia recruited from 2009 to 2014 at 16 university hospitals in France and Belgium, with standardised clinical and imaging data and leukocyte DNA collected to study multisite disease and to search for susceptibility genes.

label: Anglo-Scandinavian Cardiac Outcomes Trial
other synonyms: Anglo Scandinavian Cardiac Outcomes Trial|Anglo-Scandinavian cardiac Outcomes Trial
definition: A multicentre randomised controlled trial that recruited hypertensive men and women aged 40–79 with at least three other cardiovascular risk factors, mostly through family practices in the United Kingdom, Ireland and the Nordic countries between February 1998 and May 2000, to compare an amlodipine-based with an atenolol-based antihypertensive regimen for preventing coronary and other cardiovascular events (the Blood Pressure-Lowering Arm), those with total cholesterol of 6.5 mmol/L or less being also randomised to atorvastatin or placebo in a factorial Lipid-Lowering Arm.
diseases: patients with: cardiovascular disorder (MONDO:0004995)|patients with: hypertensive disorder (MONDO:0005044)

label: The Ashkenazi Jewish Dataset
other synonyms: AJ GWAS dataset|Ashkenazi Jewish Dataset
definition: A case-control sample of people of Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry from the New York area, with Parkinson's disease cases recruited at the Center for Parkinson's Disease and Other Movement Disorders at Columbia University and controls evaluated in the same way, assembled from two Columbia University studies, the Genetic Epidemiology of PD study (PD EPI) and the AJ Study, for a genome-wide association study of Parkinson's disease.

label: Assessment, Serial Evaluation, and Subsequent Sequelae of Acute Kidney Injury Study
other synonyms: ASSESS-AKI Study|Assessment, Serial Evaluation, and Subsequent Sequelae in Acute Kidney Injury Study|Assessment, Serial Evaluation, and Subsequent Sequelae of AKI Study
definition: A prospective, matched cohort study, funded by the US National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, that enrolled hospitalised adults with and without acute kidney injury (AKI), matched on clinical research centre, pre-admission chronic kidney disease and other risk factors, at centres in the United States and Canada between December 2009 and February 2015, together with children undergoing cardiac surgery, and followed them after discharge to examine how an episode of AKI affects the development and progression of chronic kidney disease, cardiovascular events and death.

label: Age-related diseases: Understanding Genetic and non-genetic influences - a study at the University of Regensburg
other synonyms: Age-related diseases: understanding genetic and non-genetic influences - a study at the University of Regensburg|Altersbezogene Untersuchungen zur Gesundheit der Universität Regensburg|AugUR study
definition: A population-based cohort of mobile people aged 70 and over from the city and county of Regensburg in eastern Bavaria, Germany, invited from random samples of the local residents' registries and examined at the University Hospital Regensburg in two baseline surveys (2013–2015 and 2017–2019), with interviews, medical and eye examinations, biobanking and genotyping and later follow-up, set up by the University of Regensburg as a research platform for late-onset chronic diseases and their genetic and non-genetic causes.

label: Bambui (Brazil) Cohort Study of Ageing
other synonyms: Bambui Cohort Study of Ageing|Bambuí (Brazil) Cohort Study of Ageing|Bambuí (Brazil) Cohort Study of Aging|Bambuí Cohort Study of Ageing|Bambuí Health and Aging Study
definition: A population-based cohort of the residents aged 60 and over of the town of Bambuí, in Minas Gerais, south-eastern Brazil, identified by a complete census on 1 January 1997 and examined at baseline in February–May 1997 with interviews, blood tests, blood pressure measurements and electrocardiograms, then followed with annual interviews, repeated examinations and death ascertainment to study health and mortality in older adults.

label: Biology, Affect, Stress, Imaging and Cognition study
other synonyms: The Biology, Affect, Stress, Imaging and Cognition Study
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of pregnant women in Uppsala County, Sweden, invited at their routine ultrasound examination at gestational week 16–18 at Uppsala University Hospital from September 2009 to November 2018 and followed to one year postpartum with web surveys, biological samples and medical-record data, to study the biopsychosocial causes and predictors of perinatal depression.

label: Baltimore Breast Cancer Study
definition: A case-control study of breast cancer in the greater Baltimore area, Maryland, United States, in which incident breast cancer cases and controls frequency-matched to them on race and age were recruited from February 1993 to August 2003 at six hospitals, including the University of Maryland Medical Center and the Baltimore Veterans Affairs Medical Center, to identify and characterise markers of disease aggressiveness and poor outcome.

label: Beaver Dam Eye Study
definition: A population-based cohort of the residents of the city and township of Beaver Dam, Wisconsin, United States, aged 43 to 84 years at a private census begun in 1987. They were examined at baseline in 1988–1990 and re-examined about every five years (up to a 25-year follow-up in 2014–2016) by the University of Wisconsin-Madison, to study the prevalence, incidence and risk factors of age-related eye diseases, such as age-related macular degeneration and cataract, and of visual impairment.
diseases: population study of: age-related macular degeneration (MONDO:0005150)

label: BioImage Study: A Clinical Study of Burden of Atherosclerotic Disease in an At-Risk Population
other synonyms: BioImage Study|High Risk Plaque BioImage study
definition: A prospective observational cohort of asymptomatic adults at risk of, but without, clinical atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (men aged 55–80 and women aged 60–80). They were recruited in 2008–2009 by the High-Risk Plaque Initiative from members of the Humana health plan in Chicago, Illinois, and Fort Lauderdale, Florida, United States, and examined with vascular imaging and blood sampling, to identify imaging and circulating biomarkers that predict near-term atherothrombotic events.
diseases: at risk of: atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (MONDO:1060134)

label: Barbados National Cancer Study
definition: A nationwide population-based case-control study of breast and prostate cancer in Barbados-born residents of Barbados. It was run by Stony Brook University with the Barbados Ministry of Health and the University of the West Indies and funded by the US National Human Genome Research Institute. Its breast cancer arm enrolled every histologically confirmed incident breast cancer identified by the island's only pathology department, at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital, from July 2002 to March 2006, with controls randomly selected from a national database and frequency-matched by age. The aim was to study environmental and genetic risk factors in this predominantly African-origin population.
diseases: patients with: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|patients with: prostate cancer (MONDO:0008315)
exposures: designed to study: exposure event (ExO:0000002)|designed to study: exposure to eating behavior (ECTO:6000021)

label: Brigham and Women's Rheumatoid Arthritis Sequential Study
other synonyms: Brigham Rheumatoid Arthritis Sequential Study|Brigham and Women's Hospital Rheumatoid Arthritis Sequential Study
definition: A single-centre prospective observational registry cohort of adults with rheumatoid arthritis diagnosed by a rheumatologist, enrolled from March 2003 at the Brigham and Women's Hospital Arthritis Center in Boston, Massachusetts, United States. Participants are followed with annual visits, semi-annual questionnaires and stored blood samples, to find biomarkers that predict drug response, toxicity, disease activity and prognosis and to describe the natural history of treated rheumatoid arthritis.

label: British Society for Surgery of the Hand Genetics of Dupuytren's Disease study
definition: A UK collection of adults with Dupuytren's disease who had been treated surgically for it. Saliva samples for DNA, and diseased palmar fascia removed at surgery, were collected by the British Society for Surgery of the Hand Genetics of Dupuytren's Disease (BSSH-GODD) consortium for genetic studies of the disease.

label: Cambridgeshire Parkinson's Incidence from GP to Neurologist
definition: An observational, longitudinal, population-representative incident cohort of people newly diagnosed with parkinsonism or Parkinson's disease in the county of Cambridgeshire, United Kingdom, between December 2000 and December 2002. Cases were referred through general practitioners, neurologists, geriatricians, Parkinson's disease specialist nurses and hospital discharge coding, and were followed from diagnosis by the University of Cambridge with clinical, neuropsychological and genetic assessments, to describe the natural history of Parkinson's disease.
diseases: patients with: Parkinson disease (MONDO:0005180)|patients with: parkinsonian disorder (MONDO:0021095)

label: Canadian Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection Study
other synonyms: CanSCAD Cohort Study|CanSCAD Study|Canadian SCAD Cohort Study|Canadian SCAD Study|Canadian Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection Cohort Study|Canadian spontaneous coronary artery dissection study
definition: A multicentre, prospective, observational cohort of patients presenting with acute non-atherosclerotic spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD), run from the University of British Columbia and enrolled at cardiac centres in Canada and the United States since June 2014, whose precipitating stressors, predisposing conditions and core-laboratory-reviewed angiograms are recorded and who are followed for cardiovascular events, to establish the natural history of SCAD and the outcomes of its treatment. Its first phase, the Canadian SCAD Cohort Study (enrolment 2014 to 2018, three-year follow-up), was extended from December 2018 as the Canadian SCAD Study, with international enrolment, a genetic sub-study and follow-up of up to ten years.

label: Copenhagen City Heart Study
other synonyms: Østerbroundersøgelsen
definition: A prospective cardiovascular population study of an age-stratified random sample of adults aged 20 years or older living in the Østerbro district and part of Nørrebro around Rigshospitalet in Copenhagen, Denmark, launched in 1975 with a first examination in 1976–1978 and re-examinations in 1981–1983, 1991–1994, 2001–2003 and 2011–2013, whose participants are followed through the Danish national registers. Its original purpose was the prevention of coronary heart disease and stroke; lung disease, dementia, ageing, genetics and other topics were added later.
diseases: population study of: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)|population study of: stroke disorder (MONDO:0005098)

label: Chicago Cancer Prone Study
other synonyms: University of Chicago Cancer Prone Registry|University of Chicago Cancer Prone Study
definition: A registry of individuals and families at high risk of cancer, established in 1992 at the Cancer Risk Clinic, a hospital-based preventive oncology clinic of the University of Chicago, United States, whose participants receive genetic testing and counselling at enrolment. It is also run as a hospital-based case-control study of the genetics of breast cancer in young patients, enrolling women with histologically confirmed breast cancer through the clinic, with early-onset cases and African Americans oversampled, and cancer-free controls matched on sex and age from patients of the same hospital, with questionnaires adopted from the Breast Cancer Family Registry and blood samples.
diseases: at risk of: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|at risk of: cancer (MONDO:0004992)

label: Comprehensive Sickle Cell Centers Collaborative Data Project
other synonyms: Collaborative Data Project|Comprehensive Sickle Cell Centers Collaborative Data project
definition: A multicentre observational cohort and database of children and adults with sickle cell disease receiving care at the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute's Comprehensive Sickle Cell Centers in the United States, run from March 2005 to September 2008 at nine of the centres and their satellite sites, which collected clinical data abstracted from medical records, yearly health and lifestyle interviews and quality-of-life questionnaires, and from 2007 blood and DNA samples for a genotype-phenotype repository, to describe the disease's complications and identify participants for future clinical trials.

label: Cardiovascular Genome Center cohort
other synonyms: CGC cohort|Cardiovascular Genome Center|Cardiovascular Genome Center Registry|Cardiovascular Genome Centre
definition: A hospital-based registry cohort of the Cardiovascular Genome Center of Yonsei University College of Medicine, enrolling from November 2000 patients who visited the cardiology division of Severance Hospital in Seoul, South Korea, for chest symptoms, cardiovascular risk-factor control or a health check-up, with clinical data collected by trained nurses, blood samples for DNA and, where symptoms warranted, coronary angiography, for genetic research on coronary artery disease and other cardiovascular and metabolic conditions.
diseases: patients with: cardiovascular disorder (MONDO:0004995)|patients with: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)

label: Cancer Genetic Markers of Susceptibility
other synonyms: Cancer Genetic Markers of Susceptibility project|National Cancer Institute Cancer Genetic Markers of Susceptibility|National Cancer Institute Cancer Genetic Markers of Susceptibility initiative
definition: A three-year initiative of the US National Cancer Institute, begun in 2006, that ran multi-stage genome-wide association studies of prostate and breast cancer in case-control sets drawn from existing studies (for prostate cancer, men from the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial, the American Cancer Society Cancer Prevention Study II, the Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study and the French Prostate Case-Control Study; for breast cancer, postmenopausal women from the Nurses' Health Study, with replication in further cohorts), and shared its genotype data and results with the research community.
diseases: patients with: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|patients with: prostate cancer (MONDO:0008315)

label: Canadian Cystic Fibrosis Gene Modifier Study
other synonyms: Canadian CF Gene Modifier Study|Canadian CF Modifier Study|Canadian Consortium for Genetic Studies|Canadian Cystic fibrosis Gene Modifier Study|Canadian Gene Modifier Study
definition: A population-based study of people with cystic fibrosis and their parents in Canada, led from the Hospital for Sick Children in Toronto, which recruited patients without regard to genotype or lung function through specialised CF clinics across the country, first from 2003 to 2006 and then in a second phase, with clinical data from clinic records and DNA for genome-wide genotyping and sequencing, to identify genetic modifiers of cystic fibrosis lung disease and of complications such as meconium ileus, liver disease and CF-related diabetes.

label: Center for HIV/AIDS Vaccine Immunology
other synonyms: NIAID Center for HIV/AIDS Vaccine Immunology
definition: A consortium of universities and academic medical centres established by the US National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases from 2005 to 2012 and led from Duke University, to determine the host and virus factors associated with HIV transmission, infection and control and so advance HIV vaccine development. Its clinical studies enrolled participants at sites in Africa and the United States, and its Host Genetics Core assembled genome-wide genotyped samples of people with HIV-1 from existing cohorts, including the European and Australian cohorts of the Euro-CHAVI consortium and participants of the US Military HIV Natural History Study and the Multicenter AIDS Cohort Study.

label: Chinese Keratoconus Cohort Study
other synonyms: Chinese Keratoconus Cohort|Chinese keratoconus cohort study
definition: A hospital-based, dynamic, longitudinal prospective cohort of patients with keratoconus, established at Henan Eye Hospital in Zhengzhou, China, which since January 2019 has enrolled patients from a large geographical area, collecting questionnaire data on demographics, lifestyle, eye rubbing, medical, surgical and family history and visual function, eye and general examinations, biological specimens and data on patients' first-degree relatives, with follow-up at 3, 6 and 12 months and yearly thereafter, to study genes, environment and their interaction in keratoconus progression and its prevention.

label: Chronic Kidney Disease in Children Study
other synonyms: CKiD Study|Chronic Kidney Disease in Children|Chronic Kidney Disease in Children Prospective Cohort Study
definition: A multicentre prospective observational cohort of children with chronic kidney disease in the United States and Canada, funded since 2003 by the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases and coordinated from Children's Mercy Hospital in Kansas City and Johns Hopkins (later the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia), which since 2005 has enrolled children aged 6 months to 16 years at paediatric nephrology centres and later also young adults. Participants have annual visits with measured glomerular filtration rate, questionnaires on cognition, behaviour and quality of life, cardiovascular assessments and stored biosamples and DNA, to identify risk factors for the decline of kidney function and its effects on cardiovascular risk, neurocognitive function and behaviour, and growth.

label: UCLA Consortium for Neuropsychiatric Phenomics
other synonyms: Consortium for Neuropsychiatric Phenomics
definition: A sample of adults aged 21–50 studied at the University of California, Los Angeles, by the Consortium for Neuropsychiatric Phenomics, one of the NIH Roadmap interdisciplinary research consortia of 2007–2012: mainly healthy White non-Hispanic or Hispanic adults recruited by community advertisement in the Los Angeles area, with smaller groups with schizophrenia, bipolar disorder or ADHD recruited through local clinics and online portals. Participants had diagnostic interviews, neurocognitive testing and blood sampling for genotyping, and a subset had structural, diffusion and functional MRI, to study memory and response-inhibition phenotypes dimensionally from genome to syndrome.
diseases: patients with: attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (MONDO:0007743)|patients with: bipolar disorder (MONDO:0004985)|patients with: schizophrenia (MONDO:0005090)

label: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease in Dusty Areas
other synonyms: COPD in Dusty Areas|COPD in dusty areas
definition: A longitudinal observational cohort, begun in 2012 and based at Kangwon National University Hospital, of residents of six districts with cement plants in Gangwon (Kangwon) and Chungbuk provinces, South Korea, comprising people with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or airflow limitation and volunteers with normal spirometry, examined with questionnaires, spirometry, chest CT and blood and urine sampling, to study the clinical course and outcomes of COPD in people exposed to cement dust.
diseases: patients with: chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (MONDO:0005002)
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to cement dust (ECTO:7000026)

label: Cohort in Lung Transplantation
other synonyms: COhort of Lung Transplantation|Cohort for Lung Transplantation|Cohort of Lung Transplantation
definition: A prospective multicentre cohort of lung transplant candidates enrolled before transplantation at eleven French lung transplant centres and the Erasme Hospital in Brussels between September 2009 and the end of 2018, coordinated by Nantes University Hospital, with clinical data and biological samples from recipients, and samples from their organ donors, followed every six months after transplantation (samples for up to five years, clinical data for up to ten), set up to discover early predictors of chronic lung allograft dysfunction.

label: Cooperative Study of Sickle Cell Disease
definition: A multicentre prospective study of the natural history of sickle cell disease, initiated in 1977, that enrolled patients with sickle cell disease of all ages, from newborns to adults and from mild to hospital-based cases, at 23 centres across the United States from 1978 (patients older than six months until 1981, infants until 1988), and followed them with standardised examinations and records of acute and chronic complications and organ damage, later phases following the infant cohort and adult participants until 1998, to identify the factors contributing to the morbidity and mortality of the disease.

label: Dallas Heart Study
definition: A single-site, multiethnic, population-based probability sample of residents of Dallas County, Texas, aged 18 to 65, weighted to be about half African American and run by the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center, surveyed and examined in 2000–2002 (DHS-1) and re-examined in 2007–2009 together with spouses and other new participants (DHS-2), designed to produce unbiased estimates of ethnic differences in cardiovascular health and to support research on their biological and social mechanisms using genetics, imaging, and clinical and social-science methods.

label: Danish Testicular Cancer Late Treatment Effects Cohort
definition: A nationwide, population-based cohort of long-term testicular cancer survivors treated in Denmark in 1984–2007, identified in the Danish Testicular Cancer (DaTeCa) clinical database and surveyed by questionnaire on late effects in 2014–2016 by the Department of Oncology at Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen University Hospital, with linked hospital, pathology and national registry data and a biobank of blood and sputum samples, set up to analyse late effects of treatment and inform future follow-up programmes.

label: Drakenstein Child Health Study
definition: A population-based birth cohort run by the University of Cape Town in the Drakenstein area of Paarl, a poor peri-urban community 60 km from Cape Town, South Africa, which enrolled pregnant women at 20–28 weeks' gestation at two primary health clinics (TC Newman and Mbekweni) between March 2012 and March 2015 and follows the mother–child pairs from pregnancy until the children are at least five years old, to investigate early-life determinants of child health, first among them early lower respiratory tract infection, through environmental, infectious, nutritional, genetic, psychosocial, maternal and immunological measures.
diseases: population study of: respiratory tract infectious disorder (MONDO:0024355)

label: Dental Strategies Concentrating on Risk Evaluation
other synonyms: Pittsburgh Dental SCORE
definition: A sub-study of Heart SCORE (Heart Strategies Concentrating on Risk Evaluation), a community-based cohort begun in 2003 of White and African American adults aged 45–75 in the greater Pittsburgh area, Pennsylvania, set up to investigate racial disparities in cardiovascular disease, in which a subgroup of participants had extended dental and periodontal examinations following the COHRA1 protocols and gave blood or saliva for DNA in 2007–2010, run by the University of Pittsburgh.

label: Diabetes Gene Discovery Group
definition: A French case–control sample of people of European ancestry assembled for a genome-wide association study of type 2 diabetes: people with type 2 diabetes, a family history of diabetes in first-degree relatives and a BMI below 30, recruited at the CNRS UMR8090 unit in Lille and the Endocrinology-Diabetology Department of the Corbeil-Essonnes Hospital, and normoglycaemic controls drawn mostly from the D.E.S.I.R. cohort of volunteers attending French health examination centres.

label: Diabetes Multi-omic Investigation of Drug Response
definition: A diverse cohort of adults with type 2 diabetes who are members of the Henry Ford Health System with pharmacy-covered health insurance and live in southeast Michigan and the Detroit metropolitan area, invited on the basis of two or more recorded diagnoses of type 2 diabetes and an HbA1c of at least 6.5%, who at enrolment completed a research survey, clinical examination and specimen collection, and whose genome-wide genotypes are linked to longitudinal electronic records of laboratory results and medication fills to study the genetics of response to diabetes drugs.

label: Detroit Neighborhood Health Study
other synonyms: The Detroit Neighborhood Health Study
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of adults aged 18 or older living in the city of Detroit, Michigan, most of them African American, drawn from a random probability sample of the city's households and interviewed by telephone in annual waves from 2008 to 2013, with blood specimens collected from a subset, to study how biological variation, stressful and traumatic experiences and environmental factors contribute to post-traumatic stress disorder, depression and other psychopathology.
diseases: population study of: post-traumatic stress disorder (MONDO:0005146)|population study of: psychiatric disorder (MONDO:0002025)

label: Endometrial Cancer Association Consortium
definition: An international consortium of population- and hospital-based endometrial cancer studies in Europe, North America and Australia, whose cases of European ancestry were genotyped on the iCOGS and OncoArray arrays and compared with country-matched controls, mainly from the Breast Cancer Association Consortium, in genome-wide association studies of endometrial cancer risk.

label: European Challenge for Healthy Aging
other synonyms: ECHA study|European Challenge for Healthy Aging project|European Challenge for Healthy Aging study
definition: A European family study of longevity that recruited people aged 90 or older, many of them centenarians, in Southern Denmark, Languedoc-Roussillon in France and Calabria in Italy, together with one of their children and, in a cousin-pair design, a child of a sibling who was or was not also long-lived, to investigate genetic and environmental factors in longevity and healthy ageing.

label: Pittsburgh Epidemiology of Diabetes Complications Study
other synonyms: Epidemiology of Diabetes Complications study
definition: A prospective cohort study of people with childhood-onset type 1 diabetes (onset before age 17) who were diagnosed, or seen within a year of diagnosis, at Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh between 1950 and 1980, followed since a baseline examination in 1986–1988 with biennial examinations and questionnaires for ten years and later questionnaires and examinations, to ascertain the incidence of and risk factors for complications of type 1 diabetes.

label: Scottish AMD study
definition: A clinic-based case-control study of age-related macular degeneration in Scotland, collected by a group in Edinburgh with funding from the Chief Scientist Office (Scotland), whose cases with advanced or intermediate AMD and controls were ascertained by fundus examination or photography; its cases and controls replicated the association of complement C3 with AMD and were contributed to the International AMD Genomics Consortium's genome-wide association study.

label: Estudo Longitudinal de Saúde do Adulto
other synonyms: Brazil Longitudinal Study of Adult Health|Brazilian Longitudinal Study of Adult Health|Brazilian Longitudinal Study of Adult Health (ELSA)|Estudo Longitudinal de Saude do Adulto|Estudo Longitudinal de Saude do Adulto cohort|Longitudinal Study of Adult Health
definition: A multicentre cohort of active and retired employees aged 35–74 years of six Brazilian universities and research institutions, with study centres in state capitals of north-eastern, south-eastern and southern Brazil, examined at baseline in 2008–2010 and at later visits and followed by annual telephone interviews, to investigate the development of chronic diseases, primarily diabetes and cardiovascular diseases.
diseases: population study of: cardiovascular disorder (MONDO:0004995)|population study of: diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005015)

label: Epidemiology of Burkitt Lymphoma in East African Children and Minors
other synonyms: EMBLEM study|Epidemiology of Burkitt Lymphoma in East-African Children and Minors|Epidemiology of Burkitt lymphoma in East African children and minors
definition: A case-control study of childhood Burkitt lymphoma in malaria-endemic East Africa, sponsored by the US National Cancer Institute's intramural research program, that in 2010–2016 enrolled population-based cases and controls aged 0–15 years from six rural regions, two each in Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania, and used questionnaires, blood samples and genetic data to investigate infectious, immunological and genetic risk factors for Burkitt lymphoma.

label: Essen-Heidelberg
definition: A German case-control study of cutaneous melanoma, of patients with histologically confirmed cutaneous melanoma and healthy controls from Germany genotyped genome-wide, approved by the ethics committee of University Hospital Essen and funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft, whose data were contributed to international meta-analyses of melanoma genome-wide association studies.

label: FActeurs de RIsque et de récidives de la maladie thromboembolique Veineuse
other synonyms: Etude des Facteurs de Risque de thrombose Veineuse|Facteurs de Risques et de Récidives de la Maladie Thromboembolique Veineuse
definition: A French multicentre case-control study of venous thromboembolism, run in 11 centres from 2003 to 2009, that enrolled consecutive adult inpatients and outpatients treated for a first objectively documented deep vein thrombosis and/or pulmonary embolism, without active cancer or malignancy in the previous 5 years, whose blood was mostly sampled in the week after diagnosis, and hospital controls matched for age, sex and centre with no history of venous or arterial thrombosis; the patients were also followed prospectively, to study risk factors for a first venous thromboembolism and for its recurrence.

label: European/International Fibromuscular Dysplasia Registry and Initiative
other synonyms: European/International FMD Registry|European/International FMD Registry and Initiative|European/International Fibromuscular Dysplasia Registry|FMD European/International Registry and Initiative
definition: A registry of patients with fibromuscular dysplasia, launched in December 2015 at the First Brussels National Meeting on FMD and endorsed by the European Society of Hypertension in 2016, that enrols prevalent and incident adult patients whose multifocal or focal FMD lesions in at least one arterial bed were shown by CT angiography, MR angiography or catheter angiography, at centres in Europe and a few other countries, recording their clinical characteristics, imaging, visits and vascular interventions on an online platform with an associated DNA and RNA biobank, to characterise the clinical profiles, complications and management of the disease. It also takes in data from existing national registries such as the French NOMADE and Polish ARCADIA-POL registries.

label: FinDonor 10 000 study
other synonyms: FinDonor 10000
definition: A prospective cohort of whole-blood donors aged 18–70 recruited by the Finnish Red Cross Blood Service alongside standard donation at three fixed donation sites in the Helsinki metropolitan area of Finland (Kivihaka, Sanomatalo and Espoo) from May 2015 to December 2017, with blood samples taken at their donation visits during the study for blood counts, CRP, ferritin and soluble transferrin receptor and for DNA, and health and lifestyle questionnaires at enrolment and again in 2018, to study iron status and the genetic and lifestyle factors affecting iron stores in blood donors.

label: National FinHealth 2017 Study
other synonyms: FinHealth 2017 Study|FinHealth 2017 Survey|FinHealth Study|national FinHealth 2017 study
definition: A national health examination survey of adults aged 18 or older living in mainland Finland, run by the Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (THL) at 50 study locations between January and May 2017 in a representative sample drawn from the Population Register by one- and two-stage stratified random sampling, in which participants answered questionnaires on sociodemographic factors, health, quality of life, lifestyle, diseases and medication and attended a health examination with physical measurements and blood sampling, to monitor the health, functional capacity and welfare of the Finnish population and the prevalence and risk factors of common health problems. It combined the protocols of the FINRISK surveys and the Health 2000 and 2011 surveys.

label: FinnTwin12 Cohort
other synonyms: FinnTwin12 Study|The Younger Finnish Twin Cohort
