definition: A population-based longitudinal cohort of the twins born in Finland in 1983–1987, the youngest of the three Finnish Twin Cohorts, identified through Finland's Central Population Registry and enrolled with their biological parents in the year they reached age 11, with twin, parent and teacher questionnaires and ratings at baseline and follow-up surveys at ages 14, 17, about 22 and about 37; a subset was studied intensively with in-school assessments and peer nominations at age 12, psychiatric interviews at ages 14 and 22, and neurocognitive tests and DNA collection in early adulthood. It was designed to identify individual, familial and school and neighbourhood risks for substance use before its onset and to follow trajectories of use, abuse and their consequences into adulthood.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to Tobacco Use (ECTO:6000041)|designed to study: exposure to alcohol consumption (ECTO:0001082)|designed to study: exposure to substance abuse (ECTO:6000007)

label: Finnish Twin Study on Aging
definition: A study of the genetic and environmental effects on the disablement process in older women, in which female twin pairs aged 63–76, recruited from the Older Finnish Twin Cohort, took part in laboratory examinations of physical functioning, muscle strength and power, hearing and other health measures, with blood sampling, in Jyväskylä, Finland, in 2000–2001 and again at a 3-year follow-up, and have since been followed for mortality, by researchers of the Gerontology Research Center of the University of Jyväskylä.

label: Follow-up of Ovarian Cancer Genetic Association and Interaction Studies
other synonyms: Follow-up of Ovarian Cancer Genetic Association and Interaction Studies of the Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium|The Follow-up of Ovarian Cancer Genetic Association and Interaction Studies
definition: A post-GWAS research programme on epithelial ovarian cancer, funded by the US National Cancer Institute (U19-CA148112) as the ovarian cancer consortium of the Genetic Associations and Mechanisms in Oncology (GAME-ON) initiative, led from Moffitt Cancer Center and built on the collaboration of the Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium, that pools genome-wide and further genotyping data (including exome-chip and OncoArray genotyping) from the case-control studies of that consortium, to discover and replicate susceptibility variants, including histotype-specific variants and variants associated with survival, to study their biological mechanisms, and to investigate gene–gene and gene–environment interactions and risk prediction.

label: Marburg-Münster Affective Disorders Cohort Study
other synonyms: FOR2107 Marburg-Münster Affective Disorders Cohort Study|FOR2107 consortium|Marburg Münster Affective Disorders Cohort Study|The FOR2107 consortium
definition: The human cohort of the German Research Foundation (DFG) research unit FOR2107 on the neurobiology of the major psychoses, recruited between 2014 and 2018 at the Universities of Marburg and Münster, Germany, through local psychiatric hospitals and newspaper advertisements: adults aged 18–65 with major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, schizoaffective disorder or schizophrenia, healthy people at genetic and/or environmental risk, and healthy controls, deeply phenotyped with MRI, clinical course, neuropsychology, personality, risk and protective factors and biomaterials (blood, stool, urine, hair, saliva) at baseline and again at a 2-year follow-up, to identify how genetic and environmental factors shape brain structure and function and the course of these disorders.
diseases: patients with: bipolar disorder (MONDO:0004985)|patients with: major depressive disorder (MONDO:0002009)|patients with: schizoaffective disorder (MONDO:0005487)|patients with: schizophrenia (MONDO:0005090)

label: Genes and Blood Clotting Study
definition: A family-based study of healthy young people aged 14–35, recruited at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, United States, between June 2006 and January 2009 from the university's undergraduate and graduate students together with their biological siblings, with blood samples for measuring plasma haemostatic proteins (such as von Willebrand factor and plasminogen), genome-wide genotyping and a survey of common morphological traits, to identify the genetic factors behind variation in blood clotting in healthy people, using its sibling structure for linkage as well as association analysis.

label: Genetic Analysis of Psoriasis Consortium
other synonyms: GAP consortium
definition: An international consortium of psoriasis genetics research groups in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Austria, Finland, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain and Sweden, with a management committee chaired from King's College London, that pools its members' collections of people of European descent with psoriasis vulgaris, together with controls from national control collections, for genetic association studies of psoriasis, including a genome-wide association study with the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium 2 and an Immunochip case–control study.

label: Ghana Breast Health Study
other synonyms: Ghana breast health study
definition: A population-based case–control study of breast cancer, a collaboration of the US National Cancer Institute with three major hospitals in Accra and Kumasi, Ghana (Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital and Peace and Love Hospital), that in 2013–2015 enrolled women aged 18–74 recommended for biopsy of a breast lesion suspicious for malignancy, or treated for breast cancer, at these hospitals, and population controls sampled by household enumeration of the surrounding districts and frequency-matched on age and district, collecting interviews and tumour tissue, blood, saliva and faecal samples to study breast cancer risk factors in a West African population.

label: GenomALC
other synonyms: Genetics of alcoholic liver cirrhosis consortium|GenomALC Multinational Study
definition: A multicentre international case–control study of alcohol-related cirrhosis, run by the GenomALC Consortium of researchers in Australia, France, Germany, Switzerland, the United Kingdom and the United States with funding from the US National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism, that from September 2012 recruited, at liver and alcohol treatment clinics and from existing repositories of the participating centres, people who had drunk heavily (at least 80 g of alcohol a day for men or 50 g for women) for at least ten years, with alcoholic cirrhosis (cases) or without significant liver disease (controls), with interviews, clinical records and blood samples, to find genetic factors that predispose drinkers to cirrhosis. A second sample, GenomALC-2, added DNA and data that research groups in these countries and Belgium had collected for earlier genetic studies of alcohol-related liver disease.
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to alcohol abuse (ECTO:6000009)

label: Melanoma Genetics Consortium
other synonyms: GenoMEL Consortium|GenoMEL consortium|International Melanoma Genetics Consortium
definition: An international non-profit consortium, established in 1997, of most of the research groups working on the genetics of familial melanoma, in Europe, North America, Australia and elsewhere, funded by the European Commission's Sixth Framework Programme and the US National Cancer Institute, which pools data and samples from its members' melanoma-prone families and case–control series to find melanoma susceptibility genes and how they interact with environmental factors such as ultraviolet radiation. Its genome-wide association study combined melanoma cases, prioritised for family history, multiple primaries or early onset, and controls from the same populations, contributed by member groups in Europe, Israel and Australia, with French and UK population controls.

label: GENetics of SEPsis-induced ARDS Network
other synonyms: GEN-SEP Network|Genetics of Sepsis Network|Genetics of Sepsis-induced ARDS Network
definition: A multicentre observational cohort of adult patients of European ancestry with sepsis of any cause admitted to a network of intensive care units in Spain, recruited through the GEN-SEP Network of Spanish investigators in two periods (2002–2015 and 2016–2019) and followed for the development of acute respiratory distress syndrome and for 28-day survival, whose DNA is used in genetic studies of sepsis-associated ARDS and sepsis outcomes.
diseases: patients with: acute respiratory distress syndrome (MONDO:0006502)|patients with: infectious disease with sepsis (MONDO:1040015)

label: Genetics of Early Onset Stroke Study
other synonyms: Genetics of Early Onset Stroke|Genetics of Early Onset Stroke study|Genetics of Early-Onset Stroke|Genetics of Early-Onset Stroke Study|genetics of early onset stroke study|genetics of early-onset stroke study
definition: A population-based case–control study of early-onset ischaemic stroke, run from the University of Maryland, Baltimore, that recruited women and men aged 15–49 with a first ischaemic stroke, identified by discharge surveillance at 59 hospitals of the greater Baltimore–Washington area of the United States and by referral from regional neurologists, in four periods between 1992 and 2008, together with controls without stroke found by random-digit dialling and matched on age and region of residence, in a biracial sample of European American and African American participants; it was designed to identify the genetic determinants of early-onset ischaemic stroke and their interactions with environmental risk factors.

label: Genetics of Osteoarthritis Consortium
other synonyms: GO Consortium|Genetics of Osteoarthritis|Genetics of Osteoarthritis consortium
definition: A global collaboration that aims to bring together all available genetic studies of osteoarthritis, meta-analysing genome-wide association data on osteoarthritis at different joint sites (hip, knee, hand, finger, thumb and spine) and related traits from its contributing cohorts and biobanks in Europe, East Asia, North America and Australia, among them UK Biobank, arcOGEN, deCODE, the HUNT Study, the Estonian Biobank, the Rotterdam Study, FinnGen and the Million Veteran Program.

label: Genetics of Childhood Cancer Treatment
definition: A multinational retrospective cohort of paediatric cancer patients treated between 1975 and 2020 at hospitals in the Netherlands, Italy and Australia, made up of osteosarcoma and brain tumour cohorts and mostly treated with cisplatin or carboplatin, assembled by the Genetics of Childhood Cancer Treatment consortium for pharmacogenetic research such as studies of platinum-induced hearing loss.
diseases: patients with: childhood malignant neoplasm (MONDO:0006517)|patients with: low grade glioma (MONDO:0021637)|patients with: medulloblastoma (MONDO:0007959)|patients with: osteosarcoma (MONDO:0009807)

label: Genetic Origin of Dupuytren Disease and Associated Fibromatosis study
other synonyms: Genetic Origin of Dupuytren Disease Study|Genetic Origin of Dupuytren Disease study
definition: A case collection of people with Dupuytren disease recruited from 2007 through plastic and hand surgery clinics in the Netherlands, with blood samples for DNA and surgeon-recorded clinical data such as age at onset, family history, bilateral and ectopic disease and recurrence, for genetic studies of Dupuytren disease.

label: Genetics of Impulsivity project
definition: A study of healthy young adults aged 18–30 of self-reported Caucasian, non-Hispanic ancestry with low levels of alcohol and drug use, recruited from the community at the University of Chicago and the University of Georgia in the United States, and from the Georgia site's undergraduate research pool, who completed a laboratory battery of impulsivity measures (delay discounting, response inhibition, risk-taking and impulsive personality traits) and gave saliva DNA for genotyping, to study the genetic basis of impulsivity.

label: Genetics of Latinos Diabetic Retinopathy
other synonyms: Genetics of Latinos Diabetic Retinopathy Study
definition: A family-based study of Latinos of Mexican or Central American origin in the Los Angeles area, run jointly by Cedars-Sinai Medical Center and the Los Angeles Biomedical Research Institute at Harbor-UCLA Medical Center, which from 2007 recruited probands with type 2 diabetes and either diabetic retinopathy or diabetes of at least ten years' duration together with their siblings and parents, with retinopathy graded from fundus photographs, to study the genetics of diabetic retinopathy and other complications of diabetes.
diseases: patients with: diabetic retinopathy (MONDO:0005266)|patients with: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: Global Parkinson's Genetics Program
other synonyms: Global Parkinson's Disease Genetics Program
definition: A worldwide programme, the first resource project of the Aligning Science Across Parkinson's initiative, that genotypes and sequences people with Parkinson's disease, and some controls, from existing and newly collected patient and cohort collections, working with established Parkinson's disease consortia and focusing on populations under-represented in genetic research, and shares the harmonised data to find genetic causes of and risk factors for typical and monogenic Parkinson's disease.

label: Genomic Research on Asthma in the African Diaspora
other synonyms: Genomic Research on Asthma in the African Diaspora study
definition: A case-control collection of self-reported African American children and adults with physician-diagnosed asthma and non-asthmatic controls from the Baltimore–Washington, DC metropolitan area, brought together by the Genomic Research on Asthma in the African Diaspora consortium from eight NIH-funded asthma studies and one study of healthy African Americans, to study genetic contributions to asthma and its disparities in people of African descent.

label: Genomic Research in Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency and Sarcoidosis Study
other synonyms: Genomic Research in Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency and Sarcoidosis study
definition: A multicentre observational study in the United States, solicited by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute and run by a genomics and informatics centre with several clinical centres, that enrolled adults with sarcoidosis across defined clinical phenotypes and adults over 35 with the PiZZ or PiMZ alpha-1 antitrypsin genotypes, with questionnaires, chest CT, lung function tests, bronchoalveolar lavage and blood samples, to study the role of the lung microbiome and genome-wide gene expression in the two diseases.
diseases: patients with: alpha 1-antitrypsin deficiency (MONDO:0013282)|patients with: sarcoidosis (MONDO:0019338)

label: Genomics of Resistance to Immunodeficiency Virus
other synonyms: Genetics of Resistance to Immunodeficiency Virus
definition: A collection of DNA samples, established in France in 1995, from HIV-1-infected people of European descent living in France with extreme courses of infection: long-term non-progressors (infected for more than eight years with CD4 T-cell counts above 500/mm3 and no symptoms) and rapid progressors. It is used to identify host genes associated with slow and rapid progression to AIDS, with genetic analyses comparing its members with seronegative French controls from another study.
diseases: patients with: AIDS (MONDO:0012268)|patients with: HIV infectious disease (MONDO:0005109)

label: Guangzhou Twin Eye Study
other synonyms: Guangzhou Twins Eye Study|Guangzhou twin eye study
definition: A longitudinal twin study in Guangzhou, China, that from 2006 enrolled twin pairs aged 7 to 15 years from the population-based Guangzhou Twin Registry, living near the Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center, together with some of their parents or siblings. It collected DNA and baseline eye measurements, then examined the twins annually until 2018 for progressive traits such as cycloplegic refraction, axial length, height and weight, to study the genetic and environmental causes of common eye diseases, particularly myopia.
diseases: population study of: eye disorder (MONDO:0005328)|population study of: glaucoma (MONDO:0005041)|population study of: myopia (MONDO:0001384)

label: Guangzhou cohort
definition: A cohort of high myopes and hyperopes recruited in Guangzhou, China, one of three Chinese cohorts combined in a genome-wide association meta-analysis of ocular axial length.
diseases: patients with: High myopia (HP:0011003)|patients with: hyperopia (MONDO:0004891)

label: Guangzhou Colorectal Cancer Study
other synonyms: Asian Consortium, Colorectal Cancer Guangzhou|Guangzhou CRC Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of colorectal cancer in Guangzhou, China. Its cases are patients with histopathologically confirmed colorectal cancer recruited at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center between 2002 and 2012, and its controls are cancer-free men and women recruited in the same period from the physical examination centres of several large hospitals in Guangdong. Its four case-control collections (Guangzhou-1 to Guangzhou-4) were genotyped for genome-wide association studies of colorectal cancer in East Asians.

label: Hemophilia Growth and Development Study
definition: A multicentre longitudinal study, established in 1988 at 14 hemophilia treatment centres in the United States, of boys and young men aged 6 to 19 years with moderate to severe hemophilia, HIV-infected through clotting factor concentrates or HIV-uninfected, with their non-hemophiliac, HIV-uninfected male siblings as a comparison group, followed until 1996/97 to study the impact of HIV on physical growth and sexual maturation, immune function, and neurological and neuropsychological functioning.
diseases: patients with: HIV infectious disease (MONDO:0005109)|patients with: hemophilia (MONDO:0018660)

label: Hordaland Health Study
other synonyms: Helseundersøkelsen i Hordaland|Helseundersøkelsene i Hordaland|Hordaland Health Studies
definition: A population-based health study of residents of Hordaland County in Western Norway, begun in 1992-93 as the Hordaland Homocysteine Study by the Norwegian Health Screening Service, the University of Bergen and the Municipal Health Service in Hordaland, which invited residents by year of birth and place of residence, re-examined part of them together with further birth cohorts in 1997-99, and since 2018 has re-examined those born in 1950-51 who took part in both surveys, to study chronic diseases such as cardiovascular disease, cancer, osteoporosis, anxiety and depression and their prevention.

label: Hong Kong Children Eye Study
definition: A population-based cohort study of eye conditions, run by the Chinese University of Hong Kong since 2015, that recruits ethnic Chinese children aged 6 to 8 years from randomly selected primary schools across Hong Kong, together with their parents, and follows the children up, to determine the occurrence and development of refractive errors, strabismus, amblyopia and other eye disorders and their environmental and genetic determinants.
diseases: population study of: allergic disease (MONDO:0005271)|population study of: amblyopia (MONDO:0001020)|population study of: eye disorder (MONDO:0005328)|population study of: refractive error (MONDO:0004892)|population study of: strabismus (MONDO:0003432)

label: Hong Kong Diabetes Biobank
definition: A multicentre prospective cohort and biobank of adults with diabetes, started in 2014 and coordinated by the Chinese University of Hong Kong, which enrols people attending routine diabetes complication assessment at the diabetes centres of major public hospitals across Hong Kong, with the assessment methods of the Hong Kong Diabetes Register, and follows them for diabetes-related outcomes, to serve as a territory-wide diabetes register and biobank for epidemiological research and for the discovery and replication of genetic, epigenetic and other biomarkers of diabetes and its complications.

label: Healthy Zhejiang One Million People Cohort
other synonyms: HOPE Cohort|Healthy Zhejiang One Million Cohort
definition: A newly established community-based prospective cohort in Zhejiang Province, China, which since June 2021 has been enrolling participants from urban and rural areas at several project sites, among them people attending routine physical examinations, and collecting blood and serum at enrolment.

label: Health and Prevention Enhancement
other synonyms: Health and Prevention Enhancement cohort|Health and Prevention Enhancement study
definition: A retrospective, population-based cohort of Koreans who had health check-ups at the Healthcare System Gangnam Center of Seoul National University Hospital in Seoul, South Korea, from October 2003, with repeated check-up data, advanced diagnostic imaging and record linkage for cancer and death, designed to investigate the association of diagnostic imaging results and biomarkers with the predisease stage of non-communicable diseases such as cancers and metabolic diseases in an average-risk population.

label: Initiative on Nephropathy, of relevance to public health, which is Chronic, possibly in its Initial stages, and carries a Potential risk of major clinical End-points
other synonyms: INCIPE (NE Italy CKD and Nephropathy Study)|INCIPE study|Initiative on Nephropathy, of relevance to public health, which is Chronic, possibly in its Initial stages, and carries a Potential risk of major clinical Endpoints
definition: A population-based survey of Caucasian adults aged 40 years or older, randomly selected in 2006 from the patient lists of randomly chosen general practitioners in four areas of the Veneto region (Verona, Padova and Venice) in north-eastern Italy, with centralised laboratory measurement of kidney function and albuminuria, set up at the University of Verona to determine the prevalence of chronic kidney disease and its risk factors; two subsets of its participants were genotyped for genetic studies.
diseases: population study of: chronic kidney disease (MONDO:0005300)

label: International Stuttering Project
definition: A continually recruiting collection of people with clinically ascertained developmental stuttering, assembled by the International Stuttering Project, a collaboration of researchers and clinicians in the United States, Australia and Ireland formed in 2020 to illuminate the genetic aetiology of stuttering, which recruits through stuttering clinics, research laboratories and stuttering associations in these countries and online and genotypes its participants at Vanderbilt University Medical Center.

label: INTERHEART study
other synonyms: A Global Study of Risk Factors for Acute Myocardial Infarction|INTERHEART Study
definition: A standardised case-control study of first acute myocardial infarction, which from February 1999 to March 2003 enrolled patients presenting to hospital with a first myocardial infarction and age- and sex-matched hospital- or community-based controls without heart disease at 262 centres in 52 countries on every inhabited continent, to establish the importance of modifiable and psychosocial risk factors for myocardial infarction in all regions of the world.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to Physical Activity (ECTO:6000039)|designed to study: exposure to alcohol consumption (ECTO:0001082)|designed to study: exposure to eating behavior (ECTO:6000021)|designed to study: exposure to smoking (ECTO:6000013)|designed to study: exposure to social circumstances (ECTO:6000027)

label: International Tuberculosis Host Genetics Consortium
definition: A consortium established to study the host genetics of tuberculosis through collaborative, equitable data sharing, combining case-control genome-wide association studies from nine countries across Europe, Africa and Asia in a multi-ancestry meta-analysis of tuberculosis susceptibility.

label: Indiana University-Purdue University Indianapolis cohort
other synonyms: IUPUI cohort|IUPUI dataset|IUPUI sample|Indiana University-Purdue University Indianapolis|US Indiana Study
definition: A collection of 3D facial images, self-reported age, height, weight and ancestry, and DNA from volunteers recruited without restriction on ancestry (minors with a parent's or guardian's consent) in Indianapolis, Indiana and in Twinsburg, Ohio under one Indiana University-Purdue University Indianapolis ethics protocol, with support from the US National Institute of Justice, and genotyped to study the genetics of facial shape and of other visible traits such as head hair shape.

label: International Warfarin Pharmacogenetics Consortium
definition: A consortium of research groups in North and South America, Europe and Asia, formed with the Pharmacogenomics Knowledge Base (PharmGKB) as its data broker, that pools and curates the clinical and genetic data of warfarin-treated patients from its members' centres, to develop and evaluate pharmacogenetic algorithms for estimating the stable warfarin dose and to study the genetic determinants of warfarin dose across populations, including a genome-wide association study of African Americans from its US sites.

label: Karolinska Breast Cancer Study
other synonyms: KARBAC cohort|KARBAC study
definition: A breast cancer case-control study in Stockholm, Sweden, whose cases are consecutive breast cancer patients treated at the oncology departments of Huddinge and Söder hospitals from 1998 to 2000 and women with familial breast cancer without BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations seen at the Department of Clinical Genetics of Karolinska University Hospital from 2000, and whose controls are blood donors from the same region, used to study inherited susceptibility to breast cancer.

label: Korea National Cancer Center gastric cancer case-control study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of gastric cancer at the National Cancer Center in Goyang, South Korea, that from March 2011 to December 2014 recruited patients recently diagnosed with gastric cancer at its Center for Gastric Cancer as cases and cancer-free people attending health-screening check-ups at its Center for Cancer Prevention and Detection as controls, with lifestyle and food-frequency questionnaires and blood DNA genotyped on an exome array, to study dietary and genetic risk factors for gastric cancer.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to antioxidant via ingestion (ECTO:0900200)|designed to study: exposure to mercury via ingestion (ECTO:0900006)

label: Korea-NCC (National Cancer Center) Colorectal Cancer Study
other synonyms: Korea National Cancer Center Study|Korean-National Cancer Center CRC Study|Korean-National Cancer Center Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of colorectal cancer at the National Cancer Center in Goyang, South Korea, whose cases are patients newly diagnosed with colorectal cancer at its Center for Colorectal Cancer from 2010 and whose controls are people attending the national health check-up programme at its Center for Cancer Prevention and Detection, with lifestyle and food-frequency questionnaires and genome-wide genotyping, contributing to the Asia Colorectal Cancer Consortium's studies of genetic susceptibility to colorectal cancer.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to vitamin B via ingestion (ECTO:0900029)

label: Low Concentration Atropine for Myopia Progression Study
other synonyms: LAMP Study|Low-Concentration Atropine for Myopia Progression Study
definition: A randomised, double-masked, placebo-controlled trial at the Chinese University of Hong Kong Eye Centre that from 2016 to 2017 enrolled children aged 4 to 12 with myopia in both eyes, limited astigmatism and documented myopic progression in the previous year, assigned them to nightly 0.05%, 0.025% or 0.01% atropine eye drops or placebo, and followed them in later phases (placebo switched to atropine, re-randomisation to continued treatment or washout, and longer-term follow-up), to evaluate the efficacy and safety of low-concentration atropine for slowing myopia progression.

label: Leipzig Childhood Obesity cohort
other synonyms: Extended Geno- and Phenotyping of Overweight and Obese Children and Adolescents|LEIPZIG Kids|Leipzig Childhood Obesity Cohort|Leipzig Childhood Obesity Study|Leipzig Obesity Childhood Cohort|Leipzig childhood obesity cohort
definition: An obesity-enriched cohort of children and adolescents from the Leipzig area, Germany, recruited through the paediatric obesity outpatient clinic of Leipzig University Medical Center and run by its Center for Pediatric Research, with oral glucose tolerance tests, serum and DNA samples collected at clinic visits and regular follow-up, some into adulthood, to identify genetic variants and biomarkers underlying childhood obesity and its metabolic consequences.

label: Lung Oncology Research & Discovery
other synonyms: Lung Oncology Research and Discovery
definition: An ongoing single-site, case-only cohort of patients who have undergone lung cancer surgery since 1999 at the Quebec Heart and Lung Institute (Institut universitaire de cardiologie et de pneumologie de Québec – Université Laval) in Quebec City, Canada, with diagnoses confirmed by pathology of the resected specimens, clinical data and consent to the institute's biobank, assembled by a translational research programme towards precision medicine in lung cancer and used for germline genetic and tumour molecular studies.

label: Multicenter AIDS Cohort Study
definition: A prospective multicentre cohort study of gay and bisexual men with and without HIV-1 infection, first enrolled in 1984–1985 at sites in Baltimore/Washington DC, Chicago, Pittsburgh and Los Angeles in the United States, with later enrolment waves, and followed with interviews, physical examinations, laboratory testing and specimen banking every six months, to study the natural and treated history of HIV infection and AIDS and its risk factors; in 2019 it was combined with the Women's Interagency HIV Study into the MACS/WIHS Combined Cohort Study.
diseases: at risk of: AIDS (MONDO:0012268)|at risk of: HIV infectious disease (MONDO:0005109)

label: Manchester Lung Health Check
other synonyms: Manchester Lung Health Check cohort
definition: A community-based targeted lung cancer screening programme in socioeconomically deprived areas of Manchester, England, run by Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust, which began as a pilot in 2016 and continued in later programmes. It invites ever-smokers registered with local general practices (aged 55–74 in the pilot, 55–80 later) to a nurse-led Lung Health Check on mobile units, with lung cancer risk calculation (PLCOm2012), symptom assessment, spirometry and smoking cessation advice, offers annual low-dose CT screening to those at high risk, and follows attendees for lung cancer outcomes.
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to tobacco smoking (ECTO:6000029)

label: Mayo Vascular Disease Biorepository
other synonyms: Mayo Clinic Vascular Disease Biorepository|Mayo Vascular diseases Biorepository|Vascular Disease Biorepository|Vascular Diseases Biorepository - Mayo Clinic
definition: An electronic medical record-linked biorepository at Mayo Clinic, begun in 2006, that archives DNA, plasma and serum and a questionnaire from consecutive adult patients with known or suspected atherosclerotic vascular disease (such as carotid artery stenosis, abdominal aortic aneurysm or peripheral arterial disease) referred for non-invasive vascular evaluation or exercise stress testing at the Mayo Clinic Gonda Vascular Center, ascertaining disease and comorbidities with electronic phenotyping algorithms, to discover genetic and circulating biomarkers of atherosclerotic vascular disease.

label: Manchester Cancer Research Centre Biobank
other synonyms: Manchester Cancer Research Centre
definition: A research tissue bank of the Manchester Cancer Research Centre, established in 2008 and run from The Christie NHS Foundation Trust, that collects tissue, blood and other samples, with consent to use them and data about the donors for research, from patients at four NHS trusts in Greater Manchester, mainly people undergoing surgery where cancer is a possible diagnosis, to supply samples for cancer research.

label: MELARISK study
other synonyms: MELARISK collection
definition: A French study of genetic susceptibility to cutaneous melanoma that recruited histologically confirmed melanoma patients of European ancestry, enrolled for a family history of melanoma, multiple primary melanomas or diagnosis before age 40, through a nationwide network of French dermatology departments and oncogenetic clinics between 1992 and 2011, with interview, clinical examination and questionnaire data on melanoma risk factors; in genome-wide association studies its cases were compared with population-based French controls.

label: Multicenter Hemophilia Cohort Studies
other synonyms: Multicenter Hemophilia Cohort Study
definition: A prospective cohort study of the US National Cancer Institute of people with hemophilia or related congenital coagulation disorders at hemophilia treatment centres: the first Multicenter Hemophilia Cohort Study (MHCS-I), begun in 1982 at 16 centres in the United States and Europe, followed its participants to study the cause and natural history of HIV infection and AIDS, and the second (MHCS-II) invited all HCV-seropositive patients aged 13 or older at 52 participating centres in 2001–2005, to quantify the impact of hepatitis C, hepatitis B and HIV infections.
diseases: patients with: HIV infectious disease (MONDO:0005109)|patients with: hemophilia (MONDO:0018660)|patients with: hepatitis B virus infection (MONDO:0005344)|patients with: hepatitis C virus infection (MONDO:0005231)

label: Myeloma XI trial
other synonyms: Myeloma XI|Myeloma-XI trial
definition: A UK open-label, randomised, phase 3 adaptive-design trial for patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma at 110 National Health Service hospitals in England, Wales and Scotland, recruiting from 2010, which assigned patients by age and fitness to intensive (transplantation) or non-intensive pathways and had three randomisation stages, including induction regimens and lenalidomide maintenance against observation.

label: MRC Myeloma IX trial
other synonyms: Medical Research Council Myeloma IX trial|Myeloma IX|Myeloma-IX trial
definition: A UK Medical Research Council open-label randomised trial that enrolled adults aged 18 or older with newly diagnosed symptomatic multiple myeloma at 120 UK centres between May 2003 and November 2007, allocating them to an intensive pathway (induction followed by high-dose melphalan and autologous stem-cell transplantation) or a non-intensive pathway, and randomising first-line bisphosphonate (zoledronic versus clodronic acid) with induction chemotherapy and, later, maintenance treatment.

label: Mexican Genomic Database for Addiction Research
definition: A genomic database drawn from the second phase of the 2016 Mexican National Survey of Tobacco, Alcohol, and Drug Use (Encodat 2016), a nationwide household survey that excluded regions where most people speak a Native American language, whose participants answered questionnaires on substance use and psychiatric symptoms and gave buccal DNA samples, assembled by Mexico's National Institute of Psychiatry Ramón de la Fuente Muñiz and National Institute of Genomic Medicine for genetic studies of addiction and related psychiatric and pharmacogenetic traits.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to Tobacco Use (ECTO:6000041)|designed to study: exposure to alcohol consumption (ECTO:0001082)|designed to study: exposure to drug abuse (ECTO:6000008)

label: Nicotine Addiction Genetics Finland study
other synonyms: Finnish Nicotine Addiction Genetics Project|Nicotine Addiction Genetics - Finland study|Nicotine Addiction Genetics-Finland study
definition: The Finnish arm of the multisite Nicotine Addiction Genetics consortium (Finland, Australia and the United States), in which twin pairs from the older Finnish Twin Cohort (born 1938–1957) concordant for ever-smoking, with priority to heavier smokers, were recruited in 2001–2005 together with their family members, mainly siblings, and assessed by a structured diagnostic psychiatric interview and DNA sampling to study the genetics of smoking behaviour and nicotine dependence.
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to tobacco smoking (ECTO:6000029)

label: Netherlands Study of Cognition, Environment and Genes
other synonyms: Netherlands Study of Cognition|Netherlands Study on Cognition, Environment and Genes
definition: A Dutch study of individual differences in cognition and cognition-related disorders. It has a general-population sample of volunteers recruited through media advertisements or the Science Live research programme of the NEMO Science Center in Amsterdam, who performed cognitive tasks and completed an online questionnaire on life events, personality, environment and behaviour, and a genetically informative family sample of twins and their siblings.

label: UK Nephropathy Family Study and Oxford Regional Prospective Study
definition: A combined sample of two cohorts of young people with childhood-onset type 1 diabetes in England, analysed as one study in genome-wide association studies of diabetic kidney disease and type 1 diabetes. The Oxford Regional Prospective Study recruited children diagnosed with type 1 diabetes before the age of 16 in the Oxford Health Authority region in 1986–1996. The Nephropathy Family Study recruited adolescents aged 10–16 years with type 1 diabetes, and their parents, in four English regions in 2000–2005. Both cohorts were followed with annual measurements of HbA1c and the urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio.
diseases: patients with: diabetic kidney disease (MONDO:0005016)|patients with: type 1 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005147)

label: Nephropathy Family Study
other synonyms: UK Nephropathy Family Study
definition: A longitudinal study of young people with type 1 diabetes in England, set up in 2000 within the Genetic Resource Investigating Diabetes (GRID) study of the JDRF/Wellcome Trust Diabetes and Inflammation Laboratory. In 2000–2005 it recruited adolescents aged 10–16 years who had developed type 1 diabetes before the age of 16 in East Anglia, Birmingham, Bristol and Oxford, together with their parents. It followed them with annual urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratios and HbA1c measurements for phenotypic and genetic study of the early pathogenesis of microalbuminuria.
diseases: patients with: Moderate albuminuria (HP:0012594)|patients with: type 1 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005147)

label: Nigerian Breast Cancer Study
other synonyms: Nigerian breast cancer study
definition: A case-control study of breast cancer in women aged 18 or older, begun in 1998 in Ibadan, Nigeria. Women with invasive breast cancer are recruited at University College Hospital, Ibadan (from 2014 also at Lagos State University Teaching Hospital). Women without cancer are enrolled as controls from the hospital's outpatient clinics and from communities randomly selected in its catchment area. Enrolment was extended to Cameroon and Uganda in 2011 with the same questionnaire and protocol. It collects questionnaire data and biospecimens to study epidemiological and inherited risk factors for breast cancer in African women.

label: National Joint Registry
other synonyms: National Joint Registry for England and Wales|National Joint Registry for England, Wales, Northern Ireland, and the Isle of Man|National Joint Registry for England, Wales, Northern Ireland, the Isle of Man and the States of Guernsey
definition: A national registry of joint replacement surgery, set up by the Department of Health and the Welsh Government, that has recorded hip and knee replacements since April 2003 (ankle, elbow and shoulder replacements since 2010–2012) in NHS and independent hospitals in England and Wales, joined by Northern Ireland in 2013, the Isle of Man in 2015, Guernsey in 2019 and Jersey in 2025. Each procedure is recorded with the implant used and, with the patient's consent, the patient's details, to monitor the outcomes of implants, hospitals and surgeons.

label: National Psoriasis Victor Henschel BioBank
other synonyms: Henschel Biobank|National Psoriasis Foundation Victor Henschel Tissue Repository|National Psoriasis Victor Henschel Biobank|Victor Henschel Biobank
definition: A biobank of biological samples, including DNA, and clinical information from volunteers in the United States with psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis and from unaffected controls. The National Psoriasis Foundation created it in 2006, with the financial backing of the Henschel family, to advance genetic research on psoriatic disease. Its samples were made available to researchers internationally for case-control and family studies until the biobank was retired in 2025.
diseases: patients with: psoriasis (MONDO:0005083)|patients with: psoriatic arthritis (MONDO:0011849)

label: National Survey of Physical Traits
other synonyms: National Survey of Physical Traits Project|National Survey of Physical Traits Study
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of Han Chinese adults, a sub-project of China's National Science & Technology Basic Research Project, recruited as volunteers in four sub-cohorts in Taizhou (Jiangsu province; 2015 and 2019), Zhengzhou (Henan province; 2017) and Nanning (Guangxi province; 2018). Participants were photographed and assessed for physical traits such as facial, ear and fingerprint features, and gave blood for genotyping and for DNA methylation, proteomic and metabolomic profiling, to study the genetic and molecular basis of human physical traits and common diseases.

label: New York Genome Center ALS Consortium
other synonyms: NYGC ALS Consortium|NYGC ALS consortium|The New York Genome Center's ALS Consortium
definition: A consortium formed in 2015 around the New York Genome Center, through which 41 ALS clinics and research institutions in the United States, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, Greece and Israel contribute blood and post-mortem brain and spinal cord tissue from people with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, other neurological diseases and non-neurological controls. The samples are whole-genome and RNA sequenced at the New York Genome Center and their clinical data harmonised into an openly accessible genomic resource for ALS research.

label: NZ AAA Genetics Study
other synonyms: New Zealand (NZ) Vascular Genetics Study AAA GWAS dataset|New Zealand Vascular Genetic Study AAA GWAS dataset
definition: A case-control study of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) in New Zealand. The Vascular Research Consortium of New Zealand recruited men and women with AAA (infrarenal aortic diameter of at least 30 mm on ultrasound or CT scan, about 80% after surgical repair), nearly all of Anglo-European ancestry, and elderly Anglo-European controls in whom AAA was excluded by abdominal ultrasound and who were also screened for peripheral and carotid artery disease. Its participants were genotyped in two genome-wide case-control sets for genetic studies of AAA.

label: Pancreatic Cancer Case-Control Consortium
other synonyms: International Pancreatic Cancer Case-Control Consortium|The Pancreatic Cancer Case-Control Consortium
definition: An international consortium that pools data from case-control studies of pancreatic cancer, conducted in North America, Europe, China and Australia, to study risk factors such as tobacco and alcohol use, diabetes and pancreatitis; cases and controls from several member studies were also genotyped together for a genome-wide association study of pancreatic cancer.

label: UPenn Local TGCT Study
other synonyms: Inherited Genetic Variation and Predisposition to Testicular Germ Cell Tumor: UPenn Local TGCT Study|Penn GWAS
definition: A case-control study of inherited susceptibility to testicular germ cell tumour at the University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, whose genome-wide association scan compared men with testicular germ cell tumour seen at the University of Pennsylvania Health System or Fox Chase Cancer Center with male controls from the Philadelphia region drawn from the PennCATH study.
diseases: patients with: testicular germ cell tumor (MONDO:0010108)

label: Phenotype, Genotype & Biomarkers in ALS and Related Disorders
other synonyms: CReATe Consortium's Phenotype-Genotype-Biomarker study|Phenotype Genotype Biomarker study|Phenotype-Genotype and Biomarker Study of the CReATe Consortium|Phenotype-Genotype-Biomarker study
definition: A prospective, longitudinal observational study of the CReATe Consortium (Clinical Research in ALS and Related Disorders for Therapeutic Development), led from the University of Miami, that from 2014 enrolled patients with familial or sporadic amyotrophic lateral sclerosis or a related disorder (primary lateral sclerosis, progressive muscular atrophy, hereditary spastic paraplegia, frontotemporal dementia or multisystem proteinopathy), and some of their family members, at clinical sites in the United States, South Africa and Germany, with repeated motor, cognitive and functional assessments and collection of blood, urine and cerebrospinal fluid, to study phenotype-genotype relationships and develop biomarkers for therapy development.
diseases: patients with: amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (MONDO:0004976)|patients with: hereditary spastic paraplegia (MONDO:0019064)|patients with: lateral sclerosis (MONDO:0018155)|patients with: progressive muscular atrophy (MONDO:0018687)

label: PLATelet inhibition and patient Outcomes
other synonyms: PLATO trial|PLATelet Inhibition and Patient Outcomes|PLATelet inhibition and patient Outcomes trial|Platelet Inhibition and Patient Outcomes
definition: An international, phase III, randomised, double-blind trial funded by AstraZeneca that enrolled patients hospitalised with acute coronary syndrome (ST-elevation ACS scheduled for primary percutaneous coronary intervention, or non-ST-elevation ACS) at 862 centres in 43 countries between October 2006 and July 2008, to compare ticagrelor with clopidogrel for preventing death from vascular causes, myocardial infarction and stroke; blood samples from its genetic and biomarker substudies have been used for genome-wide association studies.

label: Pustular Psoriasis, Elucidating Underlying Mechanisms
other synonyms: Pustular psoriasis: eLucidating Underlying Mechanisms
definition: A UK research study sponsored by Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust and run as the sister mechanistic study of the APRICOT trial of anakinra, which recruited people with pustular psoriasis through specialist dermatology centres across the UK, together with disease controls, healthy volunteers and patients' relatives, and collected blood and optional skin and hair samples to identify genes, immune pathways and treatment responses involved in pustular psoriasis.

label: Primary Open-Angle African American Glaucoma Genetics Study
other synonyms: Primary Open-Angle African American Glaucoma Genetics study|primary open-angle African American glaucoma genetics study
definition: A case-control genetic study of primary open-angle glaucoma led by the University of Pennsylvania's Scheie Eye Institute, which since July 2010 has enrolled self-identified Black adults (African American, African descent or African Caribbean) aged 35 or over from the Philadelphia region, mainly from University of Pennsylvania eye clinics and also through community screenings, two other Philadelphia ophthalmology practices and the Penn Medicine Biobank, with glaucoma specialists classifying them as cases, controls or glaucoma suspects, to identify genetic and clinical risk factors for the disease.

label: Project MinE
other synonyms: Project MinE ALS Sequencing Consortium|Project MinE ALS sequencing Consortium|Project MinE ALS sequencing consortium
definition: An international collaboration of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis research groups from about 16 countries, coordinated from the ALS Centre Netherlands at University Medical Center Utrecht and begun with a pilot in Dutch patients, in which people with ALS and matched controls are recruited through the groups' ALS clinics under a common protocol with a standardised core clinical data set and their whole genomes sequenced, to identify and fine-map genetic risk loci for ALS and share the data with researchers.

label: Pulmonary Hypertension and the Hypoxic Response in Sickle Cell Disease
other synonyms: Pulmonary Hypertension and Hypoxic Response in Sickle Cell Disease|Pulmonary Hypertension and the Hypoxic Response in SCD
definition: A prospective multicentre observational study of children and adolescents aged 3–20 years with sickle cell disease, examined at steady state, and of controls without the disease matched by age, sex and ethnicity, recruited at Howard University Hospital and Children's National Medical Center in Washington, DC, and the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, with echocardiography, six-minute walk tests and blood markers, designed to identify factors in pre-symptomatic children that predict pulmonary hypertension and other cardiopulmonary complications.
diseases: patients with: pulmonary hypertension (MONDO:0005149)|patients with: sickle cell disease (MONDO:0011382)

label: Queen Square Brain Bank for Neurological Disorders
other synonyms: Queen Square Brain Bank
definition: A research tissue bank at the UCL Queen Square Institute of Neurology in London that archives brains and other tissue from donors across the UK, registered through its donor scheme during life, who had neurological and mostly neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson's disease, multiple system atrophy and progressive supranuclear palsy, and from neurologically normal controls, and supplies well-characterised tissue and data for research.
diseases: patients with: nervous system disorder (MONDO:0005071)|patients with: neurodegenerative disease (MONDO:0005559)

label: Genome-Wide Association Study on Calcific Aortic Valve Stenosis in Quebec
other synonyms: Calcific Aortic Valve Stenosis in Quebec
definition: A case-control study of calcific aortic valve stenosis at the Institut universitaire de cardiologie et de pneumologie de Québec – Université Laval, Canada, in which blood and aortic valve tissue are collected from patients undergoing aortic valve replacement for the disease and compared with controls (in its first phase, patients without valve disease undergoing cardiac surgery, mostly coronary artery bypass, at the same institute; in its second, CARTaGENE participants without valvular heart disease), to identify genetic susceptibility to the disease; its valve tissues, collected in 1998–2019, are also used for gene expression studies.

label: REDS-III Brazil Sickle Cell Disease Cohort
other synonyms: Brazil SCD Cohort Study|Brazil Sickle Cell Disease Cohort Study|REDS-III Brazil SCD Cohort|REDS-III Brazil SCD cohort study|Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study III Brazil Cohort Study
definition: A cohort of children and adults with sickle cell disease, randomly sampled from the active patients of six care sites in the Brazilian states of Minas Gerais (Belo Horizonte, Juiz de Fora and Montes Claros), Rio de Janeiro, Pernambuco (Recife) and São Paulo and enrolled in 2013–2015 as the Brazilian component of the NHLBI REDS-III programme, with clinical data, a blood biorepository and genome-wide genotyping, to characterise the clinical and transfusion outcomes of sickle cell disease in Brazil and support genotype–phenotype studies.

label: Raine Eye Health Study
other synonyms: Raine eye health study|Western Australian Pregnancy (Raine) Cohort 20 year follow up Eye Study|Western Australian Pregnancy Cohort (Raine) Eye Health Study
definition: The eye study of the offspring (Generation 2) of the Raine Study pregnancy cohort in Western Australia, in which participants completed a comprehensive eye assessment at the cohort's 20-year follow-up, including visual acuity, orthoptic assessment, cycloplegic autorefraction, ocular biometry and anterior and posterior segment photography, to determine the prevalence of and risk factors for eye disease in young adults and characterise their ocular biometric parameters.

label: Racial Variability in Genotypic Determinants of Breast Cancer Risk Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of breast cancer conducted in the Philadelphia and Detroit metropolitan areas of the United States from 1999 to 2003, whose cases, diagnosed with invasive ductal breast cancer within 18 months of recruitment and over-sampled for diagnosis before age 40, were identified in the University of Pennsylvania Health System and the Karmanos Cancer Institute or recruited through local advertisement, with controls without breast cancer recruited in the same way.

label: Genome-Wide Association Study of Adiposity in Samoans
other synonyms: Genome Wide Association Study of Adiposity in Samoans|Genome-wide Association Study of Adiposity in Samoans|Samoan Adiposity Study|Samoan Genome-Wide Association Study
definition: A population-based cross-sectional study of adults with four Samoan grandparents, recruited from February to July 2010 in 33 villages across all four census regions of the independent nation of Samoa (Apia Urban Area, Northwest Upolu, the rest of Upolu and Savai'i), with anthropometry, fasting blood biomarkers, dietary, physical activity, health and socio-demographic data and genome-wide genotyping, to identify genetic variation that increases susceptibility to obesity and cardiometabolic traits in Samoans.

label: Sanford Biobank
other synonyms: Sanford Health|Sanford Health BioBank|Sanford Health Biobank
definition: A hospital-based biobank of adult patients of Sanford Health, a rural health system of the Upper Midwest of the United States based in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, who since 2011 have elected to provide specimens for research, genotyped on the Illumina Global Screening Array and linked to the health system's clinical records for genetic studies such as of cardiovascular disease.

label: Salvador-SCAALA study
other synonyms: SCAALA cohort|SCAALA-Salvador|Salvador-SCAALA|Salvador-SCAALA project|Social Changes, Asthma, and Allergy in Latin America cohort
definition: A cohort of children from 24 low-income areas of Salvador, Bahia, in north-eastern Brazil, first enrolled aged 0–3 years in 1997, 2001 and 2003 to evaluate the health effects of the city's sanitation programme and followed from 2005, at ages 4–11, with further surveys (questionnaires, anthropometry, stool, blood and house-dust samples, skin prick tests and, later, genome-wide genotyping), to study social, environmental, infectious, immunological and genetic risk factors for asthma and allergic diseases; it is the Brazilian study of the Social Changes, Asthma and Allergy in Latin America (SCAALA) programme.
diseases: population study of: allergic disease (MONDO:0005271)|population study of: asthma (MONDO:0004979)
exposures: designed to study: exposure event (ExO:0000002)|designed to study: exposure to allergen via inhalation (ECTO:0900047)|designed to study: exposure to organism (ECTO:3000000)|designed to study: exposure to particulate matter (ECTO:7000068)

label: San Francisco City Clinic Cohort
other synonyms: San Francisco City Clinic Cohort Study|San Francisco City Clinic cohort
definition: A cohort of homosexual and bisexual men recruited in 1978–1980 at the San Francisco municipal sexually transmitted disease clinic for studies of sexually transmitted hepatitis B, whose stored serum specimens, follow-up examinations and questionnaires, and linkage to AIDS surveillance and death registries were later used to study the natural history, transmission and cofactors of HIV infection and AIDS.
diseases: at risk of: AIDS (MONDO:0012268)|at risk of: HIV infectious disease (MONDO:0005109)|at risk of: hepatitis B virus infection (MONDO:0005344)

label: Silent Cerebral Infarct Multi-Center Clinical Trial
other synonyms: Silent Cerebral Infarct Transfusion Trial|Silent Infarct Transfusion trial
definition: A multicentre, single-blind randomised clinical trial at 29 centres in the United States, Canada, France and the United Kingdom, which from December 2004 to May 2010 screened children aged 5 to 15 years with sickle cell anaemia (haemoglobin SS or Sβ0 thalassaemia) and no history of stroke by brain MRI, and randomly assigned those with silent cerebral infarcts to regular blood transfusions or standard care, to test whether transfusion therapy reduces the recurrence of cerebral infarcts.
diseases: patients with: cerebral infarction (MONDO:0002679)|patients with: sickle cell disease (MONDO:0011382)

label: Swiss Kidney Project on Genes in Hypertension
other synonyms: Swiss Kidney Project On Genes in Hypertension
definition: A multicentre family- and population-based study of adults of European descent in Switzerland, in which index participants drawn at random from population samples in the city of Lausanne (the CoLaus study), the canton of Geneva (the Bus Santé study) and the canton of Bern (the cantonal phone directory) were recruited from December 2009 to April 2013 together with their first-degree relatives and re-examined about three years later, to study genetic and environmental determinants of blood pressure, kidney function and other cardiometabolic outcomes; it is the Swiss part of the European Project on Genes in Hypertension.

label: SLOVENIA study
other synonyms: Slovenia study
definition: A clinical study of children and young people aged 5–18 of Slovenian origin with a physician diagnosis of mild-to-moderate persistent asthma and hospital records at tertiary health centres in Slovenia, part of them regularly treated with inhaled corticosteroids under medical supervision, with lung function measured after six weeks of inhaled corticosteroid treatment. It is one of the asthma studies enrolled in the Pharmacogenomics in Childhood Asthma (PiCA) consortium, which studies the genetics of response to asthma treatment.

label: Santiago Longitudinal Study
definition: A cohort of healthy, full-term infants from low- to middle-income neighbourhoods of Santiago, Chile, recruited through community clinics in 1991–1996 for an iron-deficiency anaemia preventive trial or a neuromaturation study, and followed up through childhood, adolescence and adulthood in studies of nutrition, development, substance use and cardiometabolic risk.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to iron supplementation (ECTO:2000097)|designed to study: exposure to nutrient (ECTO:9001695)

label: Shanghai Women's and Men's Health Studies
acronyms: SMWHS|SWHS/SMHS|SWMHS|Shanghai Men and Women's Health Studies
other synonyms: Shanghai Men and Women's Health Study|Shanghai Mens and Shanghai Womens Health Studies
definition: The Shanghai Women's Health Study and the Shanghai Men's Health Study taken together: two population-based prospective cohorts of middle-aged and elderly Chinese adults in urban Shanghai, China, which recruited women in 1996–2000 and men in 2002–2006 and whose data and biospecimens are often analysed jointly, for example in nested case–control and genome-wide association studies.

label: Swedish National Myeloma Biobank
other synonyms: Swedish Myeloma Biobank
definition: A national biobank of samples from patients with multiple myeloma in Sweden, based at Skåne University Hospital in Lund, whose patients' germline DNA has been genotyped for genome-wide association studies of inherited susceptibility to multiple myeloma.

label: Seoul National University Hospital Diabetes Study
definition: A case–control study of Korean patients with type 2 diabetes from the Diabetes Clinic of Seoul National University Hospital, South Korea, excluding patients positive for GAD antibodies, and of nondiabetic control subjects aged 60 or over with no history of diabetes in themselves or their first-degree relatives, used as a replication study in the Asian Genetic Epidemiology Network meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies of type 2 diabetes.

label: Hispanic Community Children's Health Study/Study of Latino Youth
other synonyms: Study of Latino Youth|Study of Latino Youth Study
definition: An ancillary study of the Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos that in 2012–2014 enrolled Hispanic/Latino children aged 8–16 whose parents or legal guardians took part in HCHS/SOL, at its field centres in the Bronx, Chicago, Miami and San Diego, United States, to examine how youth's lifestyle behaviours and cardiometabolic risk factors relate to acculturation, parenting and family behaviours, and psychosocial functioning.

label: Sao Paulo Heart Failure Cohort
other synonyms: Sao Paolo Heart Failure Cohort
definition: A cohort of adults with symptomatic (stage C) heart failure of different aetiologies, prospectively enrolled from the outpatient clinic of the Heart Institute of the University of São Paulo Medical School in São Paulo, Brazil. Its genotyped participants, with atrial fibrillation ascertained from electrocardiograms and medical records, have contributed to genome-wide association studies of atrial fibrillation.

label: Singapore Preconception Study of Long-Term Maternal and Child Outcomes
other synonyms: Singapore PREconception Study of long-Term maternal and child Outcomes
definition: A preconception, longitudinal cohort of Chinese, Malay or Indian women aged 18–45 who intended to conceive and deliver in Singapore, recruited in February 2015–October 2017 through a preconception clinic at KK Women's and Children's Hospital and through public outreach, and followed with their children from before conception through pregnancy into early childhood. Its aim is to study how nutrition, lifestyle and maternal mood before and during pregnancy affect the offspring's epigenome, duration of gestation, fetal growth, and metabolic and neural phenotypes.
exposures: designed to study: exposure event (ExO:0000002)|designed to study: exposure to lifestyle (ECTO:6000015)|designed to study: exposure to pregnancy diet intake (ECTO:2000076)

label: Swiss Pediatric Sepsis Study
definition: A nationwide, prospective, multicentre cohort of neonates and children younger than 17 with blood culture-proven bacterial sepsis meeting criteria for systemic inflammatory response syndrome, enrolled from September 2011 to December 2015 at ten tertiary and regional paediatric hospitals in Switzerland, including all five university centres and all paediatric intensive care units, to study the incidence, clinical features and outcomes of paediatric sepsis.
diseases: patients with: bacterial infectious disease with sepsis (MONDO:0005229)

label: Systematic Treatment Enhancement Program for Bipolar Disorder
definition: A long-term, multicentre study funded by the US National Institute of Mental Health that enrolled outpatients aged 15 or older with any subtype of bipolar disorder at 22 academic medical centres in the United States and followed them over seven years. All participants entered a naturalistic standard care pathway, with randomized care pathways for acute and refractory depression, to answer questions about the effectiveness of treatments for bipolar disorder.

label: Simultaneous Study of Gemcitabine-Docetaxel Combination adjuvant treatment, as well as Extended Bisphosphonate and Surveillance-Trial
other synonyms: SUCCESS A trial|SUCCESS-A study|SUCCESS-A trial|Simultaneous Study of Gemcitabine-Docetaxel Combination Adjuvant Treatment, as Well as Extended Bisphosphonate and Surveillance-Trial
definition: An open-label, multicentre, randomised phase III trial in Germany, sponsored by Ludwig-Maximilians-University Munich, that enrolled adult patients with invasive early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence from 2005 to 2007 and compared, in a 2×2 factorial design, adjuvant FEC–docetaxel chemotherapy with or without gemcitabine and two versus five years of zoledronic acid, with an affiliated translational research programme on circulating tumour cells, serum tumour markers and pharmacogenetics.

label: Seoul National University Prospectively Enrolled Registry for Renal Cell Carcinoma-Nephrectomy
other synonyms: SUPER-RCC-Nephrectomy|Seoul National University Prospectively Enrolled Registry for RCC-Nephrectomy
definition: A prospective, biobank-linked registry at Seoul National University Hospital, South Korea, that since March 2016 has enrolled patients clinically diagnosed with renal cell carcinoma who undergo surgical treatment (ablation, or partial, radical or cytoreductive nephrectomy), collecting standardised clinical, pathological, quality-of-life and survival data and blood and tumour samples stored in the hospital's Human Biobank. It is the nephrectomy sub-cohort of the renal cell carcinoma arm (SUPER-RCC) of the Seoul National University Prospectively Enrolled Registry for Genitourinary Cancer (SUPER-GUC).

label: Triple A Barcelona Study
other synonyms: Triple-A Barcelona Study
definition: A prospective, hospital-based longitudinal registry, started in 2019, of consecutive individuals with abdominal aortic aneurysm seen at the vascular and endovascular surgery units of the Hospital de la Santa Creu i Sant Pau and the Hospital del Mar in Barcelona, Spain, with aortic diameter measurements by CT or ultrasound, clinical data and DNA, RNA and plasma samples collected at follow-up visits, to study aneurysm growth and its predictors and to inform surveillance intervals.

label: Trans-National Asthma Genetic Consortium
definition: A consortium of research groups worldwide, established to increase sample sizes for genome-wide association meta-analysis of asthma, that pooled asthma genome-wide association studies of European, African, Japanese and Latino ancestry, among them studies of the GABRIEL, EVE, EAGLE, APCAT, CARe and Australian Asthma Genetics consortia, into a multi-ancestry meta-analysis, with a separate analysis of childhood-onset asthma, to identify asthma risk loci.

label: LITMUS Metacohort
other synonyms: EPoS Consortium|LITMUS metacohort|The European NAFLD Registry-Metacohort
definition: The part of the European NAFLD Registry, a prospective observational cohort of adults with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease sponsored by Newcastle University, made up of patients with biopsy-characterised NAFLD who were recruited at liver centres across Europe from 2010 to December 2017 in the FLIP, EPoS and HEPAmet studies of NAFLD pathogenesis, or came from earlier single-centre cohorts, and used by the IMI2 LITMUS project to evaluate non-invasive biomarkers. Patients recruited since 2018 form the Registry's separate LITMUS Study Cohort.
diseases: patients with: metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MONDO:0013209)

label: Brain Bank for Aging Research
other synonyms: Brain Bank for Aging Research, Tokyo Metropolitan Institute for Geriatrics and Gerontology
definition: A brain bank at the Tokyo Metropolitan Geriatric Hospital and Institute of Gerontology in Tokyo, Japan, which registers, with the consent of relatives, the brains and other tissues of consecutive autopsies of patients of the hospital, which provides community-based general and emergency care to older people, together with their clinical data, for clinicopathological and genetic research on ageing-related neurodegenerative, movement and cognitive disorders.
diseases: population study of: Mental deterioration (HP:0001268)|population study of: movement disorder (MONDO:0005395)

label: Tasmanian Ophthalmic Biobank
definition: A biobank of the Menzies Institute for Medical Research at the University of Tasmania, run with the Royal Hobart Hospital and associated public and private eye clinics in Tasmania, Australia, that collects DNA samples and clinical information from Tasmanian residents diagnosed with a range of eye diseases, and from adults without eye disease recruited from the community as controls, to investigate eye disease.

label: Transcriptomic Analysis of Left Ventricular Gene Expression
other synonyms: TRANSCRIBE Program|TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression|Whole Genome Expression of Left Ventricular Myocardium During Cardiac Surgery
definition: A prospective cohort at Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston, United States, begun in 2009, of adults undergoing aortic valve surgery with or without coronary artery bypass grafting, from whom left ventricular myocardium is biopsied at the apical vent site at the start and end of the ischaemic period of cardiopulmonary bypass, together with blood and DNA, to study how genetic variation shapes cardiac gene expression and its response to ischaemia.

label: Trondheim Parkinson's Disease Study
other synonyms: Trondheim PD Cohort|Trondheim PD cohort|Trondheim Parkinson's disease study
definition: A prospective longitudinal cohort of patients with Parkinson's disease, collected since 1997 from sequential new referrals to the Department of Neurology at St. Olav's Hospital in Trondheim, Norway (some followed since 1980), most living within about 50 miles of Trondheim, established mainly for genetic studies of Parkinson's disease and followed for disease course, cognition and survival.

label: Taiwan Super Control Study
definition: A population-based sample of Han Chinese individuals in Taiwan, selected at random from the healthy controls of the Taiwan Han Chinese Cell and Genome Bank, who had been recruited by stratified three-stage probability cluster sampling through the registry of the non-aboriginal townships and city districts of Taiwan. It was genotyped genome-wide with support from the Academia Sinica Genomic Medicine Multicenter Study.

label: Taizhou Longitudinal Study
other synonyms: The Taizhou Longitudinal Study
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of adults from urban and rural areas of Taizhou, Jiangsu Province, China, initiated in 2007 by Fudan University and the Taizhou government, with baseline interviews, physical examinations, biochemical assays and collection of blood and other biospecimens, and follow-up through health records and repeated assessments, to study environmental and genetic risk factors for common non-communicable diseases.
exposures: designed to study: exposure event (ExO:0000002)|designed to study: exposure to eating behavior (ECTO:6000021)|designed to study: exposure to lifestyle (ECTO:6000015)|designed to study: exposure to occupation (ECTO:0001591)

label: UK Aneurysm Growth Study
other synonyms: United Kingdom Aneurysm Growth Study
definition: A UK national prospective cohort of men recruited in 2011–2019 through the NHS abdominal aortic aneurysm screening programmes of England, Wales and Scotland, which invite men in the year of their 65th birthday: men with a small aneurysm detected at screening, together with screened men without an aneurysm as controls, followed with annual postal questionnaires and, for those with an aneurysm, ultrasound surveillance scans, to study the growth of small abdominal aortic aneurysms.

label: Danish T2D Case-Control Study
other synonyms: Danish T2D case-control study
definition: A type 2 diabetes case-control sample of Danish participants, undertaken by the Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Basic Metabolic Research at the University of Copenhagen, that brings together people from several Danish studies, among them the Vejle Diabetes Biobank, Inter99, Health2006, Health2008 and DanFunD: cases with type 2 diabetes by self-report, anti-diabetic treatment or fasting or 2-hour plasma glucose, and controls with normal fasting and, where measured, 2-hour plasma glucose, genotyped genome-wide for genetic studies of type 2 diabetes.

label: CoFAR Eosinophilic Esophagitis Registry
other synonyms: Eosinophilic Esophagitis (EoE) Databank (CoFAR 5)|Eosinophilic Esophagitis Databank|NIH CoFAR EoE cohort|NIH Consortium of Food Allergy Research (CoFAR) EoE Cohort|US NIH CoFAR EoE cohort
definition: A registry of children and adults aged 6 months to 65 years with biopsy-confirmed eosinophilic esophagitis, enrolled at a single visit in 2011–2016 at the five US sites of the NIAID-funded Consortium of Food Allergy Research (in New York, North Carolina, Denver, Little Rock and Baltimore), with medical history questionnaires and blood or saliva samples genotyped at Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center, to characterise the disease and establish its genetic basis.

label: Vanderbilt Online Musicality Study
definition: An online study of adults aged 18 or over who speak English fluently, conducted by researchers at Vanderbilt University Medical Center in Nashville, Tennessee, and recruited worldwide, mainly through ResearchMatch and also through Vanderbilt newsletters and research mailing lists, Reddit, Facebook advertising and social media sharing. Participants completed web-based questionnaires on music engagement and auditory tasks of musical rhythm and speech perception, and those with a US mailing address were invited to return mail-in saliva samples for genotyping, to study the genetics of musicality.

label: Viva la Familia Study
other synonyms: VIVA LA FAMILIA Study|Viva La Familia|Viva La Familia Study
definition: A family study of Hispanic children in Houston, Texas, conducted at the USDA/ARS Children's Nutrition Research Center of Baylor College of Medicine, which in 2000–2005 recruited families through a proband aged 4–19 with a BMI above the 95th percentile, together with the proband's siblings aged 4–19 and their parents. The children were phenotyped in depth (anthropometry, body composition by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, diet, physical activity, energy expenditure and metabolic risk factors) and followed up after one year, to map genetic and environmental contributions to childhood obesity and its comorbidities.

label: Western Australian Melanoma Health Study
definition: A population-based collection of adult melanoma cases resident in Western Australia and diagnosed between January 2006 and September 2009, identified through the Western Australian Cancer Registry and invited by mail with their diagnosing doctor's consent, with registry pathology data, a telephone questionnaire on melanoma risk factors such as sun exposure and skin type, and blood samples for DNA, RNA and serum, established to investigate the genetic epidemiology of melanoma.

label: Warfarin Anticoagulation in Patients in sub-Saharan Africa
other synonyms: WARfarin anticoagulation in PATients in Sub-Saharan Africa|Warfarin Anticoagulation in Patients in Sub-Saharan Africa
definition: An observational study of adults taking warfarin at a stable maintenance dose for venous thromboembolism, atrial fibrillation or valvular heart disease, Black African and, in South Africa, also of mixed ancestry, recruited from June 2018 to March 2020 at outpatient clinics and hospital departments in Uganda and South Africa by the NIHR Global Health Research Group on warfarin anticoagulation in sub-Saharan Africa (the University of Liverpool, the Infectious Diseases Institute in Kampala and the University of Cape Town), with clinical data and blood samples for genotyping, to develop clinical and genetic warfarin dosing algorithms for sub-Saharan African patients.

label: Women's Environmental Cancer and Radiation Epidemiology Study
other synonyms: WECARE Study|Women's Environment, Cancer, and Radiation Epidemiology Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of contralateral breast cancer, designed to examine the joint roles of radiation exposure and genetic susceptibility, in which women diagnosed before age 55 with a first primary invasive breast cancer who later developed contralateral breast cancer were individually matched to women with unilateral breast cancer. Participants were identified through population-based cancer registries in the United States, Canada and Denmark and recruited in two phases, WECARE I (2001–2004) and WECARE II (2009–2012).
diseases: patients with: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|patients with: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to radiation (ECTO:0000001)|designed to study: exposure to radiation therapy (ECTO:2000079)

label: Wills Eye Hospital GWAS
other synonyms: Wills Eye Hospital
definition: A case-control study of uveal melanoma run at the University of Pennsylvania for a genome-wide association study of the cancer and of differences between tumours with monosomy and disomy of chromosome 3, whose cases were patients treated at Wills Eye Hospital in Philadelphia, recruited through the UPenn Genetic Diagnostic Laboratory with blood samples and clinical and tumour data, and whose controls were selected from participants of the Penn Medicine Biobank.

label: WOBASZ II
other synonyms: Multi-centre National Population Health Examination Survey|Multicenter National Health Survey II|Multicentre National Population Health Examination Survey
definition: A cross-sectional national health examination survey of a random sample of residents of Poland aged over 20, drawn from the national identity card registry by three-stage sampling stratified by voivodeship, type of urbanisation and gender, and examined in 2013–2014 with face-to-face questionnaire interviews, physical examinations and blood samples to assess the prevalence, treatment and control of cardiovascular diseases and their risk factors. It continued the first WOBASZ survey of 2003–2005 with a new, independent sample and was coordinated by the Institute of Cardiology in Warsaw with medical universities in Gdansk, Katowice, Krakow, Lodz and Poznan.

label: Oxford Regional Prospective Study of Childhood Diabetes
acronyms: ORPS|Oxford Regional Prospective Study of Childhood Diabetes (ORPS)
other synonyms: Oxford Regional Prospective Study|Oxford regional prospective study
definition: A population-based inception cohort of children diagnosed with type 1 diabetes before the age of 16 in the Oxford Health Authority region of the United Kingdom, established in 1986, who were recruited within three months of diagnosis until 1997 and followed prospectively with annual measurements of HbA1c and urinary albumin excretion to determine the natural course of microalbuminuria during childhood and adolescence.
diseases: patients with: Moderate albuminuria (HP:0012594)|patients with: type 1 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005147)

label: Study of Underlying Genetic Determinants of Vitamin D and Highly Related Traits
other synonyms: SUNLIGHT Consortium|SUNLIGHT consortium
definition: A consortium, formed in 2008, of cohort studies from the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, the Netherlands, Germany, Sweden, Italy and Finland that meta-analyses their genome-wide association results for circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentration in people of European descent, to identify genetic determinants of vitamin D status and insufficiency.

label: International Cannabis Consortium
definition: A consortium established to combine the results of genome-wide association studies from cohorts in Europe, the United States, Canada and Australia, beginning with lifetime cannabis use, in order to identify the genetic variants underlying individual differences in cannabis use.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to cannabis (ECTO:0100005)

label: Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia cohort 1
other synonyms: COHRA etiology study|Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia, cohort 1
