definition: A cross-sectional, family-based study, the first cohort of the Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia, that from 2003 recruited households with at least one biological parent–child pair (the child aged 1–18 years), together with all other household members, mainly in rural counties of central West Virginia and western Pennsylvania, United States, and assessed them by interviews, questionnaires, oral health and microbiological examinations and DNA collection to study how individual, family and community factors contribute to oral disease in Appalachia.
diseases: population study of: dental caries (MONDO:0005276)|population study of: mouth disorder (MONDO:0006858)

label: Shikamachi health improvement practice genome cohort study
other synonyms: SHIKA study|SHIP genome cohort study|Shika study|Shika-machi Super Preventive Health Examination|Shikamachi Health Improvement Practice genome cohort
definition: A longitudinal community-based observational study, commissioned by the town and conducted since 2011 by Kanazawa University, of residents of Shika Town on the Noto Peninsula, Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan, which aims to find ways of preventing lifestyle-related diseases: residents aged 40 and over in four model districts of the town complete questionnaires on diet, lifestyle and health and undergo a comprehensive health examination, with blood taken for biochemical tests and DNA.

label: Bicuspid aoRtic vAlVe gEnetic research
other synonyms: BRAVE study|University of Leicester Bicuspid aoRtic vAlVe gEnetic research
definition: An ongoing multicentre genetic study led by the University of Leicester, United Kingdom, with support from the NIHR Leicester Biomedical Research Centre, that recruits patients with bicuspid aortic valve disease, identified from clinic and discharge letters and confirmed by cardiac imaging, together with relatives of patients with a family history of the disease, who are offered cascade echocardiographic screening, and collects clinical questionnaire data and blood for DNA to study the genetic causes of bicuspid aortic valve disease.

label: Defining the Basis of Fibromuscular Dysplasia
other synonyms: DEFINE Study|DEFINE-FMD Study|DEFINE-FMD study|Define-FMD Study
definition: An observational case-control study at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York, United States, that since 2013 has enrolled adults with fibromuscular dysplasia and, since its expansion, adults with spontaneous coronary artery dissection or cervical artery dissection, together with healthy controls from the general population matched to the fibromuscular dysplasia cases by age and sex, and collects blood (DNA, plasma and serum) and skin-biopsy fibroblasts for a systems-genetics study of the key drivers of these arterial diseases.
diseases: patients with: cervical artery dissection (MONDO:0006061)|patients with: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)|patients with: fibromuscular dysplasia (MONDO:0006761)

label: Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia cohort 2
other synonyms: COHRA2 study|Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia 2|Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia Cohort 2|Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia, cohort 2
definition: A prospective mother–child cohort of the Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia, a collaboration of the University of Pittsburgh and West Virginia University, that since 2011 has enrolled healthy, English-speaking, White pregnant women aged 18 and over in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and across West Virginia, United States, and follows the women and their children from pregnancy into early childhood with oral examinations, questionnaires and oral microbial and DNA samples, to study the genetic, microbial and environmental factors in oral health.

label: Genetic Analysis of Idiopathic Thrombophilia 2 Project
other synonyms: GAIT-2 Project|GAIT-2 study|Genetic Analysis of Idiopathic Thrombophilia 2
definition: A family-based study, run at the Hospital de la Santa Creu i Sant Pau in Barcelona, of extended Spanish families recruited from 2006 to 2010 through a proband with idiopathic thrombophilia (recurrent thrombosis, a spontaneous thrombosis with an affected first-degree relative, or thrombosis before age 45, with known biological causes excluded), each family having at least ten living members in three or more generations. It follows the GAIT-1 Project with a new set of families and studies the genetic basis of thrombosis risk and of intermediate phenotypes such as thrombin generation.
diseases: at risk of: thrombophilia (MONDO:0002305)|at risk of: venous thromboembolism (MONDO:0005399)

label: Human Reproductive Behaviour Consortium
definition: A consortium of cohort studies that carries out genome-wide association meta-analyses of human reproductive behaviour, such as age at first sex, age at first birth, number of children ever born and childlessness, in people of European ancestry; after a first study of age at first birth and number of children ever born, it meta-analysed cohorts for age at first sex and age at first birth.

label: SerGenCovid-19
other synonyms: Serum Genetic Covid-19 study
definition: A cohort of adult volunteers living across Italy, selected by the Italian National Research Council (CNR) from respondents to its EPICOVID-19 web survey who had agreed to be recontacted, who completed an online health and lifestyle questionnaire and gave blood at collection centres in several Italian regions, with repeat sampling about 5 and 10 months later, between May 2021 and February 2022. It was set up to study the serological and genetic factors in the immune response to SARS-CoV-2 infection and COVID-19 vaccination and in susceptibility to infection, and to build a serum and DNA biobank.

label: CALGB 40502
other synonyms: NCCTG N063H
definition: A randomised, three-arm phase III trial led by the Cancer and Leukemia Group B, with the North Central Cancer Treatment Group (as N063H), the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group and the Southwest Oncology Group taking part, that enrolled patients aged 18 or over with locally recurrent (stage IIIC) or metastatic (stage IV) breast cancer and no prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease at institutions in the United States from 2008 to 2011, comparing first-line paclitaxel once per week with nab-paclitaxel or ixabepilone once per week, each given with bevacizumab (optional from March 2011), with progression-free survival as the primary end point.

label: Asklepios Study
other synonyms: ASKLEPIOS study|Asklepios study
definition: A longitudinal population study by investigators of Ghent University, Belgium, of men and women aged about 35 to 55 and free from overt cardiovascular disease, randomly sampled from the population lists of the twinned communities of Erpe-Mere and Nieuwerkerken (partners and relatives living there were also eligible), examined at a single local study site in 2002–2004 and again in 2011–2016, to study the interplay between ageing, cardiovascular haemodynamics and inflammation in preclinical cardiovascular disease.

label: CORtisol NETwork consortium
other synonyms: CORNET consortium|CORtisol NETwork|CORtisol NETwork Consortium|Cortisol Network
definition: A consortium of population-based cohorts in Europe and Australia with genome-wide genotypes and morning plasma cortisol measured in blood sampled at a controlled time of day, funded by the Chief Scientist Office of the Scottish Government and the British Heart Foundation, that combines their participants of European ancestry in genome-wide association meta-analyses of morning plasma cortisol, formed to identify genetic determinants of inter-individual variation in hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis function.

label: Amsterdam Born Children and their Development
other synonyms: Amsterdam-Born Children and their Development|The Amsterdam Born Children and their Development Study
definition: A prospective, multi-ethnic birth cohort run from Amsterdam UMC that recruited pregnant women living in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, at their first prenatal visit between January 2003 and March 2004, and follows their children from pregnancy into young adulthood to identify factors in pregnancy and early childhood that explain later health and health inequalities, with particular attention to differences between ethnic groups.

label: 100-plus Study
other synonyms: 100-plus Study of cognitively healthy centenarians|The 100-plus Study of cognitively healthy centenarians
definition: An ongoing prospective cohort study, started in 2013 at the Alzheimer Center Amsterdam (Amsterdam UMC), of Dutch-speaking centenarians in the Netherlands who report being cognitively healthy, as confirmed by an informant, and since 2017 also of their first-degree family members and partners, set up to identify characteristics associated with escaping or delaying cognitive decline. Centenarians are visited at home for interviews, neuropsychological testing and blood sampling, followed annually until death, and offered post-mortem brain donation.

label: Two Sister Study
other synonyms: The Two Sister Study
definition: A family-based study of young-onset breast cancer, conducted by the US National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences as an offshoot of the Sister Study, that in 2008–2010 enrolled women diagnosed with breast cancer before age 50 who had a sister in the Sister Study, together with their parents, and used the breast cancer-free Sister Study sisters as matched controls, to study genetic and environmental causes of young-onset breast cancer. The affected women are followed prospectively as breast cancer survivors.

label: Women's Health Study: From Adolescence to Adulthood
other synonyms: The Women's Health Study: From Adolescence to Adulthood|The Women's Health Study: from Adolescence to Adulthood
definition: A longitudinal cohort of the Boston Center for Endometriosis (Boston Children's Hospital and Brigham and Women's Hospital, Boston) that in 2012–2018 enrolled adolescent and adult females aged 7–55 with surgically diagnosed endometriosis at the two hospitals, together with participants without endometriosis from their clinics and the local community, collected blood and urine samples at enrolment, and follows participants with annual questionnaires, compliant since 2014 with the World Endometriosis Research Foundation's EPHect standards.

label: African Ancestry Breast Cancer Genetic Consortium
other synonyms: African American Breast Cancer Genetic consortium|African Ancestry Breast Cancer Genetic consortium|African Ancestry Breast Cancer Genetics Consortium|African-ancestry Breast Cancer Genetic Consortium|African-ancestry Breast Cancer Genetic consortium
definition: A consortium for genetic studies of breast cancer in women of African ancestry that pools whole-genome sequencing data, new Multi-Ethnic Genotyping Array genotypes and existing genotype data on breast cancer cases and controls from more than 20 studies in the United States, Africa and Barbados, among them the samples of the AMBER, ROOT, AABC and GAME-ON OncoArray consortia, for genome-wide association analyses and polygenic risk prediction.

label: Australian Asthma Genetics Consortium
definition: An Australian research consortium, supported by the National Health and Medical Research Council, that pooled genotyped physician-diagnosed asthma cases and controls of European ancestry from several Australian studies, among them studies of the Queensland Institute of Medical Research, the Lung Institute of Western Australia, the Busselton Health Study and the Tasmanian Longitudinal Health Study, into a genome-wide association study of asthma first reported in 2011. Its data have since been used in international meta-analyses of asthma and allergic disease.

label: Aarhus Prostate Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based, retrospective case-control study of prostate cancer at Aarhus University Hospital, Denmark, whose cases are men treated for prostate adenocarcinoma at the hospital's Department of Urology in Skejby and whose controls are age-matched men treated for myocardial infarction or undergoing coronary angioplasty with no prostate cancer diagnosis in the Danish Cancer Register or the Danish Cause of Death Register. It is one of the studies of the PRACTICAL consortium and was genotyped in the consortium's prostate cancer OncoArray project.

label: Amsterdam Breast Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based breast cancer case-control study run from the Netherlands Cancer Institute – Antoni van Leeuwenhoek Hospital (NKI-AVL) in Amsterdam, whose cases are women diagnosed with breast cancer before age 50 (operable invasive cancers diagnosed in 1970–1994 in four Dutch hospitals and, for the iCOGS and OncoArray genotyping, patients diagnosed in 1995–2011 at the NKI-AVL) and whose controls are women recruited through the Sanquin blood bank. A familial arm, ABCS-F, adds breast cancer patients without BRCA1/2 mutations from the NKI-AVL family cancer clinic, and the study contributes to the Breast Cancer Association Consortium.

label: Amsterdam Breast Cancer Study – Familial
other synonyms: Amsterdam Breast Cancer Study - Familial
definition: The familial arm of the Amsterdam Breast Cancer Study, whose cases are breast cancer patients of any age without a pathogenic BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation who were counselled and tested from 1995 at the family cancer clinic of the Netherlands Cancer Institute – Antoni van Leeuwenhoek Hospital in Amsterdam, and whose controls are healthy women from the general population recruited through the blood bank. The Breast Cancer Association Consortium lists it as a study separate from the main ABCS.

label: Australian Breast Cancer Tissue Bank
definition: A breast cancer biobank, headquartered at the Westmead Institute for Medical Research of the University of Sydney, that since 2005 has collected tumour tissue, blood and linked clinical and follow-up data from consenting patients with breast cancer at collection sites across Australia and provides them for research. It contributes breast cancer cases to the Breast Cancer Association Consortium.

label: Anonymous Blood Donor Cohort
other synonyms: 3D Population Controls|Anonymous Blood Donor Cohort (3D Population Controls)|Anonymous blood donor cohort
definition: A population-based sample of anonymous Danish blood donors used as population controls in genetic studies, contributed under the abbreviation DKctrl, with self-reported anthropometry, to the GIANT consortium's genome-wide meta-analyses of height and body mass index. The study its contributors cite for it recruited its healthy controls among blood donors of the Danish Blood Donor Corps in the Copenhagen area.

label: Adelaide Blood Pools
other synonyms: Adelaide Blood pool|Adelaide population-based cohort in Blood pooling design
definition: A population-based sample of unrelated adults from Adelaide, Australia, with measured central corneal thickness, whose members in the thinnest and thickest fifths of the distribution had equal volumes of whole blood pooled before DNA extraction and genotyped as case and control pools in a genome-wide association study of central corneal thickness.

label: Aneurysm Consortium
other synonyms: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Consortium|Aneurysm Consortium AAA GWAS|Aneurysm Consortium AAA GWAS dataset|Aneurysm Consortium GWAS|The Aneurysm Consortium
definition: A consortium of investigators in the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand formed to carry out a genome-wide association study of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Its GWAS dataset pools AAA cases with DNA from eight centres in those countries and from the UK Small Aneurysm Trial, recruited from inpatients, outpatient clinics and population screening programmes, and compares them with Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium 2 controls from the 1958 British Birth Cohort and the UK National Blood Service.

label: Autism Case-Control cohort
other synonyms: ACC cohort|Autism CaseControl cohort
definition: A case-control collection for genome-wide studies of autism spectrum disorders assembled at the Center for Applied Genomics of the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, combining people with autism spectrum disorders from several US sites, diagnosed with the Autism Diagnostic Interview and Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule and from simplex and multiplex families (with some of their parents and siblings), with control subjects without autism spectrum disorders from the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia.

label: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes
definition: A randomised, multicentre, double 2×2 factorial trial cohort of middle-aged and older adults with type 2 diabetes at high risk of cardiovascular events because of existing cardiovascular disease or additional risk factors, recruited in 2001–2005 through seven clinical networks in the United States and Canada with funding from the US National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute. All participants were randomised to intensive or standard glycaemic control and, in two sub-trials, to intensive or standard blood-pressure control or to fenofibrate or placebo added to simvastatin, to test whether these strategies reduce major cardiovascular events.
diseases: patients with: cardiovascular disorder (MONDO:0004995)|patients with: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: Anglo-Cardiff Collaborative Trial
other synonyms: Anglo Cardiff Collaborative Trial
definition: A population of adults in East Anglia and Wales, United Kingdom, selected at random from local general practice lists and open-access cardiovascular risk assessment clinics and studied by investigators in Cambridge and Cardiff, comprising healthy people as well as people with cardiovascular risk factors or disease, whose peripheral and central blood pressure, wave reflection and aortic pulse wave velocity were measured, with questionnaires and blood samples, to study vascular ageing, arterial stiffness and central blood pressure across the adult lifespan.

label: Alcoholic Cirrhosis GWAS
definition: A genome-wide association study of alcohol-related cirrhosis in people of European descent that meta-analysed two case–control data sets, one from Germany and one from the United Kingdom, comparing patients with alcohol-related cirrhosis with drinking controls to find genetic risk loci for the disease; its discovery results were published in 2015 and its summary statistics have been reused by later studies of cirrhosis.
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to alcohol abuse (ECTO:6000009)

label: University of Manchester Longitudinal Study of Cognition in Normal Healthy Old Age
other synonyms: Age and Cognitive Performance Research Cohort|Manchester Longitudinal Cognitive Ageing Cohort|Manchester and Newcastle Age and Cognitive Performance Research Cohort|Manchester and Newcastle Longitudinal Studies of Cognitive Ageing|Manchester and Newcastle Longitudinal Studies of Cognitive Aging|University of Manchester Age and Cognitive Performance Research Cohort
definition: A longitudinal cohort of healthy community-dwelling volunteers in middle and old age, recruited in Greater Manchester and Newcastle upon Tyne, England, between 1983 and the early 1990s by the University of Manchester's Age and Cognitive Performance Research Centre to chart trajectories of cognitive function in normal old age; participants took alternating batteries of cognitive tests every two years until 2003, with questionnaires on health and behaviour repeated until 2017. Blood was collected for DNA extraction, a Manchester subsample was physically examined and gave saliva, serum and plasma in 2003, and some participants donated their brains to the Manchester Brain Bank.

label: St. Göran Bipolar Project
other synonyms: St G_ran Bipolar Project|St. Göran Project
definition: A longitudinal naturalistic cohort of outpatients with bipolar disorder, launched in 2005 by the Karolinska Institutet and the St. Göran bipolar outpatient clinic (the Affective Center) of Northern Stockholm Psychiatry in Stockholm, Sweden, with a second centre in Gothenburg from 2009, which consecutively enrols patients treated at these clinics, with age- and sex-matched population controls randomly selected by Statistics Sweden. It combines clinical ratings, cognitive testing, blood and cerebrospinal fluid sampling, brain imaging and genetics, with follow-up planned at 7 and 14 years, to identify predictors of long-term outcome in bipolar disorder.

label: Alzheimer's Disease Cardiff Cohort
other synonyms: AD Cardiff Cohort
definition: A case–control cohort of people with sporadic early- or late-onset Alzheimer's disease and elderly controls screened for dementia, recruited from community and hospital settings in the United Kingdom between the early 2000s and 2020 with funding from the Medical Research Council, the Moondance Foundation and Health and Care Research Wales, and assessed with a standardised clinical and neuropsychological protocol. Its longitudinal clinical and cognitive data and blood samples support genome-wide genotyping, plasma biomarker and induced pluripotent stem cell studies of Alzheimer's disease.

label: Analyse des DEterminants génétiques et environnementaux de la Leucoaraiose dans une population de sujets Agés Hypertendus présentant des troubles cognitifs DEbutants
other synonyms: ADELAHYDE study|ADELAHYDE-Nancy study|Analyse des DEterminants génétiques et environnementaux de la Leucoaraïose dans une population à sujets Agés HYpertendus présentant des troubles cognitifs DEbutants
definition: A single-centre cohort study at Nancy University Hospital, France, of older treated hypertensive patients with subjective memory complaints, recruited in the early 2000s through local press advertisements and general practitioners of the Inserm clinical investigation centre network, who had cognitive testing, brain MRI for white matter hyperintensities, measurements of arterial stiffness, carotid structure and endothelial function, and DNA and serum banking, and were re-examined about eight years later (ADELAHYDE-2), to identify genetic, environmental and vascular determinants of leukoaraiosis and cognitive decline.
diseases: patients with: hypertensive disorder (MONDO:0005044)|patients with: subjective cognitive decline (MONDO:0850292)

label: Evolution de la Rigidité Artérielle
other synonyms: ERA-France study
definition: A longitudinal study of the determinants of arterial ageing in French adults of a Paris cohort followed at the Centre d'Investigations Préventives et Cliniques, re-examined years apart with measurements of aortic stiffness and carotid atherosclerosis, and with leukocyte telomere length measured at successive examinations.

label: ADHD-VHIR study
definition: A case–control collection of the Psychiatric Genetics Unit of the Vall d'Hebron Research Institute (VHIR) in Barcelona, Spain, of adults of European origin with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, recruited and evaluated at the Hospital Universitari Vall d'Hebron, and of unrelated blood donors screened for lifetime ADHD symptoms, genotyped genome-wide to identify loci conferring susceptibility to persistent ADHD.

label: Action in Diabetes and Vascular disease: Preterax and Diamicron-MR Controlled Evaluation
other synonyms: Action in Diabetes and Vascular Disease: PreterAx and DiamicroN Modified-Release Controlled Evaluation|Action in Diabetes and Vascular Disease: Preterax and Diamicron MR Controlled Evaluation|Action in Diabetes and Vascular disease: preterAx and diamicroN mr Controlled Evaluation|Action in Diabetes and Vascular disease; preterAx and diamicroN-MR Controlled Evaluation
definition: A multinational randomised controlled trial with a 2×2 factorial design, conducted from 2001 by 215 collaborating centres in 20 countries in Asia, Australasia, Europe and North America among people with type 2 diabetes diagnosed at age 30 or older, aged 55 or older and with cardiovascular disease or at least one other cardiovascular risk factor, which compared a fixed combination of perindopril and indapamide with placebo, whatever the initial blood pressure, and an intensive gliclazide modified-release-based glucose control regimen targeting an HbA1c of 6.5% or less with standard glucose control, for their effects on major macrovascular and microvascular events; surviving participants were followed after the trial in ADVANCE-ON.

label: Aneurysm-Express Biobank Study
other synonyms: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Express Biobank Study|Aneurysm Express Biobank Study|Aneurysm-Express Biobank Cohort|Aneurysm-Express biobank|Aneurysm-Express biobank study|Aneurysm-Express study
definition: A biobank study at University Medical Center Utrecht and St. Antonius Hospital Nieuwegein, the Netherlands, set up in 2003 as a derivative of the Athero-Express, of patients undergoing open surgical repair of abdominal aortic and other arterial aneurysms, which stores aneurysm wall tissue collected during surgery together with blood, clinical data and three years of follow-up for cardiovascular events, to study aneurysm heterogeneity in relation to postoperative outcomes.
diseases: patients with: abdominal aortic aneurysm (MONDO:0005350)|patients with: aortic aneurysm (MONDO:0005160)

label: Atrial Fibrillation Biobank LMU
other synonyms: AFLMU Biobank|AFLMU study|Atrial Fibrillation Biobank Ludwig Maximilian University Study
definition: A biobank and ongoing prospective registry of patients with atrial fibrillation from the arrhythmia clinic of the Department of Medicine I, University Hospital Munich, Ludwig-Maximilians-University, Germany, established within the Arrhythmia-Biobank-LMU with support from the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research, which collects blood samples and clinical data and follows patients for recurrence of atrial fibrillation after rhythm-control interventions such as catheter ablation.

label: Early Treatment of Atrial Fibrillation for Stroke Prevention Trial
other synonyms: EAST-AFNET 4 biosample study|EAST-AFNET 4 trial|EAST-AFNET4 biosample study|EAST-AFNET4 trial|Early Therapy of Atrial Fibrillation for Stroke Prevention Trial
definition: An investigator-initiated, multicentre, parallel-group, open, blinded-outcome-assessment randomised trial sponsored by the Atrial Fibrillation Network (AFNET), which from July 2011 to December 2016 randomised patients with atrial fibrillation diagnosed within the previous year and cardiovascular risk factors, at 135 sites in 11 European countries, to early rhythm control therapy or usual care, to test whether early rhythm control prevents cardiovascular complications; its biosample substudy took blood at enrolment from consenting patients.

label: AFTER EU
other synonyms: AFTER (EURAGEDIC) European Rational Approach for the Genetics of Diabetic Complications|AFTER EU study
definition: The Danish part of the European Rational Approach for the Genetics of Diabetic Complications (EURAGEDIC) study: a case–control sample of adults with type 1 diabetes attending the outpatient clinic of the Steno Diabetes Center, Denmark, recruited from 1993 to 2000, with diabetic nephropathy (cases) or with persistent normoalbuminuria after more than 15 years of diabetes (controls), whose blood samples and clinical data were collected to study genetic risk factors for diabetic nephropathy and who were followed prospectively for mortality and cardiovascular and renal outcomes.
diseases: patients with: diabetic kidney disease (MONDO:0005016)|patients with: type 1 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005147)

label: Autism Genome Project
other synonyms: AGP Consortium|Autism Genome Project Consortium
definition: An international consortium of autism genetics research groups at more than 50 centres in North America and Europe, initiated by the National Alliance for Autism Research (later Autism Speaks) and the US National Institutes of Health and formed from four existing consortia (the Autism Genetics Cooperative, the Autism Genetic Resource Exchange, the Collaborative Programs of Excellence in Autism and the International Molecular Genetic Study of Autism Consortium). It pools the families with autism spectrum disorder collected at its sites, diagnosed with the ADI-R and ADOS, for genome-wide linkage, copy number variation and association studies.

label: Autism Genetic Resource Exchange
other synonyms: Autism Genetics Resource Exchange|autism genetic resource exchange
definition: A resource of biomaterials (cell lines, DNA and serum) and genetic and phenotypic data from families with autism spectrum disorder recruited from across the United States, mostly multiplex families with two or more affected members, whose diagnostic assessments (ADI-R and ADOS) and blood draws are done in the families' homes. It was established in 1997 by the Cure Autism Now Foundation and the Human Biological Data Interchange, is now managed by Autism Speaks, and makes its samples and data available to qualified researchers.

label: San Francisco Bay Area Adult Glioma Study
other synonyms: San Francisco Adult Glioma Study|UCSF Adult Glioma Study|University of California, San Francisco Adult Glioma Study
definition: A case-control study of adult glioma run by the University of California, San Francisco since 1991, whose cases are adults with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed glioma: population-based cases living in six San Francisco Bay Area counties (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, San Francisco, San Mateo and Santa Clara), identified through the regional cancer registry's rapid case ascertainment, and, from 2002, clinic-based cases recruited at the UCSF Neuro-oncology Clinic. Its controls were found by random-digit dialling in the same counties and frequency-matched to cases on age, sex and ethnicity, and later drawn from UCSF clinics; it studies environmental, immunological and genetic risk factors for glioma.

label: Aichi Colorectal Cancer Study
other synonyms: Aichi CRC Studies|Aichi CRC Study|Aichi Study|Asian Consortium, Colorectal Cancer Aichi
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of colorectal cancer at Aichi Cancer Center in Nagoya, Japan, part of the centre's Hospital-based Epidemiologic Research Program (HERPACC): its first collection (Aichi-1) took colorectal cancer cases and cancer-free controls, frequency-matched on age and sex, from the first-visit outpatients enrolled in HERPACC-II in 2000–2005, and its second (Aichi-2) recruited further cases and matched controls at the same hospital. Both collections were genotyped for the Asia Colorectal Cancer Consortium's genome-wide association studies of colorectal cancer in East Asians.

label: African American Breast Cancer Epidemiology and Risk Consortium
other synonyms: AMBER Consortium|AMBER consortium|African American Breast Cancer Epidemiology and Risk|African American Breast Cancer Epidemiology and Risk consortium|African American breast cancer epidemiology and risk consortium|The African American Breast Cancer Epidemiology and Risk consortium
definition: A consortium, funded by the US National Cancer Institute as a Program Project, that pools the questionnaire data, tumour tissue and DNA of four epidemiological studies of breast cancer in African American women in the United States (two case-control studies, the Carolina Breast Cancer Study and the Women's Circle of Health Study, and two cohorts, the Black Women's Health Study and the Multiethnic Cohort Study), with tumour subtyping, genotyping and data harmonisation done centrally in shared cores, to study the causes of breast cancer subtypes, especially oestrogen receptor-negative breast cancer, in African American women.

label: Acute Myocardial Infarction Gene Study
other synonyms: AMI Gene Study|AMI Gene Study/Dortmund Health Study|Acute Myocardial Infarction Gene Study/Dortmund Health Study
definition: A German case-control study of myocardial infarction whose cases were enrolled in 2004–2006 in a prospective multicentre registry at 4 heart centres and 6 cardiology departments in North Rhine-Westphalia, Lower Saxony and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania: consecutive men younger than 65 admitted with ST- or non-ST-segment elevation acute myocardial infarction, all of whom underwent cardiac catheterisation and revascularisation. Its controls are participants of the population-based Dortmund Health Study, and the case-control sample served as a replication study for the Myocardial Infarction Genetics Consortium's genome-wide association study of early-onset myocardial infarction.

label: Amsterdam UMC COVID-19 Biobank
other synonyms: Amsterdam UMC COVID study group|Amsterdam UMC COVID-19 biobank|Amsterdam UMC Covid-19 Biobank
definition: A prospective cohort and biobank, set up by the Amsterdam UMC COVID study group, of adult patients admitted with COVID-19 from 2020 to the COVID-19 wards and intensive care units of the two academic hospitals of Amsterdam UMC (locations University of Amsterdam and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam) in the Netherlands, which stores their clinical data and left-over and serially collected biological samples. Its genotyped patients, with controls, were contributed to the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative's genome-wide association meta-analyses of COVID-19.

label: Australian National Endometrial Cancer Study
definition: A nationwide population-based case-control study of endometrial cancer in Australia, run by a study group at QIMR Berghofer Medical Research Institute in Brisbane, whose cases are women aged 18–79 years newly diagnosed with histologically confirmed primary endometrial cancer between July 2005 and December 2007, identified through major hospitals and state cancer registries, and whose controls are women randomly selected from the Australian Electoral Roll and frequency-matched to the cases by state of residence and five-year age group. Participants gave risk-factor information by telephone interview and blood samples, and the cases were followed for survival, to study the causes and outcomes of endometrial cancer.

label: Lübeck Registry of Structural Heart Disease
other synonyms: Luebeck Angiographic Study
definition: A registry of patients with heart disease treated at the University of Lübeck hospital (University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein, Campus Lübeck) in Germany, with blood samples and clinical data, whose angiography sample (Angio-Lueb) consists of consecutive patients referred for coronary angiography and classified from the angiogram as having coronary artery disease or myocardial infarction or not. It has provided cases for genetic association studies of coronary artery disease, with population controls from KORA, and of dilated cardiomyopathy.
diseases: patients with: Abnormal heart morphology (HP:0001627)|patients with: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)|patients with: dilated cardiomyopathy (MONDO:0005021)|patients with: myocardial infarction (MONDO:0005068)

label: Australia and New Zealand Multiple Sclerosis Genetics Consortium
other synonyms: ANZgene Consortium|ANZgene Study|Australian and New Zealand Multiple Sclerosis Genetics Consortium|The Australia and New Zealand Multiple Sclerosis Genetics Conortium
definition: A multiple sclerosis case-control collection assembled for genome-wide association studies by the Australia and New Zealand Multiple Sclerosis Genetics Consortium (ANZgene), a collaboration of multiple sclerosis research groups in Australia and New Zealand, whose cases are people with multiple sclerosis of European ancestry from Australia and New Zealand; its genome-wide scan compared them with shared genotype data from controls of European ancestry from Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States, and further ANZgene cases and controls were collected for replication and fine-mapping, to identify genetic variants that influence susceptibility to multiple sclerosis.

label: Australian & New Zealand Registry of Advanced Glaucoma
other synonyms: Australia and New Zealand Registry of Advanced Glaucoma|Australian and New Zealand Registry of Advanced Glaucoma
definition: A prospective registry, run from the Department of Ophthalmology at Flinders University in Adelaide, of people with glaucoma referred by their eye practitioners across Australia and New Zealand: mainly people with advanced glaucoma (chiefly primary open-angle glaucoma with severe visual field loss), but also with less advanced, secondary and developmental glaucomas such as Axenfeld–Rieger malformation, whose clinical information and blood or saliva samples are collected by post. It was set up to find genetic risk factors for glaucoma blindness, and relatives of participants who carry myocilin mutations are offered cascade genetic testing.

label: Alberta Ovarian Tumor Types Study
other synonyms: Alberta Ovarian Tumor Types study
definition: A population-based, retrospective study of the histological types of ovarian carcinoma in the province of Alberta, Canada, whose cases are women with ovarian carcinoma identified through the Alberta Cancer Registry and sampled by histological type (endometrioid, clear cell, mucinous and high-grade serous carcinoma), with archival tumour tissue and pathology reports reviewed by a gynaecological pathologist, clinical data abstracted from medical charts and yearly updates of vital status, to study molecular and clinical differences between the types and survival.

label: Australian Prostate Cancer BioResource
definition: A national prostate cancer tissue bank in Australia, organised as a network of nodes in several states (among them Queensland, New South Wales and South Australia), that since the mid-2000s has collected radical prostatectomy tissue, blood, and clinical, pathology and follow-up data from men with prostate cancer, recruited through their urologists at diagnosis or before surgery at participating hospitals under common standard operating procedures, and supplies them for research, including genetic association studies of prostate cancer.

label: Aberdeen Prospective Osteoporosis Screening Study
definition: A population-based osteoporosis screening study and longitudinal cohort of women from the Aberdeen area of north-east Scotland, selected at random from Community Health Index (primary care) records within 25 miles of Aberdeen and invited, when aged 45–54, to a baseline health visit with bone density measurement in 1990–1994, with further visits in 1997–1999, when blood was taken for DNA, and in 2007–2011, to study bone loss, osteoporotic fracture risk and falls and their dietary, medical and genetic determinants.

label: Apixaban for Reduction in Stroke and Other Thromboembolic Events in Atrial Fibrillation
other synonyms: Apixaban for reduction in stroke and other ThromboemboLic events in atrial fibrillation|Apixaban for the Prevention of Stroke in Subjects With Atrial Fibrillation
definition: A multinational, randomised, double-blind, double-dummy phase 3 trial, sponsored by Bristol-Myers Squibb and Pfizer, in which patients with atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter and at least one additional risk factor for stroke, enrolled from 2006 at over 1,000 centres in about 40 countries, were randomly assigned to apixaban or warfarin to test whether apixaban is non-inferior to warfarin in preventing stroke or systemic embolism. The trial ended in 2011; its participants' baseline blood samples and genotypes have since been used in biomarker and genetic studies.

label: Aarhus Osteoporosis Study
definition: A case–control study of osteoporosis at Aarhus University Hospital, Denmark, whose cases are osteoporotic men and women with vertebral fractures and low bone mineral density and whose controls are normal individuals, assessed with dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, radiographs and bone turnover markers and genotyped for candidate-gene studies and for replication of genome-wide association findings on bone mineral density and fracture. It took part in the GENOMOS consortium and in the GEFOS meta-analysis of bone mineral density and fracture.

label: Amsterdam Resuscitation Studies
other synonyms: AmsteRdam REsuscitation STudies|AmsteRdam Resuscitation Studies
definition: An ongoing prospective, community-based registry, set up in June 2005 and run from the Academic Medical Center in Amsterdam, of all out-of-hospital cardiac arrests with a resuscitation attempt by emergency medical services in the province of North Holland, the Netherlands, which collects resuscitation and ECG data, outcomes, medical history from hospitals and general practitioners, medication use from community pharmacies and, since July 2007, DNA from patients with documented ventricular tachycardia or fibrillation. It studies the outcome and the clinical, pharmacological, environmental and genetic determinants of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, taking controls from pharmacy and general-practice databases for case–control analyses.

label: Alzheimer's Research Trust Collaboration
other synonyms: ART Collaboration|ARUK Consortium|Alzheimer's Research UK Consortium
definition: A collaboration of United Kingdom Alzheimer's disease research groups at the Universities of Nottingham, Manchester, Southampton and Bristol, Queen's University Belfast and the Oxford Project to Investigate Memory and Ageing, funded by the Alzheimer's Research Trust (renamed Alzheimer's Research UK, after which the collaboration is called the ARUK Consortium), that pooled DNA from people with probable or post-mortem-confirmed Alzheimer's disease and from elderly controls into a DNA bank hosted at the University of Nottingham. Its cases and controls formed one of the sample collections of the GERAD genome-wide association study of Alzheimer's disease.

label: Arsenic Health Risk Assessment and Molecular Epidemiology
other synonyms: Arsenic Health Risk Assessment and Molecular Epidemiology study in Central Europe
definition: A hospital-based case–control study of basal cell carcinoma of the skin and of bladder and kidney cancers in relation to low-level inorganic arsenic in drinking water, funded by the European Commission and conducted in 2002–2004 in counties of Hungary, Romania and Slovakia with arsenic in groundwater. Its incident cases, and its controls drawn from general surgery, orthopaedic and trauma in-patients of hospitals across the same areas and frequency matched to the cases by age, sex and county, all aged 30–79, were assessed for lifetime arsenic exposure, urinary arsenic metabolites and genetic susceptibility.
diseases: patients with: basal cell carcinoma (MONDO:0020804)|patients with: kidney cancer (MONDO:0002367)|patients with: urinary bladder cancer (MONDO:0001187)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to arsenic in water via ingestion (ECTO:0080000)

label: Athens Study of Psychosis Proneness and Incidence of Schizophrenia
definition: A study of young men aged 18–24 doing compulsory military service in Greece, randomly selected in successive waves during their first two weeks at the National Basic Air Force Training Center in Tripolis, who completed self-rated questionnaires on schizotypy and psychopathology and computerised neurocognitive and eye-movement tasks and gave DNA, a subgroup being reassessed at discharge two years later. Led from the University Mental Health Research Institute in Athens, it studies psychosis proneness and its cognitive and genetic correlates in the general population.
diseases: population study of: psychotic disorder (MONDO:0005485)|population study of: schizophrenia (MONDO:0005090)

label: Australian Twin Eye Study
other synonyms: Australian Twin Eye study
definition: An Australian twin study of eye traits that combines twins, and some of their siblings, given an eye examination in the Twins Eye Study in Tasmania or in the Brisbane Adolescent Twin Study, with measures such as cycloplegic refraction, intraocular pressure and retinal photographs and with genome-wide genotypes, used in heritability, linkage and genome-wide association studies of ophthalmic traits. Its participants were recruited through the Australian Twin Registry, existing twin studies, schools and publicity.

label: AtheroGene Registry
other synonyms: AtheroGene Study|AtheroGene registry|AtheroGene study|Atherogene Registry|Large AtheroGene Study
definition: A prospective clinical cohort of patients with coronary artery disease (at least one coronary stenosis over 30% on angiography), from stable angina to acute coronary syndromes, enrolled in successive phases from November 1996 to early 2004 when they underwent coronary angiography at the Department of Medicine II of the Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz or the Bundeswehrzentralkrankenhaus Koblenz, Germany, and followed for cardiovascular death and non-fatal myocardial infarction. It studies clinical, genetic and laboratory determinants of the progression and outcome of coronary atherosclerosis, and for genetic case–control analyses also recruited healthy controls from the Rhein-Main area.

label: Australian Twin Migraine
other synonyms: Australia ATM|Australian Twin Migraine GWA Study|Australian Twin Migraine GWA study
definition: A genome-wide association case–control sample of unrelated Australians of European descent, one from each family, drawn from the twins and their relatives studied at the Queensland Institute of Medical Research (QIMR) who were genotyped genome-wide: migraine cases, identified in semi-structured telephone interviews based on the International Classification of Headache Disorders (ICHD-II) or by self-report and chosen preferentially for severity, and population controls from families with no known migraine. It is one of the studies of the International Headache Genetics Consortium.

label: Asthma UK Genetics of Severe Asthma
definition: A genetic study of severe asthma in the United Kingdom, supported by Asthma UK, which recruited people of European ancestry with severe asthma (Global Initiative for Asthma classes 3–5) at UK centres and compared them in genome-wide association studies with controls without asthma or wheeze, to identify genetic determinants of severe asthma and whether they differ from those of mild to moderate asthma.

label: Amsterdam UMC dilated cardiomyopathy GWAS cohort
other synonyms: Amsterdam UMC cohort
definition: A case–control dataset for genome-wide association studies of dilated cardiomyopathy assembled at Amsterdam UMC, the Netherlands. Its cases are adult index patients referred by secondary or tertiary cardiologists to Amsterdam UMC for genetic testing for dilated cardiomyopathy, with the diagnosis confirmed from the medical chart and a left ventricular ejection fraction below 50%, and its controls are unrelated participants of the Netherlands Twin Register.

label: Austrian Diabetic Nephropathy Study
other synonyms: Austrian Diabetes Nephropathy Study
definition: A clinic-based cohort study of patients with type 1 diabetes in the state of Salzburg, Austria, initiated in 2012 as the Austrian study of the International Diabetic Nephropathy Consortium (InterDiane), which follows the protocol of the Finnish Diabetic Nephropathy Study to identify risk factors for diabetic nephropathy and other chronic complications of type 1 diabetes. Patients are recruited consecutively at the outpatient departments of Paracelsus Medical University Hospital Salzburg and Diakonissen-Wehrle Hospital Salzburg, with clinical data drawn mainly from the Type 1 diabetes Registry of the state of Salzburg, and are re-examined every 1 to 1.5 years.
diseases: patients with: diabetic kidney disease (MONDO:0005016)|patients with: type 1 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005147)

label: Bipolar Affective Case Control Study
other synonyms: Bipolar Affective Disorder Case Control Study|Bipolar Association Case-Control Study
definition: A case–control genetic association study of bipolar disorder in the United Kingdom, funded by GlaxoSmithKline, whose cases are people with bipolar disorder recruited in London and diagnosed with the Schedules for Clinical Assessment in Neuropsychiatry (SCAN) interview and the Operational Criteria Checklist, and whose controls are ethnically matched subjects recruited in the UK; its control group has also served as UK controls in genome-wide association studies of other disorders.

label: Arizona Study of Aging and Neurodegenerative Disorders and Brain and Body Donation Program
other synonyms: Arizona Study of Aging and Neurodegenerative Disorders|Arizona Study of Aging/Brain and Body Donation Program|Banner Health study|Brain and Body Donation Program
definition: A brain and body donation programme and clinicopathological study of ageing and neurodegenerative disorders at Banner Sun Health Research Institute in Arizona, United States, started in 1987. Its participants, mostly cognitively normal volunteers from the retirement communities of metropolitan Phoenix together with people recruited because they have Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease or cancer, receive standardized general medical, neurological, neuropsychological and movement-disorder assessments during life and, for most, a full pathological examination after death.
diseases: population study of: Alzheimer disease (MONDO:0004975)|population study of: Parkinson disease (MONDO:0005180)|population study of: cancer (MONDO:0004992)|population study of: neurodegenerative disease (MONDO:0005559)

label: BARCODE1
other synonyms: BARCODE 1|The BARCODE 1 Study: The Use of Genetic Profiling to Guide Prostate Cancer Targeted Screening
definition: A community-based prostate cancer risk-screening study in the United Kingdom, coordinated by the Institute of Cancer Research, that invites men of European ancestry via their general practitioners to undergo a germline genetic profile test of prostate cancer risk single nucleotide polymorphisms. Men in the highest genetic-risk stratum are offered MRI-led prostate screening and targeted biopsy; the study began with a feasibility pilot before opening to wider recruitment.

label: Therapeutic Trial collection
definition: A collection of patients with relapsing–remitting multiple sclerosis or a clinically isolated syndrome with MRI signs of demyelination, assembled by Bayer Schering Pharma from four of its clinical trials: three studies of interferon beta-1b (BENEFIT, BEYOND and the 16-year long-term follow-up of the pivotal interferon beta-1b trial in relapsing–remitting multiple sclerosis) and one of a CCR1 antagonist. It was genotyped genome-wide and used as multiple sclerosis cases in genetic studies of susceptibility.

label: Berlin Birth Cohort
other synonyms: Berlin Birth Cohort study
definition: A birth cohort of mother–child pairs recruited at delivery in the 2000s from women with singleton pregnancies giving birth consecutively at the obstetrics department of the Charité university hospital in Berlin, Germany, with maternal blood, umbilical cord blood, placentas and birth measurements collected at birth. It is used to study maternal and fetal influences, including genetic ones, on birth weight, pregnancy outcomes and maternal physiology in pregnancy.

label: British Breast Cancer Study
definition: A UK case-control study of breast cancer, led by investigators at the Institute of Cancer Research and the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, which in 2001–2008 recruited women with bilateral breast cancer identified through English and Scottish cancer registries and breast cancer clinics, and clinic patients with breast cancer and at least two affected female first-degree relatives, together with controls who were friends or non-blood relatives of the cases. It is one of the studies of the Breast Cancer Association Consortium.

label: Biobank of the Americas-Genomelink
other synonyms: Biobank of the Americas – GenomeLink
definition: A cohort of participants drawn from the customer base of Genomelink, a direct-to-consumer genetic-traits testing platform, who provided informed consent and completed surveys online as part of the Biobank of the Americas.

label: British Columbia Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma study
other synonyms: British Columbia Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of non-Hodgkin lymphoma in British Columbia, Canada, which invited residents of Greater Vancouver and Greater Victoria aged 20–79 with non-Hodgkin lymphoma diagnosed from March 2000 to February 2004, identified through the BC Cancer Registry (excluding HIV-positive and post-transplant cases), together with population controls from the Client Registry of the British Columbia Ministry of Health frequency-matched to the cases on sex, age and area of residence, to study environmental and genetic risk factors for the disease.

label: British Columbia Familial Hypercholesterolemia Registry
other synonyms: British Columbia Familial Hypercholesterolemia|British Columbia Familial Hypercholesterolemia cohort
definition: A registry of people with clinically diagnosed heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia in British Columbia, Canada, based at the Healthy Heart Program Prevention Clinic of St. Paul's Hospital in Vancouver, which enrols clinic patients meeting the Dutch Lipid Clinic Network criteria, invites their relatives for evaluation and follows adult participants prospectively as an open observational cohort. Set up as the first such registry in Canada to improve the identification and management of the condition, it is also used to study its cardiovascular outcomes and genetic causes.

label: New York Breast Cancer Family Registry
other synonyms: Metropolitan NY Registry|Metropolitan New York Registry|Metropolitan New York Registry of Breast Cancer Families|New York Site of the Breast Cancer Family Registry|New York site of the Breast Cancer Family Registry
definition: The New York site of the Breast Cancer Family Registry, known as the Metropolitan New York Registry and run from Columbia University in New York City, which from 1995 enrolled families with breast or ovarian cancer through clinical and community settings in the New York metropolitan area (New York, New Jersey and Connecticut), including Ashkenazi Jewish and minority families, when a woman had breast or ovarian cancer before age 45 or both cancers, a man had breast cancer, several relatives were affected or a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation was known. Affected and unaffected probands and their relatives gave family-history and epidemiological questionnaires and blood samples and are contacted annually for follow-up, for studies of the genetic epidemiology of breast cancer.
diseases: at risk of: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|at risk of: ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170)

label: Philadelphia Breast Cancer Family Registry
other synonyms: Philadelphia site of the Breast Cancer Family Registry
definition: The Philadelphia site of the Breast Cancer Family Registry, run from Fox Chase Cancer Center in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, which from 1996 enrolled families with breast or ovarian cancer through family cancer clinics and community outreach in the Philadelphia area, including Ashkenazi Jewish and minority families, when a woman had breast or ovarian cancer before age 35, both cancers, or bilateral breast cancer first diagnosed before 50, a man had breast cancer, affected relatives spanned two generations or a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation was known. Affected and unaffected probands and their relatives gave family-history and epidemiological questionnaires and blood samples and are contacted annually for follow-up, for studies of the genetic epidemiology of breast cancer.
diseases: at risk of: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|at risk of: ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170)

label: Utah Breast Cancer Family Registry
other synonyms: Utah Cooperative Breast Cancer Registry|Utah site of the Breast Cancer Family Registry
definition: The Utah site of the Breast Cancer Family Registry, run from the Huntsman Cancer Institute at the University of Utah in Salt Lake City, which from 1996 enrolled families with breast or ovarian cancer through family cancer clinics and community outreach in the Salt Lake City area, and later further families carrying BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations, when a woman had breast or ovarian cancer before age 45 or both cancers, a man had breast cancer, three relatives in two generations were affected (one before age 45) or a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation was known. Affected and unaffected probands and their relatives gave family-history and epidemiological questionnaires and blood samples and are followed up by annual contact and by linkage to population-based cancer registries, for studies of the genetic epidemiology of breast cancer.
diseases: at risk of: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|at risk of: ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170)

label: Barry Caerphilly Growth Study
other synonyms: Barry Caerphilly Growth study|Barry-Caerphilly Growth Study
definition: A cohort of children born consecutively from March 1972 to October 1974 in the towns of Barry and Caerphilly, South Wales, whose mothers were recruited early in pregnancy through general practitioners into a randomised controlled trial, set up in 1972 by the Medical Research Council Epidemiology Unit (South Wales) and the Welsh National School of Medicine in Cardiff, of milk tokens for pregnant women and their children up to five years of age, with the children examined by trained nurses at intervals from birth to five years. The children who completed the trial were traced and re-examined at 23–27 years of age in 1997–1999 to study how birth size, infant feeding, early growth and childhood illness relate to adult blood pressure, adiposity, insulin resistance, haemostatic factors and lung function.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to cow milk (liquid) via ingestion (ECTO:0070204)|designed to study: exposure to eating behavior (ECTO:6000021)

label: Breast Cancer in Northern Israel Study
other synonyms: Breast Cancer In Northern Israel Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of breast cancer in northern Israel, conducted by the Clalit National Cancer Control Center in Haifa with family medicine, surgery, pathology and oncology teams across the region, which since January 2000 has enrolled consecutively diagnosed breast cancer patients living in a defined area of northern Israel and cancer-free controls randomly selected from the Clalit Health Services register of insured people in the same area, matched on age, ethnic group and primary care clinic. Participants are interviewed about their medical history, medication use and health habits and give a blood sample, for studies of breast cancer risk factors, including genetic ones.

label: Blood-Cell Consortium
other synonyms: Blood Cell Consortium
definition: An international consortium of cohort studies and biobanks, organised in red blood cell, white blood cell and platelet working groups, that meta-analyses genetic associations with blood-cell counts and indices in participants of European, African, Hispanic/Latino, East Asian and South Asian ancestry, first with exome-array genotypes and later (its second phase, BCX2) with genome-wide imputed data, to identify common and rare variants that influence blood-cell traits.

label: Bavarian Endometrial Cancer Cases and Controls Study
other synonyms: Bavarian Endometrial Cancer Study
definition: A single-centre case-control study of endometrial cancer at the University Hospital Erlangen in Bavaria, Germany, conducted between 2002 and 2008 to investigate genetic and epidemiological risk factors for endometrial cancer, whose cases were incident cases referred to the hospital by surrounding practitioners or prevalent cases approached during follow-up care after treatment there for primary endometrial cancer, with epidemiological information from a structured interview questionnaire and clinical data from health records.

label: Belfast Elderly Longitudinal Free-living Ageing Study
other synonyms: BELFAST study|Belfast Elderly Longitudinal Free-living Ageing STudy|Belfast Elderly Longitudinal Free-living Aging STudy|Belfast Elderly Longitudinal Free-living Aging Study
definition: A longitudinal study of ageing by the Belfast Longevity Group of Queen's University Belfast, Northern Ireland, of 'elite' octogenarians and nonagenarians, and some centenarians: community-living, apparently well, independently mobile and mentally competent people recruited through their general practitioners in the Greater Belfast area and seen at home by a research nurse, who took their medical history, anthropometric and blood pressure measurements and blood samples for DNA and laboratory tests, with nutrition and lifestyle questionnaires, to study the immunological, cardiovascular, nutritional and genetic factors of healthy ageing and longevity.

label: Flanders-Belgian AD cohort
other synonyms: Flanders-Belgian study cohort
definition: A case-control cohort for genetic studies of Alzheimer's disease, drawn from a prospective study of Alzheimer's disease in Flanders, Belgium, whose genetic studies are run from the University of Antwerp: unrelated patients with early- or late-onset possible or probable Alzheimer's disease, diagnosed by consensus of at least two neurologists at the memory clinics of the Hospital Network Antwerp (Middelheim and Hoge Beuken) and the University Hospitals Leuven and at other neurology centres of the Belgian Neurology (BELNEU) consortium, and healthy unrelated control individuals from Belgium, patients' partners or community volunteers, with blood samples for DNA, cell lines and plasma and, for some patients, cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers.

label: Boston Early-Onset COPD Study
other synonyms: Boston Early-Onset COPD study|Boston Early-Onset Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease study
definition: A family study begun in 1994 at Brigham and Women's Hospital, Boston, to find genetic determinants of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease other than alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, which enrols extended pedigrees, mainly in New England, ascertained through probands with severe COPD (FEV1 at most 40% predicted) before age 53 and without severe alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, recruited from lung transplant and general pulmonary clinics, together with their first- and second-degree relatives aged 10 years or older.
diseases: patients with: chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (MONDO:0005002)

label: Bangladesh Vitamin E and Selenium Trial
definition: A population-based, 2×2 factorial, double-blind randomised controlled chemoprevention trial in Bangladesh that enrolled adults with manifest arsenical skin lesions from the Narayanganj, Comilla, Noakhali and Chandpur districts, through field offices in Araihazar and Matlab, between April 2006 and August 2009, and gave them vitamin E (alpha-tocopherol), selenium (L-selenomethionine), both or placebo for six years to test the prevention of non-melanoma skin cancer, with all-cause and cancer mortality, diabetes and oxidative stress biomarkers as secondary endpoints.
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to arsenic (ECTO:9000032)|participants with exposure: exposure to arsenic in water via ingestion (ECTO:0080000)

label: Black Women with Breast Cancer: Etiology, Survival, and Treatment Outcomes Study
other synonyms: BEST study|Black Women: Etiology and Survival of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer study|Black Women: Etiology and Survival of Triple-negative Breast Cancers (BEST) Study|Black Women: Etiology and Survival of Triple-negative Breast Cancers Study|The Black Women: Etiology and Survival of Triple-Negative Breast Cancers (BEST) Study
definition: A population-based longitudinal cohort of self-identified Black women diagnosed with invasive breast cancer at age 50 or younger, identified through the state cancer registries of Florida and Tennessee (diagnoses from 2005 to 2018; its first phase recruited women diagnosed in Florida in 2009–2012), who completed a questionnaire on sociodemographic, reproductive, epidemiologic and lifestyle factors, released their medical records and tumour tissue and gave saliva for germline genetic testing, now based at Vanderbilt University Medical Center, to study the causes, inherited predisposition, treatment and survival of breast cancer, including triple-negative breast cancer, in young Black women.

label: Baltic Familial Breast and Ovarian Cancer Consortium
other synonyms: Baltic Familial Breast Ovarian Cancer Consortium
definition: A collection of carriers of BRCA1 and BRCA2 pathogenic variants from families seen in clinical cancer genetics services in Lithuania and Latvia, gathered by a collaboration of Lithuanian (BFBOCC-LT) and Latvian (BFBOCC-LV) hereditary breast and ovarian cancer research groups and contributed as one study to the Consortium of Investigators of Modifiers of BRCA1 and BRCA2, for studies of genetic modifiers of cancer risk in carriers.
diseases: at risk of: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|at risk of: ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170)

label: Brains for Dementia Research
other synonyms: Brains for Dementia Research cohort
definition: A longitudinal brain-donation cohort in the United Kingdom, established in 2008 with funding from Alzheimer's Research UK and the Alzheimer's Society, of volunteers with dementia and volunteers without cognitive impairment (the latter aged 65 or over, apart from spouses or partners of participants with dementia), recruited through a network of six dementia research centres (King's College London, Bristol, Manchester, Oxford, Cardiff and Newcastle) and their university brain banks, who undergo standardised clinical and psychometric assessments during life and have consented to donate their brains for dementia research after death.

label: Scottish Bipolar Family Study
other synonyms: Bipolar Family Study
definition: A prospective longitudinal study based at the University of Edinburgh of young people aged 16–25 at entry who were well but at high familial risk of mood disorder, having at least one first-degree or two second-degree relatives with bipolar I disorder (identified through patients with bipolar I disorder referred by psychiatrists across Scotland), and of unrelated controls with no personal or family history of bipolar disorder drawn from their social networks, assessed clinically and with brain MRI on three occasions about two years apart to study changes that precede the onset of mood disorders.
diseases: at risk of: bipolar disorder (MONDO:0004985)|at risk of: mood disorder (MONDO:0005371)

label: Brazilian Immunogenetics of Asthma and Schistosomiasis
other synonyms: Brazilian Immunogenetics of Asthma & Schistosomiasis study|Brazilian Immunogenetics of Asthma and Schistosomiasis study
definition: A family-based study of asthma and schistosomiasis in five rural communities of the district of Conde, Bahia, north-eastern Brazil, an area endemic for Schistosoma mansoni about 200 km north of Salvador, in which residents aged 5 to 85, most of them members of two large pedigrees, were enrolled by whole-population ascertainment from July to September 2004 by the Federal University of Bahia and Johns Hopkins University, with later follow-up visits, to study the genetic control of total serum IgE, S. mansoni infection intensity and asthma; it is one of the studies of the Consortium on Asthma among African-ancestry Populations in the Americas (CAAPA).
diseases: population study of: asthma (MONDO:0004979)|population study of: schistosomiasis (MONDO:0015254)
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to Schistosoma mansoni (ECTO:3000174)

label: Biobank Innovations for Chronic Cerebrovascular Disease With Alzheimer's Disease Study
other synonyms: Biobank Innovation for Chronic Cerebrovascular Disease With Alzheimer's Disease Study|Biobank Innovations for Chronic Cerebrovascular Disease with ALZheimer's Disease Study
definition: A prospective, longitudinal, multicentre biobank cohort of older adults with cognitive complaints (subjective cognitive decline, mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, vascular and other dementias) enrolled from October 2016 to December 2020 at five South Korean university hospitals (Ajou University Hospital, Samsung Medical Center, Inha University Hospital, Pusan National University Hospital and Chonnam National University Hospital), planned and funded by the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency for the Korea Biobank Project to bank biospecimens and data for research on Alzheimer's disease, chronic cerebrovascular disease and mixed pathology; participants have clinical and neuropsychological assessments and blood tests, subsets have brain MRI, amyloid PET, Korea Biobank Array genotyping, actigraphy and skin fibroblast sampling, and follow-up is planned annually.
diseases: patients with: Alzheimer disease (MONDO:0004975)|patients with: cerebrovascular disorder (MONDO:0011057)|patients with: cognitive disorder (MONDO:0002039)|patients with: dementia (MONDO:0001627)

label: Breast Cancer in Galway Genetic Study
other synonyms: Breast Cancer In Galway Genetic Study
definition: A case-control study of breast cancer in the West of Ireland whose cases are unselected breast cancer patients recruited from University College Hospital Galway and surrounding hospitals in the West of Ireland since 2001, and whose controls are women over 60 years of age with no personal history of any cancer and no family history of breast or ovarian cancer, identified from retirement groups in the West of Ireland in 2001–2008; it is one of the studies of the Breast Cancer Association Consortium (BCAC).

label: Bipolar Genome Study
definition: A case-control genetic study of bipolar disorder in the United States, initiated in 2006 as the genetic component of the NIMH-sponsored Genetics Initiative for Bipolar Disorder Consortium to carry out genome-wide association studies: cases with bipolar disorder of European and African American ancestry, collected through the consortium's eleven US collection sites (mostly from multiplex families or sibling pairs for the first, GAIN-funded genotyping; without regard to family history for the later TGen genotyping), and controls from the NIMH Genetics Initiative control sample collected for the Molecular Genetics of Schizophrenia study.

label: Biological pathways of risk and resilience in Syrian refugee children
other synonyms: Biological Pathways of Risk and Resilience in Syrian Refugee Children
definition: A longitudinal cohort of Syrian refugee children aged 8–16 and their primary caregivers, from families who had fled the war in Syria within the previous four years and were living in informal tented settlements in the West and Central Beqaa regions of Lebanon, recruited by purposive cluster sampling from October 2017 to January 2018 and followed up once a year later, with interviews of children and caregivers and children's saliva (for genotyping and DNA methylation) and hair (for cortisol, DHEA and testosterone), to study how psychosocial and biological factors shape resilience and mental health problems; it was funded by the US National Institute of Child Health and Human Development and sponsored by Queen Mary University of London.
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to violence (ECTO:6000001)

label: Biological Determinants of Peritoneal Dialysis
other synonyms: Biological Determinants of PD|Biological Determinants of Peritoneal Dialysis (Bio-PD) study
definition: An international observational cohort study, led from the University of Washington, of adults with kidney failure treated with peritoneal dialysis who had a peritoneal equilibration test soon after starting it, set up to find common genetic variants that influence peritoneal solute transfer rate and ultrafiltration. Participants were enrolled prospectively at centres in Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom and the United States from 2013 to 2018, and DNA and clinical data were added from earlier peritoneal dialysis studies in the United Kingdom (PD-CRAFT), Belgium, Sweden and Hong Kong.

label: A systems BIOlogy Study to TAilored Treatment in Chronic Heart Failure
other synonyms: A Systems Biology Study to Tailored Treatment in Chronic Heart Failure|BIOlogy Study to TAilored Treatment in Chronic Heart Failure|Systems Biology Study to Tailored Treatment in Chronic Heart Failure
definition: A multicentre, prospective, observational European study of adults with new-onset or worsening heart failure who were treated with loop diuretics but received no more than half the target doses of ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers and/or beta-blockers, and whose physicians intended to start or up-titrate these drugs. Its index cohort was enrolled at 69 centres in 11 European countries between December 2010 and December 2012 and its validation cohort at six centres in Scotland between October 2010 and April 2014; funded by the European Commission's Seventh Framework Programme, it combined clinical data, biomarkers, genome-wide genotyping and proteomics to find patient profiles that predict response to guideline-recommended therapy.

label: Human genetic determinants of severe malaria in Malawi
other synonyms: Blantyre-Wellcome Trust Project in Blantyre, Malawi|Malawi-Liverpool Wellcome Clinical Research Programme, Blantyre
definition: An unmatched case-control study of severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria at Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital, Blantyre, Malawi, run by the Malawi-Liverpool Wellcome Trust Clinical Research Programme with the Blantyre Malaria Project. Its cases are children aged 2 months to 14 years admitted with severe malaria (cerebral malaria or severe malarial anaemia) in 1994-2007, its controls are cord-blood samples from infants born at the same hospital in 2006-2007, and blood was also taken from some cases' parents; it is the Malawi partner study of the MalariaGEN Consortial Project 1 and its genome-wide association studies of severe malaria.

label: Begleitende Evaluierung innovativer Testverfahren zur Darmkrebsfrüherkennung
other synonyms: Evaluation of novel markers for early detection of colorectal cancer
definition: An ongoing, prospective, multicentre diagnostic study of participants in the German screening colonoscopy programme, recruited since November 2005 at a preparatory visit before colonoscopy at gastroenterology practices in southern Germany, who donate blood and stool samples and answer a questionnaire. Run from the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) in Heidelberg, it evaluates new blood and stool tests for the early detection of colorectal cancer and advanced adenomas against the findings of screening colonoscopy.

label: Bloodomics
other synonyms: Bloodomics project|Identification of risk genes for atherothrombosis in coronary artery disease by transcriptome and proteome analysis and high throughput exon resequencing|Integrated Project Bloodomics
definition: A European Union Sixth Framework Programme integrated project (June 2004 to November 2008), coordinated by the University of Cambridge with clinical coronary artery disease centres, genomics groups and the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute, that sought genes and pathways of atherothrombosis in coronary artery disease through platelet transcriptome and proteome analysis and exon resequencing. For genetic association studies it assembled a Dutch case-control collection, with cases from the Academic Medical Center Amsterdam Premature Atherosclerosis Study (AMC-PAS) and the AGNES study of first ST-elevation myocardial infarction and controls from Sanquin blood donors, and a German one, with cases and controls from the Ludwigshafen Risk and Cardiovascular Health (LURIC) study and additional blood-donor controls from Mannheim.
diseases: patients with: atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (MONDO:1060134)|patients with: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)

label: BRCA-gene mutations and breast cancer in South African women
other synonyms: BRCA gene mutations and breast cancer in South African women|BRCA-gene mutations and Breast Cancer in South African Women
definition: A South African study of BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations in women with breast cancer and their families, based at the University of Pretoria and funded by the Cancer Association of South Africa. The women it identifies as carriers of pathogenic BRCA1 or BRCA2 variants are contributed to the Consortium of Investigators of Modifiers of BRCA1/2 (CIMBA) for studies of genetic modifiers of breast and ovarian cancer risk in carriers.

label: Bavarian Ovarian Cancer Cases and Controls
other synonyms: Bavarian ovarian cancer study
definition: A case-control study of ovarian cancer in Erlangen, northern Bavaria, Germany, supported by the ELAN programme of the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, whose cases were recruited through the hospital in Erlangen and whose controls were randomly selected women from Erlangen, both enrolled from May 2002 to August 2008 and interviewed. It is one of the studies of the Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium (study code BAV) and contributes to its pooled epidemiological analyses and genome-wide association studies of ovarian cancer.

label: Belgian Ovarian Cancer Study
other synonyms: Belgium Ovarian Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of ovarian cancer at University Hospitals Leuven, Belgium, funded by the Belgian National Cancer Plan (Nationaal Kankerplan). It is one of the studies of the Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium (study code BEL) and contributes cases and controls to its genome-wide association studies of ovarian cancer risk and to its analyses of ovarian cancer outcome.

label: Bonn-Mannheim MDD study
other synonyms: Bonn/Mannheim MDD study
definition: A German case-control study of major depressive disorder whose cases were consecutive admissions with a DSM-IV lifetime diagnosis of major depressive disorder to the psychiatric inpatient units of the University of Bonn and of the Central Institute of Mental Health in Mannheim, diagnosed by best-estimate consensus from a structured interview (SCID-I or SADS), medical records and family history and excluding bipolar disorder, non-affective psychosis and substance-related depression, and whose controls came from the German population-based studies PopGen, KORA and Heinz Nixdorf Recall. It is one of the cohorts of the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium's major depressive disorder working group (cohort code boma).

label: BOMA-Bipolar Study
other synonyms: BOMA-Bipolar Study, University of Bonn and CIMH Mannheim|German BP sample
definition: A German case-control sample for genome-wide association studies of bipolar disorder, from the University of Bonn and the Central Institute of Mental Health in Mannheim, whose cases, nearly all with bipolar I disorder diagnosed by DSM-IV best-estimate consensus from structured interviews (SADS-L or SCID), were recruited from consecutive admissions to psychiatric inpatient units, and whose controls were drawn from the German population-based studies PopGen, KORA and Heinz Nixdorf Recall. It is one of the samples of the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium's bipolar disorder working group.

label: Genetic determinants of COVID-19 complications in the Brazilian population
other synonyms: BRACOVID Study|BRACOVID study
definition: A genetic study of COVID-19 severity in Brazil, based at the University of São Paulo Medical School, which enrolled people infected with SARS-CoV-2 in the São Paulo metropolitan area: patients hospitalised with COVID-19 at the Instituto do Coração (InCor) and the Instituto Central do Hospital das Clínicas, and people with a previous infection who were not hospitalised, found through serological surveys or SARS-CoV-2 PCR testing of health professionals and the general population.
