DNA came from blood samples already taken for clinical tests or serology, with questionnaire or hospital-record data; it was designed to identify genetic risk factors for COVID-19 severity in the Brazilian population and contributes to the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative.

label: Biologics in Rheumatoid Arthritis Genetics and Genomics Study Syndicate
definition: A multicentre observational study of patients with rheumatoid arthritis treated with biologic drugs at rheumatology centres across the United Kingdom, which collects their blood samples for DNA, RNA and cellular studies together with clinical, laboratory and adherence data, to study genetic and other predictors of response to biologic therapy. Its first patients, starting anti-TNF therapy, were identified through the British Society for Rheumatology Biologics Register; from November 2008 patients were recruited before starting a biologic and followed up prospectively for 12 months.

label: Bangladesh Risk of Acute Vascular Events Study
definition: A case-control study of first-onset acute myocardial infarction in Bangladesh, established in 2011 by the University of Cambridge with the International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research, Bangladesh (icddr,b) and the National Institute of Cardiovascular Disease (NICVD) in Dhaka, whose cases are adults admitted to the NICVD's emergency rooms with a first myocardial infarction and whose controls, frequency-matched by age and sex, are hospital visitors without cardiovascular disease; with questionnaire data, electrocardiograms and stored blood samples, it was set up to study environmental, genetic, lifestyle and biochemical determinants of coronary heart disease in Bangladeshis.
diseases: patients with: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)|patients with: myocardial infarction (MONDO:0005068)

label: Belgian case-control study on bladder cancer risk
other synonyms: Belgian Case Control Study of Bladder Cancer|Belgian case control study on bladder cancer|Belgian case control study on bladder cancer risk|Belgian case-control study on bladder cancer
definition: A population-based case-control study of bladder cancer in the Belgian province of Limburg, whose cases are people with histologically confirmed incident transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder diagnosed between 1999 and 2004, identified through the Limburg Cancer Registry and invited by their urologists and general practitioners, and whose controls are inhabitants of the province aged 50 or over sampled at random through the Crossroads Bank of Social Security, stratified by municipality and socioeconomic status; it was used to study occupational, dietary and genetic risk factors for bladder cancer.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to micronutrient via ingestion (ECTO:0900369)|designed to study: exposure to polycyclic arene (ECTO:9000433)|designed to study: exposure to smoking (ECTO:6000013)|designed to study: exposure to vegetable food product via ingestion (ECTO:0070232)

label: Breast Cancer Study of the University Clinic Heidelberg
other synonyms: Breast Cancer Study of the University of Heidelberg
definition: A case-control study of breast cancer in Germany whose cases are women diagnosed with breast cancer in 2007-2009 at the University Women's Clinic Heidelberg and whose controls are female blood donors recruited in the same years at the Institute of Transfusion Medicine and Immunology in Mannheim; it is one of the studies of the Breast Cancer Association Consortium.

label: Beijing Type 2 Diabetes Studies
definition: A type 2 diabetes case-control sample of unrelated Han Chinese from Beijing, China, made up of people with type 2 diabetes and nondiabetic controls, used in genetic association studies of type 2 diabetes and glycaemic traits.

label: Brisbane Twin Nevus Study
other synonyms: Brisbane Twin Naevus Study|TWin Mole study
definition: A study of the Queensland Institute of Medical Research (QIMR) in Brisbane, Australia, that from 1992 to 2016 examined annual new samples of 12-year-old twins from south-east Queensland, with their siblings nearest in age, counting their naevi and recording their sun behaviour, and re-examined them two years later; set up to investigate genetic factors in naevus development and other risk factors for melanoma, it also includes the twins' parents and is the twin mole study of the Brisbane Longitudinal Twin Study.

label: Bus Santé
other synonyms: Bus Sante|Bus Santé study|Bus santé
definition: A repeated cross-sectional population-based health examination survey of adults living in the canton of Geneva, Switzerland, which since 1992 has examined in a mobile unit, each year, a new random sample of residents drawn from the cantonal residents list and stratified by age and sex, collecting questionnaires, physical measurements and blood samples on risk factors for cardiovascular and other lifestyle-related chronic diseases.

label: Camargo Cohort Study
other synonyms: Camargo Cohort|Camargo cohort|Camargo cohort study|Cantabria-Camargo|Cantabria-Camargo study
definition: A prospective community-based cohort of postmenopausal women and men aged 50 years and older who attended a primary care centre in Camargo, Cantabria, in northern Spain, for a regular health examination or for medical reasons, enrolled between February 2006 and February 2011 and re-evaluated in later waves to study the prevalence and incidence of metabolic bone diseases and the risk factors for osteoporosis and fragility fractures.
diseases: population study of: bone fracture (MONDO:0005315)|population study of: metabolic bone disorder (MONDO:0800486)|population study of: osteoporosis (MONDO:0005298)

label: Cantabria Osteoporosis Case-control
other synonyms: Cantabria osteoporosis case-control study
definition: A clinic-based, cross-sectional case-control study of patients with osteoporosis and control individuals, including volunteers, living in Cantabria in northern Spain and recruited in Santander, used to study genetic and hormonal determinants of bone mineral density and osteoporotic fracture.

label: Coronary Artery Disease and Genomics
other synonyms: CADomics Study|CADomics study|Cadomics study|Coronary Artery Disease and Omics|Coronary Artery Disease and genomics
definition: A German case-control study of coronary artery disease that pools patients with angiographically documented coronary artery disease from the hospital catheter-laboratory-based AtheroGene Registry, enrolled in 1999–2004 at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz and the German Federal Armed Forces Central Hospital in Koblenz, with controls without a history of myocardial infarction from the population-based Gutenberg Heart Study of the city of Mainz and the Mainz-Bingen district, assembled for genome-wide association studies of coronary artery disease.

label: Caerphilly Prospective Study
other synonyms: Caerphilly Prospective Heart Disease study|Caerphilly study
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of men aged 45–59 years from the town of Caerphilly and its surrounding villages in South Wales, United Kingdom, identified from electoral rolls and general practice lists and first examined in 1979–1983 by the MRC Epidemiology Unit (South Wales) to study risk factors for coronary heart disease, then re-examined in later phases that added cognitive testing and follow-up for dementia and other chronic diseases.
diseases: population study of: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)

label: Amagasaki Study
other synonyms: CAGE-Amagasaki Study|Cardio-metabolic Genome Epidemiology Network, Amagasaki|Cardio-metabolic Genome Epidemiology Network, Amagasaki Study|Cardio-metabolic Genome Epidemiology Study - Amagasaki
definition: An ongoing population-based cohort of people aged over 18 years in Amagasaki, Hyogo Prefecture, Japan, consecutively enrolled for a baseline examination between September 2002 and August 2003, which is one of the member studies of the Cardio-metabolic Genome Epidemiology (CAGE) Network and whose samples are used in genetic studies of blood pressure, lipids and other cardiometabolic traits.

label: Kyushu University Fukuoka Cohort Study
other synonyms: Fukuoka Cohort|Fukuoka Cohort Study|Fukuoka Study
definition: A community-based prospective cohort of middle-aged and older Japanese men and women in Fukuoka, Japan, run by Kyushu University, who took part in a baseline survey with a questionnaire and DNA collection between February 2004 and August 2007 and are followed up to investigate lifestyle factors and genetic susceptibility to lifestyle-related diseases such as cardiovascular diseases, cancer and diabetes mellitus.

label: Hospital-based Cohort Study at the National Center for Global Health and Medicine
other synonyms: NCGM Hospital-based Cohort Study|National Center for Global health and Medicine hospital-based cohort study
definition: A hospital-based prospective cohort at the National Center for Global Health and Medicine in Tokyo, Japan, whose participants, drawn from the hospital's clinical practice and annual medical check-ups, are enrolled for detailed examination of lifestyle and lifestyle-related diseases such as cardiovascular diseases, cancer and diabetes mellitus to investigate the relationship between genetic and non-genetic factors.

label: Calcium Intake Fracture Outcome Study
other synonyms: Calcium Intake Fracture Outcome study|Calcium intake fracture outcome study|Longitudinal Study of Aging in Women|Perth Longitudinal Study of Ageing Women|Perth Longitudinal Study of Aging Women
definition: A five-year randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of daily calcium carbonate supplementation for fracture prevention in ambulant, community-dwelling women aged 70 years or older, recruited in 1998 from the general population of Western Australia through the electoral roll, whose participants were followed after the trial ended in 2003 in two observational studies to 2013 and through linked Western Australian hospital and death records, the whole study being known as the Perth Longitudinal Study of Ageing Women.

label: CALEX-family study
other synonyms: CALEX family study|Calex family study|Calex-family|Calex-family study
definition: A Finnish three-generation family study run by researchers at the University of Jyväskylä, built on the Calex study, a cohort of girls recruited in school grades 4 to 6 through schools in the city of Jyväskylä and its surroundings in Central Finland (some of whom first took part in a two-year randomised calcium, vitamin D and dairy supplementation trial) and followed through puberty for about 7.5 years; in 2007–2008 the girls, then young women, and their brothers, mothers, fathers, grandmothers and grandfathers were invited to the same bone, body-composition and blood measurements, to study the heritability and determinants of bone mass, body composition and related metabolic traits across generations.

label: Cancer de Mama
other synonyms: CAMA-Mexican Breast Cancer Study|Cancer de Mama study|Cáncer de Mama
definition: A population-based case–control study of breast cancer in Mexican women aged 35 to 69, carried out from January 2004 to December 2007 in Mexico City, Monterrey and Veracruz by investigators of the Mexican National Institute of Public Health, in which women with newly diagnosed, untreated breast cancer were recruited at twelve public hospitals of the Mexican Social Security Institute, the Institute of Security and Social Services of State Workers and the Ministry of Health, and controls, frequency-matched to the cases by age, health-care institution and region, were chosen by multistage random household sampling; participants were interviewed on health, diet and physical activity, measured and gave blood samples, to study risk factors for breast cancer in Mexico.

label: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences Cancer Hospital Study
other synonyms: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences Cancer Hospital|Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences Cancer Hospital study
definition: A lung cancer case–control study of ethnic Han Chinese, carried out from 1997 to 2008, in which cases were recruited from Beijing and surrounding provinces at the Cancer Hospital of the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences in Beijing, China, and cancer-free controls from the same region and period were drawn from a community nutritional survey, to study genetic susceptibility to lung cancer; its never-smoking women take part in the genome-wide association studies of the Female Lung Cancer Consortium in Asia.

label: Canadian screening study
other synonyms: Canadian Screening Study
definition: A Canadian lung cancer case–control sample, drawn as nested case–control sets for the OncoArray lung cancer genome-wide association project from three low-dose computed tomography screening programmes for smokers: the International Early Lung Cancer Action Program site in the Greater Toronto Area organised by Princess Margaret Hospital (enrolling since 2003), the PanCan study, which screened smokers aged 50 to 75 in eight cities across Canada from 2008 to 2011, and the screening programme of the British Columbia Cancer Agency (BCCA), which enrolled heavy smokers from 1990 to 2007.
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to tobacco smoking (ECTO:6000029)

label: Prostate Cancer Genetics Study
definition: A case–control study of more aggressive prostate cancer in men recruited from 2001 to 2004 at the major medical institutions of Cleveland, Ohio, United States (the Cleveland Clinic, University Hospitals of Cleveland and their affiliates), in which cases were newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed prostate cancers of higher grade, stage or prostate-specific antigen level, and age-matched controls were men without prostate cancer undergoing standard annual medical examinations at the same institutions, to study genetic and environmental risk factors for aggressive prostate cancer.

label: Canadian Asthma Primary Prevention Study
other synonyms: Canadian Childhood Cohorts: Canadian Asthma Primary Prevention Study
definition: A prenatally randomised controlled trial, begun in 1995 at university hospital-based centres in Vancouver and Winnipeg, Canada, of infants at high risk of asthma (with at least one first-degree relative with asthma or two with other IgE-mediated allergic diseases) identified before birth, whose families were assigned either to a multifaceted intervention in the first year of life (avoidance of house dust mite, pet allergens and environmental tobacco smoke, encouragement of breastfeeding with partially hydrolysed formula supplementation, and delayed introduction of solid foods) or to a control group, and whose children were followed as a birth cohort with paediatric allergist assessments to age 15, to test the primary prevention of asthma and allergy.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to allergen (ECTO:0000726)|designed to study: exposure to allergen via inhalation (ECTO:0900047)|designed to study: exposure to human milk (raw) via ingestion (ECTO:0070224)|designed to study: exposure to smoke (ECTO:7000059)

label: Carotid Atherosclerosis Progression Study
definition: A community-based prospective cohort study in Germany in which adults aged about 19 to 90, volunteers from among the members of a German primary health-care scheme, had vascular risk factors and carotid intima–media thickness measured by ultrasound at baseline and again after about three years, and were followed for about ten years for myocardial infarction, stroke, transient ischaemic attack and death, to study the progression of early carotid atherosclerosis and its value in predicting vascular events.

label: Cáncer de Pulmón en Asturias
other synonyms: CAncer de PUlmon en Asturias|Cancer de Pulmon en Asturias|Cancer de Pulmon en Asturias study|Lung Cancer in Asturias|The Cancer de Pulmon en Asturias study
definition: A hospital-based case–control study of lung cancer in Asturias, northern Spain, run by the Molecular Epidemiology of Cancer Unit of the University Institute of Oncology of the University of Oviedo, which from October 2000 used a standard protocol to recruit incident, histologically confirmed lung cancer cases aged 30 to 85 living in the areas of the main hospitals of Asturias (in Gijón, Avilés, Oviedo and Mieres), with controls admitted to the same hospitals for conditions unrelated to the exposures studied and individually matched by ethnicity, sex, age and hospital; participants were interviewed on tobacco, diet, occupation and environmental exposures and gave blood or mouthwash samples, to study lifestyle, occupational and genetic risk factors for lung cancer.

label: Collaborative Atorvastatin Diabetes Study
other synonyms: Collaborative AtoRvastatin Diabetes Study|Collaborative Atorvastatin Diabetes Trial|Collaborative Atorvastatin in Diabetes Trial
definition: A multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of atorvastatin 10 mg daily for the primary prevention of cardiovascular disease in men and women aged 40–75 with type 2 diabetes, no history of cardiovascular disease, LDL cholesterol of 4.14 mmol/l or less and at least one further risk factor (retinopathy, albuminuria, current smoking or hypertension), who were randomised between November 1997 and June 2001 at centres in the United Kingdom and Ireland. It was run as a collaboration of Diabetes UK, the NHS Research and Development Directorate and Pfizer UK, and was stopped early when its prespecified efficacy criterion was met.

label: Cholesterol and Recurrent Events
other synonyms: Cholesterol and Recurrent Events study|Cholesterol and Recurrent Events trial
definition: A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled secondary-prevention trial of pravastatin 40 mg daily in men and postmenopausal women aged 21–75 who had had a myocardial infarction 3 to 20 months earlier and had average cholesterol levels (total cholesterol below 240 mg/dl and LDL cholesterol of 115–174 mg/dl), enrolled at 80 hospitals and affiliated centres in the United States and Canada and followed for about five years to test whether lowering cholesterol reduces fatal coronary heart disease and nonfatal myocardial infarction. It was initiated by its investigators and funded by Bristol-Myers Squibb.
diseases: patients with: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)|patients with: myocardial infarction (MONDO:0005068)

label: Childhood Asthma Research and Education Network
other synonyms: Childhood Asthma Research and Education|Childhood Asthma Research and Education network|Childhood Asthma Research and Education program
definition: A paediatric asthma clinical research network created in 1999 by the US National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, made up of five clinical centres (University of California, San Diego; University of Arizona, Tucson; Washington University, St. Louis; University of Wisconsin, Madison; National Jewish Medical and Research Center, Denver) and a data coordinating centre at Penn State University, Hershey, to evaluate new and existing asthma therapies in children through multicentre randomised clinical trials. Its trial cohorts include the Prevention of Early Asthma in Kids (PEAK) trial in preschool children at high risk of asthma and the CLIC and PACT trials in school-aged children with mild-to-moderate persistent asthma.

label: Carotene and Retinol Efficacy Trial
other synonyms: Beta Carotene and Retinol Efficacy Trial|Beta-Carotene and Retinol Efficacy Trial|β-Carotene and Retinol Efficacy Trial
definition: A multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of daily beta-carotene (30 mg) plus retinyl palmitate (25,000 IU) for the primary prevention of lung cancer in people at high risk of it, namely male and female heavy smokers and former smokers and asbestos-exposed men, recruited at centres in Seattle, Portland, San Francisco, Irvine, Baltimore and New Haven, United States, in a pilot phase from 1985 and an efficacy phase from 1989. The intervention was stopped in January 1996, 21 months early, because it increased lung cancer incidence and mortality; participants were followed through 2005, and the serum, plasma, whole blood and lung tissue collected during the trial form the CARET Biorepository.
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to asbestos (ECTO:9000033)|participants with exposure: exposure to tobacco smoking (ECTO:6000029)

label: Clinical Antipsychotic Trials of Intervention Effectiveness
other synonyms: CATIE schizophrenia trial
definition: A multiphase randomised trial of the effectiveness of antipsychotic drugs in adults aged 18–67 with chronic schizophrenia, run under the US National Institute of Mental Health's CATIE programme in 2001–2004 at 57 clinical sites across the United States (public mental health, academic, Veterans Affairs and managed care settings), whose double-blind first phase compared the first-generation drug perphenazine with the second-generation drugs olanzapine, quetiapine, risperidone and ziprasidone for up to 18 months, with all-cause treatment discontinuation as the primary outcome. Participants could join an optional genetic sub-study by donating DNA.

label: Comorbidity and Trauma Study
definition: A retrospective case–control study of genetic and environmental contributions to heroin dependence, funded by the US National Institute on Drug Abuse in 2003 and run by Washington University, the Queensland Institute of Medical Research and the National Drug and Alcohol Research Centre (University of New South Wales), which from 2004 recruited opioid-dependent adults from opioid substitution (maintenance) treatment clinics in the greater Sydney area, Australia, and neighbourhood controls with little or no lifetime opioid use from socially disadvantaged areas served by the same clinics. Participants gave blood for DNA and completed a psychiatric diagnostic interview (SSAGA-OZ) with added assessments of childhood trauma, family history and borderline personality disorder.

label: Croatian Colorectal Cancer Genetic Study
other synonyms: Croatia CRC case-control study|Croatia case-control CRC study
definition: A case–control study of colorectal cancer in Croatia, whose cases are patients with colorectal cancer recruited from November 2008 at the surgery departments of two tertiary hospitals in Zagreb that receive patients from across the country, and whose population controls without a history of cancer were drawn at random, by age and sex, from the '10,001 Dalmatians' study of the general population of Split and the islands of Vis and Korčula. Its participants were genotyped for known colorectal cancer risk variants and later genome-wide, for European colorectal cancer genome-wide association studies.

label: Cambridgeshire Case-Control Study
other synonyms: Cambridgeshire Case-Control Population|Cambridgeshire case-control study
definition: A population-based case–control study of type 2 diabetes in Cambridgeshire, United Kingdom, whose cases are Europid men and women with type 2 diabetes (onset after age 30 without insulin treatment in the first year after diagnosis) randomly selected from general practice diabetes registers in a geographically defined region of Cambridgeshire, and whose controls were recruited at random from the same population sampling frames and individually matched to cases for age, sex and general practice, with diabetes excluded by medical record search and an HbA1c below 6%. It was funded by the Medical Research Council with support from NHS Research and Development and the Wellcome Trust.

label: Cleveland Clinic GeneBank Study
other synonyms: Cleveland Clinic Gene Bank|Cleveland Clinic GeneBank|Cleveland Clinic GeneBank study|Cleveland Clinic Genebank|GeneBank|GeneBank Study|GeneBank at the Cleveland Clinic: Molecular Determinants of Coronary Artery Disease
definition: A single-centre prospective cohort and sample repository of consecutive adults undergoing elective diagnostic coronary angiography or elective cardiac computed tomographic angiography at the Cleveland Clinic, Cleveland, Ohio, United States, enrolled from 2001 to 2007 with blood samples, extensive clinical and laboratory characterisation and adjudicated follow-up for death, myocardial infarction and stroke, set up to study the genetic and molecular determinants of coronary artery disease.

label: Cleveland Clinic FMD Biorepository
definition: A biorepository of DNA and clinical data from adults with fibromuscular dysplasia enrolled at the Cleveland Clinic, Cleveland, Ohio, United States, from consecutive patients seen at its dedicated fibromuscular dysplasia referral clinic, each giving a blood or saliva sample, used in genetic studies of fibromuscular dysplasia and of arterial dissection, including spontaneous coronary artery dissection.

label: Crete Cancer Genetics Program
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of breast cancer in Crete, Greece, run under the Crete Cancer Genetics Program with the approval of the Scientific Council of the University General Hospital of Heraklion and funded by the University of Crete, whose breast cancer cases and controls were genotyped on the OncoArray within the Breast Cancer Association Consortium.

label: China Cardiovascular Health Study
other synonyms: China Cardiovascular Health Study project
definition: A population-based study of cardiovascular disease and its risk factors in Chinese adults, carried out by the Department of Epidemiology of Fuwai Hospital (National Center for Cardiovascular Diseases, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and Peking Union Medical College), Beijing, with field centres in several provinces, including Jiangsu, Shandong and Henan, and funded by the Ministry of Science and Technology of China.

label: Cross Cancer Institute Prostate Brachytherapy Cohort
other synonyms: CCI Prostate|Cross Cancer Institute–Brachytherapy
definition: A hospital-based case series of men with prostate cancer treated with iodine-125 (125I) brachytherapy implants as monotherapy at the Cross Cancer Institute, Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, and identified through its clinics, who gave saliva samples for DNA and whose clinical, dosimetric and toxicity data were compiled retrospectively, assembled to study genetic and other predictors of late toxicity after prostate brachytherapy.

label: Connecticut Endometrial Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of endometrial cancer conducted in Connecticut, United States, from December 2004 to March 2009 by investigators at the Yale School of Public Health and Yale Cancer Center, which enrolled women aged 35–80 newly diagnosed with primary endometrial cancer from October 2004 through September 2008, identified at 28 Connecticut hospitals by the Yale Cancer Center Rapid Case Ascertainment Shared Resource, and controls frequency-matched on age and found by random-digit dialling, who were interviewed at home and gave biological specimens, to study risk factors for endometrial cancer.

label: Besta Cerebrovascular Diseases Registry
other synonyms: Besta Stroke Register|Cerebrovascular Diseases Registry|Milano Besta Institute Stroke Study
definition: A registry of stroke patients at the Carlo Besta Neurological Institute (Fondazione IRCCS Istituto Neurologico Carlo Besta), Milan, Italy, including consecutive Italian patients with stroke referred to the institute from 2000 to 2009, funded by the Italian Ministry of Health; its imaging-confirmed ischaemic stroke cases, subtyped by stroke neurologists with the TOAST criteria, were genotyped and studied with Italian PROCARDIS participants as controls in genome-wide association studies of stroke.

label: Central and Eastern European Renal Cell Carcinoma Study
other synonyms: CEERCC case-control study|Central and Eastern European Kidney Cancer Study|Central and Eastern European RCC case-control study|Central and Eastern European Renal Cancer Study|Central and Eastern European Renal Cell Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based multicentre case–control study of renal cell carcinoma conducted by the International Agency for Research on Cancer and the US National Cancer Institute at seven centres in Moscow (Russia), Bucharest (Romania), Lodz (Poland) and Prague, Olomouc, Ceske Budejovice and Brno (Czech Republic), which recruited newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed cases aged 20–79 between August 1999 and January 2003 and controls admitted to the same hospitals for conditions unrelated to smoking or genitourinary disease, some of them recruited in parallel for IARC's lung and head and neck cancer case–control studies. Participants were interviewed with standardised questionnaires on lifestyle, diet and medical, residential and occupational history and gave blood for DNA, to study the causes of the region's high kidney cancer rates.

label: CEFALO
other synonyms: CEFALO study|Cefalo
definition: An international population-based case–control study of primary intracranial brain tumours in children and adolescents aged 7–19 in Denmark, Norway, Sweden and Switzerland, whose cases were diagnosed between 2004 and 2008 and identified through hospitals and national cancer registries, and whose controls were drawn at random from population registries and matched by age, sex and region. The children and their parents were interviewed in person, mainly to find out whether mobile phone use and other exposures raise the risk of brain tumours; saliva DNA from part of the participants was genotyped in candidate-gene studies.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to radiowave radiation (ECTO:8000054)

label: Color Genomics
other synonyms: Color Genomics participants|Color genomics study
definition: A research cohort of people whose healthcare provider ordered clinical-grade multi-gene panel testing for inherited disease risk, such as hereditary breast and ovarian cancer, from Color Genomics, a commercial genetic testing laboratory in Burlingame, California, and who gave electronic informed consent, under a Western Institutional Review Board protocol, for their de-identified samples, sequence data and health histories, self-reported through an online tool, to be used in research.
diseases: at risk of: hereditary breast ovarian cancer syndrome (MONDO:0003582)

label: Candidate Gene Association Resource
other synonyms: CARe Consortium|Candidate Gene Association Resource Consortium|Candidate gene Association Resource|Candidate-gene Association Resource|NHLBI CARe Project|NHLBI Candidate Gene Association Resource|National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute Candidate Gene Association Resource
definition: A shared genotype–phenotype resource set up by the US National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute in 2006, which brought DNA samples and phenotype data from nine NHLBI cohort studies (ARIC, CARDIA, the Cleveland Family Study, the Cardiovascular Health Study, the Cooperative Study of Sickle Cell Disease, the Framingham Heart Study, the Jackson Heart Study, MESA and the Sleep Heart Health Study) to the Broad Institute, genotyped their European American, African American, Hispanic and Chinese American participants on a candidate-gene array (the ITMAT-Broad-CARe array) and the African American participants of five of the cohorts genome-wide, and makes the data available to approved researchers, to find genetic variants associated with cardiovascular, pulmonary, haematological and sleep-related traits.

label: Copenhagen General Population Study
other synonyms: Herlev/Østerbroundersøgelsen
definition: A prospective general-population cohort run from Herlev and Gentofte Hospital, Copenhagen University Hospital, and modelled on the Copenhagen City Heart Study, which from 2003 to 2015 invited adults aged 20–100 living in the greater Copenhagen area, identified through the Danish Civil Registration System (all those aged 40 or over and a quarter of those aged 20–39), and examined them with a questionnaire, a physical examination, lung function tests and blood sampling with DNA extraction. Participants are re-examined in a second round that began in 2014 and are followed through the national Danish health registries for cardiovascular, pulmonary and other diseases and death.

label: China Multi-Center Collaborative Study of Cardiovascular Epidemiology 1998
other synonyms: China Multi-Center Collaborative Study of Cardiovascular Epidemiology
definition: A population-based cohort of Chinese men and women aged 35–59, selected in 1998 by cluster random sampling in several provinces of China for the 1998 survey of the China Multi-Center Collaborative Study of Cardiovascular Epidemiology (a separate sample from that study's 1992–1994 cohort), whose participants were followed up in 2007–2008, 2012–2015 and 2018–2020 under the uniform protocol of the China-PAR project to study cardiovascular risk factors and incident atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

label: Chingford 1000 Women Study
other synonyms: Chingford 1,000 Women Study|Chingford Study|Chingford cohort|Chingford general population cohort|Chingford general population survey|Chingford study
definition: A prospective population-based cohort of women aged 45–64 registered with a large general practice in Chingford, North-East London, United Kingdom, recruited in 1988–1989 to study osteoarthritis, osteoporosis and other musculoskeletal disease and assessed annually for over 20 years (to 2010) with clinical examinations, nurse-administered questionnaires, hand and knee radiographs and bone density measurements; deaths are traced through the Office for National Statistics.
diseases: population study of: musculoskeletal system disorder (MONDO:0002081)

label: Chinese Prostate Cancer Genetic and Environmental Correlation Study
definition: A case–control study of prostate cancer in Han Chinese men run by the CHIPGECS collaborative group of Chinese hospitals and universities with Barts Cancer Institute, Queen Mary University of London, which recruited hospital patients with a pathological diagnosis of primary prostate cancer and cancer-free men of comparable age from the community or from hospital attendees having routine physical examinations, in several regions of China (south, southeast, southwest, central and northeast), and whose samples were genotyped with the PRACTICAL consortium on the iCOGS and OncoArray arrays.

label: ChooseWell 365
other synonyms: ChooseWell 365 Study
definition: A randomized clinical trial among employees of Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston, Massachusetts, aged 20 to 75, who regularly paid for food at the hospital's traffic-light-labelled cafeterias with their employee ID, enrolled between September 2016 and February 2018 and followed for 24 months to test whether a 12-month automated, personalized intervention (feedback on their cafeteria purchases, health and lifestyle tips, social norm comparisons and financial incentives) prevented weight gain and improved diet.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to eating behavior (ECTO:6000021)

label: Children's Health Study
other synonyms: Childrens Health Study|Southern California Children's Health Study|USC Children's Health Study
definition: A prospective study of schoolchildren in southern California, run by the University of Southern California, that from 1993 recruited successive cohorts from school classrooms in 16 communities chosen to differ in regional air pollution (fourth, seventh and tenth graders in 1993, fourth graders in 1996, and kindergarten and first-grade children in 2002–2003) and followed them through school with yearly questionnaires and lung function tests, to study the chronic effects of air pollution and other environmental and genetic factors on children's respiratory health, asthma and lung function growth.
diseases: population study of: asthma (MONDO:0004979)|population study of: respiratory system disorder (MONDO:0005087)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to air pollution (ECTO:8000036)

label: Copenhagen Ischemic Heart Disease Study
other synonyms: Copenhagen Ischaemic Heart Disease Study|Copenhagen ischaemic Heart Disease Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of ischaemic heart disease in Denmark whose cases are patients from the greater Copenhagen area referred for coronary angiography to Copenhagen University Hospital from 1991 onwards, with ischaemic heart disease documented by coronary stenosis or atherosclerosis on angiography, a positive exercise electrocardiogram or myocardial infarction, and whose controls without ischaemic heart disease are sampled from the Copenhagen General Population Study; with the Copenhagen City Heart Study and the Copenhagen General Population Study it is used in genetic and Mendelian randomization studies of cardiovascular disease.

label: Community Intervention of Metabolic Syndrome in China and Chinese Family Health Study
other synonyms: Community Intervention of Metabolic Syndrome in China & Chinese Family Health Study
definition: A community-based cohort of Chinese adults aged 18 or over recruited in 2007–2008 by three-stage cluster random sampling at four survey sites, in Shandong, Henan and Jiangsu provinces, chosen for their different levels of economic development; it is one of the sub-cohorts of the Prediction for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Risk in China (China-PAR) project, followed up with the other sub-cohorts under a uniform protocol in 2012–2015 and 2018–2020 to study cardiovascular risk factors and incident cardiovascular disease.

label: Mayo Clinic Center for the Individualized Treatment of Alcoholism Study
other synonyms: A Probe Study of Acamprosate: Genes Associated With Response|Mayo Clinic Center for Individualized Treatment of Addiction|Mayo Clinic Center for Individualized Treatment of Alcohol Dependence|Mayo Clinic Center for Individualized Treatment of Alcoholism study|Mayo Clinic Center for the Individual Treatment of Alcohol Dependence|Mayo Clinic Center for the Individualized Treatment of Alcoholism study
definition: A pharmacogenomic study of acamprosate response in alcohol dependence, conducted from 2008 to 2013 by the Mayo Clinic Center for the Individualized Treatment of Alcoholism, which enrolled men and women aged 18–80 with a primary diagnosis of current alcohol dependence (DSM-IV-TR) whose last drink was at least 5 days before enrolment, from community-based residential and outpatient treatment programmes affiliated with Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota, and Mayo Clinic Health System sites in Austin and Albert Lea, Minnesota, and La Crosse, Wisconsin, treated them with acamprosate for 3 months in an open-label, naturalistic prospective design and collected DNA and plasma to identify biomarkers of treatment response.
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to alcohol abuse (ECTO:6000009)

label: ChiLdhood Arthritis Risk factor Identification sTudY
other synonyms: CLARITY JIA Biobank|Childhood Arthritis Risk Factor Identification Study
definition: A case-control study and biobank of juvenile idiopathic arthritis at the Royal Children's Hospital in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, begun in February 2008, whose cases are children aged 18 or under with juvenile idiopathic arthritis diagnosed by age 16, recruited at hospital clinic visits within six months of diagnosis (incident) or later (prevalent, diagnosed since 1997), and whose controls are healthy Victorian-born children undergoing minor elective surgery at the hospital's Day Surgery Unit; families complete questionnaires on clinical, epidemiological and environmental factors and the children give a blood sample, to identify genomic and environmental risk factors for the disease.

label: California Men's Health Study
other synonyms: California Mens Health Study
definition: A prospective multiethnic cohort of men aged 45 to 69 who were members of the northern and southern California regions of the Kaiser Permanente health plan, recruited in 2002–2003 through a two-stage mailed or online questionnaire with mailing strategies to enrich the cohort with non-white men, and followed through linkage with the health plan's electronic clinical, laboratory, hospitalisation, cancer registry and mortality data, mainly to study the causes of prostate cancer and also of other cancers and non-cancerous conditions in men.

label: Spanish National Cancer Centre Breast Cancer Study
definition: A case-control study of breast cancer of the Spanish National Cancer Research Centre (CNIO) in Madrid, Spain, whose cases, recruited in 2000–2005, are consecutive breast cancer patients from three public hospitals, two in Madrid and one in Oviedo, and women with at least one affected first-degree relative recruited through the CNIO family cancer clinic in Madrid, and whose controls are women free of breast cancer attending the Menopause Research Centre in Madrid or a free medical check-up for female members of the College of Lawyers in Madrid; it is one of the studies of the Breast Cancer Association Consortium.

label: Nutrition, Metabolism and Atherosclerosis Clinic cohort
other synonyms: CNMA cohort|Clinique de nutrition métabolisme et athérosclérose|Nutrition, Metabolism and Atherosclerosis Clinic|Nutrition, Metabolism and Atherosclerosis Clinic (CNMA) of Institut de recherches cliniques de Montréal
definition: A retrospective clinic-based cohort of patients with familial hypercholesterolaemia caused by a known mutation, identified by genetic screening among the patients with dyslipidaemia attending the lipid clinic (Nutrition, Metabolism and Atherosclerosis Clinic) of the Institut de recherches cliniques de Montréal in Montreal, Canada, whose clinical records and lipid profiles, measured after a washout of cholesterol-lowering medication, are used to study genetic and clinical modifiers of lipid levels and cardiovascular disease in familial hypercholesterolaemia.

label: Chonnam National University Lung Cancer Study
definition: A case–control study of lung cancer based at Chonnam National University Hwasun Hospital in Jeollanam-do, South Korea. From 2000 it enrolled consecutive patients, all ethnic Koreans, with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed incident lung cancer, excluding secondary or recurrent tumours, and compared them with population-based controls to study genetic susceptibility to lung cancer. Its never-smoking women were genotyped genome-wide as one of the studies of the Female Lung Cancer Consortium in Asia.

label: An Epidemiological Study of Periodontal Disease and Diabetes: Cytokine Genes and Inflammation Factors
other synonyms: COBRE for Oral Health|COBRE for Oral Health Study|Center of Biomedical Research Excellence for Oral Health pilot project
definition: A cross-sectional genetic and epidemiological study of periodontal disease and caries in Gullah African Americans with type 2 diabetes from the Sea Islands and coastal low country of South Carolina. The Medical University of South Carolina ran it as the first project funded through its NIH Center of Biomedical Research Excellence (COBRE) for Oral Health. Participants were recruited in 2004–2006 from Project SuGAR, community health fairs and churches, were examined at MUSC in Charleston or at four off-site centres and gave blood for DNA, so that periodontal disease could be related to diabetes control, cytokine genes and inflammation. Their data form one of the studies of the Sea Islands Genetics Network.
diseases: patients with: periodontal disorder (MONDO:0002635)|patients with: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: Copenhagen Cardiovascular Genetic study
other synonyms: The Copenhagen Cardiovascular Genetic study
definition: A biobank of whole blood left over from the clinical care of patients admitted in 2010–2017 to six cardiology departments in the Capital Region of Denmark, around Copenhagen. The samples are linked to Danish clinical registries such as the Eastern Danish Heart Registry, and genotyped subsets of the patients, for example those who underwent coronary angiography in 2010–2014, are used to study the genetics of coronary artery disease, heart failure and other cardiovascular disease.
diseases: patients with: cardiovascular disorder (MONDO:0004995)|patients with: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)

label: Colorectal Cancer Genetic Susceptibility Study
other synonyms: Colorectal Cancer Genetics Study|Colorectal Cancer Susceptibility Study
definition: A Scotland-wide study run from Edinburgh from 1999 that approached patients newly diagnosed with colorectal cancer at age 55 or younger. Research nurses visited them at home to take a family pedigree, give genetic counselling and take blood for genetic testing, to evaluate a strategy for finding families with hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer and to study inherited susceptibility to colorectal cancer. Population controls matched by age, sex and area of residence were recruited through the Scottish NHS. Its early-onset cases and controls formed the Scotland1 genome-wide association study of colorectal cancer.
diseases: patients with: Lynch syndrome (MONDO:0005835)|patients with: colorectal cancer (MONDO:0005575)

label: ColoCare Study
other synonyms: ColoCare study|International ColoCare Study
definition: An international, multicentre prospective cohort of adults newly diagnosed with invasive colorectal cancer of any stage. It began at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center in Seattle in 2007 and from 2009 added sites in Tampa, Heidelberg (Germany), Salt Lake City, Los Angeles, St. Louis and Memphis. Patients are enrolled before surgery. They complete questionnaires and give blood, urine and stool at enrolment and repeatedly during five years of follow-up, tumour and adipose tissue are collected at surgery, and treatment and outcome data are abstracted from medical records, so that biomarkers and modifiable lifestyle factors that predict recurrence, survival, treatment toxicity and quality of life can be found.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to Physical Activity (ECTO:6000039)|designed to study: exposure to alcohol consumption (ECTO:0001082)|designed to study: exposure to dietary supplement, vitamin(s) and fatty acids via ingestion (ECTO:0070245)|designed to study: exposure to eating behavior (ECTO:6000021)

label: Colorectal cancer: Longitudinal, Observational study on Nutritional and lifestyle factors that influence colorectal tumour recurrence, survival and quality of life
other synonyms: COLON study|COlorectal cancer: Longitudinal, Observational study on Nutritional and lifestyle factors that may influence colorectal tumour recurrence, survival and quality of life|Colorectal Cancer: Longitudinal Observational study on Nutritional and lifestyle factors that influence colorectal tumor recurrence, survival and quality of life|Colorectal cancer: Longitudinal, Observational study on Nutritional and lifestyle factors that may influence colorectal tumour recurrence, survival and quality of life|Longitudinal, observational study on nutritional and lifestyle factors for colorectal cancer and related outcomes
definition: A multicentre prospective cohort of patients newly diagnosed with colorectal cancer of any stage, recruited in 2010–2020 at 11 hospitals in the Netherlands by investigators at Wageningen University. Participants complete questionnaires on diet, dietary supplements, physical activity, body weight and quality of life and give blood at diagnosis and 6 months, 2 years and 5 years later, while clinical data come from the Netherlands Cancer Registry and hospital records. The aim is to learn how diet and other lifestyle factors influence recurrence, survival and quality of life after colorectal cancer.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to Physical Activity (ECTO:6000039)|designed to study: exposure to dietary supplement, vitamin(s) and fatty acids via ingestion (ECTO:0070245)|designed to study: exposure to eating behavior (ECTO:6000021)

label: Post-Columbian Study of Environmental and Heritable Causes of Breast Cancer
other synonyms: COLUMBUS Consortium|Colombian Study of Environmental and Heritable Causes of Breast Cancer|Post Columbian Study of Environmental and Heritable Causes of Breast Cancer
definition: A case–control study of breast cancer in Latin American women, led by investigators at the Universidad del Tolima in Ibagué, Colombia, and the University of California, Davis. From 2011 it recruited women with incident invasive breast cancer, through population cancer registries and large cancer hospitals in Bogotá, Ibagué and Neiva in central Colombia and Pasto in the south, together with cancer-free controls from the same institutions matched on education, socioeconomic status and local origin. A Mexican arm comprises cases diagnosed from 2010 at the Social Security hospital in Mexico City, with blood-donor controls from the same hospital. The study investigates inherited and environmental causes of breast cancer, and its Colombian and Mexican arms, genotyped on different arrays, are analysed as separate datasets.

label: Consortium for the Investigation of Renal Malignancies
other synonyms: CONFIRM Kidney Study|Consortium For the Investigation of Renal Malignancies
definition: A kidney cancer study run by Cancer Council Victoria with QIMR Berghofer, the Victorian and Queensland cancer registries and hospitals and familial cancer clinics across Australia; its Queensland arm is called the CARE Study. Its population-based case–control family component recruited, through the Victorian and Queensland cancer registries, people diagnosed in 2009–2015, at age 18–74, with histologically confirmed renal cell carcinoma, with siblings and partners of cases as controls. The study also enrolled people with a strong family history of kidney cancer or a hereditary kidney cancer syndrome. Participants completed questionnaires on health, lifestyle and family and medical history and gave blood, so that lifestyle, environmental and genetic causes of kidney cancer could be investigated.
diseases: patients with: kidney cancer (MONDO:0002367)|patients with: renal cell carcinoma (MONDO:0005086)

label: Danish National Patient Register
other synonyms: Danish National Hospital Register|Danish National Patient Registry|Danish National Registry of Patients|Landspatientregisteret
definition: A nationwide Danish hospital register, established in 1977 from the hospital discharge records that Denmark's counties were asked to submit and now kept by the Danish Health Data Authority, that records every patient discharged from Danish non-psychiatric hospitals since 1977 and psychiatric inpatients and emergency-department and outpatient specialty-clinic contacts since 1995, with diagnoses, examinations, treatments and surgical procedures. Kept primarily to monitor hospital use for health-care planning, it is also used, through linkage by personal identification number, for disease monitoring, quality assurance and research.

label: Duke Neurogenetics Study
other synonyms: Duke Neurogenetics study
definition: A study of young adult university students aged 18–22, most of them Duke University undergraduates recruited on campus in Durham, North Carolina, United States, who between 2010 and 2016 completed self-report and behavioural measures, functional and structural brain MRI and genotyping in Duke University's Laboratory of NeuroGenetics. People with psychiatric diagnoses were not excluded, as the study set out to relate variation in behaviour, brain and genes to risk for psychopathology.

label: Dubbo Osteoporosis Epidemiology Study
other synonyms: Dubbo Osteoporosis Epidemiology study
definition: A prospective population-based study of osteoporosis and fracture that in 1989 invited all men and women aged 60 or over living in Dubbo, New South Wales, Australia, a city chosen because its age and sex structure resembled Australia's and its isolation allowed near-complete ascertainment of fractures, and recruited further participants from 2000. Run by investigators of the Garvan Institute of Medical Research, Sydney, it reassessed participants every two to three years with interviews and bone densitometry and recorded fractures from the area's radiology services until 2020.
diseases: population study of: bone fracture (MONDO:0005315)|population study of: osteoporosis (MONDO:0005298)

label: Danish Osteoporosis Prevention Study
definition: An investigator-initiated, partly randomised multicentre trial in Denmark that in 1990–1993 enrolled healthy white women aged 45–58 in early menopause, recruited by direct mailing to a random sample of women from the general population, and allocated them, open label, to hormone replacement therapy or no treatment either at random or by their own choice. Planned to run for 20 years, with its randomised treatment stopped in 2002, it was set up to test whether hormone replacement therapy started soon after menopause prevents osteoporotic fractures and to find clinical, biochemical and densitometric predictors of low bone mass and fracture.
diseases: population study of: bone fracture (MONDO:0005315)|population study of: osteoporosis (MONDO:0005298)

label: Diseases of the Ovary and their Evaluation Study
other synonyms: Diseases of the Ovary and Their Evaluation Study|Diseases of the Ovary and their Evaluation
definition: A population-based case–control study of epithelial ovarian cancer in western Washington State, United States, run from Seattle with funding from the US National Cancer Institute, that enrolled women aged 35–74 diagnosed in 2002–2009 in a 13-county area, identified through the region's SEER cancer registry, together with controls from the same area identified by random-digit dialling, and collected in-person interviews and, from cases, tumour tissue.

label: Danish Psychiatric Central Research Register
other synonyms: Danish Psychiatric Central Register|Psychiatric Central Research Register
definition: A nationwide Danish register of patients treated in psychiatric departments, with records collected systematically from 1938 and computerised from 1969, covering all admissions to psychiatric hospitals and psychiatric wards of general hospitals in Denmark, the Faroe Islands and Greenland and, since 1995, all psychiatric outpatient contacts, with dates of treatment, diagnoses, referral, place and mode of admission and municipality of residence. Kept within a psychiatric epidemiology research unit and fed since 1995 through the Danish National Patient Register, it is used for national health planning and psychiatric epidemiological research.

label: Danish Pelvic Mass Study
other synonyms: Danish Pelvic Mass study|Pelvic Mass Study
definition: A prospective Danish study that from September 2004 enrolled consecutive women aged 18 or older admitted for surgery because of a suspected pelvic mass to the Gynaecologic Clinic of Copenhagen University Hospital, Rigshospitalet, collecting their blood and tumour tissue with clinical data to identify factors that distinguish benign from malignant pelvic masses and predict the prognosis of ovarian cancer.
diseases: patients with: Pelvic mass (HP:0031501)|patients with: ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170)

label: Assessment of Risk for Colorectal Tumors in Canada
other synonyms: ARCTIC Genome Project|Assessment of Risk in Colorectal Tumors In Canada|Assessment of Risk in Colorectal Tumors in Canada|Assessment of Risk of Colorectal Tumors in Canada|Assessment of Risk of Colorectal Tumours in Canada
definition: A colorectal cancer genomics project in Ontario, Canada (the ARCTIC Genome Project), hosted by Cancer Care Ontario and funded by Genome Canada through the Ontario Genomics Institute and other agencies, whose case-control sample consists of participants of the Ontario Familial Colorectal Cancer Registry: people aged 20–74 with colorectal cancer diagnosed in 1997–2000 and identified through the population-based Ontario Cancer Registry, and population controls randomly selected and frequency-matched to them by sex and five-year age group. They were genotyped genome-wide to find common variants associated with colorectal cancer, and the sample has since been used for risk-prediction and DNA methylation studies.

label: Breast Cancer Collaborative Registry
definition: A web-based multicentre breast cancer registry developed at the University of Nebraska Medical Center's Eppley Cancer Center in Omaha, Nebraska, United States, and maintained by the Fred & Pamela Buffett Cancer Center as part of its integrated Cancer Repository for Cancer Research (iCaRe2), into which participating cancer centres in the US Midwest enrol breast cancer patients, breast cancer survivors and women at increased risk of breast cancer. Under common protocols it collects questionnaire data on demographic, medical, family, lifestyle, dietary and environmental factors, clinical and follow-up data and biospecimens for research on breast cancer diagnosis, prevention, treatment and survivorship.

label: Bipolar Disorder Research Network
other synonyms: UK Bipolar Disorder Research Network
definition: A cohort of adults of European ancestry with bipolar disorder (bipolar I or II disorder, schizoaffective disorder of bipolar type or bipolar disorder not otherwise specified) recruited from across the United Kingdom by the Bipolar Disorder Research Network, an ongoing research programme run from Cardiff and Worcester, systematically through NHS community mental health teams and lithium clinics and non-systematically through media advertising and patient charities such as Bipolar UK. Participants are interviewed by trained psychologists and psychiatrists with the Schedules for Clinical Assessment in Neuropsychiatry and their case notes reviewed, to study the genetic and environmental causes of bipolar and related mood disorders.

label: Center for Education and Drug Abuse Research
other synonyms: Center for Education and Drug Abuse research
definition: A longitudinal family high-risk study of the development of substance use disorder, run in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States, by the Center for Education and Drug Abuse Research of the University of Pittsburgh, a Center of Excellence funded by the National Institute on Drug Abuse and completed in 2015, which recruited nuclear families of a father with or without a lifetime substance use disorder (or with another psychiatric disorder), his partner and their biological child aged 10–12 (at first sons only, daughters from its second funding cycle) and followed the index children to age 30; index children and their siblings were genotyped under the Genes, Environment and Development Initiative.

label: International Consortium on Lithium Genetics
other synonyms: Consortium of Lithium Genetics|Consortium on Lithium Genetics|International Consortium of Lithium Genetics
definition: An international consortium of lithium researchers, established in 2008 on the initiative of the International Group for the Study of Lithium-Treated Patients (IGSLI) and the Unit on the Genetic Basis of Mood and Anxiety Disorders of the US National Institute of Mental Health, whose participating sites in Europe, America, Asia and Australia pool genotyped patients with bipolar disorder treated with lithium, their long-term response rated retrospectively on the Alda scale, for genome-wide studies of the genetic basis of lithium response.

label: Cohort of Norway
other synonyms: COhort of NORway|Cohort Norway|Cohort of Adults in Norway|General Cohort of Adults in Norway
definition: A Norwegian multipurpose collection of health data and blood samples pooled from ten regional population-based health surveys conducted in 1994–2003, among them the fourth and fifth surveys of the Tromsø Study, the second Nord-Trøndelag Health Study (HUNT II), the Hordaland Health Study, the Oslo Health Study, the Oppland and Hedmark Health Study and the Troms and Finnmark Health Study. Participants, invited through the Population Registry of Norway, answered about 50 common core questions, had standardised examinations and gave non-fasting blood samples, and consented to linkage with national health registries; the collaboration is run by the Norwegian Institute of Public Health with the universities of Bergen, Oslo, Tromsø and Trondheim.

label: CONsorzio Studi ITaliani sui Tumori Ereditari Alla Mammella
other synonyms: Consorzio Italiano Tumori Ereditari Alla Mammella
definition: An Italian consortium of cancer genetics services and research groups studying hereditary breast cancer, among them the Fondazione IRCCS Istituto Nazionale dei Tumori and the Istituto Europeo di Oncologia in Milan and centres in Aviano, Bari, Florence, Genoa, Rome and Varese, with genetic testing by the Cogentech Cancer Genetic Test Laboratory in Milan. It contributes carriers of BRCA1 and BRCA2 pathogenic variants, most of them ascertained through cancer genetics clinics, as one study to the Consortium of Investigators of Modifiers of BRCA1 and BRCA2 (CIMBA) for research on genetic modifiers of cancer risk in carriers.
diseases: at risk of: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|at risk of: ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170)

label: COPD Pathology: Addressing Critical gaps, Early Treatment & diagnosis and Innovative Concepts
other synonyms: COPACETIC cohort|COPD Pathology: Addressing Critical gaps, Early Treatment and Innovative Concepts|COPD Pathology: Adressing Critical gaps, Early Treatment & diagnosis and Innovative Concepts
definition: A cohort of male heavy smokers (at least 20 pack-years) aged 50–75, participants of the Dutch-Belgian NELSON lung cancer screening trial recruited by the University Medical Centers of Groningen and Utrecht in the Netherlands, with spirometry, low-dose chest CT and blood DNA and RNA. It was assembled and genotyped genome-wide as the discovery cohort of the European Union FP7 project COPACETIC, begun in 2008 under the coordination of UMC Utrecht, to find genetic determinants of susceptibility to COPD and emphysema in smokers, and its lung function was measured again after about three years.
diseases: at risk of: chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (MONDO:0005002)|at risk of: pulmonary emphysema (MONDO:0004849)
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to tobacco smoking (ECTO:6000029)

label: Copenhagen Breast Cancer Study
definition: A Danish study at Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen University Hospital, that recruits and genetically counsels carriers of BRCA1 and BRCA2 pathogenic variants ascertained through cancer genetics clinics, under approval of the research ethics committees of the Capital Region of Denmark, and contributes them as one study to the Consortium of Investigators of Modifiers of BRCA1 and BRCA2 (CIMBA) for research on genetic modifiers of cancer risk in carriers.
diseases: at risk of: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|at risk of: ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170)

label: Copenhagen Lung Cancer Study
other synonyms: Copenhagen lung cancer study
definition: A hospital-based lung cancer case–control study in Copenhagen, Denmark, whose cases are patients diagnosed histologically with treatable lung cancer from 2012 onwards (recruited 2012–2013) and whose controls are participants of the Copenhagen General Population Study without lung cancer; it was genotyped in the lung cancer OncoArray project of the International Lung Cancer Consortium for studies of genetic susceptibility to lung cancer.

label: Corea (Genetics of COVID-related Manifestation)
other synonyms: Corea study|Genetics of COVID-related Manifestation
definition: A South Korean case–control study of host genetic factors in COVID-19, contributed to the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative, that compares patients with COVID-19, among them hospitalised patients, with controls, all of Korean ancestry, under the ethics approval of Kangbuk Samsung Medical Center, Seoul National University Bundang Hospital and Seoul National University Hospital; its data collection was coordinated with the Kangbuk Samsung Cohort Study and its participants were genotyped on the Axiom Asia Precision Medicine Research Array.

label: COloRectal tumour Gene Identification study
other synonyms: CORGI Consortium|CORGI study|COloRectal tumour Gene Identification|Colorectal Tumour Gene Identification study
definition: A UK family study that since 1999 has recruited, through Clinical Genetics Departments throughout the United Kingdom, members of families with colorectal tumours who developed colorectal cancer by age 80 or significant colorectal adenomas (three or more, with severe dysplasia or villous histology, or presenting before age 45; adenoma-only cases having a first- or second-degree relative with colorectal cancer), with their unaffected spouses or partners as controls, to identify genes that predispose to colorectal tumours. Its cases and controls formed the first UK genome-wide association study of colorectal cancer (UK1) and later sample sets.
diseases: patients with: colorectal adenoma (MONDO:0005484)|patients with: colorectal cancer (MONDO:0005575)

label: China Osteoporosis Study
other synonyms: China osteoporosis study|Connecticut Ovary Study
definition: A genetic study of osteoporosis-related traits in unrelated Han Chinese adults recruited in and around the cities of Xi'an and Changsha, China, whose bone mineral density was measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, set up to identify genes underlying osteoporosis.

label: Copenhagen Prostate Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of prostate cancer in Copenhagen, Denmark, whose cases are unselected men with pathologically confirmed, mainly clinically detected prostate cancer recruited at two Copenhagen University Hospital sites, Herlev Hospital in 2008–2011 (Copenhagen Prostate Cancer Study 1, CPCS1) and Rigshospitalet in 2010–2011 (Copenhagen Prostate Cancer Study 2, CPCS2), and whose controls are prostate-cancer-free men from the Copenhagen general population who took part in the Copenhagen City Heart Study or the Copenhagen General Population Study. Participants are white men of Danish descent who completed questionnaires and gave blood samples for DNA.

label: Center for Prostate Disease Research Multicenter National Database
other synonyms: CPDR multicenter national clinical database|Center for Prostate Disease Research|Center for Prostate Disease Research Multi-center National Database|Center for Prostate Disease Research multicenter national database|Triservice Multicenter Prostate Cancer Longitudinal Database
definition: A longitudinal clinical research database of military health care beneficiaries who consent to enrolment, typically at prostate biopsy for suspected prostate cancer, at United States military treatment facilities (Walter Reed and other Army, Navy and Air Force medical centres, now with one civilian centre), run by the Department of Defense Center for Prostate Disease Research of the Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences, which records their demographic, clinical, pathology, treatment, quality-of-life and outcome data. It began as prospective data collection at Walter Reed Army Medical Center in January 1994, with retrospective data back to 1980, and is linked to a biospecimen bank of blood and tissue collected at Walter Reed since 1993.

label: California Pacific Medical Center Research Institute Cohort
other synonyms: CPMC Research Institute Cohort|CPMC Research Institute cohort|California Pacific Medical Center Breast Health Cohort|California Pacific Medical Center Research Breast Health Cohort|California Pacific Medical Center Research Institute cohort
definition: A cohort of women having screening mammography at the Breast Health Center of California Pacific Medical Center in San Francisco, California, United States, an imaging facility of the San Francisco Mammography Registry (part of the NCI Breast Cancer Surveillance Consortium), who completed the registry's demographic and risk-factor questionnaire and, from 2004 to 2011, were asked to give blood for research and consent to genotyping; breast cancers are ascertained by linkage to the California Cancer Registry.

label: Canadian Pharmacogenomics Network for Drug Safety
other synonyms: Canadian Pharmacogenomics Network for Drug Safety Database|Canadian Pharmacogenomics Network for Drug Safety cohort|Genotype-specific Approaches to Therapy in Childhood|Genotype-specific Approaches to Therapy in Children
definition: A pan-Canadian collection of children and adults treated with drugs of interest who have been enrolled since 2005 by trained surveillance clinicians at major Canadian hospitals (first paediatric hospitals, as the Genotype-specific Approaches to Therapy in Childhood network), either as cases of serious adverse drug reactions, such as anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity or cisplatin-induced hearing loss, or as drug-tolerant controls, and whose clinical data and biological samples are collected for genetic association studies to find genomic predictors of adverse drug reactions. The network is based at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver.

label: Hong Kong Cardiovascular Risk Factor Prevalence Study
definition: A prospective population-based cohort of Hong Kong Chinese adults aged 25–74, recruited in 1995–1996 through randomly generated telephone numbers from the general population of Hong Kong for a baseline survey of the prevalence of cardiovascular risk factors (CRISPS-1), with a comprehensive assessment including a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test, and re-examined with similar protocols in 2000–2004, 2005–2008, 2010–2012 and 2016–2018 (CRISPS-2 to CRISPS-5) to study the development of cardiovascular risk factors such as diabetes and hypertension.
diseases: population study of: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)|population study of: diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005015)

label: Collaborative Study on the Genetics of Asthma
other synonyms: Collaborative Studies on the Genetics of Asthma|NHLBI Collaborative Studies on the Genetics of Asthma
definition: A multicentre family study of the genetics of asthma supported by the US National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, in which African American, European American and Hispanic families were ascertained through two siblings with asthma at centres at Johns Hopkins University, the University of Chicago, the University of Minnesota and the University of Maryland, to identify loci contributing to asthma and asthma-associated phenotypes.

label: Center for Translational Molecular Medicine – Circulating Cells Cohort
other synonyms: CIRCULATING CELLS study|CTMM - CIRCULATING CELLS Cohort|CTMM - Circulating Cells|CTMM Circulating Cells|Center for Translational Molecular Medicine|Center for Translational Molecular Medicine-Circulating Cells Cohort|Circulating Cells Cohort|Circulating Cells cohort|Circulating Cells study
definition: A multicentre prospective cohort of patients with stable or unstable angina pectoris undergoing coronary angiography at four medical centres in the Netherlands, recruited from March 2009 to September 2011 in the CIRCULATING CELLS project of the Center for Translational Molecular Medicine, whose blood cell fractions were isolated and characterised to find cellular biomarkers that predict adverse cardiovascular events.

label: California Teachers Study
definition: A prospective cohort of female California teachers and administrators, established in 1995-1996 among members of the California State Teachers Retirement System who completed a detailed mailed questionnaire on possible risk factors for breast and other cancers, with cancer outcomes identified by linkage to the California Cancer Registry.
diseases: population study of: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|population study of: cancer (MONDO:0004992)

label: Chinese University of Hong Kong Diabetes Study
definition: A case–control study of type 2 diabetes in southern Han Chinese residents of Hong Kong, conducted by the Chinese University of Hong Kong. Its cases are patients with type 2 diabetes selected from the Prince of Wales Hospital Diabetes Registry (the Hong Kong Diabetes Register), either with early-onset diabetes and a positive family history or selected at random, excluding classic type 1 diabetes, and its controls, with normal glucose tolerance, were recruited from hospital staff, a community-based cardiovascular risk screening programme and a population-based cardiovascular risk screening programme for adolescents.

label: Chennai Urban Rural Epidemiology Study
definition: A population-based epidemiological study of diabetes and its complications in adults aged 20 years or more in Chennai, southern India, run by the Madras Diabetes Research Foundation. A representative sample of the city's residents, from wards chosen by systematic random sampling, was screened for diabetes in a door-to-door survey in 2001–2003; everyone found to have diabetes and every tenth participant then underwent detailed anthropometric, biochemical and complication studies, and they were followed up in 2012–2014.
diseases: population study of: diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005015)|population study of: diabetic kidney disease (MONDO:0005016)|population study of: diabetic neuropathy (MONDO:0006626)|population study of: diabetic retinopathy (MONDO:0005266)

label: China Pulmonary Thromboembolism Registry Study
other synonyms: China pUlmonary Thromboembolism REgistry Study|China pUlmonary thromboembolism REgistry Study
definition: An ongoing national, prospective, multicentre registry of patients with suspected or confirmed acute pulmonary embolism, with or without deep vein thrombosis, enrolled at medical centres of the China PE-DVT network across China and led from the China-Japan Friendship Hospital in Beijing, to describe the spectrum, trends, causes and outcomes of pulmonary embolism in China. Started in January 2009 with in-hospital outcomes, it has followed patients for at least three months since July 2011 and, since August 2016, has collected their blood samples and followed them for at least two years.
diseases: patients with: Deep venous thrombosis (HP:0002625)|patients with: pulmonary embolism (MONDO:0005279)

label: CVPath Institute Sudden Cardiac Death registry
other synonyms: CVPath Sudden Death Autopsy Registry|CVPath Sudden Death Registry
definition: An autopsy registry of people who died suddenly and unexpectedly, whose hearts have been referred since the mid-1990s to CVPath Institute in Gaithersburg, Maryland, by the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner of the State of Maryland through an ongoing cardiovascular pathology consultation service. The cause of death is determined by detailed histopathological examination of the heart and coronary arteries, and DNA extracted from the archived tissue is used to study the genetics of sudden cardiac death and of coronary plaque.

label: Cleveland Clinic Foundation/Veteran Affairs Medical Center Cohort
definition: A clinic-based case–control collection for genetic studies of age-related macular degeneration in Cleveland, Ohio, whose cases, graded by the Age-Related Eye Disease Study criteria, and controls without signs of macular degeneration or a family history of retinal disease, mostly of European descent, gave blood samples at the Cole Eye Institute of the Cleveland Clinic and at the Veterans Affairs eye clinic.

label: Czech post-MONICA study
other synonyms: Czech Post-MONICA Study|Czech post-MONICA Study
definition: A series of independent cross-sectional surveys of cardiovascular risk factors in the Czech Republic that continued the country's WHO MONICA Project surveys: random 1% samples of residents aged 25–64 years, stratified by age and sex and drawn from health insurance registers, were examined in the same districts in 1997/98, 2000/01, 2007/08 and 2016/17 by investigators in Prague (the Institute for Clinical and Experimental Medicine, and Charles University and Thomayer Hospital). DNA from its participants has also served as general-population controls in genetic studies.

label: Dutch Asthma GWAS
other synonyms: Dutch Asthma GWAS study
definition: A genome-wide association sample of asthma from the north of the Netherlands, assembled by the Dutch Asthma Genetics Consortium in two phases that were genotyped separately and meta-analysed: a family-based phase whose asthmatic cases came from a trio and family study, with non-asthmatic spouses or the untransmitted alleles of the trios as controls, and a case–control phase whose asthmatics came from earlier clinical and genetic studies of the investigators' research institute, with controls from COPACETIC, a population-based lung cancer screening study of male smokers. Cases had a physician's diagnosis of asthma, asthma symptoms and bronchial hyperresponsiveness; controls had no asthma, COPD or significant airway obstruction.

label: Dutch Autoimmune Hepatitis Study Group
other synonyms: Dutch AIH Study|Dutch AIH Study Group|Dutch AIH Study Group Consortium
definition: A national registry of patients with autoimmune hepatitis in the Netherlands kept by the Dutch Autoimmune Hepatitis Study Group, a collaboration of Dutch tertiary referral and general hospitals supported by the Netherlands Association for the Study of the Liver, which includes known patients retrospectively and new patients prospectively. Its patients have been studied for the treatment and outcome of the disease, and its adult patients with type 1 autoimmune hepatitis were genotyped for a genome-wide association study of the disease.

label: The Danish study of Functional Disorders
other synonyms: Danish Study of Functional Disorders|The Danish study of functional disorders
definition: A Danish population-based cohort of men and women aged 18 to 76, drawn at random from the national registers among people born in Denmark and living in the western part of greater Copenhagen and examined at the Research Centre for Prevention and Health, Glostrup, from 2011 to 2015, set up to study the epidemiology of functional somatic syndromes (such as fibromyalgia, irritable bowel syndrome and chronic fatigue syndrome) and bodily distress syndrome. It merges a follow-up examination of the Health2006 cohort (DanFunD part one, 2011-2012) with a new random sample examined from 2012 to 2015 (DanFunD part two).

label: Deprenyl and tocopherol antioxidative therapy of parkinsonism
other synonyms: Deprenyl And Tocopherol Antioxidative Therapy Of Parkinsonism|Deprenyl and Tocopherol Antioxidative Therapy of Parkinsonism
definition: A double-blind, multicentre, placebo-controlled clinical trial of the Parkinson Study Group that enrolled patients with early, otherwise untreated Parkinson's disease at sites in the United States and Canada and randomised them, in a 2 x 2 factorial design, to deprenyl, tocopherol (vitamin E), both or placebo, to test whether long-term treatment extends the time until disability requires levodopa therapy.

label: Dortmund Bladder Cancer Study
other synonyms: Dortmund bladder cancer study|The Dortmund Bladder Cancer Study
definition: A German hospital-based case-control study of urinary bladder cancer at the Department of Urology of St.-Josefs-Hospital Dortmund-Hörde, in the Ruhr area (a former coal, iron and steel industry region), whose cases have confirmed bladder cancer and whose controls are cancer-free patients of the same department admitted for benign urological diseases, enrolled from July 2009 to July 2010; it has contributed to genome-wide association studies of bladder cancer.

label: Diet, Cancer and Health
other synonyms: Danish Diet, Cancer and Health Cohort|Danish Diet, Cancer and Health cohort|Danish EPIC Diet, Cancer and Health cohort|Diet, Cancer and Health cohort|Diet, Cancer, and Health
