definition: A Danish prospective cohort of the Danish Cancer Society that recruited men and women aged 50 to 64, born in Denmark, living in Aarhus or Copenhagen and without a cancer diagnosis, between 1993 and 1997, collecting questionnaires, a clinical examination and biological samples to investigate how diet and lifestyle relate to the risk of cancer and other chronic diseases. It is an associated cohort of the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to eating behavior (ECTO:6000021)|designed to study: exposure to lifestyle (ECTO:6000015)

label: Case-Control Study of Prostate Cancer among African Americans in Washington, DC
definition: A set of case-control studies of genetic risk factors for prostate cancer in which unrelated self-described African American men were recruited between 2001 and 2005 from the Division of Urology at Howard University Hospital in Washington, DC, United States, with age-matched controls ascertained from the prostate cancer screening population of the same division.

label: Depression Case Control Study
other synonyms: Depression Case Control study|Depression Case-Control study|depression case-control study
definition: A case–control study of recurrent major depressive disorder in the United Kingdom, funded by the Medical Research Council, that recruited unrelated patients who had had at least two episodes of major depression of at least moderate severity, diagnosed with the Schedules for Clinical Assessment in Neuropsychiatry (SCAN) interview, at three UK sites (London, Cardiff and Birmingham), together with healthy controls; it is one of the three studies making up the RADIANT depression sample.

label: deCODE CAD/MI Study
other synonyms: deCODE CAD
definition: A case-control sample of Icelanders assembled by deCODE genetics for genetic studies of coronary artery disease and myocardial infarction, with cases identified from the Icelandic myocardial infarction registry (MONICA criteria, infarction before age 75) or hospital discharge diagnoses and contacted through deCODE's cardiovascular disease genetics programme, and population controls recruited through other deCODE genetic research programmes.
diseases: patients with: coronary artery disorder (MONDO:0005010)|patients with: myocardial infarction (MONDO:0005068)

label: Deterioration of Kidney Allograft Function Genomics
other synonyms: Deterioration of Kidney Allograft Function Genomics Cohort|Genomics of Deterioration of Kidney Allograft Function
definition: A prospective observational cohort of kidney and simultaneous pancreas–kidney transplant recipients enrolled at the time of transplantation between 2005 and 2011 at five US and two Canadian transplant centres, the genetic study of the prospective arm of the Long-term Deterioration of Kidney Allograft Function (DeKAF) study, which with DNA from the recipients and from their living or deceased donors studies genetic influences on acute rejection, graft failure and immunosuppressant concentrations and adverse effects.
diseases: patients with: end stage renal failure (MONDO:0004375)

label: DEMOKRITOS study
other synonyms: Hellenic Cooperative Oncology Group
definition: A Greek breast cancer case-control study conducted in collaboration with the Hellenic Cooperative Oncology Group, in which triple-negative breast cancer cases were enrolled from 1997 to 2010 in hospitals serving Athens, Thessaloniki, Ioannina, Patras and Chania (Crete), with population-based unaffected women of the same age range from Athens as controls; it contributed to the Triple Negative Breast Cancer Consortium.

label: De Novo Parkinson Cohort
other synonyms: De Novo Parkinson study|De Novo Parkinson's cohort|de novo Parkinson's cohort
definition: A prospective, longitudinal, observational single-centre study in Kassel, central Germany, of early untreated Parkinson's disease patients and matched healthy controls, aimed at improving early diagnosis and prognosis of Parkinson's disease.

label: Depression Genes and Networks
other synonyms: Depression Genes Networks study|Depression Genes and Networks cohort|Depression Genes and Networks study
definition: A United States case-control study of major depressive disorder whose participants, adults of European ancestry aged 21 to 60 with recurrent or chronic major depressive disorder and controls who had never had a depressive episode, were recruited by a survey research company from a nationally representative survey research panel, assessed by online screening and telephone interview, genotyped genome-wide and profiled by RNA sequencing of whole blood.

label: Data from an Epidemiological Study on the Insulin Resistance Syndrome
other synonyms: Data from an Epidemiological Study on the Insulin Resistance syndrome|Data from an Epidemiological Study on the Insulin Resistance syndrome study|Data from the Epidemiological Study on the Insulin Resistance Syndrome|Data of an Epidemiological Study on the Insulin Resistance syndrome study|Epidemiological Study on the Insulin Resistance syndrome study
definition: A French prospective cohort of men and women aged 30 to 64 years, volunteers insured by the French social security system who attended ten of its health examination centres in west-central France, followed for nine years to clarify the development of the insulin resistance syndrome.

label: Dutch Familial Bilateral Breast Cancer Study
definition: A Dutch breast cancer case-control study whose cases are BRCA1/2 mutation-negative familial bilateral breast cancer patients selected from five clinical genetics centres (Erasmus University Medical Center/Daniel den Hoed, the Netherlands Cancer Institute, Leiden University Medical Center, University Medical Center Utrecht and VU University Medical Center), with patient recruitment organised by the Netherlands Collaborative Group on Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer (HEBON), and whose controls are women aged 55 or over without breast cancer from the Rotterdam Study; it was genotyped for genome-wide association studies of breast cancer.

label: Dutch Familial Colorectal Cancer Study
definition: A Dutch colorectal cancer case-control series, whose cases had a family history of cancer and whose controls were population-based, that was one of the eight case-control series genotyped for the 11q23.1 risk variant rs3802842 in a 2008 study of colorectal cancer risk.

label: Gastrointestinal Cancer Clinic of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Study
other synonyms: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute - Gastrointestinal Cancer Clinic|Gastrointestinal Cancer Clinic of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute
definition: A case series of patients with pathologically confirmed pancreatic cancer identified sequentially at the outpatient gastrointestinal cancer clinic of the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in Boston, United States, which contributed cases to the PanScan III genome-wide association study of pancreatic cancer.

label: Dongfeng-Tongji cohort study
other synonyms: DFTJ cohort|Dongfeng-Tongji Cohort Study|Dongfeng-Tongji Cohort study|Dongfeng-Tongji cohort|Tongji-Dongfeng cohort study
definition: A prospective cohort of retired employees of the Dongfeng Motor Corporation, a large state-owned car manufacturer in Shiyan, Hubei province, China, who completed questionnaires, medical examinations and blood sampling at a baseline survey in 2008–2010; further retirees were recruited at the first follow-up survey in 2013, and participants are re-surveyed about every five years.

label: Danish HIV Cohort Study
other synonyms: Danish HIV cohort study
definition: A nationwide, prospective, population-based cohort of all people with HIV aged 16 or older treated at Denmark's specialised HIV centres since 1 January 1995, which keeps enrolling newly diagnosed people and immigrants with HIV and records demographic, clinical and laboratory data on their infection and care, linkable to the Danish national registers.

label: Danish National Health Service Register
other synonyms: Danish Health Service Register|Danish National Health Service Register for Primary Care|National Danish Health Service Register
definition: A national administrative register of the services provided under Denmark's public health insurance by the contractors of primary health care (general practitioners, practising specialists, dentists, physiotherapists, psychologists and others), which covers everyone living in Denmark with data from 1990 and records the citizen, the provider and the service but little clinical information; collected for administrative and research purposes, it is linked by personal identification number to the other national registers.

label: DietCompLyf Breast Cancer Survival Study
other synonyms: DietCompLyf breast cancer survival study|DietCompLyf study|The Role of Diet, Complementary Treatment and Lifestyle in Breast Cancer Survival|The Role of Diet, Complementary Treatments & Lifestyle in Breast Cancer Survival
definition: A multicentre prospective cohort of women under 75 with grade I–III invasive primary breast cancer, recruited 9–15 months after diagnosis from 56 hospitals in the United Kingdom, who gave clinical, dietary, lifestyle, complementary-therapy and quality-of-life data and blood and urine samples every year for five years. Run from the University of Westminster, London, and funded by the charity Against Breast Cancer, it studies how dietary phytoestrogens and other diet and lifestyle factors relate to breast cancer recurrence and survival.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to lifestyle (ECTO:6000015)|designed to study: exposure to phytoestrogen (ECTO:9002037)

label: Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network Prospective Study
other synonyms: A Multi-Center, Longitudinal Study of Drug-and CAM-Induced Liver Injury|DILIN - Prospective Study|DILIN Prospective Study|DILIN prospective study|Drug Induced Liver Injury Network|Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network
definition: The prospective registry study of the US Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network (DILIN), which the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases set up in 2003. Since September 2004 it has enrolled children aged 2 or over and adults referred to the network's clinical sites within 6 months of a suspected liver injury caused by a prescription or over-the-counter drug or a herbal or dietary supplement. Causality is adjudicated by expert review, clinical data and blood (DNA), serum and some tissue samples are collected, and confirmed cases are followed for at least 6 months, in order to study the clinical, genetic, environmental and immunological risk factors and the outcomes of drug-induced liver injury.

label: Danish Longevity Study
other synonyms: Danish longevity study
definition: A genetic study population of long-lived Danes, nonagenarians and centenarians drawn from the Longitudinal Study of Danish Centenarians, the Danish 1905 and 1911–12 Birth Cohort Studies, the Study of Danish Old Sibs and the Longitudinal Study of Ageing Danish Twins, used as the long-lived cases of studies of the genetics of human longevity.

label: UK Young Lacunar Stroke DNA Study
other synonyms: DNA Lacunar 2|UK Young Lacunar DNA Study|Young Lacunar DNA|Young Lacunar Stroke DNA Resource
definition: A UK case-control collection for genetic studies of lacunar stroke, in which Caucasian patients aged 70 or under with a clinical lacunar syndrome and a compatible subcortical infarct on MRI were recruited from 72 specialist stroke centres throughout the UK between 2002 and 2012, and unrelated Caucasian controls free of cerebrovascular disease were sampled, stratified by age and sex, from general practice lists in the same areas.

label: Dutch Renal Cell Cancer Study
other synonyms: Dutch RCC Study
definition: A case–control study of renal cell carcinoma in the region of Nijmegen, the Netherlands, run by Radboud University Nijmegen Medical Centre with the Comprehensive Cancer Centre East, whose cases of European descent form a hospital-based series (patients of the hospital's outpatient urology clinic who had given blood and lifestyle data from 1999 onwards for studies of gene–environment interactions in urological disease and were found through the cancer registry to have renal cell carcinoma) and a population-based series recruited in 2009 through the regional cancer registry (patients diagnosed in 1995–2008 before the age of 75). Its controls are participants of the population-based Nijmegen Biomedical Study.

label: Dutch HeFH cohort
other synonyms: Dutch HeFH Cohort|The Dutch heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia screening program
definition: A prospective cohort drawn from the Dutch national cascade-screening programme for heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, which enrolled participants between 1994 and 2013: adult carriers of a heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia variant free of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease at enrolment who consented to genetic analysis and linkage of their health records, together with relatives from the same families confirmed as non-carriers and matched to them by age and sex, followed for incident coronary artery disease.

label: European American and Polish height panels
other synonyms: European American and Poland Extreme Height panels
definition: Two case-control panels of self-described white adults sampled from the tails of the height distribution (the 5th to 10th and the 90th to 95th percentiles), one of European Americans born in the United States and one of people born in Poland, studied under the approval of the Institutional Review Board of Children's Hospital, Boston, and genotyped to validate variants associated with adult height.

label: Edinburgh Artery Study
other synonyms: Edinburgh artery study
definition: A study of peripheral arterial disease in the general population of Edinburgh, Scotland, based on an age-stratified sample of 1,592 men and women aged 55 to 74 selected from the age-sex registers of ten general practices in the city and assessed by questionnaire and ankle brachial pressure index, funded by the British Heart Foundation and genotyped for genetic studies such as the DIAGRAM consortium’s meta-analysis of type 2 diabetes and the UCLEB consortium’s Mendelian randomisation analyses.
diseases: population study of: peripheral arterial disease (MONDO:0005386)

label: European Collaborative Study
other synonyms: European Collaborative GWAS
definition: A European genome-wide association study of classical Hodgkin lymphoma that genotyped, at the Centre National de Génotypage in France, cases from five European Hodgkin lymphoma studies (the EPILYMPH Study, the Scotland and Newcastle Lymphoma Group, the Young Adult Hodgkin's Disease Case–Control Study, the Scandinavian Lymphoma Etiology Study and the Northern Dutch Hodgkin Lymphoma Study) and compared them with generic controls chosen by country from earlier genome-wide association studies of other cancers in populations of European ancestry, among them ARCAGE, the IARC Central Europe Study, the Pancreatic Cancer Cohort Consortium, the Nijmegen Biomedical Study and the Wellcome Trust Case–Control Consortium. It was the European discovery sample of the 2014 Hodgkin lymphoma GWAS meta-analysis with the University of Southern California and University of Chicago GWAS.

label: Etude Cas-Témoins de l'Infarctus du Myocarde
other synonyms: ECTIM Study|ECTIM study|Enquête Cas-Témoins de l'Infarctus du Myocarde|Etude Cas-Témoin de l'Infarctus du Myocarde|Etude Cas-Témoin sur l'Infarctus du Myocarde|Etude Cas-Témoins sur l'Infarctus du Myocarde
definition: A multicentre case-control study of myocardial infarction based on the WHO MONICA centres of Belfast (Northern Ireland) and Lille, Strasbourg and Toulouse (France), set up to investigate why coronary heart disease is more than three times as common in middle-aged men in Northern Ireland as in France. Between 1988 and 1991 it recruited men aged 25–64 who had had a myocardial infarction, examined 3 to 9 months after the event, and control men sampled from the general population. Its cases and controls have been used in many candidate-gene studies of myocardial infarction and lipids, and an extension study later recruited men and women in the MONICA areas of Belfast and Glasgow.

label: Edinburgh Osteoporosis Study
definition: A clinic-based, cross-sectional study of patients referred for assessment of osteoporosis in Edinburgh and the Lothians, Scotland, supported by Arthritis Research UK, with bone mineral density measurements, fracture histories documented from medical records and radiographs, and DNA. It has been used in genetic association studies of bone density and fracture, including de novo replication genotyping for the GEFOS consortium's meta-analyses and the replication stages of vertebral fracture GWAS.

label: Eastern European Bladder Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based case–control study of bladder cancer in Hungary, Romania and Slovakia, the bladder cancer component of the ASHRAM case–control study of cancer risk from environmental arsenic exposure, whose cases were diagnosed from 2002 to 2004 and whose hospital-based controls were recruited from 2002 to 2004 in the same countries.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to arsenic in water via ingestion (ECTO:0080000)

label: Estudio Familiar de Influencia Genetica en Alzheimer
other synonyms: Estudio Familiar de Influencia Genetica de Alzheimer
definition: A family study of Caribbean Hispanics from families multiply affected by late-onset Alzheimer's disease, recruited at the Taub Institute for Research on Alzheimer's Disease and the Aging Brain in New York and from clinics in the Dominican Republic, with follow-up of unaffected family members, to study the genetics of familial late-onset Alzheimer's disease.

label: Emory Genebank Study
other synonyms: Emory GeneBank|Emory GeneBank Study
definition: A study of patients undergoing cardiac catheterization at Emory University hospitals, the Emory Clinic and Grady Memorial Hospital in Atlanta, Georgia, United States, designed to investigate the relationship of biochemical and genetic factors with coronary artery disease; patients with angiographic coronary artery disease or a history of myocardial infarction or coronary revascularisation serve as cases and those without coronary artery disease on catheterization as controls in genetic studies.

label: Epidemiology & Genetics Lymphoma Case-Control Study
other synonyms: Epidemiology & Genetics Unit Lymphoma Case-Control study|Epidemiology and Genetics Lymphoma Case-Control Study|Epidemiology and Genetics Lymphoma Case–Control Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of lymphoma in the north of England, run from York, whose cases are patients aged 16 to 69 newly diagnosed with non-Hodgkin or Hodgkin lymphoma between 1998 and 2003 while resident in defined areas, and whose controls were matched to cases on sex, date of birth and area of residence and drawn from general practice registers.

label: ADDITION-Ely Case-Control Study
other synonyms: ADDITION-Ely case-control study|Ely case-control study|Ely case_control study
definition: A type 2 diabetes case-control study in the United Kingdom whose cases had previously undiagnosed type 2 diabetes, defined by World Health Organization oral glucose tolerance test criteria, found by population-based stepwise screening of 40- to 69-year-olds in the UK Cambridge arm of the ADDITION study or by oral glucose tolerance testing in the MRC Ely Study, and whose controls were participants of the MRC Ely Study, a population-based cohort of white European adults without diagnosed diabetes from a similar sampling frame as the cases, confirmed free of diabetes by oral glucose tolerance test.

label: European Male Ageing Study
other synonyms: European Male Aging Study|European male ageing study
definition: A multicentre prospective population-based cohort of men aged 40–79 years recruited from population registers in eight European centres (Florence, Leuven, Lodz, Malmö, Manchester, Santiago de Compostela, Szeged and Tartu) with an age-stratified sample at each centre, who completed a detailed questionnaire on personal and medical history, lifestyle and sexual function, designed to examine the prevalence, incidence and geographical distribution of gender-specific and general symptoms of ageing in men and their endocrine, genetic and psychosocial predictors, particularly age-related changes in hormone levels.

label: Epidemiological Study of Familial Breast Cancer
other synonyms: EMBRACE study|Epidemiological study of BRCA1 & BRCA2 mutation carriers|Epidemiological study of BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutation carriers
definition: A prospective cohort study in the United Kingdom and the Republic of Ireland, coordinated in Cambridge, of carriers of pathogenic BRCA1 or BRCA2 variants, non-carrier relatives from carrier families and untested potential carriers, recruited through regional cancer genetics centres around the time of genetic testing, to characterise cancer risks in BRCA1 and BRCA2 carriers and their relatives.
diseases: at risk of: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|at risk of: ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170)

label: Environmental and genetic risks factors study in adult lymphoma
other synonyms: Environmental and Genetic Risks Factors Study in Adult Lymphoma
definition: A French multicentre hospital-based case-control study of lymphoid neoplasms (non-Hodgkin lymphoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, lymphoproliferative syndromes and multiple myeloma), conducted in the main hospitals of Bordeaux, Brest, Caen, Nantes, Lille and Toulouse from September 2000 to December 2004, whose cases were recently diagnosed patients aged 18 to 75 living in each hospital's catchment area and whose controls were patients of the same hospitals, mainly from orthopaedic and rheumatology departments, to study environmental, infectious and genetic risk factors for these neoplasms.
exposures: designed to study: exposure event (ExO:0000002)

label: Early-Onset Prostate Cancer Family Study
other synonyms: Early Onset Prostate Cancer Study|The Early Onset Prostate Cancer Study
definition: A population-based study of early-onset prostate cancer run by Cancer Council Victoria in Melbourne, Australia, whose participants are men diagnosed with prostate cancer before the age of 56, ascertained through the Victorian Cancer Registry.

label: Eplerenone Post-Acute Myocardial Infarction Heart Failure Efficacy and Survival Study
other synonyms: EPHESUS trial|Eplerenone Post-acute myocardial infarction Heart failure Efficacy and SUrvival Study|The Eplerenone Post-Acute Myocardial Infarction Heart Failure Efficacy and Survival Study
definition: A double-blind, placebo-controlled randomised trial of eplerenone, a selective aldosterone blocker, added to optimal medical therapy in patients enrolled 3 to 14 days after an acute myocardial infarction complicated by left ventricular dysfunction (ejection fraction of 40% or less) and heart failure or diabetes, followed for death and cardiovascular hospitalisation; a biomarker substudy of its patients has serial blood measurements.
diseases: patients with: acute myocardial infarction (MONDO:0004781)|patients with: diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005015)|patients with: heart failure (MONDO:0005252)

label: Epidemiological Study of Prostate Cancer
other synonyms: EPIdemiology of Prostate CAncer|Epidemiological study of prostate cancer|Epidemiology of Prostate Cancer
definition: A population-based case-control study of prostate cancer in the Hérault département in the south of France, whose cases are men under 75 newly diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2012-2013 while living in Hérault, identified in all of its public and private cancer centres, and whose controls are men without prostate cancer randomly selected from Hérault's general population with quotas on age and socioeconomic status, set up to study environmental and genetic risk factors for prostate cancer.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to occupation (ECTO:0001591)

label: EPIC Obesity study
other synonyms: EPIC-Obesity Study|European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition - Obesity Study|European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition _ Obesity study cohort
definition: A representative sample of the EPIC-Norfolk cohort (men and women of European descent aged 39 to 79, recruited in Norfolk, United Kingdom, in 1993-1997), genotyped genome-wide for genetic association studies of body mass index and obesity.

label: EPICOLON
other synonyms: EPICOLON Consortium|EPICOLON consortium|EPICOLON project|EPICOLON study
definition: A prospective, multicentre, population-based study of colorectal cancer across Spain, started in 1999 by the Gastrointestinal Oncology Group of the Spanish Gastroenterological Association, which in two phases (EPICOLON I in 25 hospitals and EPICOLON II in 14) recruited consecutive unselected patients newly diagnosed with colorectal cancer and hospital controls matched by age and sex with no personal or family history of cancer, mainly to study Lynch syndrome and familial colorectal cancer.

label: Epidemiology of Functional Disorders
other synonyms: EPIFUND study|EPIdemiological study of FUNctional Disorders|epidemiology of functional disorders
definition: A prospective population-based study of pain in North West England, in which adults aged 25 to 65 years recruited from the registers of three general practices in socio-economically diverse areas answered postal questionnaires on pain and psychological factors at baseline and were followed up at about 15 months and 4 years; it has been used to study the onset, persistence and genetics of chronic widespread pain.

label: Johns Hopkins Epidemiology-Genetics Program Ashkenazi Jewish schizophrenia case-control sample
other synonyms: Epidemiology genetic program AJ schizophrenia case-control samples
definition: A case-control sample of Ashkenazi Jewish people with schizophrenia, including schizoaffective disorder, and screened Ashkenazi Jewish controls, all reporting four grandparents of Ashkenazi Jewish descent, recruited in the United States by the Epidemiology-Genetics Program in Psychiatry of Johns Hopkins University: the cases through advertisements, talks and letters to the Jewish community and a study website, interviewed in person and diagnosed by consensus, and the controls at Jewish community meetings, community centres and synagogues.
diseases: patients with: schizoaffective disorder (MONDO:0005487)|patients with: schizophrenia (MONDO:0005090)

label: EpiHealth
other synonyms: EpiHealth cohort study|EpiHealth study|Epidemiology for Health|Epidemiology for Health cohort
definition: A Swedish population-based cohort study of men and women aged 45 to 75, recruited from 2011 through test centres in Uppsala and Malmö, who answered an internet-based lifestyle questionnaire and gave blood samples and physiological measurements at the test centre, and who are followed for disease outcomes through nationwide medical registers, set up to study interactions between genes and lifestyle in common diseases.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to lifestyle (ECTO:6000015)

label: EpiLymph
other synonyms: Epilymph case-control study in six European countries
definition: A multicentre case-control study of incident lymphoma conducted in 1998–2004 in the Czech Republic, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy and Spain, whose controls were frequency-matched to cases on age, sex and country and drawn at random from population registers in Germany and Italy and from patients of the cases' hospitals elsewhere, and whose participants were interviewed in person about their medical and family history and environmental exposures, to investigate risk factors for lymphoma.

label: EPI-NPC-2005 study
other synonyms: EPI-NPC-2005 project|EPI-NPC-2005 sample
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of nasopharyngeal carcinoma in Guangdong, southern China, whose cases are Guangdong residents under 80 with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed nasopharyngeal carcinoma identified at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center in Guangzhou between October 2005 and October 2007, and whose frequency-matched controls are Guangdong residents without cancer recruited among people attending health examinations at large general hospitals of the province; it was set up to study dietary, environmental and genetic risk factors for the disease.
exposures: designed to study: exposure event (ExO:0000002)|designed to study: exposure to human gammaherpesvirus 4 (ECTO:3000273)

label: EPIPARK
definition: A population-based cohort set up in 2010 in Lübeck, Germany, in which inhabitants screened by mailed questionnaire were assigned to groups ranging from healthy controls to people with suspected early motor signs of parkinsonism, alongside Parkinson's disease patients, and selected participants were examined in person and followed up, to investigate the specificity of non-motor symptoms for Parkinson's disease.

label: Epidemiologisch Preventief Onderzoek Zoetermeer
other synonyms: Epidemiologic Study of Cardiovascular Risk Indicators|Epidemiological Prevention Study Zoetermeer|Epidemiological Prevention Study of Zoetermeer|Epidemiological Prevention study Of Zoetermeer
definition: A population-based follow-up study begun in 1975 in Zoetermeer, the Netherlands, which examined inhabitants aged from 5 to 91 years to study the determinants of chronic diseases; participants aged 60 to 90 were later sampled for brain MRI in 1995–1996 and rescanned in 1999–2000 and 2008.
diseases: population study of: cardiovascular disorder (MONDO:0004995)|population study of: rheumatic disorder (MONDO:0005554)

label: Evaluation of Risk of ALL Treatment-Related Side-Effects
other synonyms: ERASE cohort|ERASE study|Evaluation of ALL Treatment-related Side-Effects|Evaluation of Risk of ALL Treatment-related Side-Effects|Evaluation of Risk of ALL treatment-related Side-Effects
definition: A national retrospective study of children aged 1 to 18 years diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia or lymphoblastic lymphoma between 1998 and 2013 at six tertiary paediatric oncology centres in Australia and treated on Berlin-Frankfurt-Münster- or Children's Oncology Group-based protocols, with annotation of treatment, survival and treatment-related toxicities and a germline genome-wide association study, to find clinical and genetic risk factors for side-effects of treatment.
diseases: patients with: acute lymphoblastic leukemia (MONDO:0004967)|patients with: lymphoblastic lymphoma (MONDO:0000873)

label: European Randomised Study of Screening for Prostate Cancer
other synonyms: European Randomised study of Screening for Prostate Cancer|European Randomized Study of Screening for Prostate Cancer|European Study of Screening for Prostate Cancer|European randomised study of screening for prostate cancer
definition: A multicentre randomised trial of prostate-specific antigen (PSA) screening, begun in 1993 in the Netherlands and Belgium and joined by centres in Sweden, Finland, Italy, Spain, Switzerland and France, in which men aged 50 to 74 identified from population registers were randomly assigned to screening, generally every four years, or to no intervention, and followed for prostate cancer incidence and mortality.

label: Etude Sur les Cancers et les Leucémies de l'Enfant
other synonyms: ESCALE study|Epidemiological Study on childhood Cancer and Leukemia|Study on Environmental and Genetic Risk Factors of Childhood Cancers and Leukemia
definition: A nationwide registry-based case-control study carried out in France in 2003–2004 of children under 15 years old diagnosed with acute leukaemia, lymphoma, a malignant central nervous system tumour or neuroblastoma, and population controls frequency-matched to them on age and sex, whose mothers were interviewed by standardised telephone questionnaire, to investigate environmental and genetic risk factors for childhood cancers and leukaemia.
diseases: patients with: acute leukemia (MONDO:0010643)|patients with: brain neoplasm (MONDO:0021211)|patients with: lymphoma (MONDO:0005062)|patients with: neuroblastoma (MONDO:0005072)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to emissions from petroleum combustion (ECTO:7000156)

label: Essen Obesity Study
other synonyms: Essen Obesity study
definition: A German cross-sectional study of early-onset extreme obesity, made up of a case-control study of extremely obese children and adolescents recruited in hospitals specialised in the inpatient treatment of extreme obesity, with healthy lean controls ascertained at the University of Marburg, and a nuclear family study of obese children and adolescents ascertained in the same way together with both their biological parents (the Essen Obesity Trios), whose genotypes have been used in genome-wide association studies of obesity and body mass index.

label: Edinburgh Type 2 Diabetes Study
other synonyms: Edinburgh Type 2 diabetes Study
definition: A prospective cohort of men and women aged 60 to 75 years with established type 2 diabetes living in the Lothian region of central Scotland, randomly selected by sex and age band from the Lothian Diabetes Register and recruited in 2006–2007, established to investigate risk factors for, and mechanisms of, the development and progression of micro- and macrovascular complications of type 2 diabetes and of its less well-characterised complications, with follow-up examinations and linkage to hospital records.

label: EUDRAGENE
other synonyms: Eudragene
definition: A European collaboration, supported by the European Commission's 5th Framework Programme, that established a DNA case-control collection for studying the genetic basis of susceptibility to serious adverse drug reactions, ascertaining cases mainly through adverse drug reaction reports to pharmacovigilance centres; its cases have been used in genetic studies of drug-induced liver injury, statin-induced myopathy and other reactions.
diseases: patients with: Adverse drug response (HP:0020172)|patients with: drug-induced liver injury (MONDO:0005359)|patients with: drug-induced myopathy (MONDO:0100637)

label: EURODIAB Family Study
definition: A European genetic study of diabetic nephropathy and retinopathy in type 1 diabetes, combining a family-based design of affected offspring and their family members with a larger case-control component, whose participants were ascertained through 28 centres across Europe, some of which had taken part in the EURODIAB Prospective Complications Study.
diseases: patients with: diabetic kidney disease (MONDO:0005016)|patients with: diabetic retinopathy (MONDO:0005266)|patients with: type 1 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005147)

label: European Special Populations Research Network
other synonyms: European Special Population Network consortium|European Special Population Research Network|European Special Populations Network
definition: A consortium of family-based genetic studies of isolated European populations, funded as a European Union Sixth Framework Programme project, whose samples (the Erasmus Rucphen Family study in the Netherlands, MICROS in South Tyrol, Italy, the Northern Swedish Population Health Study, the Orkney Complex Disease Study in Scotland and the Vis study in Croatia) were genotyped on a common platform and analysed together in genome-wide association studies.

label: Ewha Womans University Hospital PCOS Study
other synonyms: Ewha Woman's University Hospital PCOS Study|Ewha Woman’s University Hospital PCOS GWAS|Ewha Woman’s University Hospital PCOS study
definition: A case-control study of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) in Korean women, whose women with PCOS and control women with regular menstrual cycles were recruited at the endocrinology and gynaecology clinics of Ewha Womans University Hospital (Mokdong Hospital) in Seoul, South Korea, from December 2008 to 2010, and genotyped for a genome-wide association study of PCOS.

label: Exeter 10,000 Study
other synonyms: Exeter 10,000|Exeter 10,000 cohort|Exeter 10,000 study|Exeter 10,000/Peninsula Research Bank|Exeter 10000
definition: An unselected population cohort of adult volunteers in South West England, recruited from 2010 to 2018 through general practices, workplaces, community events and local media, whose samples are held in the Peninsula Research Bank, run by the NIHR Exeter Clinical Research Facility as a recall-by-genotype resource for research on type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease and healthy ageing.

label: European Youth Heart Study
other synonyms: European youth heart study|The European Youth Heart Study
definition: A school-based population study of risk factors for future cardiovascular disease in children aged 9 and 15 years, randomly sampled through schools in Denmark, Estonia, Norway, Portugal and Sweden in the late 1990s, with objectively measured physical activity and fitness; its Danish part, recruited in 1997, has been followed longitudinally into early adulthood.

label: French-Canadian Family Study on Factor V Leiden Thrombophilia
other synonyms: F5L Family Study|F5L Thrombophilia French-Canadian Pedigree study|F5L family study|F5L-families study|F5Leiden Cohort|French-Canadian FVL family study|French-Canadian family study on Factor V Leiden
definition: A family study of five extended French-Canadian pedigrees, identified between 2005 and 2006 at the Thrombosis Clinic of the Ottawa Hospital, Canada, through single probands with objectively diagnosed idiopathic venous thromboembolism who carried the factor V Leiden mutation, whose consenting relatives were genotyped genome-wide and measured for plasma haemostatic factors.

label: Familial Breast Cancer Study
other synonyms: Genetics of Familial Breast Cancer Study|ICR Familial Breast Cancer Study
definition: A study coordinated from the Institute of Cancer Research, Sutton, that from 1995 recruited people with breast cancer and a family history of the disease, as the index cases of their families, through cancer genetics clinics throughout the United Kingdom, whose clinicians and counsellors formed the Breast Cancer Susceptibility Collaboration (UK), for research into inherited susceptibility to breast cancer.

label: Finnish Colorectal Cancer Predisposition Study
definition: A population-based series of colorectal cancer patients, run from the University of Helsinki, in which tumour and normal tissue were collected from consecutive newly diagnosed patients at nine central hospitals in south-eastern Finland in 1994–1998, and afterwards at two of them, to find hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer and other inherited predisposition to colorectal cancer; its genetic association studies compared the patients with Finnish blood donors from the same region.

label: Fukuoka Colorectal Cancer Study
other synonyms: Fukuoka colorectal cancer study
definition: A community-based case-control study of colorectal cancer among residents of Fukuoka City and three adjacent areas of Japan, comparing patients having surgery for a first diagnosis of colorectal cancer at eight hospitals, interviewed from 2000 to 2003, with community controls randomly selected and frequency-matched on sex, age and residence, surveyed in 2001 and 2002; diet and lifestyle were assessed by in-person interview and blood was taken for genotyping, to study dietary, behavioural and genetic factors in colorectal carcinogenesis.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to eating behavior (ECTO:6000021)

label: Fremantle Diabetes Study
other synonyms: Fremantle Diabetes Study Phase 2|Fremantle Diabetes Study Phase II|Fremantle diabetes study phase II
definition: A community-based longitudinal observational study of people with known diabetes living in a postcode-defined area around the port city of Fremantle, Western Australia, run in two separately recruited phases, Phase I (1993–1996) and Phase II (2008–2011). Participants were identified from hospital, clinic and primary-care lists and local advertising, assessed in detail at entry and followed for diabetes complications and mortality.

label: Fuchs Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy Controls
other synonyms: Fuchs’ Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy Controls
definition: The unaffected controls of a multicentre genetic study of Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy in the United States: people of European descent aged 60 or older, recruited at the study's clinical sites and matched by age, sex and ancestry to its index cases, whose corneas were graded free of the dystrophy on slit-lamp examination and whose refractive error and central corneal thickness were measured at baseline.

label: Fels Longitudinal Study
other synonyms: FELS LONGITUDINAL STUDY|Fels longitudinal study
definition: A family-based longitudinal study of growth, development and body composition begun in 1929 in Yellow Springs, Ohio, United States, whose participants are usually enrolled at birth and followed with serial examinations until death or infirmity, now run under Wright State University in Dayton, Ohio, with genotype data used in genetic analyses of adiposity and liver fat.

label: Framingham Eye Study
definition: An ophthalmological study nested within the Framingham Heart Study in Framingham, Massachusetts, United States, in which participants of the Heart Study's original cohort were given eye examinations in 1973–1975 to evaluate senile cataract, age-related macular degeneration, glaucoma and retinopathy, and offspring of the original participants were examined in 1989–1991.
diseases: population study of: cataract (MONDO:0005129)|population study of: diabetic retinopathy (MONDO:0005266)|population study of: glaucoma (MONDO:0005041)|population study of: macular degeneration (MONDO:0003004)

label: Finnish Genetic Study of Arrhythmic Events
other synonyms: Finnish Genetic Study for Arrhythmic Events
definition: A prospective case-control study run from the University of Oulu that since 1998 has collected medical records and medicolegal autopsy data from consecutive victims of out-of-hospital sudden cardiac death in the Oulu University Hospital District, northern Finland, with survivors of an acute coronary event treated at Oulu University Hospital as controls, to study the characteristics and genetic background of sudden cardiac death.

label: FinnTwin16
other synonyms: FinnTwin16 Cohort|FinnTwin16 study|Finntwin16|Finntwin16 study
definition: A population-based longitudinal study of Finnish twins from five consecutive birth cohorts (1975–1979) and their families, one of the three cohorts of the Finnish Twin Cohort Study, begun in 1991 with baseline assessments of the twins and their parents when the twins were aged 16 and followed with questionnaire waves at ages 17 and 18½, in young adulthood and later, the fifth wave also assessing the twins' spouses or partners.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to Physical Activity (ECTO:6000039)|designed to study: exposure to alcohol consumption (ECTO:0001082)|designed to study: exposure to smoking (ECTO:6000013)

label: Older Finnish Twin Cohort
other synonyms: Older Twin Cohort|The Older Finnish Twin Cohort|older Finnish Twin Cohort|older Finnish Twin Cohort Study|older Finnish Twin Cohort study
definition: A population-based longitudinal cohort of twins from same-sex pairs born in Finland before 1958, identified from the population register and established in 1974, who answered health questionnaires in 1975, 1981, 1990 and 2011–2012, were screened for dementia in later waves, took part in clinical studies of subsamples and are followed up through national medical registers; it was expanded to opposite-sex pairs born 1938–1957, and is the oldest of the three Finnish Twin Cohorts.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to smoking (ECTO:6000013)

label: FINRISK 1997
other synonyms: FINRISK 1997 cohort
definition: The 1997 survey of the National FINRISK Study, a population-based cross-sectional survey of a stratified random sample of people aged 25–74 living in five geographical areas of Finland (the Helsinki, southwestern Finland, North Karelia, Oulu and Kuopio regions), examined for chronic-disease risk factors and followed up for incident cardiovascular disease and mortality.

label: Finnish Randomized Study of Screening for Prostate Cancer
other synonyms: Finnish Randomised Study of Screening for Prostate Cancer
definition: A randomised trial of prostate-cancer screening in Finland, the largest component of the European Randomized Study of Screening for Prostate Cancer, enrolling men aged 55–67 during 1996–1999 and inviting those randomised to its screening arm to prostate-specific-antigen-based screening at four-year intervals.

label: Finland SO replication
definition: A Finnish case-control sample of multiple sclerosis patients with at least one parent born in Southern Ostrobothnia, the internal isolate on the western coast of Finland with an increased prevalence of multiple sclerosis, and anonymous population controls collected at the Central Hospital of Seinäjoki in Southern Ostrobothnia, that was genotyped as the isolate replication set of a 2010 genome-wide association study of multiple sclerosis in that isolate.

label: FIRE-3
other synonyms: FIRE-3 trial|Multicenter Randomized Trial Evaluating FOLFIRI Plus Cetuximab Versus FOLFIRI Plus Bevacizumab in First Line Treatment of Metastatic Colorectal Cancer.|Phase 3 Randomized Clinical Trial (FOLFIRI + cetuximab, FOLFIRI + bevacizumab
definition: An open-label, randomised phase 3 trial, led from the Ludwig-Maximilians-University of Munich, that from January 2007 to September 2012 recruited patients aged 18–75 with KRAS (exon 2) wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer at centres in Germany and Austria and assigned them to first-line FOLFIRI plus cetuximab or FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab.

label: Fudan Lung Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of lung cancer in ethnic Chinese in the Shanghai area of China, whose cases were patients presenting with primary lung cancer and whose controls were patients diagnosed with diseases unrelated to any cancer at four hospitals (Shanghai Changhai Hospital, Jiangsu Taizhou People's Hospital, Zhongshan Hospital of Fudan University and Shanghai Chest Hospital); it is one of the studies pooled in the Female Lung Cancer Consortium in Asia.

label: Flemish Study on Environment, Genes and Health Outcomes
other synonyms: FLEMENGHO study|FLEmish study on Environment, Genes and Health Outcome|Flemish Study on Environment, Genes, and Health Outcomes
definition: An observational, community-based prospective cohort study of cardiovascular risk factors and outcomes in adults, whose family-based population sample was randomly recruited between 1985 and 2010, stratified by age and sex, from a geographically defined area in northeastern Belgium, and followed up with in-person examinations and records of health outcomes.

label: Fleurbaix-Laventie Ville Santé II study
other synonyms: FLVS II Study|Fleurbaix Laventie Ville Santé II Study|Fleurbaix Laventie Ville Santé II study|Fleurbaix Laventie Ville Santé Study II|Fleurbaix-Laventie Ville Sant_ II study|Fleurbaix-Laventie Ville-Santé II study
definition: The second phase of the Fleurbaix Laventie Ville Santé study: a prospective, community-based study of nuclear families (parents and their children) living in the two small towns of Fleurbaix and Laventie in northern France, recruited in 1999 among the families of the first phase (FLVS I, families with a child in primary school in 1992) and examined again in 2001, to identify determinants of adiposity and of weight and adiposity changes in the general population.

label: Framingham Offspring Study
other synonyms: Framingham Heart Study Offspring Cohort|Framingham Offspring|Framingham offspring study
definition: A community-based cohort of offspring and spouses of the original Framingham Heart Study participants, recruited from 1971 to study cardiovascular disease and the familial clustering of its risk factors, followed with repeated in-person examinations and telephone contacts.

label: Familial Ovarian Tumor Study
other synonyms: Familial Ovarian Tumour Study|Toronto Ovarian Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of epithelial ovarian cancer in Ontario, Canada, whose cases, aged 20–79 and diagnosed from 1995 to 1999, were identified through the Ontario Cancer Registry, with family-based controls and population-based controls drawn from women attending a screening clinic at Women's College Hospital, Toronto; it is the Toronto site of the Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium.

label: Further Cardiovascular Outcomes Research with PCSK9 Inhibition in Subjects with Elevated Risk
other synonyms: FOURIER trial|Further Cardiovascular Outcomes Research With PCSK9 Inhibition in Subjects With Elevated Risk|TIMI 59
definition: A multinational, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (TIMI 59) of whether adding the PCSK9 inhibitor evolocumab to statin therapy reduces major cardiovascular events in patients aged 40 to 85 with clinically evident atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (a history of myocardial infarction, non-haemorrhagic stroke or symptomatic peripheral artery disease) and raised LDL or non-HDL cholesterol.

label: Fundación Pública Galega de Medicina Xenómica
other synonyms: Galician Public Foundation of Genomic Medicine
definition: A study of carriers of pathogenic BRCA1 or BRCA2 variants, with and without breast cancer, at the Fundación Pública Galega de Medicina Xenómica, the genomic medicine foundation of the Galician Health Service (SERGAS) in Santiago de Compostela, Spain, which contributes its carriers to the Consortium of Investigators of Modifiers of BRCA1 and BRCA2.
diseases: at risk of: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|at risk of: ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170)

label: FRagmin and Fast Revascularisation during InStability in Coronary artery disease II
other synonyms: Fragmin and Fast Revascularization during Instability in Coronary Artery Disease
definition: A prospective randomised multicentre trial at 58 hospitals in Sweden, Norway and Denmark in which patients with unstable coronary-artery disease were assigned to an early invasive or a non-invasive treatment strategy, together with placebo-controlled long-term treatment with the low-molecular-mass heparin dalteparin (Fragmin), to compare the two strategies.

label: Genetic Epidemiology of Ovarian Cancer Study
other synonyms: Family Registry for Ovarian Cancer|Family Registry for Ovarian Cancer Study|Genetic Epidemiology of Ovarian Cancer
definition: A population-based case-control study of ovarian cancer run from Stanford, California, and formerly called the Family Registry for Ovarian Cancer, whose cases were women diagnosed from 1997 into the early 2000s identified through the Greater Bay Area Cancer Registry in Northern California and whose controls were identified by random-digit dialling in the same area, frequency matched on age and race/ethnicity; one of the studies of the Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium.

label: Family Study of Cocaine Dependence
other synonyms: Family Study on Cocaine Dependence|FinnTwin, Family Study of Cocaine Dependence
definition: A family study of cocaine dependence at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis, Missouri, in which adults with cocaine dependence recruited from chemical dependency treatment centres in the St. Louis area, and community controls matched to them on age, ethnicity, gender and zip code and recruited through driver's licence records, each took part with a full sibling, to study family, neighbourhood and genetic contributions to substance dependence; recruitment targeted equal numbers of men and women and of European-Americans and African-Americans.

label: Fudan-Huashan Study
definition: A type 2 diabetes case-control sample of Han Chinese from Beijing or Shanghai, China, made up of people with type 2 diabetes and nondiabetic controls, that was one of the four sample sets of the stage 1 genome-wide scan of a 2013 genome-wide association study of type 2 diabetes in Chinese Hans.

label: Genetics in Atrial Fibrillation
other synonyms: Genetics in AF
definition: A Norwegian study of early-onset lone atrial fibrillation that enrolled, between 2009 and 2016, people diagnosed with atrial fibrillation before age 50 in the absence of clinical or echocardiographic signs of cardiovascular disease, hypertension, or metabolic or pulmonary disease; all participants had a clinical examination with ECG and echocardiography and gave blood for DNA.

label: German Alzheimer's disease Integrated Genome Research Network
other synonyms: Alzheimer's disease Integrated Genome Research Network|German Alzheimer disease Integrates Genome Research Network
definition: A German genome-wide association dataset of Alzheimer's disease cases and controls from the Alzheimer's disease Integrated Genome Research Network (AD-IG) of the German National Genome Research Network (NGFN), a Federal Ministry of Education and Research-funded project of the Homburg group, used for in silico replication in the 2011 GERAD+ genome-wide association study of Alzheimer's disease.

label: Genetic Association Information Network
definition: A public-private partnership of the Foundation for the US National Institutes of Health that, through a series of collaborative genome-wide association studies, genotyped samples from case-control studies of bipolar disorder, diabetic nephropathy, major depressive disorder, psoriasis and schizophrenia and a trio study of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, and made the resulting individual genotype and phenotype data available to researchers through dbGaP.
diseases: patients with: attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (MONDO:0007743)|patients with: bipolar disorder (MONDO:0004985)|patients with: diabetic kidney disease (MONDO:0005016)|patients with: major depressive disorder (MONDO:0002009)|patients with: psoriasis (MONDO:0005083)|patients with: schizophrenia (MONDO:0005090)

label: Genetics of Asthma International Network
definition: A multinational family study of asthma that in 1999-2001 recruited, at centres in Europe (among them the United Kingdom, Greece and Norway), Australia and the United States, nuclear families of probands aged 7-35 years with physician-diagnosed asthma and their symptomatic siblings, together with their parents, who were assessed by questionnaire, lung function and allergen skin prick testing, to search for asthma susceptibility loci and quantitative asthma phenotypes.

label: Bipolar Disorder Genetic Association Information Network
other synonyms: Genetic Association Information Network Bipolar Sample|NIMH Bipolar Disorder Genetic Association Information Network
definition: The sample of the first genome-wide association study of the Bipolar Genome Study, funded through the Genetic Association Information Network (GAIN): unrelated cases with bipolar disorder of European American and African American ancestry from the collections of the NIMH Genetics Initiative for Bipolar Disorder in the United States, and controls matched by ethnicity, age and sex who were ascertained throughout the United States for the Molecular Genetics of Schizophrenia collaboration, all genotyped on the Affymetrix 6.0 array.

label: GAIN Major Depressive Disorder Study
other synonyms: GAIN-MDD study|Genetic Association Information Network-MDD|Genetic Association Information Network-MDD Study|Major Depression Stage 1 Genomewide Association in Population-Based Samples Study|Major Depression: Stage 1 Genomewide Association in Population-Based Samples
definition: A case-control genome-wide association study of major depressive disorder in the Netherlands, one of the six initial studies of the Genetic Association Information Network of the Foundation for the US National Institutes of Health, whose cases, with a lifetime diagnosis of major depressive disorder, came mainly from the Netherlands Study of Depression and Anxiety and also from the population-based cohorts NEMESIS, ARIADNE and the Netherlands Twin Register, and whose controls, selected for low genetic liability to major depressive disorder, came mainly from the Netherlands Twin Register and also from the Netherlands Study of Depression and Anxiety.

label: Genetics of Asthma in Latino Americans
other synonyms: GALA Study|GALA study|Genetics of Asthma in Latino Americans (GALA) Study|Genetics of Asthma in Latino Americans Study|Genetics of Asthma in Latino Populations
definition: A multicentre, international, family-based study of childhood asthma run from the University of California, San Francisco, which recruited Mexican and Puerto Rican children with asthma and their parents (parent–child trios) in Mexico City, the San Francisco Bay Area, Puerto Rico and New York City, to identify clinical and genetic risk factors for asthma.

label: GALicia Estudio Oncológico de coloN
other synonyms: GALicia Estudio Oncologico de coloN
definition: A colon cancer study in Galicia, Spain, carried out with the University Hospital of Santiago de Compostela (its surgery and pathology departments and biobank) and health research institutes in Santiago de Compostela and Vigo, whose participants were included in genome-wide association studies of colorectal cancer that pooled the studies of the CORECT, CCFR and GECCO consortia.

label: Gwangju Alzheimer's and Related Dementias
other synonyms: Gwangju Alzheimer and Related Dementias Study|Gwangju Alzheimer's & Related Dementias|Gwangju Alzheimer's and Related Dementia
definition: A community-based longitudinal cohort study of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias in South Korea, established in 2013 and run by the GARD Cohort Research Center at Chosun University in Gwangju, whose participants, aged 60 or over, come mainly from local senior citizens' centres in the city of Gwangju, with additional people with Alzheimer's disease or mild cognitive impairment recruited from Chosun University Hospital and its affiliated hospitals in Gwangju and elsewhere in Korea, and are followed with repeated clinical and neuropsychological evaluation, neuroimaging and biospecimen collection for multi-omics analyses, for early detection and monitoring of dementia.

label: Genetic Architecture of Smoking and Smoking Cessation
other synonyms: The Genetic Architecture of Smoking and Smoking Cessation
definition: A genome-wide association study of the Gene Environment Association Studies initiative (GENEVA), deposited in dbGaP as phs000404, that genotyped nicotine-dependent smokers and non-dependent smoking controls from two projects, the Collaborative Genetic Study of Nicotine Dependence (recruited in Detroit and St. Louis) and the University of Wisconsin Transdisciplinary Tobacco Use Research Center smoking cessation trials (recruited in Madison and Milwaukee, Wisconsin), with harmonised measures, to identify genetic variants that contribute to nicotine dependence, related smoking behaviours and smoking cessation.
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to Tobacco Use (ECTO:6000041)|participants with exposure: exposure to nicotine addictive consumption (ECTO:0100000)|participants with exposure: exposure to smoking (ECTO:6000013)

label: Australian Genetics of Bipolar Disorder Study
other synonyms: Australian Genetics of Bipolar Disorder|Australian Genetics of Bipolar Disorder study|GBP Study
definition: A nation-wide cohort of adults living with bipolar disorder in Australia, run by QIMR Berghofer Medical Research Institute, recruited from 2018 in three waves (a nation-wide media campaign, a Services Australia mail-out to people dispensed lithium carbonate, and a follow-up survey of the Australian Genetics of Depression Study) who completed an online survey and were asked for a saliva sample for genotyping and consent to linkage of their Pharmaceutical and Medicare Benefits Schedule records, to study the relationships between genetic risk, symptom severity, treatment response, medication side effects and health care usage in bipolar disorder.

label: Guizhou-Bijie Type 2 Diabetes Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of type 2 diabetes conducted from September 2009 to January 2010 in Bijie city, Guizhou province, China, recruiting through advertisement unrelated Han Chinese adults aged 30 to 80 with at least ten years' residence in Bijie city.

label: Gothenburg Cervical Artery Dissection Collection
other synonyms: Gothenburg cervical artery dissection collection
definition: A collection of patients with cervical artery dissection, of European origin, at the Sahlgrenska Academy of the University of Gothenburg, Sweden, drawn from the Sahlgrenska Academy Study on Ischemic Stroke and meeting the inclusion criteria of the CADISP study, which with controls from the same study formed one of the follow-up samples of the 2015 genome-wide association study of cervical artery dissection.

label: CBDB/NIMH Genetic Study of Schizophrenia
other synonyms: Clinical Brain Disorders Branch/National Institute of Mental Health sibling study|NIMH Clinical Brain Disorder Branch (CBDB) Sibling Study of Schizophrenia Genetics|NIMH Genes, Cognition and Psychosis Program|NIMH Genes, Cognition and Psychosis Study
definition: A family study of schizophrenia in the intramural research programme of the US National Institute of Mental Health, run by its Clinical Brain Disorders Branch and Genes, Cognition and Psychosis Program, that recruited patients with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder, their unaffected full siblings and healthy volunteers from local and national sources and studied them with cognitive testing, brain imaging and genotyping to identify intermediate phenotypes and risk genes for schizophrenia.

label: Greek Coronary Disease Cohort
definition: A case-control study of coronary artery disease conducted in Greece, whose cases were patients hospitalised for acute coronary syndrome or diagnosed with left main coronary artery disease during hospitalisation, and whose controls were drawn from the TEENs of Attica: Genes and Environment study and a case-control study of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.

label: German Consortium for Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer
other synonyms: German Consortium for Hereditary Breast & Ovarian Cancer|German Consortium for hereditary breast/ovarian cancer|German Consortium of Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer|German Familial Breast Cancer Study|German Familial Breast Group
definition: The research collection of the German Consortium for Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer, a nationwide consortium of university centres for familial breast and ovarian cancer in Germany, made up of index patients and relatives from families at high risk of hereditary breast and ovarian cancer who met the consortium's criteria for germline testing and were counselled and tested at its centres from the late 1990s on, with clinical and family-history data held in a central registry at the University of Leipzig; its BRCA1/2-mutation-negative familial breast cancer index cases are studied within the Breast Cancer Association Consortium and its data are also part of the Consortium of Investigators of Modifiers of BRCA1/2.
diseases: at risk of: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|at risk of: ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170)

label: Guangdong Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of lung cancer in the Guangdong area of China, whose cases are ethnic Chinese in-patients with incident, histologically confirmed primary lung cancer of any histological type diagnosed at the Guangdong Lung Cancer Institute and Guangdong General Hospital, and whose controls are healthy, cancer-free patients from the health examination clinics of the same hospitals; one of the studies of the Female Lung Cancer Consortium in Asia genotyped for its genome-wide association study of lung cancer in never-smoking women.

label: Gene-Environment Interaction in Prostate Cancer Study
other synonyms: The Gene-Environment Interaction in Prostate Cancer Study
definition: A case-control study of prostate cancer run by the Henry Ford Health System in Detroit, Michigan, United States, which enrolled men of Caucasian or African American race younger than 75 years with adenocarcinoma of the prostate living in the metropolitan Detroit tri-county area, and controls randomly selected from the same Henry Ford Health System population base, between January 2001 and December 2004, to study gene-environment interaction in prostate cancer risk.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to polycyclic arene (ECTO:9000433)

label: Gene-Environment-Development Initiative
other synonyms: Gene-Environment Development Initiative
definition: A consortium funded by the US National Institute on Drug Abuse that brought together four existing longitudinal, general-population studies with repeated assessments across childhood, adolescence and young adulthood, the Virginia Twin Study of Adolescent Behavioral Development, the Great Smoky Mountains Study and the Caring for Children in the Community study in the United States and the Christchurch Health and Development Study in New Zealand, to identify which genes, environments and developmental transitions together predict the development of drug use and misuse.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to alcohol consumption (ECTO:0001082)|designed to study: exposure to cannabis (ECTO:0100005)|designed to study: exposure to nicotine addictive consumption (ECTO:0100000)

label: Genetic Epidemiological Study of Lung Adenocarcinoma
other synonyms: Genetic Epidemiological Study for Lung AdenoCarcinoma|Taiwan Genetic Epidemiological Study for Lung Adenocarcinoma
definition: A genetic epidemiological study of lung cancer in Taiwan whose case-control component, from September 2002, recruited ethnically Han Chinese patients aged 18 years or older with histologically confirmed incident primary lung cancer from six medical centres, together with cancer-free controls matched on age, gender and ethnicity from the health-examination departments of the same hospitals, to evaluate questionnaire-based and genetic risk factors for lung cancer.

label: Genetic Lung Cancer Predisposition Study
other synonyms: GEnetic Lung CAncer Predisposition Study
definition: A case-control DNA resource for lung cancer established in March 1999 by the Institute of Cancer Research and adopted in 2002 onto the portfolio of the National Cancer Research Network, through which oncology departments across England recruited patients diagnosed with lung cancer between March 1999 and July 2004, and their spouses or partners without a history of cancer as controls, to collect DNA and clinico-pathological data for identifying low-penetrance susceptibility alleles for lung cancer.

label: Genes and Environment in Lung Cancer, Singapore Study
other synonyms: Genes and Environment in Lung Cancer Study|Genes and Environment in Lung Cancer, Singapore study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of lung cancer in ethnic Chinese women in Singapore, recruited from 2005 to 2008 in the major public-sector hospitals (Changi General Hospital, National Cancer Centre, National University Hospital, Singapore General Hospital and Tan Tock Seng Hospital), with cases of primary lung carcinoma of all histological types and controls from the same hospitals frequency-matched by 10-year age group; it is one of the studies pooled in the Female Lung Cancer Consortium in Asia.

label: Genetic Epidemiology of Migraine Study
other synonyms: GEM Study|GEM study|Genetic Epidemiology of Migraine|Genetic Epidemiology of Migraine study
definition: A Dutch population-based study of migraine embedded in the MORGEN project, in which adults aged 20 to 65 randomly selected from two Dutch county population registries (Maastricht and Doetinchem) to take part in a general health survey were screened for headache history, screen-positives were given a detailed headache questionnaire and a random subset a semistructured telephone clinical interview, and migraine was diagnosed by International Headache Society criteria, to study the prevalence, characteristics, cardiovascular risk profile and genetics of migraine.

label: Genetic Modifiers of cancer risk in BRCA1/2 mutation carriers
other synonyms: Genetic Modifiers of BRCA1 and BRCA2|Genetic Modifiers of BRCA1 and BRCA2 Study|Genetic Modifiers of Cancer Risk in BRCA1/2 Mutation Carriers
definition: A multicentre study of carriers of pathogenic BRCA1 or BRCA2 variants, run through the French National Cancer Genetics Network of the UNICANCER Genetic Group, coordinated from Lyon (Hospices Civils de Lyon and Centre Léon Bérard) and the Institut Curie in Paris, with contributing cancer genetics centres across France and at Creighton University in Omaha, United States, to identify genetic modifiers of cancer risk in these carriers.
diseases: at risk of: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|at risk of: ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170)

label: Genetic Epidemiology of Metabolic Syndrome Study
other synonyms: GEMS Study|Genetic Epidemiology of Metabolic Syndrome|Genetic Epidemiology of Metabolic Syndrome Project|Genetic Epidemiology of Metabolic Syndrome study
definition: A multicentre, multinational family-based study initiated in 1999 to identify genes associated with the metabolic syndrome and related traits, in which affected status was defined by atherogenic dyslipidaemia (low HDL cholesterol with elevated triglycerides for age, sex and country). Its first arm recruited families of Turkish and southern European and of Northern and Western European origin at six sites in Australia, Canada, Finland, Turkey, Switzerland and the United States for linkage analysis; its second arm recruited unrelated cases with atherogenic dyslipidaemia and normolipidaemic controls of Northern and Western European origin at five of the sites for genome-wide association analysis.
diseases: patients with: Abnormal circulating lipid concentration (HP:0003119)|patients with: metabolic syndrome X (MONDO:0011565)

label: Genomics of Kidney Transplantation
other synonyms: DAIT GEN-03|Genomics of Kidney Transplantation Study
definition: A prospective observational cohort of kidney or kidney-pancreas transplant recipients, enrolled within 10 days of transplantation, and kidney donors, recruited from 2012 to 2016 at transplant centres in the United States (University of Alabama in Birmingham, University of Minnesota, Hennepin County Medical Center and Mayo Clinic) and Canada (University of Alberta) in a study sponsored by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases with the Genomics of Transplantation Cooperative Research Program, to investigate the relationship between genetic variation and kidney transplant outcomes.
diseases: patients with: end stage renal failure (MONDO:0004375)|patients with: kidney disorder (MONDO:0005240)|patients with: kidney failure (MONDO:0001106)|patients with: transplant rejection (MONDO:1010185)

label: Gene-Diet Attica Investigation on childhood obesity
other synonyms: GENDAI Study|GENe-Diet Attica Investigation on childhood obesity|Gene and Diet Attica Investigation|Gene-Diet Attica Investigation on Childhood Obesity|Gene-Diet Attica investigation on childhood obesity
definition: A school-based cross-sectional study of fifth- and sixth-grade children aged 10 to 14 years, enrolled between November 2005 and June 2006 from primary schools in the Attica region of Greece, which collected anthropometric, dietary, clinical, genetic, sociodemographic and lifestyle data from the children and their families to evaluate the contributions and interactions of genetic, dietary and physical activity factors in childhood obesity.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to Physical Activity (ECTO:6000039)|designed to study: exposure to eating behavior (ECTO:6000021)

label: Génétique de la Néphropathie Diabétique
other synonyms: GENEDIAB Study|GEnétique de la NEphropathie DIABétique|Genetics of Diabetic Nephropathy|Genetique de la Nephropathie Diabetique
definition: A cross-sectional multicentre study of people with insulin-dependent (type 1) diabetes and proliferative diabetic retinopathy, and so exposed to the risk of diabetic nephropathy, conducted from May 1994 to April 1995 in 17 diabetic clinics in France and Belgium, in which participants were classified by the severity of their renal involvement, to study the genetic determinants of diabetic nephropathy.
diseases: patients with: diabetic kidney disease (MONDO:0005016)|patients with: proliferative diabetic retinopathy (MONDO:0001660)|patients with: type 1 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005147)

label: Gene MSA CH
other synonyms: Gene MSA Switzerland
definition: The Swiss site sample, recruited at University Hospital Basel, Switzerland, of people with multiple sclerosis and controls enrolled in the Genetic Multiple Sclerosis Associations (GeneMSA) study, a prospective case-control study of multiple sclerosis started in 2003 and funded by GlaxoSmithKline at three clinical centres with identical inclusion criteria, of patients of northern-European ancestry with any clinical subtype of multiple sclerosis (preferentially relapsing onset) and unrelated controls (mainly spouses or partners, friends and other volunteers) group-matched on age and sex, to study genetic influences on susceptibility and on clinical and MRI phenotype; used as a separate stratum in genome-wide meta-analyses of multiple sclerosis.

label: Gene MSA NL
other synonyms: Gene MSA Netherlands
definition: The Dutch site sample, recruited at Vrije Universiteit Medical Center in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, of people with multiple sclerosis and controls enrolled in the Genetic Multiple Sclerosis Associations (GeneMSA) study, a prospective case-control study of multiple sclerosis started in 2003 and funded by GlaxoSmithKline at three clinical centres with identical inclusion criteria, of patients of northern-European ancestry with any clinical subtype of multiple sclerosis (preferentially relapsing onset) and unrelated controls (mainly spouses or partners, friends and other volunteers) group-matched on age and sex, to study genetic influences on susceptibility and on clinical and MRI phenotype; used as a separate stratum in genome-wide meta-analyses of multiple sclerosis.

label: Gene MSA US
definition: The United States site sample, recruited at the University of California San Francisco, of people with multiple sclerosis and controls enrolled in the Genetic Multiple Sclerosis Associations (GeneMSA) study, a prospective case-control study of multiple sclerosis started in 2003 and funded by GlaxoSmithKline at three clinical centres with identical inclusion criteria, of patients of northern-European ancestry with any clinical subtype of multiple sclerosis (preferentially relapsing onset) and unrelated controls (mainly spouses or partners, friends and other volunteers) group-matched on age and sex, to study genetic influences on susceptibility and on clinical and MRI phenotype; used as a separate stratum in genome-wide meta-analyses of multiple sclerosis.

label: Genetic Predictors of Adverse Radiotherapy Effects
other synonyms: Gene-PARE project|Gene-PARE study|Genetic Predictors of Adverse Radiotherapy Effects Study
definition: A biorepository of frozen lymphocytes and DNA from patients treated with radiotherapy for cancer, with a database of their diagnosis, treatment and outcome, run from the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, whose patients include men treated for prostate cancer at the Mount Sinai Hospital in New York and patients treated in Tokyo and Chiba, Japan, and which was set up to find genetic variants that predict adverse effects of radiotherapy.

label: GenePD Study
other synonyms: GenePD study|Genome-wide scan for Parkinsons diseaseÌ¨ Initiative
definition: An international multicentre study of the genetics of familial Parkinson's disease, designed for genetic linkage analysis of affected relative pairs, that recruits families with at least two members with Parkinson's disease meeting diagnostic criteria, ascertained through a proband with an affected sibling, parent, offspring or more distant relative, at academic centres and clinics in the United States, Canada, Australia, Germany, Italy, the United Kingdom and Denmark.

label: Genetic influences on severity of COVID-19 illness in Korea
definition: A South Korean case–control study of host genetic influences on the severity of COVID-19, contributed to the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative, that compares patients hospitalised with COVID-19 with controls, all of East Asian ancestry, under the review of eight Korean institutional review boards, among them those of Chungnam National University Hospital, Keimyung University Dongsan Hospital, Myongji Hospital and Pusan National University Hospital; its cases were genotyped on version 1.1 and its controls on version 1.0 of the Korea Biobank Array (KoreanChip).

label: GENEVA study
other synonyms: GENEVA Study|Genetic evaluation of atopic dermatitis
definition: A German case-control sample for genetic studies of atopic dermatitis, whose cases are patients recruited at the tertiary dermatology clinics of the Technische Universität München (in the GENEVA study itself), the University of Kiel and the University of Bonn and diagnosed by dermatologists on skin examination, and whose controls come from the PopGen biobank and the population-based KORA surveys.

label: Dental Caries: Whole Genome Association and Gene x Environment Studies
other synonyms: Caries GENEVA Study|Dental Caries: GENEVA Genome Wide Association Study|GENEVA Dental Caries|GENEVA Dental Caries Study|GENEVA caries consortium|GENEVA dental caries project
definition: A multi-site genome-wide association study of dental caries in the NIH Gene Environment Association Studies (GENEVA) consortium, which genotyped families and unrelated individuals with dental caries data from the Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia in Pennsylvania and West Virginia, the University of Pittsburgh School of Dental Medicine Dental Registry and DNA Repository, the Iowa Fluoride Study and Iowa Bone Development Study, and the Iowa Head Start Study, United States.

label: GenNet Study
other synonyms: GenNet Network|GenNet study
definition: A family study of the genetics of blood pressure and hypertension in the United States, one of the four networks of the NHLBI Family Blood Pressure Program, which from 1995 recruited nuclear families through young and middle-aged probands with blood pressure in the upper part of the distribution and enrolled their siblings and parents regardless of blood pressure: European Americans in Tecumseh, Michigan, African Americans in Maywood, Illinois, and also Mexican American families.

label: GenomEUtwin
other synonyms: GenomEUTwin|GenomEUtwin project|GenomEUtwin study
definition: A European Community-funded research project that joined eight large twin registers (the national twin cohorts of Denmark, Finland, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway and Sweden, the UK TwinsUK cohort and an Australian twin cohort) with the multinational MORGAM population cohort, to identify genetic and lifestyle contributors to common diseases by linkage and association studies.

label: Genetic Study in Ischemic Stroke Patients treated with r-tPA
other synonyms: Genetic Study in Ischaemic Stroke Patients treated with tPA|Genetic Study in Ischemic Stroke Patients treated with recombinant tissue plasminogen activator|Genetic Study in Ischemic Stroke Patients treated with tPA|Genetic study in ischaemic stroke patients treated with tPA
