definition: A national registry and biobank of patients with primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease) in Norway, established in 1996 within the National Registry of Organ-Specific Autoimmune Diseases (ROAS) at Haukeland University Hospital, Bergen, that collects clinical information, demographics and serial biological samples from most Norwegian patients with the disease.

label: Women's College Research Institute Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer Study
other synonyms: Risk Factor Analysis of Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer
definition: A long-term study, started in 1995 at Women's College Hospital in Toronto, Canada, of women aged 18 or over carrying a BRCA1 or BRCA2 (later also PALB2) mutation, whatever their cancer history, recruited from Canada, the United States, Europe, Asia, the Caribbean and Latin America and followed by questionnaires every two years, to study hormonal, reproductive and lifestyle factors in the prevention and treatment of hereditary breast and ovarian cancer; it contributes carriers to CIMBA.
diseases: at risk of: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|at risk of: ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170)

label: Normative Aging Study
other synonyms: VA Normative Aging Study|Veterans Administration Normative Aging Study
definition: A longitudinal study of health and aging, established by the Veterans Administration in 1963, of healthy men aged 21 to 80 from the greater Boston area, United States, who were free of known chronic medical conditions at enrolment.

label: Netherlands Brain Bank
definition: A brain bank established at the end of 1985 at the Netherlands Institute for Brain Research, in collaboration with nursing homes in and around Amsterdam, the Netherlands, which performs rapid autopsies of donors who gave informed consent during life for the research use of their brain tissue and medical files, originally to supply post-mortem brain tissue from Alzheimer's disease patients and controls.
diseases: patients with: nervous system disorder (MONDO:0005071)|patients with: psychiatric disorder (MONDO:0002025)

label: Nashville Breast Health Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of breast cancer in the eight-county Nashville metropolitan area, Tennessee, United States, approved through Vanderbilt University Medical Center, which from April 2001 enrolled women aged 25 to 75 with newly diagnosed invasive breast cancer or ductal carcinoma in situ, found through the Tennessee State Cancer Registry and five major Nashville hospitals, and controls found by random-digit dialling and frequency-matched on age, race and county, with telephone interviews, food frequency questionnaires and buccal DNA samples.
diseases: patients with: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|patients with: ductal breast carcinoma in situ (MONDO:0005023)

label: Nanjing and Beijing Lung Cancer Studies
definition: A two-centre case-control genome-wide association study of lung cancer in Han Chinese in China, made up of the Nanjing Study (with participants from Nanjing and Shanghai) and the Beijing Study, whose cases had histopathologically or cytologically confirmed lung cancer and whose controls, frequency-matched to the cases for age, sex and region, were people receiving routine physical examinations in local hospitals or taking part in community screening for noncommunicable diseases.

label: Norwegian Bone Marrow Donor Registry
definition: The national registry of healthy volunteer bone marrow donors in Norway, held at Oslo University Hospital, whose members are HLA-typed on inclusion in the registry; random selections of registered donors, with their HLA data and samples, serve as healthy population controls in Norwegian genetic and epidemiological studies of immune-mediated disease.

label: National Brain Tumour Study
other synonyms: National Brain Tumor Study
definition: A UK study of primary brain tumours, supported by the National Cancer Research Network, whose recruited glioma cases were the case series of the replication stage of a 2015 genome-wide association study of glioma, compared with healthy UK controls from the National Study of Colorectal Cancer Genetics and the Genetic Lung Cancer Predisposition Study.

label: Nijmegen Cervical Artery Dissection Collection
other synonyms: Nijmegen cervical artery dissection collection
definition: A collection of patients with cervical artery dissection, of European origin, at Radboud University Nijmegen Medical Centre, the Netherlands, drawn in part from the FUTURE study and meeting the inclusion criteria of the CADISP study, which with controls from Nijmegen and the Rotterdam Study formed one of the follow-up samples of the 2015 genome-wide association study of cervical artery dissection.

label: North Cumbria Community Genetics Project
definition: A prospective, unselected, population-based birth cohort in West Cumbria, England, set up by the University of Newcastle and the Westlakes Research Institute, which from January 1996 to 2003 collected umbilical cord blood and tissue, with maternal consent and a short maternal lifestyle questionnaire, from babies born at the West Cumberland Hospital maternity unit in Whitehaven, storing DNA, plasma and viable cells as a resource for genetic and epidemiological studies of gene–environment interaction and health, with some children followed up in childhood.

label: Nagano Colorectal Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of colorectal cancer conducted between October 1998 and March 2002 at four hospitals in Nagano Prefecture, Japan, enrolling patients aged 20-74 with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed colorectal cancer and cancer-free controls from medical check-up examinees at the same hospitals, matched on sex, age, hospital and residential area, with self-administered and food-frequency questionnaires and blood samples.

label: NCI Bladder Cancer
other synonyms: Genome-wide association study for Bladder Cancer Risk|NCI bladder cancer GWAS
definition: The US National Cancer Institute's genome-wide association study of bladder cancer, which pooled cases with histologically confirmed bladder cancer and controls of European descent from two case-control studies in Spain and the United States (the Spanish Bladder Cancer Study and the Maine and Vermont components of the New England Bladder Cancer Study) and three prospective cohorts in Finland and the United States (the Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study, the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial and the American Cancer Society Cancer Prevention Study II Nutrition Cohort) in its first scan (NCI-GWAS1), and added a second scan (NCI-GWAS2) of further cases, including the New Hampshire component of the New England Bladder Cancer Study, with cancer-free controls from previously scanned NCI studies, to identify susceptibility loci for bladder cancer.

label: National Cancer Institute-Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Interdisciplinary Case-Control Study of Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma
other synonyms: National Cancer Institute- Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Interdisciplinary Case-Control Study of Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma|National Cancer Institute- Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Interdisciplinary Case-Control Study of Non-Hodgkins Lymphoma
definition: A multicentre population-based case-control study of non-Hodgkin lymphoma in the United States, run by the US National Cancer Institute, whose cases were people with a first primary non-Hodgkin lymphoma (excluding people infected with HIV) identified through four Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results cancer registries (Detroit, Iowa, Los Angeles and Seattle), and whose controls from the same areas were matched on area, age and race and found by random digit dialling (under 65) or from Medicare files (65 and over).

label: North Carolina Ovarian Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of epithelial ovarian cancer in 48 counties of central and eastern North Carolina, United States, in which women diagnosed with ovarian cancer from 1999 to 2008 were identified by rapid case ascertainment and controls from the same region were selected by random digit dialing and frequency-matched to the cases on age and race.

label: North Carolina Prostate Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of prostate cancer in 12 contiguous counties of western North Carolina, United States, which from November 2006 to November 2008 recruited men aged 40 to 70 with a new histological diagnosis of prostate cancer, identified through the rapid case ascertainment centre of the North Carolina Central Cancer Registry, and controls recruited by friend referral and matched to the cases on age, race and county, each giving a blood sample and completing a food-frequency and a medical and family history questionnaire.

label: National Colorectal Cancer Cohort
other synonyms: National ColoRectal Cancer Cohort|National Colorectal Cancer Cohort study|National colorectal cancer cohort (China)
definition: A prospective cohort study in China, coordinated by the Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University, of risk factors and biomarkers across the colorectal cancer continuum from aetiology to survivorship, made up of a screening cohort of people at high risk of colorectal cancer recruited from 2016 to 2020, first in Jiashan County, Zhejiang Province, and a multicentre cohort of patients newly diagnosed with colorectal cancer recruited from 2015 to 2020 at 16 hospitals in 11 provinces and followed up after surgery.

label: Norfolk Diabetes Case-Control Study
other synonyms: Norfolk Diabetes Case Control Study|Norfolk Diabetes case-control study|Norfolk Diabetes case_control study
definition: A type 2 diabetes case-control study in Norfolk, UK, whose cases were men and women with type 2 diabetes identified through general practice diabetes registers and local hospital diabetes clinic and retinal screening programme registers in Norfolk, and whose controls, free of known diabetes, were randomly selected from participants of the EPIC-Norfolk cohort.

label: Northern Dutch Hodgkin Lymphoma Study
definition: A population-based series of patients with Hodgkin lymphoma diagnosed in the northern Netherlands between 1987 and 2009, whose tumours were classified by WHO criteria and Epstein-Barr virus status and whose germline DNA, with that of first-degree relatives of patients diagnosed up to 2000, was used to study HLA associations with Epstein-Barr virus-positive and -negative Hodgkin lymphoma; its classical Hodgkin lymphoma cases were one of the five case series of the European genome-wide association study of classical Hodgkin lymphoma.

label: Newcastle Endometrial Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based series of histologically confirmed endometrial cancer cases recruited consecutively from 1992 to 2005 among women presenting for treatment at the Hunter Centre for Gynaecological Cancer, John Hunter Hospital, in Newcastle, New South Wales, Australia, with reproductive and environmental risk factors (including ethnicity) from self-reported questionnaires and recurrence, stage, grade and histology from medical records; from 2005 patients at this site were recruited by the Australian National Endometrial Cancer Study. Its cases were genotyped in the genome-wide association studies of the Endometrial Cancer Association Consortium.

label: National Eye Institute Glaucoma Human Genetics Collaboration
other synonyms: NEI Glaucoma Human genetics collaBORation|NEIGHBOR consortium|NEIGHBOR study|National Eye Institute Glaucoma Human Genetics Collaboration study
definition: A case-control study for a genome-wide association study of primary open-angle glaucoma, run by a consortium of investigators at 12 institutions across the United States, whose cases and controls, aged 35 or over and of European or Hispanic white ancestry, were collected at the 12 sites. Most came from university glaucoma and general ophthalmology clinics, and some from other studies such as the Marshfield Personalized Medicine Research Project and the CIGTS and AGIS glaucoma trials. The case and control definitions were harmonised with the GLAUGEN study, and the clinical data were reviewed centrally at the Massachusetts Eye and Ear Infirmary.

label: National Eye Institute Glaucoma Human Genetics Collaboration Heritable Overall Operational Database
other synonyms: NEIGHBORHOOD consortium|national eye institute glaucoma human collaboration heritable overall operational database
definition: A genome-wide meta-analysis resource for primary open-angle glaucoma that combines summary data from eight independent case-control and population-based datasets of European ancestry from the United States: the NEIGHBOR study, the Nurses' Health Study, the Health Professionals Follow-up Study, the Women's Genome Health Study, the Ocular Hypertension Treatment Study, and collections from Iowa, Marshfield and the Massachusetts Eye and Ear Infirmary. Cases in all datasets were defined by a harmonised glaucoma definition.

label: New England Lung Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of lung cancer, based at Dartmouth College, among residents of northern and central New Hampshire counties and the bordering region of Vermont, United States, in which cases of histologically confirmed primary incident lung cancer were identified from 2005 to 2007 through the New Hampshire State Cancer Registry and the Dartmouth-Hitchcock Medical Center Tumor Registry, and controls identified from a commercial database were matched to them on five-year age group, sex and county.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to arsenic in water via ingestion (ECTO:0080000)

label: Netherlands Mental Health Survey and Incidence Study
other synonyms: NEMESIS-Study
definition: A psychiatric epidemiological population study of non-institutionalised Dutch adults, conducted by the Trimbos Institute in Utrecht, that interviews representative samples drawn by multistage, stratified random sampling (NEMESIS-1 from 1996 and NEMESIS-2 from 2007, aged 18-64, the latter with DNA from saliva, and NEMESIS-3 from 2019, aged 18-75) with the Composite International Diagnostic Interview and follows them up to determine the prevalence, incidence, course and consequences of mental disorders.

label: National Emphysema Treatment Trial
definition: A multicentre randomised clinical trial in the United States that compared medical therapy, including pulmonary rehabilitation, with medical therapy plus lung-volume-reduction surgery in former smokers with severe bilateral emphysema and severe airflow obstruction, with survival as its primary outcome.

label: Neuss bladder cancer study
other synonyms: The Neuss Bladder Cancer Study
definition: An ongoing hospital-based case-control study of urinary bladder cancer at the Department of Urology of the Lukasklinik Neuss, Germany, about 20 km from the Ruhr area, which from June 2009 collected bladder cancer patients, with tumour stage and grade from the cancer registry, and cancer-free controls.

label: Newfoundland Osteoarthritis Study
definition: A study initiated in 2011 that consecutively recruited, until 2017, patients undergoing total knee or hip replacement, largely for osteoarthritis, at St. Clare's Mercy Hospital and the Health Science Centre General Hospital in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada. It collects blood before surgery and follows the patients up after it, to identify genetic, epigenetic and biochemical markers for osteoarthritis.

label: 1998 Singapore National Health Survey
other synonyms: 1998 Singapore National Health Study|Singapore National Health Survey
definition: A population-based, cross-sectional survey conducted between September and November 1998 of Chinese, Malay and Asian Indian Singapore residents aged 18-69, based on the World Health Organization model for field surveys of diabetes and other noncommunicable diseases and the WHO MONICA protocol, with interviewer-administered questionnaires, anthropometric and blood pressure measurements and fasting blood samples.

label: Nurses' Health Study advanced adenoma set
other synonyms: NHS (Advanced Adenoma)|Nurses Health Study, Adenoma Set
definition: The advanced colorectal adenoma case-control sample of the Nurses' Health Study, United States, genotyped for the Genetics and Epidemiology of Colorectal Cancer Consortium: participants with an advanced adenoma (1 cm or larger, or with tubulovillous or villous histology, high-grade dysplasia or carcinoma in situ) confirmed by medical record review, matched to participants who had a lower endoscopy in the same period without an adenoma on year of birth, date of blood sampling, reason for the endoscopy and timing of any prior endoscopy.

label: Clalit National Israeli Cancer Control Center lung cancer study
other synonyms: Clalit National Israeli Cancer Control Center- lung cancer study|Israel Lung Cancer Study
definition: An ongoing population-based case-control study of lung cancer in Israel, run since 2005 by the Clalit National Israeli Cancer Control Center with Carmel Medical Center and the Technion, of newly diagnosed lung cancer cases of any histology and controls matched to them on age, sex and ethnicity, all interviewed face to face and giving a blood sample, with histology, tumour blocks and clinical follow-up available for most cases.

label: Norfolk Island Health Study
other synonyms: Norfolk Island Cohort|Norfolk Island Health study|Norfolk Island cohort
definition: A population-based study established in 2000 of volunteers from Norfolk Island, a genetic isolate descended from a small admixed founder group of European and Polynesian ancestry, with questionnaires on lifestyle, medical and family history, anthropometric measurements, blood samples and a reconstructed multi-generational pedigree, to investigate genetic risk factors for complex diseases such as cardiovascular disease.

label: Pritzker Neuropsychiatric Disorders Research Consortium
other synonyms: NIMH RGR Bipolar Study 2 (Pritzker)
definition: A case–control sample for genome-wide association studies of bipolar disorder in the United States, assembled by the Pritzker Neuropsychiatric Disorders Research Consortium: its cases, of non-Ashkenazi European origin with bipolar I disorder, came from the NIMH Human Genetics Initiative repository, selected where possible as pairs of affected siblings from families collected in its multicentre bipolar family study, and from the University of Michigan Prechter Bipolar Genetics Repository; its controls came from the NIMH repository and reported no diagnosis of or treatment for bipolar disorder or schizophrenia and said they had not heard voices that others could not hear, with suspected major depression excluded. It is one of the bipolar disorder samples of the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium.

label: Upper Midwest Health Study
other synonyms: NIOSH Upper Midwest Health Study|National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health Upper Midwest Health Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of primary intracranial glioma, initiated in 1995 by the US National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health among adults aged 18 to 80 living in non-metropolitan counties of Iowa, Michigan, Minnesota and Wisconsin, to evaluate associations of glioma with farm and rural exposures, pesticides above all. Its cases had histologically confirmed glioma diagnosed from January 1995 to January 1997, and its controls, frequency-matched within state, were drawn from driver's licence and identification records (ages 18–64) and Medicare data (ages 65–80); its participants' DNA was later genotyped in National Cancer Institute genome-wide studies of glioma and of clonal mosaicism.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to pesticide (ECTO:0000530)

label: NIPT PLUS cohort
other synonyms: NIPT PLUS pregnancy cohort|Shenzhen Maternal and Neonatal NIPT PLUS cohort
definition: A cohort of pregnant women recruited in 2020 and 2021 through the pregnancy screening programme of Shenzhen Baoan Women's and Children's Hospital in Shenzhen, China, whose non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) was sequenced at greater depth than conventional NIPT, and whose genotypes and hospital records are used to replicate and validate genetic studies of pregnancy traits such as platelet counts, gestational thrombocytopenia and gestational diabetes.

label: New Jersey Ovarian Cancer Study
other synonyms: NJ Ovarian Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of epithelial ovarian cancer in New Jersey, United States, run by the Cancer Institute of New Jersey, whose cases were women with newly diagnosed invasive epithelial ovarian cancer living in six New Jersey counties, identified from January 2004 to May 2008 through the New Jersey State Cancer Registry, and whose controls were those of the EDGE (Estrogen, Diet, Genetics, and Endometrial Cancer) Study. It was designed to study phytoestrogens and ovarian cancer risk and is one of the studies of the Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium (study code NJO).
exposures: designed to study: exposure to phytoestrogen (ECTO:9002037)

label: Nanjing colorectal cancer GWAS
other synonyms: Nanjing CRC GWAS|Nanjing GWAS|Nanjing Study|Nanjing-1
definition: A case-control sample of Han Chinese adults assembled by Nanjing Medical University in Nanjing, China, for genome-wide association studies of colorectal cancer, whose cases are patients with colorectal cancer recruited at the Cancer Center of Nanjing Medical University from September 2010 and whose cancer-free controls come from the same districts of Nanjing.

label: NL4
other synonyms: Project Mine (Netherlands NL4 controls)|cohort NL4
definition: A case-control cohort from the population-based registry of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in the Netherlands, one of the cohorts of the international ALS genome-wide association study linked to Project MinE, whose cases have probable or definite ALS diagnosed by neurologists at the tertiary referral centres University Medical Center Utrecht, Academic Medical Centre Amsterdam and Radboud University Medical Center Nijmegen, and whose controls, free of neuromuscular disease and matched for age, sex and ethnicity, were ascertained through a population-based study of ALS in the Netherlands. Its genotyped controls have been reused as a Dutch control group in other genetic association studies.

label: Nijmegen Lung and Bladder Cancer sample
other synonyms: Nijmegen Lung and Bladder Cancer
definition: A Dutch sample of three groups from Nijmegen, the Netherlands: population controls from the Nijmegen Biomedical Study, patients with urinary bladder cancer recruited for the Nijmegen Bladder Cancer Study, and patients with lung cancer identified through the population-based cancer registry of the Comprehensive Cancer Center IKO and recruited for a study of gene–environment interactions in lung cancer; it was one of the samples of the ENGAGE consortium's genome-wide association analysis of the number of cigarettes smoked per day.
diseases: patients with: lung cancer (MONDO:0008903)|patients with: urinary bladder cancer (MONDO:0001187)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to Cigarette Smoking (ECTO:6000038)

label: Nijmegen Lung Cancer Study
other synonyms: The Nijmegen Lung Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of lung cancer run by Radboud University Medical Centre in Nijmegen, the Netherlands, to study gene-environment interactions. Its cases are patients diagnosed with lung cancer since 1989 at Radboud university medical center, Canisius Wilhelmina Hospital in Nijmegen or Rijnstate Hospital in Arnhem, identified through the cancer registry of the Netherlands Comprehensive Cancer Organisation, together with lung cancer cases found among participants of POLYGENE, the Nijmegen Biomedical Study and a Radboudumc urology outpatient study; its cancer-free controls are drawn from the Nijmegen Biomedical Study, a random sample of the general population of Nijmegen.
exposures: designed to study: exposure event (ExO:0000002)

label: Nashville Men's Health Study
definition: A clinic-based study of men aged 40 or older with no previous prostate cancer diagnosis who were scheduled for a diagnostic prostate biopsy at Vanderbilt University Medical Center, the Tennessee Valley Veterans Administration hospital or a large private urology practice in Nashville, Tennessee, United States, recruited from 2002 under a multicentre rapid-recruitment protocol that collects clinical, biological, behavioural and body-measurement data and blood and urine, to study risk factors for prostate cancer, prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia and benign prostatic enlargement.
diseases: patients with: prostate cancer (MONDO:0008315)|patients with: prostate intraepithelial neoplasia (MONDO:0005193)

label: Nijmegen Ovarian Cancer Study
other synonyms: Nijmegen Polygene Study & Nijmegen Biomedical Study|Nijmegen Polygene Study and Nijmegen Biomedical Study
definition: A case-control study of epithelial ovarian cancer in the eastern part of the Netherlands, run by Radboud University Medical Centre in Nijmegen, which draws on the Nijmegen Biomedical Study and the Nijmegen Polygene Study and collects its data by self-completed questionnaire. It is one of the studies of the Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium (study code NTH) and contributes to its pooled epidemiological analyses and genome-wide association studies of ovarian cancer.

label: Nomura Study
other synonyms: Ehime University site|JMGP-Nomura|Nomura Cohort Study|Nomura cohort|Nomura cohort study
definition: A community-based cohort of middle-aged and elderly residents of Nomura town, a largely rural community in Ehime Prefecture, western Japan, recruited through the annual community health check-ups at the Nomura Health and Welfare Center, with a first cohort enrolled in 2002 and a second in 2014 and followed up for mortality; run from Ehime University, it is one of the general-population cohorts of the Japanese Millennium Genome Project.

label: NordicDB
other synonyms: Nordic Control database|Nordic GWAS control database
definition: A database and web portal set up in the Nordic countries that pools genome-wide SNP genotypes of control individuals from Finnish, Swedish and Danish studies, with country-specific allele frequencies, so that genetic association studies in the Nordic countries can use them as shared controls.

label: Nordic Diltiazem Study
other synonyms: Nordic Diltiazem study|Nordic diltiazem intervention study
definition: A prospective, randomised, open, blinded-endpoint multicentre trial started in 1992 that enrolled patients aged 50-74 with primary hypertension and a diastolic blood pressure of 100 mm Hg or more at primary health care centres and hospital hypertension units in Norway and Sweden, and randomly assigned them to diltiazem or to conventional treatment with diuretics, beta-blockers or both, to compare their effects on cardiovascular morbidity and mortality.

label: Norway Lung Cancer Study
definition: A population-based case-control study of non-small cell lung cancer in Western Norway, run by the National Institute of Occupational Health (NIOH) in Oslo within its lung cancer genetics project, whose cases are patients of Norwegian origin with histologically confirmed early-stage non-small cell lung cancer admitted to Haukeland University Hospital in Bergen, and whose healthy controls come from the same region and are frequency-matched to the cases on cumulative smoking; recruitment ran from 1986 to 2005.
diseases: patients with: non-small cell lung carcinoma (MONDO:0005233)

label: North of Scotland Osteoporosis Study
definition: A population-based osteoporosis screening programme of postmenopausal women aged 60-82 at baseline, recruited at centres in Aberdeen and Dingwall in the north of Scotland, who underwent bone mineral density measurement in 2001-2003 and gave questionnaire data and DNA samples.

label: Nottingham Smokers
other synonyms: Nottingham Smokers Study|Nottingham Smokers cohort|Nottingham Smokers study
definition: An ongoing collection, in Nottingham and funded by the University of Nottingham, of smokers of European ancestry over 40 years of age with a smoking history of more than 10 pack-years, whose lung function (FEV1 and FVC) was measured by spirometry at enrolment, before and after bronchodilation, and from which people with asthma were excluded; divided by spirometry into COPD cases and smoking controls, it has served as a follow-up sample in genetic association studies of lung function and COPD.
diseases: at risk of: chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (MONDO:0005002)
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to tobacco smoking (ECTO:6000029)

label: Novartis secukinumab clinical trials
other synonyms: Novartis clinical trials of secukinumab for psoriasis|Novartis secukinumab psoriasis trials|Novartis secukinumab trials cohort
definition: A pooled set of participants with psoriasis from five Novartis clinical trials of secukinumab (CAIN457A2302, CAIN457A2303, CAIN457A2304, CAIN457A2223 and CAIN457A2403), whose anonymized trial data and genotypes, collected by Novartis Pharmaceuticals, are analysed post hoc as a psoriasis-only cohort in genetic studies of psoriasis.

label: NPC Genes, Environment, and EBV study
other synonyms: NPC Genes, Environment, and EBV cohort|NPC genes, environment, and EBV|Nasopharyngeal carcinoma Genes, Environment, and EBV study
definition: A population-based case-control study of nasopharyngeal carcinoma in southern China, in which incident cases aged 20–74 years were recruited from March 2010 to December 2013, and randomly selected population controls from November 2010 to November 2014, among residents of 13 cities and counties of Guangdong Province and Guangxi Autonomous Region, with questionnaires and biospecimens collected to study the independent and interactive roles of genes, environmental exposures and Epstein–Barr virus infection in the disease; it was conducted by Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Karolinska Institutet, Guangxi Medical University and collaborating institutions.
exposures: designed to study: exposure event (ExO:0000002)|designed to study: exposure to human gammaherpesvirus 4 (ECTO:3000273)

label: Nambour Skin Cancer Study
other synonyms: Nambour Skin Cancer Prevention Study|Nambour Study
definition: A prospective community-based cohort of adults aged 20–69 years randomly selected from the electoral roll of the township of Nambour in subtropical Queensland, Australia, begun in 1986 with a survey of skin cancer prevalence and dermatologists' skin examinations; from 1992 to 1996 most participants took part in a randomised trial of daily sunscreen use and beta-carotene supplementation for skin cancer prevention, and the cohort has since been followed for skin cancers, diet and mortality.

label: National Study of Endometrial Cancer Genetics
other synonyms: National Study of Endometrial Cancer|National Study of the Genetics of Endometrial Cancer|UK National Study of Endometrial Cancer Genetics
definition: A UK study of women with histologically confirmed endometrial cancer, identified through collaborating clinicians throughout the United Kingdom, with the help of the National Cancer Research Network, from 2008 to 2013 (avoiding centres that recruited to the SEARCH study) and coordinated from the University of Oxford, to find inherited genetic variants that influence endometrial cancer risk; its cases have been compared with controls from other UK studies, such as the CORGI study and the 1958 Birth Cohort.

label: Network for the Study of Ovarian Dysfunction
Nottingham Sib Pair Asthma study
other synonyms: Nottingham sib pair asthma study
definition: A family-based study of the genetics of asthma in Nottingham, United Kingdom, whose families were recruited on the basis of pairs of siblings affected by asthma and were used in association studies of candidate genes with atopy; its index cases, children with asthma of European ancestry, later served as childhood asthma cases in a genetic study of the 17q21 asthma locus.

label: NSW non-Hodgkin lymphoma study
other synonyms: New South Wales non-Hodgkin Lymphoma study
definition: A population-based case-control study of non-Hodgkin lymphoma in adults aged 20–74 years in New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory, Australia, whose cases were diagnosed in 2000–2001 and identified through the New South Wales or Australian Capital Territory cancer registries (excluding people with HIV infection and transplant recipients), and whose controls were randomly selected from the electoral rolls and frequency-matched on age, sex and state or territory of residence.

label: Northeastern Taiwan Community Medicine Research Cohort
other synonyms: A Cohort Study on Disease Prevention and Health Promotion in Northeastern Region of Taiwan|Northeastern Taiwan community medicine research cohort
definition: A prospective community-based cohort on disease prevention and health promotion, run by the Community Medicine Research Center of Chang Gung Memorial Hospital in Keelung since 2013, that enrols volunteers aged 20 or over living in Keelung City and New Taipei City in northeastern Taiwan through community health outreach sessions with a health examination, questionnaires and biological sampling, and follows them up.

label: National Taiwan University Hospital Diabetes Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of type 2 diabetes in Han Chinese adults in Taiwan, whose cases were patients with type 2 diabetes diagnosed by American Diabetes Association criteria (onset at age 35 or older) recruited from the metabolism clinics of National Taiwan University Hospital, Taipei, and whose controls were people with normal glucose tolerance on a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test recruited from routine health examinations; it was a replication study of the Asian Genetic Epidemiology Network's type 2 diabetes genome-wide meta-analysis.

label: Neocodex–Murcia study
other synonyms: Murcia study|The Neocodex–Murcia study
definition: A Spanish case-control sample for genetic studies of Alzheimer's disease, assembled by the genomics company Neocodex in Seville, whose patients with sporadic Alzheimer's disease were diagnosed with possible or probable disease under NINCDS–ADRDA criteria by neurologists at the Virgen de la Arrixaca University Hospital in Murcia, and whose controls, of unknown cognitive status, came from the Spanish general population.

label: NYU Women's Health Study
other synonyms: NYU Women's health study|New York University Women's Health Study
definition: A prospective cohort of healthy women aged 34–65 years enrolled by New York University between 1985 and 1991 at the Guttman Breast Diagnostic Institute, a breast cancer screening centre in New York City, who gave blood at enrolment and at later annual screening visits and have been followed to study hormones, diet, environmental factors and the risk of cancer.

label: New Zealand CAD Study
other synonyms: The New Zealand CAD Study
definition: A case-control sample of patients with angiographically proven coronary artery disease (stenosis of at least 50% of the vessel diameter in at least one coronary artery) from the Otago-Southland region of New Zealand, with age-matched controls from the same region who had no history of ischaemic heart disease, assembled alongside abdominal aortic aneurysm and peripheral arterial disease series from the same region; it served as a replication sample in genetic studies of coronary artery disease.

label: Osaka Acute Coronary Insufficiency Study
definition: A prospective, multicentre observational registry of patients with acute myocardial infarction at 25 collaborating hospitals in the Osaka region of Japan, coordinated from Osaka University Graduate School of Medicine, which since 1998 has recorded demographic, procedural and outcome data and collected blood samples from consecutively enrolled patients to study the treatment and prognosis of acute myocardial infarction.

label: Oulu Breast Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based breast cancer case-control study of the University of Oulu and Oulu University Hospital, Finland, whose cases are breast cancer patients from Northern Finland, unselected for age and family history, collected at Oulu University Hospital from 2000 onwards, and whose controls are healthy female blood donors of the Finnish Red Cross from the Oulu area; it studies inherited susceptibility to breast cancer and contributes to the Breast Cancer Association Consortium.

label: Ohio Colorectal Cancer Prevention Initiative
definition: A prospective statewide study of adults who underwent surgical resection for primary invasive colorectal cancer at 51 hospitals across Ohio, United States, enrolled from 2013 to 2016, in which every tumour was screened for mismatch-repair deficiency and those meeting high-risk criteria (mismatch-repair deficiency, diagnosis before 50, multiple primary tumours or an affected first-degree relative) had multigene germline panel testing, to identify Lynch syndrome and other hereditary cancer syndromes.

label: Ontario Cancer Genetics Network
definition: A study of the Ontario Cancer Genetics Network, a Cancer Care Ontario-funded research network based at the Lunenfeld-Tanenbaum Research Institute of Mount Sinai Hospital in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, that contributes carriers of pathogenic BRCA1 and BRCA2 variants and their data to the Consortium of Investigators of Modifiers of BRCA1/2 (CIMBA) for studies of genetic modifiers of cancer risk.
diseases: at risk of: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|at risk of: ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170)

label: Ontario Familial Colorectal Cancer Registry
other synonyms: Ontario Familial Colon Cancer Registry|Ontario Registry for Studies of Familial Colorectal Cancer
definition: A population-based familial colorectal cancer registry in Ontario, Canada, one of the sites of the US National Cancer Institute's Colon Cancer Family Registry, which recruited people aged 20 to 74 with colorectal cancer diagnosed from July 1997 to June 2000, identified through the Ontario Cancer Registry, and population controls randomly sampled from Ontario residents and frequency-matched to the cases by sex and five-year age group, who completed family-history, epidemiologic and food questionnaires and gave blood samples.

label: Ogliastra Genetic Park
other synonyms: Ogliastra Genetic Park Study
definition: A population-based study of a genetic isolate in the Ogliastra region of Sardinia, Italy, in which the inhabitants of ten villages (Baunei, Escalaplano, Loceri, Perdasdefogu, Seui, Seulo, Talana, Triei, Urzulei and Ussassai), invited by public proclamations and letters to every family, took part from 2002 to 2008 in a cross-sectional epidemiological survey with blood sampling and extended pedigrees, to study the genetic and environmental determinants of complex traits.

label: Ottawa Heart Genomics Study
other synonyms: Ottawa Heart Genomic Study|Ottawa Heart Study
definition: A case-control study of coronary artery disease at the University of Ottawa Heart Institute, Ottawa, Canada, that recruited people of European ancestry without diabetes, with cases defined by more than 50% stenosis of a major coronary artery at angiography, myocardial infarction or coronary revascularisation, and controls who were either angiographically free of coronary disease or elderly and asymptomatic, genotyped in several phases for genome-wide association studies of coronary artery disease.

label: Ocular Hypertension Treatment Study
definition: A multicentre randomised clinical trial at 22 clinical centres in the United States that from 1994 to 1996 enrolled people aged 40 to 80 with ocular hypertension and no evidence of glaucomatous damage, randomised them to topical ocular hypotensive medication or close observation, and followed them for the onset of primary open-angle glaucoma.

label: Osaka-Midosuji Rotary Club
other synonyms: Midosuji Rotary Club
definition: A collection of DNA samples donated by healthy Japanese volunteers who were members of the Rotary Club of Osaka-Midosuji (Rotary International District 2660) in Osaka, Japan, used as controls in genome-wide association studies of the Japanese population, often together with BioBank Japan participants.

label: Oregon Ovarian Cancer Registry
other synonyms: Oregon Ovarian Cancer Registry and Tissue Repository
definition: An ovarian cancer registry and tissue repository at Oregon Health & Science University in Portland, Oregon, USA, which collects ovarian and fallopian tube tissue, blood samples and clinical information, and whose case-only series of women with ovarian cancer, enrolled from 2007 onwards, takes part in the Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium under the study code ORE.

label: Omaha Osteoporosis Study
other synonyms: Omaha osteoporosis study
definition: A cross-sectional study of osteoporosis and related traits in randomly recruited, healthy adult Caucasians living in Omaha, Nebraska, United States, and its surrounding areas, screened by exclusion criteria for chronic and metabolic diseases, with bone mineral density and body composition measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry. Its unrelated genotyped members formed genome-wide association samples for obesity-related traits.

label: Ovarian Cancer Prognosis and Lifestyle Study
other synonyms: OPAL Study|Ovarian cancer Prognosis And Lifestyle Study|Ovarian cancer Prognosis And Lifestyle study|Ovarian cancer Prognosis and Lifestyle study
definition: A national prospective population-based cohort of Australian women diagnosed with histologically confirmed invasive epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal or fallopian tube cancer from 2012 to 2015, run from QIMR Berghofer Medical Research Institute in Brisbane, who completed questionnaires at recruitment and repeatedly during follow-up and whose medical records were abstracted, to study how lifestyle factors relate to outcomes after an ovarian cancer diagnosis.
diseases: patients with: fallopian tube cancer (MONDO:0002158)|patients with: ovarian carcinoma (MONDO:0005140)|patients with: primary peritoneal carcinoma (MONDO:0015686)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to lifestyle (ECTO:6000015)

label: Orofacial Pain: Prospective Evaluation and Risk Assessment
other synonyms: OPPERA study|Orofacial Pain Prospective Evaluation and Risk Assessment|Prospective Evaluation and Risk Assessment
definition: A multicentre study of temporomandibular disorder (TMD) that from 2006 recruited community volunteers aged 18 to 44 years in and around four US academic health centres (in Baltimore, Buffalo, Chapel Hill and Gainesville) into a prospective cohort of people free of TMD, followed for first-onset TMD, and a baseline case-control study comparing people with chronic TMD with controls drawn from the cohort, to identify risk factors for TMD pain.
diseases: population study of: temporomandibular joint disorder (MONDO:0005473)

label: IARC Oral Cancer Multicenter study
other synonyms: IARC - oral cancer|IARC ORC multicenter study|IARC oral cancer
definition: An international hospital-based case–control study of cancer of the oral cavity and oropharynx, coordinated by the International Agency for Research on Cancer in nine countries (Italy, Spain, Northern Ireland, Poland, Canada, India, Sudan, Australia and Cuba), which interviewed its participants and collected oral exfoliated cells and blood from cases and controls, and fresh tumour biopsies from cases, to study the role of human papillomavirus in these cancers. It is one of the studies of the International Head and Neck Cancer Epidemiology Consortium, and participants from its centres in Canada, Italy, Poland and Spain were genotyped for a genome-wide association study of oral cavity and pharyngeal cancer.
diseases: patients with: oral cavity cancer (MONDO:0005515)|patients with: oropharynx cancer (MONDO:0004608)

label: Oregon Sudden Unexpected Death Study
other synonyms: Oregon-Sudden Unexpected Death Study
definition: An ongoing prospective community-based study of out-of-hospital sudden cardiac arrest and sudden cardiac death in the Portland, Oregon metropolitan area (including Multnomah County), United States, running since 2002, which ascertains cases through first responders, emergency medical services, area hospitals and the county medical examiner, reviews their medical records, and compares them with geographically matched controls, including people with coronary artery disease, some of them with blood samples for genetic studies.

label: Leiden University Medical Centre Breast Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of breast cancer in the south-west of the Netherlands, run from Leiden University Medical Centre, whose cases were consecutive patients with invasive or in situ breast cancer diagnosed in 1996–2006 at two hospitals in Leiden and Rotterdam, not selected for family history, and whose controls were healthy blood-bank donors, spouses of members of families at high breast cancer risk, and women tested at the local clinical genetics department for non-cancer conditions; it is a member study of the Breast Cancer Association Consortium.

label: The Stefanie Spielman Breast Bank and the Columbus Area Control Sample Bank
other synonyms: OSU study
definition: A breast cancer case-control study at The Ohio State University in Columbus, Ohio, whose cases are incident triple-negative breast cancer cases enrolled at the Ohio State University James Comprehensive Cancer Center from 2003 to 2011 and banked in the Stefanie Spielman Breast Bank, and whose controls, recruited from 2007 to 2011 among people seen for routine care at primary care and internal medicine clinics and frequency matched to the cases on age and ethnicity, come from the Columbus Area Control Sample Bank. It took part in the Triple Negative Breast Cancer Consortium and, through it, in Breast Cancer Association Consortium analyses.

label: Osteoporosis and Ultrasound Study
other synonyms: OPUS Study|OPUS study|osteoporosis and ultrasound study
definition: A multicentre, population-based prospective study of risk factors for osteoporotic fracture in which women aged over 55 years (with a group of younger women aged 20 to 39 years) were recruited from random population samples at five European centres (Aberdeen, Berlin, Kiel, Paris and Sheffield) between 1999 and 2001 and followed for about six years, with bone densitometry, quantitative ultrasound of bone, spine radiographs and bone turnover markers.
diseases: population study of: bone fracture (MONDO:0005315)|population study of: osteoporosis (MONDO:0005298)

label: Ovarian Cancer in Alberta and British Columbia Study
other synonyms: Ovarian Cancer in Alberta and British Columbia
definition: A population-based case-control study of ovarian cancer in the Canadian provinces of British Columbia and Alberta, running from 2002 to 2012, whose British Columbia cases were identified through the British Columbia Cancer Registry and controls through the provincial health roster, with data collected by self-completed questionnaire from 2002 to 2004 and by interview from 2004 to 2012. It is one of the studies of the Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium.

label: OVCARE Gynecologic Tissue Bank and Outcomes Unit
other synonyms: OVCARE Gyneacologic Tissue Bank and Outcomes Unit
definition: A gynaecological tissue bank and outcomes unit of British Columbia's Ovarian Cancer Research (OVCARE) program at Vancouver General Hospital and the BC Cancer Agency in Vancouver, Canada, which recruits patients, banks their biospecimens and maintains their clinical data; its ovarian cancer patients take part in the Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium, including its studies of ovarian cancer survival, under the study code VAN.

label: Oxford Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Study
other synonyms: Multimodal Assessment of Aortic Aneurysm Disease Pathogenesis
definition: A single-centre prospective cohort of patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm managed on the routine NHS pathway at the Oxford University Hospitals NHS Trust in England, followed with repeated measurements of aneurysm diameter to study the pathogenesis and growth of aneurysms and biomarkers of their progression such as flow-mediated dilatation.

label: Oxford Endometriosis Gene Study
other synonyms: OXEGENE study|Oxford Endometriosis Gene|Oxford Endometriosis Gene study
definition: A United Kingdom-based international genetic study of endometriosis, run from the University of Oxford, that from 1995 to 2006 recruited women with surgically confirmed endometriosis, both families with two or more affected sisters and single cases, through collaborating clinicians in Britain, Ireland and the United States, advertisements and its website, to identify susceptibility genes by linkage analysis and positional cloning; with the Australian Genes Behind Endometriosis Study it forms the International Endogene Study.

label: Progression to insulin deficiency: South West England cohort
other synonyms: Progression to Insulin Deficiency: South West England Cohort|South West UK cohort
definition: A cross-sectional cohort of white European adults from Devon and Cornwall in South West England who were diagnosed with diabetes between the ages of 20 and 40 and had had it for more than three years, excluding known monogenic and secondary diabetes, assembled by researchers at the University of Exeter to test whether a type 1 diabetes genetic risk score predicts progression to severe insulin deficiency (continuous insulin treatment within three years of diagnosis with low C-peptide).

label: Pancreatic Cancer: Investigation into Finding Causes Study
other synonyms: PACIFIC Study|PACIFIC Study of Group Health and Northern California Kaiser Permanente|Pacific Study|Pancreatic Cancer Investigation: Finding Causes|Pancreatic Cancer: Investigation into Finding Causes
definition: A case-control study of pancreatic cancer among members of two US health plans, Group Health in the Seattle Puget Sound area of Washington and Kaiser Permanente Northern California. It is one of the case-control studies of the Pancreatic Cancer Case-Control Consortium (PanC4) whose samples were genotyped in the PanScan genome-wide association studies.

label: Multicenter Japanese paroxysmal atrial fibrillation case-control cohort
definition: A multicentre case-control study of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation in Japan, whose cases with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and unrelated controls with no history of atrial fibrillation, all Japanese inpatients and outpatients of the cardiology departments of seven hospitals (among them Tokyo Medical and Dental University Hospital and Jichi Medical University Hospital), were enrolled from March 2020 to December 2021 and genotyped for a genome-wide association study and polygenic risk scores of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

label: PANcreatic Disease ReseArch consortium
other synonyms: PANDORA Consortium|PANDoRA consortium|PANcreatic Disease ReseArch (PANDoRA) consortium|Pancreatic disease research consortium
definition: A case-control consortium of basic and clinical research groups that pools biological samples and data from patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma and other pancreatic diseases (endocrine pancreatic tumours, chronic pancreatitis) and from healthy controls, collected mainly in European countries and also in Brazil and Japan, to find genetic factors for pancreatic cancer risk, response to treatment and survival.
diseases: patients with: chronic pancreatitis (MONDO:0005003)|patients with: pancreatic adenocarcinoma (MONDO:0006047)|patients with: pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasm (MONDO:0005815)

label: Multicentre Prospective Study on the Role of KRAS and other Genetic Alterations in the Diagnosis, Prognosis and Etiology of Pancreatic Cancer
other synonyms: PANKRAS II Study|Spanish Pancreatic Cancer Study
definition: A multicentre prospective hospital-based study of patients with pancreatic and biliary diseases, among them incident cases of exocrine pancreatic cancer, recruited from 1992 to 1995 at five general university hospitals in eastern Spain and followed for survival, to study the role of KRAS mutations and other genetic alterations, and of environmental exposures such as persistent organic pollutants and trace elements, in the diagnosis, prognosis and aetiology of pancreatic cancer.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to chemical (ECTO:0000231)|designed to study: exposure to persistent organic pollutant (ECTO:9002053)

label: Pharmacogenomics and Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Study
other synonyms: Pharmacogenomics and Risk of Cardiovascular Disease study
definition: A pharmacogenomic study of the response to statins that combines two clinical populations of white adults in the United States given a statin for a fixed period: participants of the Cholesterol and Atherosclerosis Pharmacogenetics (CAP) study, recruited at two clinical sites in Los Angeles and San Francisco and treated with simvastatin for six weeks, and participants of the Pravastatin Inflammation CRP Evaluation (PRINCE) trial, enrolled at sites across the country and treated with pravastatin for twelve weeks.

label: Parkinson's, Genes, and Environment Study
other synonyms: Parkinson's Genes and Environment Study|Parkinson's, Genes and Environment study|Parkinson's, Genes, and Environment|Parkinson, Genes, and Environment|Parkinsons, Genes and Environment
definition: A case-control study of Parkinson's disease nested in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study, the prospective cohort established by the National Cancer Institute in 1995–1996, whose cases are cohort members who reported Parkinson's disease in the cohort's 2004–2006 follow-up survey and were confirmed by their treating physicians or by medical record review, and whose controls are randomly selected cohort members who did not report Parkinson's disease, frequency-matched to the cases on year of birth, sex and ethnicity, with DNA collected from saliva.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to caffeine via ingestion (ECTO:0900049)|designed to study: exposure to smoking (ECTO:6000013)

label: Norwegian ParkWest Study
other synonyms: Parkwest
definition: A population-based longitudinal study of the incidence, neurobiology and prognosis of Parkinson’s disease in Norway, which recruited incident, untreated patients with Parkinson’s disease and control participants and follows them with a standardised examination programme; its patients contribute to genetic studies of Parkinson’s disease progression.

label: Predictive Values of Blood Pressure and Arterial Stiffness in Institutionalized Very Aged Population Study
other synonyms: PARTAGE study|Predictive Values of Blood Pressure and Arterial Stiffness in Institutionalized Very Aged Population|Predictive Values of Blood Pressure and Arterial Stiffness in Institutionalized Very Aged Population (PARTAGE) Study
definition: An observational cohort of people aged 80 years or older living in 72 nursing homes in France and Italy, recruited between January 2006 and June 2008 by four French and two Italian university hospital centres and followed for two years, to determine how well blood pressure and arterial stiffness predict mortality and major cardiovascular events in very old institutionalised people.

label: Canary Prostate Active Surveillance Study
other synonyms: Canary PASS|Prostate Active Surveillance Study
definition: A multi-institutional prospective cohort and biorepository of men with clinically localized prostate cancer managed by active surveillance, enrolled from 2008 at clinical sites in the United States and Canada and followed under a protocol of regular prostate-specific antigen tests and surveillance biopsies, supported by the Canary Foundation to discover and confirm biomarkers that distinguish aggressive from indolent disease.

label: Pathways Study
other synonyms: Pathways study
definition: A prospective cohort of women aged 21 or older newly diagnosed with invasive breast cancer at Kaiser Permanente Northern California, in the United States, recruited from January 2006 within two months of diagnosis, interviewed and sampled for blood and saliva at baseline and followed for recurrence and survival, to study how lifestyle and molecular factors affect breast cancer prognosis.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to Physical Activity (ECTO:6000039)|designed to study: exposure to eating behavior (ECTO:6000021)

label: North Carolina-Louisiana Prostate Cancer Project
other synonyms: North Carolina - Louisiana Prostate Cancer Project|North Carolina-Louisiana Prostate Cancer Project Consortium|North Carolina-Louisiana Prostate Cancer Study
definition: A population-based, case-only study of African American and European American men aged 40 to 79 with newly diagnosed prostate cancer in North Carolina and Louisiana, United States, who were interviewed at home and gave blood, adipose tissue, urine and toenail samples, with medical records and tumour tissue reviewed, to investigate the social, individual and tumour-level causes of racial differences in prostate cancer aggressiveness.

label: Prostate Cancer in a Black Population
definition: A nationwide population-based case-control study of prostate cancer in Barbados, West Indies, whose cases were male citizens with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed prostate cancer identified from July 2002 to January 2011 and whose controls were age-matched residents randomly selected from a national database, designed to evaluate genetic and epidemiologic contributors to prostate cancer in this Afro-Caribbean population.

label: Prostate Cancer study Medical University Sofia
other synonyms: Prostate Cancer Study Medical University Sofia
definition: A hospital-based case–control study of prostate cancer in Sofia, Bulgaria, run by the Medical University of Sofia, whose cases are patients of the Clinic of Urology of Alexandrovska University Hospital with histopathologically confirmed prostate cancer and whose controls are patients with benign prostatic hyperplasia and low PSA and healthy men from the MMC Biobank; it contributes genotyped cases and controls to the PRACTICAL consortium.

label: Prostate Cancer Prevention Trial
definition: A phase 3 randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, administered through the Southwest Oncology Group, in which generally healthy men aged 55 or older with a normal digital rectal examination and a PSA level of 3 ng/mL or less, recruited at sites across the United States and Canada from 1994 to 1997, were assigned to finasteride (5 mg a day) or placebo for seven years and offered an end-of-study prostate biopsy, to test whether finasteride prevents prostate cancer.

label: Pathobiological Determinants of Atherosclerosis in Youth
definition: A multi-institutional autopsy study, sponsored by the US National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, in which fifteen cooperating centres in eight US communities used standardised procedures to collect arteries, blood and other tissues from black and white males and females aged 15 to 34 who died of external causes (accidents, homicides and suicides) and were autopsied between 1987 and 1994, to relate established coronary heart disease risk factors to the extent of atherosclerotic lesions in youth.

label: French Parkinson's Disease Genetics Study Group
other synonyms: French Parkinson disease Genetics Study Group|French network for the study of Parkinson disease genetics|French network for the study of Parkinson's disease genetics|Study of Parkinsons disease Genetics
definition: A French network for the study of Parkinson's disease genetics, associating university hospitals across France, through which patients with Parkinson's disease of European origin, including early-onset index cases, and some healthy controls are recruited for genetic studies, with samples prepared by the DNA and cell bank of the CRicm in Paris.

label: PEAK-25
other synonyms: PEAK Bone Mass 25 study|PEAK25 Swedish Study
definition: A longitudinal, prospective, population-based cohort of young-adult women from Malmö, Sweden, who were invited in 1999–2004 at the age of 25 (excluding women pregnant then or in the previous 12 months) and invited again about ten years later at age 35, set up to explore the genetic, clinical and lifestyle factors associated with attaining peak bone mass and with later changes in bone mass, with bone density and body composition measured by DXA.

label: Polish Endometrial Cancer Study
other synonyms: Polish Endometrial Cancer study
definition: A population-based case-control study of endometrial cancer, the endometrial component of the US National Cancer Institute's Polish Cancer Study, that in 2001–2003 enrolled women aged 20–74 years in Warsaw and Łódź, Poland: cases with incident, pathologically confirmed endometrial cancer identified through a rapid hospital-based identification system and cancer registries, and controls selected from the Polish Electronic System and frequency-matched on site and age, all interviewed in person and giving blood samples.

label: Prevention of Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Prior Heart Attack Using Ticagrelor Compared to Placebo on a Background of Aspirin-Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction 54
other synonyms: Prevention of Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Prior Heart Attack Using Ticagrelor Compared to Placebo on a Background of Aspirin|Prevention of Cardiovascular Events in Patients with Prior Heart Attack Using Ticagrelor Compared to Placebo on a Background of Aspirin|Prevention of Cardiovascular Events in Patients with Prior Heart Attack Using Ticagrelor Compared to Placebo on a Background of Aspirin-Thrombolysis In Myocardial Infarction 54
definition: A multinational, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial that recruited patients with a spontaneous myocardial infarction one to three years earlier and additional risk factors from October 2010 to April 2013 and assigned them to ticagrelor 90 mg or 60 mg twice daily or matching placebo, all on low-dose aspirin, to test whether long-term ticagrelor reduces cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or stroke.

label: Peru Genetics and Genomics of Breast Cancer Study
other synonyms: Peruvian Genetics and Genomics of Breast Cancer|Peruvian Genetics and Genomics of Breast Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based cohort of women diagnosed with invasive breast cancer in 2010 or later at ages 21 to 79 and recruited at the Instituto Nacional de Enfermedades Neoplásicas (INEN) in Lima, Peru, who complete a standardised survey and give a blood sample for genotyping, with tumour subtypes from pathology at INEN, used to study genetic ancestry and other factors in breast cancer among Peruvian women.

label: Proyecto Genes Candidatos en Asma
definition: A population-based study run by the Institute for Immunological Research of the University of Cartagena, Colombia, to identify environmental and genetic risk factors for asthma and allergies, which recruited unrelated people with asthma, diagnosed by GINA criteria with a standardised questionnaire and confirmed by a study physician from the clinical history and reversible airway obstruction on lung function testing, and unrelated controls without a personal or family history of asthma or allergies from the Social Security Clinic and outpatient health centres in Cartagena from 2002 to 2005, together with nuclear and extended families recruited through asthmatic probands. It is one of the asthma genetics studies of the Consortium on Asthma among African-ancestry Populations in the Americas (CAAPA).
exposures: designed to study: exposure event (ExO:0000002)

label: Genome Wide Association Study in Familial Parkinson Disease
other synonyms: CIDR: Genome Wide Association Study in Familial Parkinson Disease (PD)
definition: A genome-wide association sample of familial Parkinson's disease that combines unrelated cases, one per multiplex family, from two familial Parkinson's disease studies, PROGENI and GenePD, diagnosed by modified UK Parkinson's Disease Society Brain Bank criteria and primarily Caucasian and non-Hispanic, with Caucasian non-Hispanic controls without neurological disease from the NINDS repository at the Coriell Institute, genotyped at the Center for Inherited Disease Research to find genetic risk factors for Parkinson's disease.

label: Pharmacogenetics of Acute Coronary Syndrome
other synonyms: Pharmacogenetics of Acute Coronary Syndrome study
definition: A UK multicentre prospective observational cohort of patients hospitalised with a non-ST elevation acute coronary syndrome (non-ST elevation myocardial infarction or unstable angina), run at 16 hospital sites between 2008 and 2013, whose participants were followed up at one and 12 months, and annually thereafter while the study ran, for further cardiovascular events; its medication, adherence, plasma drug-level and genome-wide genotype data are used in pharmacogenetic studies of secondary-prevention cardiovascular drugs.

label: PHArmacogenetic study of Statins in the Elderly at risk
other synonyms: PHArmacogenetic study of Statin in the Elderly at risk|PHArmacogenomic study of Statins in the Elderly at risk for CHD|PHArmacogenomic study of Statins in the Elderly at risk for cardiovascular disease
definition: A genome-wide association study within the Prospective Study of Pravastatin in the Elderly at Risk (PROSPER), a trial of pravastatin in men and women aged 70 to 82 screened in Scotland, Ireland and the Netherlands from 1997 to 1999, in which the trial's participants were genotyped genome-wide to find the genetic variation responsible for individual differences in response to pravastatin; it was funded by the European Union's Seventh Framework Programme.

label: Philadelphia Cohort
other synonyms: Philadelphia cohort
definition: A case–control collection of people with epilepsy and controls of African-American and European-American ancestry, assembled in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States, with approval from the review boards of Thomas Jefferson University Hospital, the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, the University of Pennsylvania and other centres in the United States and Canada, genotyped on Illumina arrays and contributed to the genome-wide association meta-analyses of the ILAE Consortium on Complex Epilepsies.

label: Pisa Breast Cancer Study
other synonyms: Universita di Pisa|Università di Pisa
definition: A study of women carrying pathogenic BRCA1 or BRCA2 variants, run at the University of Pisa and its hospital (Azienda Ospedaliera Pisana) in Pisa, Italy, that contributes its carriers to the Consortium of Investigators of Modifiers of BRCA1/2 (CIMBA).
diseases: at risk of: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|at risk of: ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170)

label: Portuguese Island Collection
other synonyms: Portuguese island collection
definition: A collection of individuals and multiplex families with schizophrenia and/or bipolar disorder, with psychiatrically screened controls, sampled from the founder population of the Azores and Madeira archipelagos of Portugal through all the islands' psychiatric and general hospitals, taking families only if the proband's parents and four grandparents were native to the islands, with further families from mainland Portugal identified through the University of Coimbra and participants from the first- and second-generation Portuguese immigrant population of the United States; it was used in linkage and association studies of psychosis and became part of the Genomic Psychiatry Cohort.
diseases: patients with: bipolar disorder (MONDO:0004985)|patients with: schizophrenia (MONDO:0005090)

label: Parkinsonism: Incidence, Cognition and Non-motor heterogeneity in Cambridgeshire
other synonyms: Parkinsonism: Incidence and Cognitive Heterogeneity in Cambridgeshire|Parkinsonism: Incidence and Cognitive and Non-motor heterogeneity In CambridgeShire|Parkinsonism–Incidence and Cognitive Heterogeneity in Cambridgeshire
definition: A community-based cohort of people newly diagnosed with Parkinson's disease or other parkinsonism in Cambridgeshire, United Kingdom, recruited between 2006 and 2013: incident cases ascertained through general practitioners and hospital specialists between April 2008 and January 2010, in a second incidence study of the same base population as CamPaIGN, supplemented by other newly diagnosed (inception) cases. Participants are followed up every 18 months with motor, cognitive and neuropsychiatric assessments to study the natural history of Parkinson's disease; the study was sponsored by the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Trust.
diseases: patients with: Parkinson disease (MONDO:0005180)|patients with: parkinsonian disorder (MONDO:0021095)

label: Prospective Imaging Study of Ageing: Genes, Brain and Behaviour
other synonyms: Prospective Imaging Study of Ageing|Prospective Imaging Study of Aging
definition: A prospective cohort of healthy midlife and older adults from across Australia, recruited using genetic prediction to be enriched for high and low genetic risk of Alzheimer's disease and followed longitudinally with online surveys and cognitive testing, with at-risk participants and a clinical group of patients with mild cognitive impairment or early Alzheimer's disease invited for neuroimaging, detailed neurocognitive testing and blood sampling, to find the earliest signs and modifiable risk factors of Alzheimer's disease; approved by the ethics committee of QIMR Berghofer Medical Research Institute.

label: Pittsburgh Lung Screening Study
definition: A prospective, Pittsburgh-based cohort of current and former cigarette smokers aged 50-79 (at least half a pack a day for 25 years and, for former smokers, quit within the last 10 years), enrolled in 2002-2005 for computed-tomography lung cancer screening and long-term follow-up.
exposures: participants with exposure: exposure to Cigarette Smoking (ECTO:6000038)

label: Pharmacogenomics of Metformin
other synonyms: Pharmacogenomics of metformin study
definition: A pharmacogenomic study of glycaemic response to metformin and sulfonylureas in adults with type 2 diabetes who are members of Kaiser Permanente in the United States, with drug response defined from HbA1c measurements and prescriptions in electronic health records. Its first cohort, PMET1 (previously named PMT2, from the Pharmacogenomics of Membrane Transporters project of the NIH Pharmacogenomics Research Network), was drawn from the Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging (GERA) cohort of the Kaiser Permanente Research Program on Genes, Environment, and Health in Northern California; Kaiser Permanente Northern California also supplied the phenotype data of a second cohort, PMET2.

label: Postmenopausal Hormones Supplementary Study to the Colon Cancer Family Registry
other synonyms: Hormones and Colon Cancer study|Postmenopausal Hormone Study|Postmenopausal Hormone study
definition: A population-based case-control study of postmenopausal hormone use and colorectal cancer among women aged 50 to 74 in 13 counties of Washington State, United States, whose cases were newly diagnosed with invasive colorectal adenocarcinoma between October 1998 and February 2002 and identified through the SEER cancer registry, and whose controls were randomly selected from driver's licence and Medicare rosters; run as a supplementary study to the Colon Cancer Family Registry.

label: Mount Sinai Hospital-Princess Margaret Multicancer Study
other synonyms: Mount Sinai Hospital-Princess Margaret Hospital Study|Mount Sinai Hospital-Princess Margaret Multicancer study|Mount-Sinai Hospital-Princess Margaret|Mount-Sinai Hospital-Princess Margaret case–control study|Princess Margaret Hospital in Toronto|The Mount-Sinai Hospital-Princess Margaret Study
definition: A hospital-based case–control study of lung and head and neck cancers conducted from 2008 in the Greater Toronto Area, Canada, at Mount Sinai Hospital (Sinai Health System) and Princess Margaret Cancer Centre, in which histologically confirmed cases seen at the hospitals' clinics and controls selected at random from family medicine clinic databases, frequency-matched on age and sex, were interviewed with a standard questionnaire on lifestyle, occupational, medical and family history.
diseases: patients with: head and neck cancer (MONDO:0005627)|patients with: lung cancer (MONDO:0008903)

label: Prospective study of Outcomes in Sporadic versus Hereditary breast cancer
other synonyms: POSH study|Prospective Study of Outcomes in Sporadic Versus Hereditary Breast Cancer|Prospective Study of Outcomes in Sporadic Versus Hereditary Breast Cancer Study|Prospective Study of Outcomes in Sporadic and Hereditary Breast Cancer|Prospective Study of Outcomes in Sporadic versus Hereditary Breast Cancer Study
definition: A prospective cohort of women in the United Kingdom diagnosed with a first primary breast cancer at age 40 or younger, recruited between June 2001 and December 2007 (with an additional category of BRCA1 or BRCA2 carriers diagnosed at 41 to 50), with family history, epidemiological and clinical data and blood collected and annual follow-up, to establish whether genetic status influences breast cancer prognosis independently of known prognostic factors.

label: Prostate Project Foundation - Postgraduate Medical School, Surrey
other synonyms: PPF-Unis / SUN study|Prostate Project Foundation-Postgraduate Medical School, Surrey|Prostate Project Foundation–Postgraduate Medical School, Surrey|SUN study
definition: A hospital-based case–control study of prostate cancer in Surrey, United Kingdom, run with the University of Surrey, in which men with confirmed prostate cancer who presented to two district hospitals (Royal Surrey County Hospital and Frimley Park Hospital) between February 2009 and March 2011 and healthy volunteers with normal PSA gave DNA samples, contributed to the PRACTICAL consortium's iCOGS genotyping.

label: Prostate cAncer Genetics in Galicia
other synonyms: PRostate cAncer Genetics in Galicia|Prostate Cancer Genetics in Galacia
definition: A population-based case-control study of prostate cancer in men of European ancestry in Galicia, Spain, run from the Cancer Genetics Unit of the Vigo University Hospital Complex (CHUVI), with samples from the biobanks of the University Hospital Complexes of Vigo and Santiago de Compostela.

label: Molecular Reclassification to Find Clinically Useful Biomarkers for Systemic Autoimmune Diseases
other synonyms: Molecular Reclassification to Find Clinically Useful Biomarkers for Systemic Autoimmune Diseases: Cross Sectional Cohort|Molecular Reclassification to Find Clinically Useful Biomarkers for Systemic Autoimmune Diseases: Inception Cohort|PRECISESADS cohort|PRECISESADS study|Systemic Autoimmune Diseases: Inception Cohort (PRECISESADSI)
definition: A European multicentre observational study of the PRECISESADS project that recruited adults with systemic autoimmune diseases (rheumatoid arthritis, systemic sclerosis, primary Sjögren's syndrome, systemic lupus erythematosus, primary antiphospholipid syndrome, mixed connective tissue disease and undifferentiated connective tissue disease) and healthy controls at 19 institutions in nine countries between December 2014 and December 2018, in a cross-sectional cohort and a prospective inception cohort, to reclassify these diseases into molecular clusters using omics profiles.
diseases: patients with: Sjogren syndrome (MONDO:0010030)|patients with: mixed connective tissue disease (MONDO:0005854)|patients with: primary antiphospholipid syndrome (MONDO:0005204)|patients with: rheumatoid arthritis (MONDO:0008383)|patients with: systemic lupus erythematosus (MONDO:0007915)|patients with: systemic sclerosis (MONDO:0005100)|patients with: undifferentiated connective tissue syndrome (MONDO:0019527)

label: Evaluation of Predictive Factors Regarding the Effectivity of Aromatase Inhibitor Therapy
other synonyms: Evaluation of PREdictive FACtors Regarding the Effectivity of Aromatase Inhibitor Therapy|Evaluation of Predictive Factors regarding the Effectivity of Aromatase Inhibitor Therapy|PREFACE Trial|PreFace Study|PreFace trial
definition: A prospective, open-label, multicentre phase IV clinical trial in Germany which in 2009-2011 enrolled postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive early breast cancer whose physician had indicated five years of upfront adjuvant letrozole, to evaluate predictive factors of aromatase inhibitor effectiveness, survival and safety, with a biomaterial collection of germline DNA, plasma, serum and tumour tissue.

label: Precision Medicine Platform for Mild Cognitive Impairment Based on Multi-omics, Imaging and Evidence-based Research & Business Development
other synonyms: Establishment of Precision Medicine Platform for Early Diagnosis of Mild Cognitive Impairment|PREMIER Consortium|PREMIER cohort|PREMIER consortium|PREMIER consortium study|PREMIER study|PREMiER study|PREcision medicine platform for mild cognitive impairment on multi-omics, imaging, and evidence-based R&BD|PREcision medicine platform for mild cognitive impairment on multi-omics, imaging, evidence-based R&BD|PRecision mEdicine platform for mild cognitive impairment based on Multi-omics, Imaging, Evidence-based R&BD|Precision Medicine Platform for MCI based on multi-omics, imaging, evidence-based R&BD|Precision Medicine Platform for Mild Cognitive Impairment Based on Multi-omics, Imaging, Evidence-Based R&BD|precision medicine platform for mild cognitive impairment based on multi-omics, imaging, evidence-based R&BD
definition: A multicentre research cohort of the PREMIER consortium, which from 2019 to 2022 enrolled people with mild cognitive impairment, with cognitively unimpaired people and people with Alzheimer's-type or frontotemporal dementia as control groups, from memory clinics, regional dementia centres and hospitals across South Korea, and assessed them with neuropsychological tests, questionnaires, brain MRI, amyloid PET and blood samples (DNA, plasma, serum) to build a platform for the early diagnosis and precision-medicine treatment of mild cognitive impairment and dementia; it is one of the cohorts of K-ROAD.
diseases: patients with: cognitive disorder (MONDO:0002039)|patients with: dementia (MONDO:0001627)

label: Pravastatin Inflammation/CRP Evaluation
other synonyms: PRavastatin Inflammation CRP Evaluation|Pravastatin Inflammation CRP Evaluation study|Pravastatin Inflammation/CRP Evaluation Study|pravastatin inflammation CRP evaluation|pravastatin inflammation/CRP evaluation
definition: An investigator-initiated, multicentre, community-based trial in office-based practices in the United States that from February to December 2000 evaluated the effect of pravastatin 40 mg/d on C-reactive protein: men and women with no prior cardiovascular disease (the primary prevention cohort) were randomly assigned, double-blind, to pravastatin or placebo for 24 weeks, and patients with known cardiovascular disease (the secondary prevention cohort) received open-label pravastatin, with lipid profiles and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein measured at baseline, 12 and 24 weeks. DNA collected from participants was later used in genome-wide studies of the lipid-lowering response to statins.

label: Prospective Atrial Fibrillation Athletic Heart Study
other synonyms: Atrial remodelling and risk of arrhythmias in endurance athletes|ProAFHeart study|Prospective Atrial Fibrillation Athletic Heart
