other synonyms: LifeGene Study|LifeGene cohort|LifeGene study|Swedish LifeGene cohort
definition: A population-based prospective cohort study and research infrastructure in Sweden, run from Karolinska Institutet, that from 2009 to 2016 recruited adults from the general population, mainly in the Stockholm region, with index persons aged 18 to 45 years invited to bring their household members, and collected questionnaires, physical assessments and biological samples with planned repeated follow-up, to study diseases with onset early in life, pregnancy and early-life exposures, and later co-morbidity.

label: SG100K
other synonyms: PRECISE-SG100K|SG100K cohort|SG100K population study
definition: A collection of four longitudinal population health cohorts in Singapore (HELIOS, the Singapore Population Health Studies, the Singapore Epidemiology of Eye Diseases and SingHeart), brought together under an NMRC grant and in partnership with Precision Health Research, Singapore (PRECISE) and the Genome Institute of Singapore in phase II of the National Precision Medicine programme, whose multi-ancestry Asian participants were whole-genome sequenced and linked to electronic health records to study the determinants and prediction of cardiovascular disease and diabetes in Asian populations.
diseases: population study of: cardiovascular disorder (MONDO:0004995)|population study of: diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005015)

label: South African Population Research Infrastructure Network
acronyms: SAPRIN|SAPRIN (South African Population Research Infrastructure Network)
other synonyms: SAPRIN population cohort
definition: A national network, established in 2016 by South Africa's Department of Science and Innovation and hosted by the South African Medical Research Council, that harmonises the longitudinal population surveillance of health and demographic surveillance system (HDSS) nodes in South Africa, starting from the rural Agincourt, DIMAMO and Africa Health Research Institute HDSSs and extending to urban nodes, to provide up-to-date longitudinal health, demographic and socioeconomic data for research and national policy.

label: Lifecourse biological pathways underlying social differences in healthy aging
acronyms: LIFEPATH|LIFEPATH (Lifecourse biological pathways underlying social differences in healthy aging)|Lifepath
other synonyms: LIFEPATH Consortium|LIFEPATH project|Lifepath Consortium
definition: A research consortium funded by the European Commission under Horizon 2020 that pooled and harmonised data from existing adult and child cohort studies in Europe, the USA and Australia, including CoLaus, SKIPOGH, Constances and the Melbourne Collaborative Cohort Study, with biomarker and omics sub-studies, to investigate the biological pathways through which socioeconomic position affects healthy ageing over the life course.

label: Vorarlberg Health Monitoring and Prevention Programme
other synonyms: VHM&PP Study Cohort|Vorarlberg Health Monitoring and Prevention Program|Vorarlberg Health Monitoring and Promotion Program
definition: A population-based cohort of adult residents of Vorarlberg, the westernmost province of Austria, enrolled from 1985 through a routine risk-factor surveillance and prevention programme run by the Agency for Social and Preventive Medicine, in which local physicians carried out a physical examination, blood test and consultation, and followed by linkage to the Vorarlberg cancer registry and death index to study metabolic and other risk factors for cancer, cardiovascular disease and mortality.

label: 45 and Up Study
other synonyms: Sax Institute's 45 and Up Study
definition: A prospective population-based cohort of men and women aged 45 years and over in New South Wales, Australia, randomly sampled from the Medicare enrolment database and recruited by postal questionnaire in 2005–2009 by the Sax Institute, with oversampling of people aged 80 and over and of rural and remote residents, repeated follow-up surveys, biospecimen sub-studies and routine linkage to mortality, hospital, pharmaceutical and other health records, as a resource for research on health and ageing.

label: International Health Cohorts Consortium
other synonyms: International Hundred K+ Cohorts Consortium|International Hundred Thousand Plus Cohort Consortium|International HundredK+ Cohorts Consortium
definition: An international consortium of large population cohorts, established in 2018 to work beyond the constraints of individual health and population cohorts, whose members are chosen for size, longitudinal health follow-up, broad participant selection, biological sample collection and a commitment to data sharing, and which maintains the IHCC Cohort Atlas, a directory of the data its member cohorts hold.

label: Massachusetts General Hospital Premature Coronary Artery Disease Study
other synonyms: MGH Premature Coronary Artery Disease Study|Massachusetts General Hospital Premature Coronary Artery Disease
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of premature coronary artery disease at Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston, United States, with recruitment reported from 1999. Its Myocardial Infarction Genetics Consortium sample comprised men aged 50 or younger and women aged 60 or younger hospitalized with myocardial infarction between 1999 and 2004, with age- and sex-matched controls recruited through newspaper advertisements in Boston and its vicinity who reported no cardiovascular disease or cardiac medication use.

label: Special Turku Coronary Risk Factor Intervention Project, Parents
other synonyms: Special Turku Coronary Risk Factor Intervention Project (STRIP) parents|Special Turku Coronary Risk Factor Intervention Project - Parents|Special Turku Coronary Risk Factor Intervention Project – Parents
definition: The parents of the infants enrolled in the Special Turku Coronary Risk Factor Intervention Project (STRIP) in Turku, Finland, between 1989 and 1992, who enrolled in the trial with their children and contributed as a parent sample to genome-wide studies of blood lipids and anthropometric traits.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to eating behavior (ECTO:6000021)

label: Identification of a risk profile to guide atrial fibrillation therapy
other synonyms: AF Risk study|AF risk profile study|AF-RISK study|AF-Risk study|identification of a risk profile to guide atrial fibrillation therapy
definition: A prospective, observational hospital-based cohort of adults with recent-onset paroxysmal or persistent atrial fibrillation for whom a rhythm-control strategy was preferred, conducted at the University Medical Center Groningen and Maastricht University Medical Center in the Netherlands between 2011 and 2016, with detailed cardiovascular phenotyping and serial rhythm monitoring to identify markers of atrial remodelling and atrial fibrillation progression and guide therapy.

label: Phenotyping Young-Onset Atrial Fibrillation Patients study
other synonyms: Young AF study|Young-AF study
definition: An observational cohort of adults with atrial fibrillation first diagnosed before age 60, recruited at the outpatient clinic of the University Medical Center Groningen, the Netherlands, in 2012–2013, combining retrospective information near the first diagnosis with prospective follow-up to characterize their clinical and familial profile, atrial fibrillation progression and cardiovascular outcomes.

label: Biomarker AF study
other synonyms: Biomarker-AF study
definition: An observational hospital-based registry of patients with atrial fibrillation at the University Medical Center Groningen, the Netherlands, combining standard clinical atrial fibrillation assessment with blood sampling and longitudinal follow-up to identify risk profiles that guide atrial fibrillation therapy.

label: Glycometabolic Intervention as adjunct to Primary percutaneous intervention in ST elevation myocardial infarction (GIPS)-III trial
other synonyms: GIPS study|GIPS-III trial|Glycometabolic Intervention as adjunct to primary Percutaneous coronary intervention in ST elevation myocardial infarction|glycometabolic intervention as adjunct to primary percutaneous coronary intervention in ST elevation myocardial infarction III study
definition: A single-centre, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial at the University Medical Center Groningen, the Netherlands, that recruited patients without diabetes undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction in 2011–2013, to test whether four months of metformin treatment preserved left ventricular function.

label: Shanghai CRC Study
other synonyms: Shanghai Studies|Shanghai Studies (Shanghai-1,2,3)|Shanghai Study
definition: A population-based colorectal cancer case-control collection in Shanghai, China, assembled for genetic studies in the Asia Colorectal Cancer Consortium from the Shanghai-1, Shanghai-2 and Shanghai-3 sample series. The early series include colorectal cancer cases and cancer-free controls from the Shanghai Women’s Health Study and Shanghai Men’s Health Study, with additional controls from Shanghai breast cancer studies; Shanghai-3 includes colorectal cancer cases newly recruited through the Shanghai Cancer Registry in 2009–2011, with controls from the health cohorts and breast cancer studies.

label: Hwasun Cancer Epidemiology Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of multiple cancers in South Korea, with disease-specific series including breast and colorectal cancer at Chonnam National University Hwasun Hospital in Jeollanam-do province. It recruits newly diagnosed cancer patients and community controls to investigate factors in cancer development and clinical progression; its disease-specific series use interview and medical-record information and blood samples.

label: Stockholm-1
other synonyms: Stockholm-1 cohort|Stockholm-1 study|The Stockholm Study
definition: A cohort of men aged 80 or younger who underwent prostate biopsy in Stockholm, Sweden, between 2005 and 2007, identified through pathology-department registries and excluding men with known prostate cancer before 2005. Participants provided blood samples and questionnaire information, with historical prostate-specific antigen measurements and cancer diagnoses, stage and grade obtained through laboratory and cancer-registry linkage, to investigate inherited susceptibility and improve prostate cancer risk prediction.

label: Childhood Cancer and Leukemia International Consortium
other synonyms: Childhood Leukemia International Consortium
definition: An international consortium established in 2007 that pools harmonized individual-level epidemiologic and germline genetic data from independent case-control and cohort studies to investigate causes of childhood leukemia and other childhood cancers, with its scope expanded to other cancers in 2019. Its collaborative analyses examine environmental and genetic risk factors, their interactions, exposure timing, and differences among disease subtypes.
exposures: designed to study: exposure event (ExO:0000002)

label: Australian Study of Causes of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia in Children
other synonyms: Australian Study of Causes of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia in Children|Aus–ALL Consortium
definition: A national, population-based multicentre case-control study in Australia that recruited children younger than 15 years with newly diagnosed acute lymphoblastic leukemia and population controls during 2003–2007. Cases were recruited through hospitals and controls through random-digit dialing, with questionnaire information and biospecimens from children and parents used to investigate environmental and genetic causes, including maternal folate supplementation and gene–environment interactions.
diseases: patients with: childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia (MONDO:0000870)
exposures: designed to study: exposure event (ExO:0000002)

label: International Lymphoma Epidemiology Consortium
other synonyms: InterLymph Consortium|InterLymph consortium
definition: An international consortium that facilitates collaboration among epidemiologic studies of lymphoma and pools individual-level data from lymphoid malignancy case-control studies to investigate lymphoma etiology and subtype-specific risk factors, including associations with rare exposures and less common lymphoma subtypes.

label: HD10 trial
other synonyms: HD10 study
definition: A randomized multicentre trial cohort of patients aged 16–75 years with newly diagnosed, biopsy-proven, early-stage Hodgkin lymphoma without adverse risk factors, assembled by the German Hodgkin Study Group to compare two or four cycles of ABVD chemotherapy followed by involved-field radiotherapy at 20 or 30 Gy.

label: HD11 trial
other synonyms: German Hodgkin Study Group HD11 trial
definition: A randomized multicentre trial cohort of patients aged 16–75 years with newly diagnosed, biopsy-proven, early unfavorable Hodgkin lymphoma, assembled by the German Hodgkin Study Group to compare four cycles of ABVD with four cycles of baseline-dose BEACOPP chemotherapy, each followed by involved-field radiotherapy at 20 or 30 Gy.

label: HD12 trial
other synonyms: HD12 study|HD12 trial of the German Hodgkin Study Group
definition: A randomized multicentre trial cohort of patients aged 16–65 years with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed, advanced-stage Hodgkin lymphoma, enrolled by the German Hodgkin Study Group from January 1999 to January 2003 to compare eight cycles of escalated-dose BEACOPP with four escalated-dose followed by four baseline-dose cycles, and to compare consolidation radiotherapy with no radiotherapy for initial bulky or residual disease.

label: International Consortium of Bladder Cancer
definition: An international consortium formed in 2005 that pools comparable data from independent bladder cancer studies to investigate environmental and genetic risk factors and their interactions. Its collaborative analyses combine case-control and case-only data, including investigations of DNA repair gene variation and cigarette smoking in bladder cancer susceptibility.
exposures: designed to study: exposure event (ExO:0000002)

label: IARC-Thai Breast Cancer Study
other synonyms: IARC-Thai Breast Cancer|IARC‐Thai Breast Cancer Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of breast cancer in Thai women in Thailand, initially recruiting women with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed breast cancer at the National Cancer Institute in Bangkok and Khon Kaen Hospital during May 2002–March 2004, with controls randomly selected among healthy women visiting patients at the same hospitals for diseases other than breast or ovarian cancer, to investigate breast cancer susceptibility, including variation in DNA repair genes.

label: European Network for Genetic And Genomic Epidemiology
other synonyms: ENGAGE Consortium|ENGAGE consortium|European Network for Genetic and Genomic Epidemiology
definition: A European research consortium that provides infrastructure to combine large population study samples and datasets across populations of European origin for genetic and genomic epidemiology, conducting genome-wide association meta-analyses of complex traits, including serum lipid levels and smoking behavior, using data from participating population cohorts, twin cohorts and clinical collections.

label: Genetic Epidemiology of Glioma International Consortium
other synonyms: GLIOGENE Consortium|Gliogene Consortium
definition: An international consortium that studies inherited susceptibility to glioma through a familial glioma study and the Glioma International Case-Control Study. It recruits families affected by multiple gliomas and coordinates multisite case-control recruitment, questionnaire data and biospecimen collection to investigate genetic risk and gene-environment interactions.

label: National Cancer Institute Adult Brain Study
definition: A hospital-based case-control study of adults aged 18 or older with newly diagnosed primary glioma or other neuroepitheliomatous tumors, meningioma, or acoustic neuroma, and patients admitted for nonmalignant conditions, recruited at referral hospitals in Boston, Phoenix and Pittsburgh, United States, between June 1994 and August 1998. Controls were frequency-matched to the case series on age, sex, race or ethnicity, hospital and residential distance from the hospital. Interviews and biological samples support investigation of brain-tumor risk factors, including cellular-telephone use, occupational exposures and genetic susceptibility.
diseases: patients with: acoustic neuroma (MONDO:0001569)|patients with: glioma (MONDO:0021042)|patients with: meningioma (MONDO:0016642)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to radiowave radiation (ECTO:8000054)

label: BRCA1 and BRCA2 Cohort Consortium
other synonyms: BRCA1 and BRCA2 cohort consortium|The BRCA1 and BRCA2 Cohort Consortium
definition: An international consortium that harmonizes risk-factor and prospective follow-up data on women carrying pathogenic BRCA1 or BRCA2 variants from the International BRCA1/2 Carrier Cohort Study, Breast Cancer Family Registry and kConFab. Participants are drawn from clinical genetics and population-based family studies to estimate breast, ovarian and contralateral breast cancer risks and investigate their genetic and non-genetic modifiers.
diseases: at risk of: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|at risk of: ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170)

label: Gene Etude Prospective Sein Ovaire
other synonyms: French National BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations carrier cohort|prospective cohort of BRCAx mutation carriers
definition: A French nationwide prospective cohort initiated in 2000 to estimate breast, ovarian and other cancer risks in women carrying pathogenic BRCA1 or BRCA2 variants and to assess lifestyle, environmental and genetic factors that modify these risks. Participants are recruited through family cancer clinics after genetic counseling and followed for primary or subsequent cancer, including women already diagnosed with cancer and those unaffected at enrollment.
diseases: at risk of: breast cancer (MONDO:0007254)|at risk of: ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170)
exposures: designed to study: exposure event (ExO:0000002)

label: National Prostate Cancer Register of Sweden
other synonyms: National Prostate Cancer Register
definition: A nationwide clinical prostate cancer registry in Sweden, originating from a regional register established in 1987 and covering the country since 1998, that records newly diagnosed prostate cancer, diagnostic workup, tumour characteristics and primary treatment to support quality assurance, benchmarking and clinical research on care and outcomes.

label: National Prostate Cancer Register of Sweden Follow-up Study
acronyms: NPCR Follow-up Study|NPCR of Sweden Follow-up Study
definition: A nationwide retrospective observational cohort of men with localized prostate cancer selected from the National Prostate Cancer Register of Sweden, with registration from January 1997 to December 2002, beginning in January 1998 in one healthcare region. Participants were aged 70 years or younger at diagnosis, had clinical local tumour stage T1–T2 and serum prostate-specific antigen below 20 ng/mL, and had no recorded signs of lymph-node or bone metastasis (N0/Nx and M0/Mx). Medical-record review and linkage to national registers were used to assess management and outcomes.

label: Florence Acute Myocardial Infarction-2 registry
other synonyms: AMI-Florence 2 registry|AMI-Florence II cohort|acute myocardial infarction in Florence 2 registry
definition: A registry of patients with acute myocardial infarction admitted to the coronary units of the six hospitals of the Florence health district, Italy, between April 2008 and April 2009, followed for survival after the infarction.

label: Chinese Glioma Genome Atlas
other synonyms: CGGA cohort
definition: A collection of primary and recurrent glioma samples, with genomic data and patient follow-up, from patients treated at Beijing Tiantan Hospital and other hospitals in China, all re-diagnosed by independent neuropathologists and made available through a cross-omics data portal.

label: CRYOSTEM
other synonyms: CRYOSTEM Consortium|CRYOSTEM cohort|CRYOSTEM collection|Cryostem biobank
definition: A French national cohort of haematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients, and for some of them their donors, sampled before transplantation, at 100 days, one and two years afterwards and when graft-versus-host disease occurred, to study the complications of haematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
diseases: at risk of: graft versus host disease (MONDO:0013730)

label: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute ALL Consortium
other synonyms: Dana Farber Cancer Institute ALL Consortium|Dana-Farber Cancer Institute (DFCI) acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) Consortium
definition: A consortium formed in 1981 by the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and other institutions in the United States and Canada that has conducted consecutive multi-institutional clinical trial protocols in childhood acute lymphoblastic leukaemia.

label: Early Life Interventions for Childhood Growth and Development in Tanzania
other synonyms: ELICIT trial|Early Life Interventions for Childhood Growth and Development In Tanzania|Early Life Interventions for Childhood growth and development in Tanzania
definition: A randomised, placebo-controlled, factorial trial of antimicrobials (azithromycin and nitazoxanide) and nicotinamide in children recruited within the first 14 days of life in rural Haydom, Tanzania, followed with their mothers through monthly home visits, with the child's length-for-age at 18 months as its primary outcome.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to nicotinamide via ingestion (ECTO:0900090)

label: Human Tissue Laboratory
other synonyms: EXODIAB biobank|Excellence in Diabetes biobank
definition: A collection of pancreatic islets and of liver, muscle, fat and other tissues, with donor information and disease history, from organ donors, established in 2007 by Lund University and Uppsala University within the Excellence of Diabetes Research in Sweden (EXODIAB) collaboration.
diseases: population study of: type 1 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005147)|population study of: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: FLAVonoids: University of Reading Study
other synonyms: FLAVURS trial
definition: A single-blind, parallel, randomised controlled dietary intervention trial in which men and women with low fruit and vegetable intake and at least a 1.5-fold increased risk of cardiovascular disease were assigned to high-flavonoid or low-flavonoid fruit and vegetables or to their habitual diet, to measure the dose-response relation with vascular function and other cardiovascular risk indicators.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to vegetable food product via ingestion (ECTO:0070232)

label: Human Metabolome study
other synonyms: HuMet Repository|HuMet study
definition: A study in which young healthy male volunteers underwent a highly controlled four-day challenge protocol of 36 hours of fasting, oral glucose and lipid tests, liquid test meals, physical exercise and cold stress, with blood, urine, exhaled air and breath condensate analysed at up to 56 time points, to analyse the dynamics of the human metabolome in response to environmental stimuli.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to decreased temperature (ECTO:0001057)|designed to study: exposure to exercise (ECTO:6000002)|designed to study: exposure to fasting intervention (ECTO:2000118)

label: Immunophenotyping Assessment in a COVID-19 Cohort
other synonyms: IMPACC study|IMmunoPhenotyping Assessment in a COVID-19 Cohort
definition: A prospective longitudinal study of adults hospitalised with COVID-19 in the United States, launched in May 2020 by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, following their clinical course and immune responses through serial sampling.

label: Interactive Diet and Activity Tracking in AARP Study
other synonyms: IDATA Study
definition: A study of adult AARP members aged 50 to 74 years recruited from the Pittsburgh area, Pennsylvania, United States, in 2012 and followed for 12 months with repeated dietary, physical activity and biomarker measurements.

label: Isala
other synonyms: Isala citizen-science project|Isala program
definition: A citizen-science cohort of women in Belgium who provided self-collected vaginal samples and completed extensive questionnaires, to characterise the vaginal microbiome and its associations with health, lifestyle and life-course events.

label: Mutographs
other synonyms: Mutographs biorepository|Mutographs project
definition: A biorepository of 7,808 people with cancer at one of eight anatomical sites, from 30 countries, whose tumour and non-tumour tissues, blood and harmonised demographic, lifestyle, environmental and clinical data were assembled between 2018 and 2022 under one protocol, to explain geographical and temporal differences in cancer incidence through mutational signature analysis.
diseases: patients with: colorectal cancer (MONDO:0005575)|patients with: esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (MONDO:0005580)|patients with: gallbladder cancer (MONDO:0005411)|patients with: gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (MONDO:0003219)|patients with: head and neck cancer (MONDO:0005627)|patients with: pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (MONDO:0005184)|patients with: renal cell carcinoma (MONDO:0005086)|patients with: urinary bladder cancer (MONDO:0001187)
exposures: designed to study: exposure to Tobacco Use (ECTO:6000041)|designed to study: exposure to alcohol consumption (ECTO:0001082)

label: NCI-UMD-German cohort
definition: A cohort of patients with resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma whose tumour tissues and clinical information were collected at the University of Maryland Medical System, Baltimore, United States, through a National Cancer Institute resource contract, and at the University Medical Center Göttingen, Germany.

label: NR-SAFE
other synonyms: NR-SAFE: a Safety Study Investigating Treatment With High-dose Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) in Parkinson's Disease
definition: A single-centre, randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind phase I trial at Haukeland University Hospital, Bergen, Norway, in which people with Parkinson's disease received 1,500 mg of nicotinamide riboside twice daily or placebo for four weeks, to evaluate the safety of high-dose nicotinamide riboside.

label: OmegaROP
other synonyms: OmegaROP study|Study of the Implication of Omega-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids in Retinopathy of Prematurity in Newborns
definition: A prospective cohort of all preterm infants born before 29 weeks of gestational age and admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit of Dijon University Hospital, France, between July 2015 and January 2018, whose erythrocyte polyunsaturated fatty acids were measured shortly after birth to evaluate their value in predicting retinopathy of prematurity.
diseases: at risk of: retinopathy of prematurity (MONDO:0006952)

label: RA-MAP Consortium
other synonyms: RA MRC/ABPI (RA-MAP) Consortium|RA-MAP Project|RA-MAP consortium
definition: A UK industry-academic precision medicine partnership, funded by the Medical Research Council and the Association of the British Pharmaceutical Industry, that recruited a cohort of patients with early rheumatoid arthritis and a cohort of healthy people receiving the hepatitis B vaccine, followed for up to 18 months with deep clinical and multi-omic phenotyping, to find predictors of disease outcome and treatment response.

label: Towards A Cure for Early Rheumatoid Arthritis
other synonyms: Towards A CurE for RA
definition: An inception cohort of newly diagnosed, initially treatment-naive patients with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, recruited from 28 centres in the United Kingdom and assessed every three months for up to 18 months, established by the RA-MAP Consortium.

label: Screening Across the Lifespan Twin Study
definition: A study in which all living twins in the Swedish Twin Registry born in 1958 or earlier were invited, between March 1998 and December 2002, to a computer-assisted telephone interview on demographics and health conditions, and whose participants were then followed for changes in health status.

label: TOFI_Asia
other synonyms: Characterising the Pre-diabetic Asian and Caucasian Phenotype: The 'TOFI' Profile|TOFI_Asia study
definition: A cross-sectional study at the Human Nutrition Unit of the University of Auckland, New Zealand, of Asian Chinese and European Caucasian adults aged 20 to 70 years across a wide range of body mass index, normoglycaemic or prediabetic, studying the greater susceptibility of Asian Chinese to visceral adiposity and type 2 diabetes.
diseases: at risk of: type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148)

label: The Effect of Dietary Bioactives on Gut Microbiome Diversity
other synonyms: Dietary BIoactives and Microbiome DivErsity study|The Effect of Dietary BIoactives on Gut Microbiome DivErsity|The Effect of Dietary Bioactives on Gut Microbiome DivErsity
definition: A randomised crossover pilot trial in which healthy adults ate two-week diets high or low in plant bioactives, with matched total fibre and separated by a four-week washout, to assess changes in the gut microbiome and in urinary and faecal metabolites.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to dietary intervention (ECTO:2000068)

label: VMET study
definition: A cohort of pregnant women with singleton pregnancies, with and without risk factors for preterm birth, recruited at hospitals in the United Kingdom and sampled with cervicovaginal swabs at up to five timepoints through pregnancy.

label: Vaginal Microbiome and Metabonome in Pregnancy study
other synonyms: Vaginal Microbiome and Metabolome in Pregnancy (VMET 2) Research Study|Vaginal Microbiome and Metabonome in Pregnancy (VMET-2) Research study
definition: A cohort of women at risk of preterm birth prospectively recruited from preterm birth prevention clinics at five hospitals in London and Edinburgh, United Kingdom, between 2014 and 2023.

label: Zambia Exclusive Breastfeeding Study
other synonyms: ZEBS study|Zambian Exclusive Breast-feeding Study
definition: A randomised trial in Lusaka, Zambia, in which HIV-infected women who planned to breastfeed exclusively to four months were assigned to counselling that encouraged abrupt weaning at four months or continued breastfeeding, to evaluate the effect of early weaning on the HIV-free survival of their children to 24 months.
exposures: designed to study: exposure to human milk (raw) via ingestion (ECTO:0070224)
